title: The Matrix
description: The Matrix. 1999. USA. Written and directed by Lana and Lilly Wachowski. Kung fu choreographer Yuen Woo-ping. With Keanu Reeves, Laurence Fishburne, Carrie-Anne Moss. 35mm. 136 min. One of the most influential science-fiction films ever made, The Matrix follows a hacker (Keanu Reeves) who discovers that the world he inhabits is an elaborate simulation engineered by machines. The Wachowskis (Lana and Lilly) imagined an action aesthetic drawing on anime, Hong Kong kung fu cinema, and John Woo’s balletic gunplay, envisioning fights that would remain legible—built on extended, uninterrupted movement even as editing, wirework, and groundbreaking visual effects gave the action a distinctly futuristic velocity. Inspired by Jet Li’s Fist of Legend (1994), they invited that film’s choreographer, Yuen Woo-ping, to join the production. His intensive fight camp transformed Reeves, Carrie-Anne Moss, and Laurence Fishburne into convincing martial artists, while his character-specific choreography and inventive wirework gave the combat an uncanny, weightless grace. The result completely reshaped the Hollywood action film.

title: Cinemas of Transgression
description: In the late 1970s, the New York Underground bred a new mutation in film and video, willfully crude and confrontational in form and content. Itself an outgrowth of punk and No Wave, its practitioners dubbed it the “Cinema of Transgression.” This program looks at the legacies of these provocations with the thesis that there are many cinemas of transgression, far beyond the initial Death-Trip. These films mock and profane the sacred cows of art and cinema, violate the material image itself, oppose the dominant politick, and confront the culture with elements it prefers to leave unexamined. title: Snake in the Eagle’s Shadow (蛇形刁手)
description: Snake in the Eagle’s Shadow (蛇形刁手). 1978. Hong Kong. Directed by Yuen Woo-ping. Martial arts direction by Yuen Woo-ping, Hsu Hsia. With Jackie Chan, Yuen Siu-tien. DCP. Courtesy Swank Motion Pictures. In Cantonese; English subtitles. 98 min. A landmark in the careers of Yuen Woo-ping and Jackie Chan, Snake in the Eagle’s Shadow marked Yuen’s directorial debut and launched Chan to instant stardom, heralding the arrival of a new kung fu icon in the wake of Bruce Lee’s untimely death in 1973. Blending intricate martial arts choreography with physical comedy, Yuen forged the formula that would define Chan’s screen persona and propel his international career. Chan, as an underdog who must master his fighting skills to defend his martial arts school from a rival clan, stars opposite the inimitable Yuen Siu-tien, Yuen Woo-ping’s father, a celebrated Peking Opera performer, actor, and martial arts director whose mentorship profoundly shaped his son’s trajectory.

Directed by Jon Buchanan. 7 mins. 16mm. SSS. 1988. USA. Directed by Henry Hills. 5 mins. 16mm. The story of underground cinema is a New York Story. American avant-garde film culture grew out of the unique conditions of New York City’s density, diversity, and collective ethos. In contrast to the dominant Hollywood model, the New York underground elevates poetics over storytelling. These films prioritize lived experience of the city, awash in memo and intimacy. They are interior monologues recollecting recognizable sites: Coney Island, Times Square, Harlem, the subway system, and others; not narratives, but histories. Ken Jacobs once said, “Stories are for Bedtime,” and, after all, this is a city that never sleeps.

title: THE SCOUT
description: Director González-Nasser spent six years working as a location scout. In this luminous directorial debut, she brings us into a day in the life of a young scout tasked with finding the perfect interiors for a television pilot. Sofía (Mimi Davila) moves in and out of other people’s intimate spaces and quotidian lives, tweaking her personality just enough to connect while struggling to find balance between her professional and personal worlds. With a mounting stack of parking tickets and the impertinent commentaries of her crew, she faces a series of small-yet-paralyzing obstacles that render her day increasingly exhausting. Through a constellation of quiet but poignant vignettes, the film offers an original view into the invisible labor of TV production, unfolding as an alternative symphony of a New York grappling with gentrification and a growing erosion of empathy.

title: YOU HAD TO BE THERE
description: The 1972 Toronto production of the musical Godspell featured an eye-popping cast of future comedy titans: Martin Short, Eugene Levy, Andrea Martin, Gilda Radner, Dave Thomas—with Victor Garber as a hippie Jesus and Paul Shaffer as musical director. YOU HAD TO BE THERE features interviews with all surviving members, hilariously recounting a production that changed the course of comedy in North America. “Joyous... the 1972 Godspell planted seeds that would grow into a tree of many branches—one branch being SNL, another SCTV, another being comedies like BEST IN SHOW.” — Matthew Carey, Deadline

title: ROUGH TREATMENT (WITHOUT ANESTHESIA)
description: A television journalist’s career and personal life unravel simultaneously in this Kafkaesque political drama and paranoid thriller that was the first of five Wajda films scripted by Agnieszka Holland. Made just before the rise of the Solidarity movement, Wajda considers this to be one of his most directly personal and politically timely works, “I made it at a time when the regime realized that other authorities—such as the authority of art—were threatening it, so it had to undermine them all in order to assert its own. Suddenly, there was no longer a social life in the department of the university where I taught. I had to react against it.”

title: KORCZAK
description: Janusz Korczak was a renowned doctor, teacher, and author who ran a Jewish orphanage in the Warsaw Ghetto, and ultimately sacrificed his life to stay with them until his deportation to Treblinka. With a bracingly unsentimental script by Agnieszka Holland, and stunning black-and-white cinematography by Robby Müller intercut with actual archival footage, Wajda recreates life in the ghetto in vivid detail. Wajda fought for years to get this film made, claiming “Jewish themes in Polish culture have been virtually banned for twenty years.”

title: FILIPIÑANA
description: 17-year-old Isabel navigates the opulent pavilions and lush green landscapes of Dr. Palanca’s luxury golf course as a newly-hired “tee girl.” Meticulously composed, highly stylized, and guided by precisely choreographed movement and deadpan delivery, FILIPIÑANA unfolds through the gradual accumulation of everyday encounters between staff and the wealthy clients of this secluded country club on the outskirts of Manila. When she attempts to return a lost golf club, Isabel uncovers a dark underbelly beneath the club’s pristine surfaces, in this sweltering, pastel-colored fairy tale of class division, institutional patriarchy, and invisible violence.

title: Diaries, Notes, and Sketches
description: Jonas Mekas famously disliked the term “experimental film” and discouraged its use to describe his work and that of his comrades in the New American Cinema. Millennium Film Workshop instead chose “Personal Cinema” as the descriptor for our ongoing series presenting new work from individual moving-image artists—a term we think would have been a lot more agreeable to Jonas. This program, which takes its name from the subtitle of Mekas’s own Walden (1968), features works in the diaristic style he pioneered, illustrating the idea of “Personal Cinema” in its purest form. title: DANTON
description: Based on The Danton Affair, a 1930s play that Wajda directed on stage in 1975, this boisterous and lavish French production starring Gerard Depardieu and scripted by Jean-Claude Carriere, may have seemed like a break from contemporary Polish politics. But Depardieu’s Danton, an earthy, plain-spoken man of the people, was widely seen as a representation of Polish solidarity leader Lech Walesa, and Wojciech Pszoniak’s reserved, cerebral Robespierre, was seen as the iron-fisted military general and Polish president Wojciech Jaruzelski. The film’s politics have been widely debated, but the movie, a rare Wajda production made outside of his own country, was a hit of the 1983 New York Film Festival and an arthouse success.

title: An Evening with Christopher Kulendran Thomas
description: Multidisciplinary artist Christopher Kulendran Thomas joins us for a screening of his recent video works, which typically appear within immersive installations speculating on our technologically mediated realities. The artist, who is based between Berlin and New York City, spent his early life in London after his family escaped ethnic oppression in Sri Lanka. Kulendran Thomas, who is of Tamil descent, often returns to this history to examine its aftermath, particularly through the Western world’s conceptualization of human rights, individual autonomy within the nation state, and socio-technological change in the region. Kulendran Thomas’s videos combine archival footage, found online videos, and AI-generated deepfakes of such cultural figures as Taylor Swift and Kim Kardashian to create critical, multifaceted narratives on these entangled topics. The screening will include Being Human (2019)—also currently on view as an installation in the Museum’s second-floor collection galleries—which considers the rise of the Sri Lankan contemporary art market in the wake of the Sri Lankan Civil War (1983–2009). Kulendran Thomas will also present excerpts from The Finesse (2022), which was recently included in the New Museum’s exhibition New Humans: Memories from the Future. This project looks closely at the Tamil independence movement and the history leading up to the civil war in Sri Lanka. The artist will also present work-in-progress excerpts from an upcoming project. The screening will be followed by a conversation between the artist and Stuart Comer, MoMA’s Lonti Ebers Chief Curator of Media and Performance. Being Human. 2019. Sri Lanka. Directed by Christopher Kulendran Thomas in collaboration with Annika Kuhlmann. 24 min. Excerpts from The Finesse. 2022. Sri Lanka/Germany. title: ASHES AND DIAMONDS
description: In the spring of 1945, weary and disillusioned by the war against the Nazis that has just ended, uncertain about a future under Communist rule, two resistance fighters are under orders to assassinate the incoming district leader. One of the fighters, the brooding Maciek, played by Zbigniew Cybulski (often called “the Polish James Dean”), falls in love with a local barmaid, and is suddenly torn about how to move forward. As Wajda said about ASHES AND DIAMONDS, almost universally regarded as his masterpiece, “I have tried to reveal to movie audiences the complicated and difficult world of a generation to which I myself belong.” This anguished, romantic, and deeply personal film is an all-time favorite of both Francis Ford Coppola and Martin Scorsese, who placed it as #3 on his top ten list for Sight and Sound.

title: THE WEDDING
description: The turn-of-the-century wedding between a famed poet and a peasant woman inspired the popular 1901 play The Wedding by Stanislaw Wyspiański. Written at a time when Polish intellectuals were trying to find connections with the country’s peasantry, the play is a satire of this idealistic urge, and an allegory for the nation’s history, making it ideal source material for this rarely screened adaptation. A kaleidoscopic whirl of activity, the film follows the revelries of the wedding guests, and things get more surreal as the evening goes on, and figures from Polish history appear, including a king’s jester, a medieval hero, and the leader of a peasant revolt. Wajda creates a fantasmagoria; he says he wanted “a film reality in which the worlds of thoughts, feelings, and occurrences might co-exist on an equal footing; where dream and reality would imperceptibly intertwine.”

Martial arts direction by the Yuen Clan (Yuen Woo-ping, Yuen Chun-yeung, Yuen Shun-yi, Yuen Cheung-yan, Yuen Yat-chor, Chiu Chung-hing). With Luen Kar-yan, Yuen Cheung-yan, Yuen Yat-chor. DCP courtesy Fortune Star Media. In Cantonese, English, Mandarin; English subtitles. 99 min. This delirious wuxia fantasy follows a young man caught between rival kung fu masters whose feud escalates into a wild struggle of magic, deception, and supernatural powers. One of Yuen Woo-ping’s most exuberantly imaginative works, The Miracle Fighters treats martial arts as a playground for invention, filled with levitating weapons, trick-trap tournaments, and a paper-sword-wielding demon in a jar. The film is also a remarkable showcase for the Yuen Clan; Yuen directs while his brothers co-choreograph and star in key roles. The result is a gleefully eccentric collision of kung fu, fantasy, slapstick comedy, and family talent.

title: LOTNA
description: Perhaps the most personally meaningful of Wajda’s World War II movies, LOTNA was likely inspired by the director’s admiration for his father, a Polish cavalry officer who was killed during the Katyń massacre in 1940. LOTNA is a beautiful white horse, given as a gift by a wealthy landowner to a Polish cavalry troop in the fateful year of 1939. As the Germans attack with planes and tanks, the underequipped Polish army relies on archaic resources, such as the cavalry. Symbolic and at times surreal, the film was controversial at the time of its release for suggesting Polish foolhardiness in the face of the Nazi threat.

title: YOU HAD TO BE THERE
description: The 1972 Toronto production of the musical Godspell featured an eye-popping cast of future comedy titans: Martin Short, Eugene Levy, Andrea Martin, Gilda Radner, Dave Thomas—with Victor Garber as a hippie Jesus and Paul Shaffer as musical director. YOU HAD TO BE THERE features interviews with all surviving members, hilariously recounting a production that changed the course of comedy in North America. “Joyous... the 1972 Godspell planted seeds that would grow into a tree of many branches—one branch being SNL, another SCTV, another being comedies like BEST IN SHOW.” — Matthew Carey, Deadline

description: Berlin’s Silver Bear winner for Best Leading Performance, Sandra Hüller fully inhabits the daunting role of a 17th-century woman who disguises herself as a male soldier, only to continue the ruse after battle, in Markus Schleinzer’s enthralling fable of faith and social intolerance. Austria’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

description: When Russia shuts down all independent media, a group of young dissident journalists must flee Moscow so they can keep reporting and not go to prison. title: Everybody Digs Bill Evans
description: Winner of the Silver Bear for Best Director at the 2026 Berlin Film Festival, Everybody Digs Bill Evans is a biographical drama film about the famous jazz pianist and composer Bill Evans. In 1961, Bill Evans is playing with what he considers the perfect musical trio until tragedy strikes in the premature death of his bass player, Scott LaFaro – his musical soulmate. Traumatised by grief, Evans stops playing for the first time since his childhood. A tug-of-war between personal torment and the seemingly safer haven of familial love will see Evans oscillate between New York and suburbia, his genius always bubbling beneath the surface. The screening on Friday 11th September will be followed by a Q&A with director Grant Gee and actor Valene Kane

title: Off-Circuit: UK PREMIERE Pin de Fartie
description: The latest production from boundlessly imaginative Argentine collective El Pampero Cine sees successive pairs of characters bid farewell: a mother and her son, a caretaker and her charge, two actors endlessly rehearsing a scene that will never be performed. A playful spin on theatrical adaptation, Alejo Moguillansky's new film is a delightfully imaginative take on Samuel Beckett's Fin de Partie , punctuated by music, tennis, and another exceptional turn by Laura Paredes. The UK Premiere screening on the 4 September will be followed by an in-person Q&A with Alejo Moguillansky.

A resourceful helicopter pilot (Kurt Russell) and the camp doctor (Richard Dysart) lead the camp crew in a desperate, gory battle against the vicious creature before it picks them all off, one by one.

description: In his final film, Luchino Visconti offers a poison-pill variation on the theme that consumed his career—the moral decay of the soul-sick aristocracy—while achieving a masterful synthesis of stylistic splendor and emotional intensity.

title: Late Fame
description: Willem Defoe plays Ed Saxberger, a forgotten New York poet, who works in the post office. After an eager and flattering young admirer appears on his doorstep, Saxberger is beckoned into a coterie of twentysomething admirers who anoint him as a rediscovered genius. Intoxicated by the attention — and by the alluring presence of Gloria, the group’s “tragic heroine” — Saxberger gradually reckons with the authenticity of his newfound poetic circle. Kent Jones's thoughtful, witty film is a wistful yet unromantic look at a lost idea of downtown New York.

description: The Donahue clan, led by husband and wife Molly and Terry (Ethel Merman and Dan Dailey), navigate the ups and downs of show biz, from their beginnings in Vaudeville to the Great Depression, in this musical comedy with songs by Irving Berlin. The family’s close bond is further tested with the arrival of the talented and driven Vicky Parker (Marilyn Monroe). Costume designer Travilla played an integral role in shaping Marilyn Monroe’s public image on- and off-screen. Together they famously produced looks that evaded censorship while still courting controversy. His designs for her showgirl characters are of particular note.
director: Walter Lang PRODUCED BY: Sol C. Siegel

title: A Man of His Time
description: A mild-mannered bureaucrat (Swann Arlaud) in 1940s Vichy France gradually comes to realize the extent of his government’s collaboration with Nazi Germany in Emmanuel Marre’s quietly sinister portrayal of the incremental evil of fascism, winner of Best Screenplay at Cannes.

title: Manhunter (4K Restoration)
description: In celebration of the 40th anniversary of Michael Mann’s Manhunter , Mann’s final cut of the film returns in a newly restored 4K version. FBI criminal profiler Will Graham is called out of early retirement to assist on a deadly case involving a murderer known as the “Tooth Fairy.” After enlisting the help of imprisoned serial killer Dr. Hannibal Lecktor, Graham and the FBI are soon entangled in a menacing cat-and-mouse game.

description: Jack Torrance (Jack Nicholson) becomes winter caretaker at the isolated Overlook Hotel in Colorado, hoping to cure his writer's block. He settles in along with his wife, Wendy (Shelley Duvall), and his son, Danny (Danny Lloyd), who is plagued by psychic premonitions. As Jack's writing goes nowhere and Danny's visions become more disturbing, Jack discovers the hotel's dark secrets and begins to unravel into a homicidal maniac hell-bent on terrorizing his family.

title: DANTON
description: Based on The Danton Affair, a 1930s play that Wajda directed on stage in 1975, this boisterous and lavish French production starring Gerard Depardieu and scripted by Jean-Claude Carriere, may have seemed like a break from contemporary Polish politics. But Depardieu’s Danton, an earthy, plain-spoken man of the people, was widely seen as a representation of Polish solidarity leader Lech Walesa, and Wojciech Pszoniak’s reserved, cerebral Robespierre, was seen as the iron-fisted military general and Polish president Wojciech Jaruzelski. The film’s politics have been widely debated, but the movie, a rare Wajda production made outside of his own country, was a hit of the 1983 New York Film Festival and an arthouse success.

title: Dust in the Wind
description: Young lovers Wan and Huen, fresh out of junior high school in the remote, mountainous mining town where they were raised, look forward to a bright future together in their new home of Taipei—only to face first the grim reality of urban life there, then a three-year separation, after Wan is drafted into the Republic of China Army, which ultimately proves fatal to their affections. Based on the personal experiences of frequent Hou co-screenwriter Wu Nien-jen, the poignant, plangent Dust in the Wind has emerged as a popular favorite among Hou’s films, his first collaboration with composer Chen Ming-chang and actor Li Tian-lu, which also features some of Mark Lee Ping-bing’s most hypnotically beautiful tracking shots. Part of Jiā: Histories of Home

title: O Brother, Where Art Thou?
description: The Coens’ country-fried, Depression era, quasi-musical take on The Odyssey borrows its title—and more than a bit of its anarchic sense of humor—from Preston Sturges’s Sullivan’s Travels, choreography cues from Busby Berkeley, and rips a few dozen pages out of the Great American Songbook for good measure. Pomaded convict Everett Ulysses McGill (George Clooney) takes a powder from a Mississippi chain gang with dimwit pals John Turturro and Tim Blake Nelson in tow and sets out to scare up his Penelope (Holly Hunter), along the way running afoul of Klansmen, gangsters, sultry creek-side sirens, and a Bible-thumping Cyclops (John Goodman), even taking a quick break en route to record a jubilant rendition of “Man of Constant Sorrow.” Part of Classical Cinema

title: Child's Play (1988)
description: When serial killer Charles Lee Ray (Brad Dourif) is mortally wounded in a police shoot-out, he uses a voodoo spell to transfer his soul into Chucky, an innocuous ‘Good Guys' doll. Young Andy (Alex Vincent) receives him as a birthday gift, and Chucky soon embarks on a killing spree. However, Charles doesn't want to be trapped in the body of the doll forever; escape is possible by transferring his personality into the first human he reveals his identity to... and naturally Andy is curious about his new toy.

title: Begotten
description: BEGOTTEN has no characters in the ordinary sense. Its final credits name three principal figures: God Killing Himself. Mother Earth. Son of Earth – Flesh on Bone. The entire film is what those names do to each other and to the earth. God Killing Himself tears open his body and dies. Mother Earth rises from what remains and takes his seed into herself. She gives birth to Son of Earth Flesh on Bone. He is cast into a barren world, seized by the Nomads, tortured, killed, and briefly returned to life by his mother.The Nomads destroy her too. The Robed Figures gather what remains of mother and son, grind their bodies down, and return them to the soil. The ground flowers.

title: Remake
description: In Remake , filmmaker Ross McElwee turns his lens on the passage of time and the uneasy space between documenting life and understanding it. The film traces McElwee’s relationship with his son Adrian, and the fragile bond the camera created between them while Adrian was alive, and now that he’s gone. Drawing from decades of footage, some shot by Ross, some by Adrian, the film becomes a layered excavation of memory and image making. Threaded through is the ghost of another project: a stalled effort by Hollywood to fictionalize McElwee’s 1986 classic, Sherman’s March . What emerges is a work shaped by absence and propelled forward by a father’s love for his son.

title: The Treasure of Bitch Islands
description: A phantasmagoric, definition-defying film from perhaps France’s premier underground filmmaker, The Treasure of Bitch Islands begins with the mysterious disappearance of an engineer who has discovered a new energy source, and follows a post-nuclear Ulysses’s voyage to locate the substances used in the engineer’s formula, only to be found and harvested on an island of mad scientists and headhunters. An anarchic allegory with a punky sensibility, part Guy Maddin pastiche, part surrealist mix-and-match, and pure cult classic. “The shoot was madness, and some of us risked our lives a few times, especially while doing a scene on the edge of this huge volcano. Ossang was really more like a rock star than a film director… I shot the film completely inspired by him and his energy, even if I was sometimes terrified.” —Darius Khondji Part of Radical Chiaroscuro: The Work of Darius Khondji

title: THE SCOUT
description: Director González-Nasser spent six years working as a location scout. In this luminous directorial debut, she brings us into a day in the life of a young scout tasked with finding the perfect interiors for a television pilot. Sofía (Mimi Davila) moves in and out of other people’s intimate spaces and quotidian lives, tweaking her personality just enough to connect while struggling to find balance between her professional and personal worlds. With a mounting stack of parking tickets and the impertinent commentaries of her crew, she faces a series of small-yet-paralyzing obstacles that render her day increasingly exhausting. Through a constellation of quiet but poignant vignettes, the film offers an original view into the invisible labor of TV production, unfolding as an alternative symphony of a New York grappling with gentrification and a growing erosion of empathy.

title: Goodbye South, Goodbye
description: One of Hou Hsiao-hsien’s unassailable 1990s masterpieces and a staggering, mesmerizing generational portrait, Goodbye South, Goodbye follows the plots and schemes of a small group of young men and women in the age of get-rich-quick late-capitalism.

title: Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall
description: Tickets Are Only Available via BFI London Film Festival Website from Tuesday 17 September 2026 10:00am: Click Here To Book One Battle After Another director Paul Thomas Anderson creates an intimate document of Geese frontman Cameron Winter’s solo piano performance at the legendary New York concert hall. In December 2025, Paul Thomas Anderson collaborated with fellow filmmaker Benny Safdie on a multi-perspective and multi-format recording of Winter's solo performance. The warm hues capture the feeling in the room, including audience reactions, to create an immersive cinematic experience for those of us who couldn’t be there. It's a rapturous celebration of live performance, whose appeal should reach far beyond the band and Winter's existing fan base.

description: The new adventure sees the residents of Mossy Bottom Farm looking forward to Halloween - until the clumsy Farmer trashes the Flock's beloved pumpkin patch. When Shaun turns mad scientist to fix the problem, things rapidly spiral out of control, leading to a wild beast roaming the woods.

title: MAN OF MARBLE
description: An aggressive documentary filmmaker fights present-day 1970s government censorship as she seeks the truth about bricklayer Matuesz Birkut, a state-manufactured proletariat hero during the Soviet-controlled 1950s. Fourteen years in the making, MAN OF MARBLE is a film-within-a-film that blends documentary, pseudo-documentary, and fictional techniques that inevitably draw comparison to CITIZEN KANE. Like Orson Welles’ masterpiece, MAN OF MARBLE is a reflection on national history and mythology and also on the very nature of filmmaking. It also turned out to prophesize the worker strikes of 1980 and the rise of the Solidarity movement.

title: MY NAME AIN’T SUZIE / FA GAI SI DOI
description: Positioned as a rebuke to the colonial fantasy of THE WORLD OF SUZIE WONG (1960), MY NAME AIN’T SUZIE spans three decades of the life of a girl from a poor fishing village who makes a name for herself as a courtesan in the Wan Chai red light district in Hong Kong. Over the course of the film, MY NAME AIN’T SUZIE confronts and redresses the occidental fantasies of the East through the protagonists’ interactions with her clients.

title: Cotton Queen
description: In a cotton-farming village in Sudan, teenage Nafisa is raised on heroic tales of battling British colonisers told by her grandmother, the village matriarch Al-Sit. But when a young businessman arrives from abroad with a new development plan and genetically engineered cotton, Nafisa becomes the centre of a power play to determine the future of the village. Awakening to her own strength, Nafisa sets out to save the cotton fields – and herself. Neither she nor her community will ever be the same again.

title: THE VANISHING (SPOORLOOS)
description:
While stopping at a motorway service station during a cycling holiday in France, Saskia disappears without a trace. Years later, her partner Rex remains consumed by the mystery, unable to accept the absence of an explanation. As his obsession deepens, he begins receiving messages from a seemingly ordinary man who claims to know exactly what happened. What follows is not a conventional investigation but a chilling confrontation with the nature of curiosity, certainty, and the human need for closure.
Adapted by Tim Krabbé from his novella The Golden Egg, The Vanishing is one of the defining European thrillers of the late twentieth century. George Sluizer's film rejects the mechanics of the conventional murder mystery in favour of a rigorously controlled study of obsession and psychological terror. Drawing much of its power from its matter-of-fact presentation of extraordinary events, the film transforms everyday spaces—petrol stations, campsites, suburban homes—into sites of profound unease. Its influence can be traced through decades of psychological thrillers, while its famously devastating conclusion remains among the most unsettling in modern cinema.

title: Heart of the Beast
description: After a harrowing plane crash, Special Forces officer James Belmont (Brad Pitt) and his combat dog, Odin, find themselves stranded deep in the Alaskan wilderness. Together, they are forced into a brutal fight for survival against the elements. From acclaimed filmmaker David Ayer, Heart of the Beast is an intense adventure thriller that explores the unbreakable bond between a man and his best friend as they face their greatest battle yet.

title: Girls Like Girls
description: Based on writer/director Hayley Kiyoko's hit single and best-selling novel of the same name and featuring all-new music from Kiyoko, GIRLS LIKE GIRLS is a heartfelt coming-of-age story set over the course of one sun-drenched summer, where new-girl-in-town Coley falls in love for the first time while learning to accept herself along the way.

title: TAKE ME HOME
description: The American Cinematheque is thrilled to announce a limited engagement of TAKE ME HOME, Liz Sargent’s feature length version of the 2024 PROOF Film Festival Grand Jury Prize winner. From an award-winning short film to a world premiere at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival with the feature is an inspirational journey, and we wish the team the best as they bring this moving film around the world.

Tom Cruise stars as oil tycoon DIGGER in this darkly comic satire of power, ego and self-preservation from Academy Award-winning director Alejandro G. Iñárritu. Shot entir...

title: MY UNDESIRABLE FRIENDS: PART II – EXILE: Chapters 1-3
description: When Russia shuts down all independent media, a group of young dissident journalists must flee Moscow so they can keep reporting and not go to prison. In her riveting follow-up to last year’s awards-sweeping MY UNDESIRABLE FRIENDS — LAST AIR IN MOSCOW, Julia Loktev follows these courageous, sharply funny women (and a few men) as they fan out across a dozen countries, to Istanbul, Tbilisi, Prague, Vienna, Amsterdam, New York, and beyond. Over the course of four years, they continue to report the truth to Russians from exile, covering their country’s war crimes, even as they face death threats and are declared extremists and terrorists—as they find new meanings of family, friendship, love, and home far from the country to which they may never return. (Viewers can follow EXILE without first seeing LAST AIR IN MOSCOW.)

title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother 35mm
description: Latif is a devoutly religious hitman who struggles to balance work, faith, and fatherhood. When his wife dies, he embarks on a desperate journey across Houston in search of breast milk for his infant daughter, all while dodging sex traffickers, an evangelical militia, and his own demons.

title: Stalker
description: Three men search a dangerous, restricted area known as the Zone looking for a secret room that supposedly grants wishes. Director Andrei Tarkovsky ( Solaris , 1972) faced unusual hardships during production, including a literally toxic location and problems with film stock that forced nearly an entire film’s worth of reshoots. But the result—one of Tarkovsky's boldest and most challenging projects—has been cited as an influential work by directors and production designers, with its stark and evocative imagery credited to Tarkovsky himself as art director, working with Aleksandr Boym and set decorator Rashit Safiullin.

description: A rich but troubled family find their lives altered by the arrival of a vagrant who tries to drown himself in their swimming pool.

New York adult film director Edward Thompson is making his latest all male, all action, all XXX but there’s another movie running in his head, a film of fantasies about an ex-love...

title: Clarissa
description: Oscar nominee Sophie Okonedo stars in twin filmmakers Arie and Chuko Esiri’s tender adaptation of Virginia Woolf’s Mrs. Dalloway, which transports the 1925 novel to contemporary Nigeria while retaining the spiritual essence of Woolf’s themes.

title: The Ninth Gate
description: Hired by a wealthy collector to authenticate a rarer-than-rare copy of Aristide Torchia’s 17th-century tome The Nine Gates of the Kingdom of Shadows, purported to allow its owner to summon the Devil, New York–based antiquarian book dealer Dean Corso (Johnny Depp) sets off for Europe—and soon finds himself contending with cutthroat cults, suspicious suicides, and a most beguiling Emmanuelle Seigner. “[Polanski] represents the essence of cinematic genius for me… [On The Ninth Gate] I learned how to appreciate the distance between the camera and the actor, and also how to move the camera—or not—at a certain point in the story. I also learned to have a strong sense of the set and its design—that the set can be an actor itself, that it can be filmed like another character in the movie. And I learned the incredible accuracy you can have when cutting from one shot to another.” —Darius Khondji Part of Radical Chiaroscuro: The Work of Darius Khondji

title: FILIPIÑANA
description: 17-year-old Isabel navigates the opulent pavilions and lush green landscapes of Dr. Palanca’s luxury golf course as a newly-hired “tee girl.” Meticulously composed, highly stylized, and guided by precisely choreographed movement and deadpan delivery, FILIPIÑANA unfolds through the gradual accumulation of everyday encounters between staff and the wealthy clients of this secluded country club on the outskirts of Manila. When she attempts to return a lost golf club, Isabel uncovers a dark underbelly beneath the club’s pristine surfaces, in this sweltering, pastel-colored fairy tale of class division, institutional patriarchy, and invisible violence.

title: Suspiria [1977]
description: Suzy (Jessica Harper) travels to Germany to attend ballet school. When she arrives, late on a stormy night, no one lets her in, and she sees Pat (Eva Axén), another student, fleeing from the school. When Pat reaches her apartment, she is murdered. The next day, Suzy is admitted to her new school, but has a difficult time settling in. She hears noises, and often feels ill. As more people die, Suzy uncovers the terrifying secret history of the place.

title: LA PRISONNIÉRE
description:
Set within the sleek, decadent world of Parisian galleries and underground fetish clubs, a young woman becomes entangled with a manipulative photographer whose erotic power games blur the line between performance and imprisonment. What begins as fascination curdles into psychological captivity as she finds herself both subject and spectator in a labyrinth of desire.
A cool, hypnotic study of control and obsession, La Prisonnière stands as the final film of Henri-Georges Clouzot. Awash in pop art colors and disorienting compositions, it transforms erotic fixation into a sleek chamber of mirrors, where liberation and confinement become indistinguishable and every gaze conceals a trap.

description: Thursday, September 10: Sneak preview and Q&A w/ star Domhnall Gleeson after the 6:15 show! On a remote Scottish isle, siblings Isla (Gayle Rankin, GLOW ) and Sandy (Grant O’Rourke, Outlander ) spend their days hunting seabirds and retelling the stories of their ancestors. They follow the strict rules inherited from their late father — protect the island, allow no incomer, survive — until one day, Daniel (Domhnall Gleeson, Ex Machina ), an awkward and socially inept council official, arrives to evacuate them. Bringing with him the strange mainland ways of laws, paperwork, veganism and internet wizardry, he turns their world upside down. Opens Fri, Sep 25, more showtimes to be announced.

title: Begotten
description: BEGOTTEN has no characters in the ordinary sense. Its final credits name three principal figures: God Killing Himself. Mother Earth. Son of Earth – Flesh on Bone. The entire film is what those names do to each other and to the earth. God Killing Himself tears open his body and dies. Mother Earth rises from what remains and takes his seed into herself. She gives birth to Son of Earth Flesh on Bone. He is cast into a barren world, seized by the Nomads, tortured, killed, and briefly returned to life by his mother.The Nomads destroy her too. The Robed Figures gather what remains of mother and son, grind their bodies down, and return them to the soil. The ground flowers.

description: When a willful young man tries to venture beyond his sequestered Pennsylvania hamlet, his actions set off a chain of chilling incidents that will alter the community forever.

title: Ghost in the Shell: 30th Anniversary Remaster
description: “My codename is Project 2501, and I am a life form that was born in a sea of information.” In the year 2029, the world looks like a hybridization of Hong Kong, Tokyo, and New York, yielding to entropy and technocracy. Cyborg Major Kusanagi, a perfect specimen of human-brained computer engineering is on the case to track and destroy an omnipotent entity known as The Puppet Master—a hacker? a virus?—who threatens world order. Her physical and existential journey deftly detailed by Oshii’s animation, combining traditional hand-drawn cells and computer-generated graphics, creating a haunting, awe-inspiring magnum opus. Part of A Cyberpunk Canon

title: The Warriors
description: “Waaarriors! Come out and play-ay!” Falsely accused of responsibility for the assassination of New York’s most powerful ganglord during a citywide summit in the Bronx’s Van Cortlandt Park, Swan (Michael Beck) and his fellow Warriors now have to fight their way back, block by block and mano a mano, to the safe shores of their Coney Island turf. The film’s knuckle-busting action choreography and its vision of NYC as a coliseum-like proving grounds for epic heroism—its source, at a distance, is Xenophon’s 4th century BC Anabasis—are delectable, but its greatness lies in its attention to character, how it lets us see a crew of provincial Brooklynites gradually discovering they’re the toughest dudes in town. Part of Classical Cinema

description: A vivid, visceral Macbeth adaptation, Throne of Blood , directed by Akira Kurosawa, sets Shakespeare’s definitive tale of ambition and duplicity in a ghostly, fog-enshrouded landscape in feudal Japan. As a hardened warrior who rises savagely to power, Toshiro Mifune gives a remarkable, animalistic performance, as does Isuzu Yamada as his ruthless wife. Throne of Blood fuses classical Western tragedy with formal elements taken from Noh theater to create an unforgettable cinematic experience. (Janus Films)

Sisters Elinor and Marianne Dashwood must leave their Sussex estate following the sudden loss of their wealthy father and are forced to move in with a distant relative. The two sisters attempt to find security and happiness whilst navigating their vastly different approaches to love.

title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

title: Digger
description: Academy Award-winning filmmaker Alejandro G. Iñárritu returns with his original film Digger, starring Tom Cruise. The most powerful man in the world (Cruise) embarks on a frantic mission to prove he is humanity’s savior before the disaster he’s unleashed destroys everything. This wildly hilarious satire was shot entirely in VistaVision.

title: The Incomer
description: Thursday, September 10: Sneak preview and Q&A w/ star Domhnall Gleeson after the 6:15 show! On a remote Scottish isle, siblings Isla (Gayle Rankin, GLOW ) and Sandy (Grant O’Rourke, Outlander ) spend their days hunting seabirds and retelling the stories of their ancestors. They follow the strict rules inherited from their late father — protect the island, allow no incomer, survive — until one day, Daniel (Domhnall Gleeson, Ex Machina ), an awkward and socially inept council official, arrives to evacuate them. Bringing with him the strange mainland ways of laws, paperwork, veganism and internet wizardry, he turns their world upside down. Opens Fri, Sep 25, more showtimes to be announced.

title: Everybody Digs Bill Evans
description: Winner of the Silver Bear for Best Director at the 2026 Berlin Film Festival, Everybody Digs Bill Evans is a biographical drama film about the famous jazz pianist and composer Bill Evans. In 1961, Bill Evans is playing with what he considers the perfect musical trio until tragedy strikes in the premature death of his bass player, Scott LaFaro – his musical soulmate. Traumatised by grief, Evans stops playing for the first time since his childhood. A tug-of-war between personal torment and the seemingly safer haven of familial love will see Evans oscillate between New York and suburbia, his genius always bubbling beneath the surface. The screening on Friday 11th September will be followed by a Q&A with director Grant Gee and actor Valene Kane

title: MY UNDESIRABLE FRIENDS: PART II – EXILE: Chapters 1-3
description: When Russia shuts down all independent media, a group of young dissident journalists must flee Moscow so they can keep reporting and not go to prison. In her riveting follow-up to last year’s awards-sweeping MY UNDESIRABLE FRIENDS — LAST AIR IN MOSCOW, Julia Loktev follows these courageous, sharply funny women (and a few men) as they fan out across a dozen countries, to Istanbul, Tbilisi, Prague, Vienna, Amsterdam, New York, and beyond. Over the course of four years, they continue to report the truth to Russians from exile, covering their country’s war crimes, even as they face death threats and are declared extremists and terrorists—as they find new meanings of family, friendship, love, and home far from the country to which they may never return. (Viewers can follow EXILE without first seeing LAST AIR IN MOSCOW.)

title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother 35mm
description: Latif is a devoutly religious hitman who struggles to balance work, faith, and fatherhood. When his wife dies, he embarks on a desperate journey across Houston in search of breast milk for his infant daughter, all while dodging sex traffickers, an evangelical militia, and his own demons.

title: Everytime
description: After a shocking accident befalls a teenage girl in Berlin, her mother, younger sister, and boyfriend drift into a state of suspended grief in Sandra Wollner’s atmospheric, constantly surprising new film, winner of the Cannes Un Certain Regard Prize. Germany’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: In The Mood For Love
description: In 1962 Hong Kong, neighbors Su Li-zhen (Mrs. Chan) and Chow Mo-wan (Mr. Chow) discover their spouses are having an affair. As they spend time together, they develop feelings for each other, but their relationship remains chaste and unspoken, reflecting societal constraints and their own moral compass.

title: 2026 New York Shorts
description: This shorts program includes the world premiere of J. Wortham’s The People’s Beach, Heather Landsman’s ee, the world premiere of Eliza Barry Callahan’s The House Call, Fanny Texier’s A Woman’s Place Is Everywhere, and the world premiere of Charlotte Wells’s New York Never Let Me Down.
director: J. Wortham, Heather Landsman, Eliza Barry Callahan, Fanny Texier, Charlotte Wells

title: The Only Living Pickpocket
description: In Noah Segan’s elegant love letter to New York, John Turturro delivers a star performance of effortless command and charisma as an aging petty thief from the Bronx who is thrust into a borough-hopping race against time.

title: Zombie Flesh Eaters [Zombi 2]
description: After an abandoned boat sails into New York harbor with a zombie aboard, a reporter teams up with the daughter of the boat's missing captain to investigate the island where he was last seen conducting research—the site of an alleged zombie outbreak.

title: UNZIPPED
description: “Isaac Mizrahi as he conceived and contorted the way through to his fall 1994 show, [dashing] around a deserted SoHo with pal Sandra Bernhard; [meeting] with Naomi Campbell, Linda Evangelista, and baby Kate Moss for fittings; and [racing] uptown to an audience with Eartha Kitt... Hair-raising deadlines, delirious Bette Davis impressions, and the hostile but exhilarating act of executing a designer’s vision come together in a work that set the bar for all fashion films after.” – Vogue

title: MAN OF MARBLE
description: An aggressive documentary filmmaker fights present-day 1970s government censorship as she seeks the truth about bricklayer Matuesz Birkut, a state-manufactured proletariat hero during the Soviet-controlled 1950s. Fourteen years in the making, MAN OF MARBLE is a film-within-a-film that blends documentary, pseudo-documentary, and fictional techniques that inevitably draw comparison to CITIZEN KANE. Like Orson Welles’ masterpiece, MAN OF MARBLE is a reflection on national history and mythology and also on the very nature of filmmaking. It also turned out to prophesize the worker strikes of 1980 and the rise of the Solidarity movement.

title: Minotaur
description: Winner of the Grand Prix at Cannes, Russian filmmaker Andrey Zvyagintsev’s riveting, razor-sharp tale of personal, patriarchal, and governmental corruption follows a wealthy CEO who begins to suspect his wife is having an extramarital affair. France’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: Free Leonard Peltier

title: Manhunter (4K Restoration)
description: In celebration of the 40th anniversary of Michael Mann’s Manhunter , Mann’s final cut of the film returns in a newly restored 4K version. FBI criminal profiler Will Graham is called out of early retirement to assist on a deadly case involving a murderer known as the “Tooth Fairy.” After enlisting the help of imprisoned serial killer Dr. Hannibal Lecktor, Graham and the FBI are soon entangled in a menacing cat-and-mouse game.

title: Whore
description: This searing melodrama investigates the life of a prostitute in a pseudo-documentary style. The life of a hooker isn’t easy…

title: Alien: Resurrection
description: The fourth entry in the Alien series brings Sigourney Weaver’s Lt. Ellen Ripley, last seen swan diving into a vat of molten steel, back from the Great Beyond—after a fashion, at least. Cloned from samples of extraterrestrial-contaminated DNA, Ripley 2.0 finds herself aboard the USM Auriga spaceship two centuries after her original’s death, and shortly thereafter contending with a new host of Xenomorphs, both fangsome foes and, now, blood relations. “Jean-Pierre… wanted to make a film that was closer to his universe, with plenty of dark humor in it… The hallways were purposely lit with green hues, which would make the actors’ skin tones come out colder… With the help of the production designer, Nigel Phelps, and the vision of Jean-Pierre, we managed in the end to make a very different kind of Alien movie.” —Darius Khondji Part of Radical Chiaroscuro: The Work of Darius Khondji

title: Chungking Express
description: A hot-shot to the heart, pop masterpiece Chungking Express tells the stories of two lovelorn cops (Takeshi Kaneshiro and Tony Leung) and the women who baffle them (Brigitte Lin and Faye Wong, who contributes a Cantopop cover of The Cranberries’ “Dreams”), its bifurcated structure suggesting the A- and B-sides of a 45. Wong’s international breakthrough introduced new audiences to his rich, sensorial brand of filmmaking, inviting one to disappear into, sink into, live inside, a voluptuary world bigger and brighter than our own—but just as heartbreaking. Part of Like the Wind: Lensed by Christopher Doyle

title: Queen at Sea
description: Starring Juliette Binoche, Tom Courtenay and Anna Calder-Marshall, Queen at Sea received its world premiere in competition at the Berlin International Film Festival earlier this year, where it won both the Silver Bear Jury Prize and the Silver Bear for Best Supporting Performance for both Courtenay and Calder-Marshall. The film follows Amanda (Binoche) and her stepfather, Martin (Courtney), at odds over a moral quandary involving Amanda’s mother, Leslie (Calder-Marshall). In the advanced stages of dementia, they quarrel over whether Leslie has lost all ability to make critical decisions in her own best interests, and, if so, who is responsible – a spouse, a child, an institution – for making such a determination? As Amanda and Martin are forced to make increasingly difficult choices, the repercussions spiral out of their control.

title: Nostalgia [Nostalghia]
description: Andrei Tarkovsky’s unforgettably haunting film, his first to be made outside Russia, explores the melancholy of the expatriate through the film’s protagonist, Gorchakov, a Russian poet researching in Italy. Arriving at a Tuscan village spa with Eugenia, his beautiful Italian interpreter, Gorchakov is visited by memories of Russia and of his wife and children, and he encounters the local mystic who sets him a challenging task. ‘Nostalgia’ is filled with a series of mysterious and extraordinary images, all of which coalesce into a miraculous whole in the film’s final shot. As in all Tarkovsky’s films, nature, the elements of fire and water, music, painting and poetry all play a major role. ★★★★ “Hauntingly beautiful” - David Parkinson, Empire

title: Sense and Sensibility (U) (AD)
description: An irresistible new take on Jane Austen ’s iconic Sense and Sensibility : a charming, witty and deeply relatable story of love and sisterhood, starring Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles .

title: 9 Temples to Heaven
description: A Thai family accompanies its ailing matriarch on a pilgrimage to nine separate Buddhist temples all in one day in this contemplative spiritual journey from Apichatpong Weerasethakul’s longtime assistant director, Sompot Chidgasornpongse. Thailand’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: The Debut
description: In Jesse Eisenberg’s theater-world comedy, Julianne Moore flings herself with delicious abandon into the role of a middle-aged New Jersey housewife who gets a part in a local stage musical despite having zero experience.

title: Cinema Paradiso [Nuovo Cinema Paradiso]
description: A winner of awards across the world including Best Foreign Language Film Oscar, 5 BAFTA Awards including Best Actor, Original Screenplay and Score, the Grand Prize of the Jury at the Cannes Film Festival and many more. Giuseppe Tornatore's loving homage to the cinema tells the story of Salvatore, a successful film director, returning home for the funeral of Alfredo, his old friend who was the projectionist at the local cinema throughout his childhood. Soon memories of his first love affair with the beautiful Elena and all the highs and lows that shaped his life come flooding back, as Salvatore reconnects with the community he left 30 years earlier.

title: FILIPIÑANA
description: 17-year-old Isabel navigates the opulent pavilions and lush green landscapes of Dr. Palanca’s luxury golf course as a newly-hired “tee girl.” Meticulously composed, highly stylized, and guided by precisely choreographed movement and deadpan delivery, FILIPIÑANA unfolds through the gradual accumulation of everyday encounters between staff and the wealthy clients of this secluded country club on the outskirts of Manila. When she attempts to return a lost golf club, Isabel uncovers a dark underbelly beneath the club’s pristine surfaces, in this sweltering, pastel-colored fairy tale of class division, institutional patriarchy, and invisible violence.

title: Digger (15) (AD)
description: Academy Award-winning filmmaker Alejandro G Iñárritu ( Birdman ) returns with his original feature starring Tom Cruise as the most powerful man in the world.

title: Report to Mother
description: Indelibly capturing the political tumult of 1970s Kerala in stark black and white, and enduring as one of South Indian cinema’s most essential works, John Abraham’s Report to Mother follows a man’s discovery of a dead body and his journey to notify the deceased’s mother.

title: The History of Concrete
description: A filmmaker applies lessons from a Hallmark movie writing workshop to pitch a documentary about concrete.

title: Remake
description: In Remake , filmmaker Ross McElwee turns his lens on the passage of time and the uneasy space between documenting life and understanding it. The film traces McElwee’s relationship with his son Adrian, and the fragile bond the camera created between them while Adrian was alive, and now that he’s gone. Drawing from decades of footage, some shot by Ross, some by Adrian, the film becomes a layered excavation of memory and image making. Threaded through is the ghost of another project: a stalled effort by Hollywood to fictionalize McElwee’s 1986 classic, Sherman’s March . What emerges is a work shaped by absence and propelled forward by a father’s love for his son.

title: Begotten
description: BEGOTTEN has no characters in the ordinary sense. Its final credits name three principal figures: God Killing Himself. Mother Earth. Son of Earth – Flesh on Bone. The entire film is what those names do to each other and to the earth. God Killing Himself tears open his body and dies. Mother Earth rises from what remains and takes his seed into herself. She gives birth to Son of Earth Flesh on Bone. He is cast into a barren world, seized by the Nomads, tortured, killed, and briefly returned to life by his mother.The Nomads destroy her too. The Robed Figures gather what remains of mother and son, grind their bodies down, and return them to the soil. The ground flowers.

title: The Diary of a Chambermaid
description: Radu Jude brilliantly explores Europe’s modern-day power and class dynamics through the trenchant story of a young Romanian woman working for a well-to-do family in Bordeaux, while her own young daughter misses her back home.

title: Cotton Queen
description: In this Arabic-language drama, a teenage girl's life in a Sudanese village is disrupted when a wealthy businessman arrives with plans to genetically engineer the local cotton crops.

title: Tai Chi Master (太極張三豐)
description: Tai Chi Master (太極張三豐). 1993. Hong Kong/China. Directed by Yuen Woo-ping. Martial arts direction by Yuen Woo-ping, Yuen Cheung-yan, Ku Huen-Chiu. With Jet Li, Michelle Yeoh, Chin Siu-ho. DCP courtesy American Genre Film Archive. In Cantonese; English subtitles. 96 min. Two friends raised together in a Shaolin monastery take radically different paths as adults, with one (Chin Siu-ho) joining a tyrannical army while the other (Jet Li) aids anti-government rebels. Directed by Yuen Woo-ping, Tai Chi Master showcases dazzling choreography, from lightning-fast hand-to-hand exchanges to elaborate wirework and inventive uses of props and terrain. Li combines extraordinary physical precision with a quietly compelling emotional arc, evolving from naive monk to serene tai chi master. Chin brings volatile energy and intensity as his friend and rival, while Michelle Yeoh adds grace and formidable martial prowess as a rebel fighter who lights up unforgettable set pieces.

title: MAN OF IRON
description: Living history, the sequel to MAN OF MARBLE, made just as the shipyard strikes were unfolding, is its mirror image. Here, the protagonist, also a journalist, is corrupted by the government when he takes an assignment to find dirt that will discredit the strike leaders. Remarkable in its timeliness, MAN OF IRON features a cameo appearance by Solidarity leader Lech Wałęsa. Filmed in January of 1981, it premiered months later at Cannes, where it won the Palme d’Or, on its way to becoming the top Polish box office hit of all time.

title: Ryuichi Sakamoto | Opus
description: His health failing, some six months before his death Sakamoto sat down before a Yamaha grand piano under the direction of his son, Sora, and gave a final command performance before the camera, a career-spanning 20-song set encompassing his time with Yellow Magic Orchestra (a new arrangement of “Tang Poo”), songs heard here for the first time (“BB,” a tribute to Bernardo Bertolucci), and soundtrack compositions for films (“The Last Emperor” and “The Sheltering Sky,” both for none other than “BB”), video games (“Lack of Love”), and even television commercials (“Aubade 2020”). A singularly elegiac concert film, almost hypnotic in its stripped-down simplicity. Q&A with cinematographer Bill Kirstein and producer Albert Tholen moderated by filmmaker Kogonada on Sunday, September 27th Part of Sakamoto on Screen Portraits of an Artist

title: Ulysses' Gaze
description: An Odyssey through the Balkans after the fall of communism following a Greek American filmmaker, known simply as “A” (Harvey Keitel), who has returned to Hellas after an absence of decades on a quest to find his own personal “Ithaca”: three reels of undeveloped film shot at the turn of the century by the Manaki Brothers, Macedonian cinema pioneers who bore witness to the last years of the Ottoman Empire. An eloquent, entrancing meditation on war, the inevitability of imperial decline, the capacity of art to render grief and loss into finer materials, and much else besides, magisterial in its melancholy. Part of Classical Cinema

title: Barrio Triste
description: In an impoverished neighborhood of 1980s Medellín, a group of disaffected teens steal a TV reporter’s camera to document their lives. Piercing the derelict landscape’s oppressive atmosphere with disarming reflections on dreams and death, their understanding of reality and hope begins to erode as reports of mysterious lights falling from the sky coincide with temporal and spatial distortions. In his striking feature debut, long-time Bad Bunny collaborator Stillz captures an intimate, formally daring portrait of Colombia's forgotten youth. Barrio Triste is heightened by a restless, intense debut score from Arca, whose fluid soundscapes anchor the film's vision. Navigating the thin line between desperation and the supernatural, Stillz delivers a beautiful, unclassifiable piece of contemporary cinema.

title: Sense and Sensibility
description: Left destitute by ruthless family members, two sisters navigate scandal, heartbreak, and strict social etiquette while searching for their perfect romantic matches.

title: Sense and Sensibility
description:
An irresistible new take on Jane Austen’s iconic Sense and Sensibility: a charming, witty, and deeply relatable story of love and sisterhood.
Three sisters experience love and heartbreak after they're forced to leave their family estate with their widowed mother and move to a humble cottage...

title: Digger
description: The most powerful man in the world embarks on a frantic mission to prove he is humanity's saviour before the disaster he’s unleashed destroys everything.

title: THE SCOUT
description: Director González-Nasser spent six years working as a location scout. In this luminous directorial debut, she brings us into a day in the life of a young scout tasked with finding the perfect interiors for a television pilot. Sofía (Mimi Davila) moves in and out of other people’s intimate spaces and quotidian lives, tweaking her personality just enough to connect while struggling to find balance between her professional and personal worlds. With a mounting stack of parking tickets and the impertinent commentaries of her crew, she faces a series of small-yet-paralyzing obstacles that render her day increasingly exhausting. Through a constellation of quiet but poignant vignettes, the film offers an original view into the invisible labor of TV production, unfolding as an alternative symphony of a New York grappling with gentrification and a growing erosion of empathy.

title: Double Freedom
description: Argentinean director Lisandro Alonso expands upon his remarkable first feature, La Libertad (NYFF39), with a contemplative, elegantly crafted sequel again following charismatic woodcutter Misael (Misael Saavedra), who must now take in his mentally unstable sister.

title: Tender Loving Care
description: Mike Leigh’s portrayal of overwhelmed, resilient lives in post-Brexit England should be received as one of his signature works, a film with a leveling sense of humor about the difficulty of asking for—and accepting—help in a world that continually lets us down.

title: The Man I Love
description: Ira Sachs’s finely detailed period drama about an emotionally complicated cabaret star and performance artist (Oscar winner Rami Malek) living with AIDS in 1980s New York is a reminder that art and imagination are keys to human survival in the darkest times.

title: Sense and Sensibility (U) (AD)
description: An irresistible new take on Jane Austen ’s iconic Sense and Sensibility : a charming, witty and deeply relatable story of love and sisterhood, starring Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles .

title: House of 1000 Corpses
description: Two young couples traveling across the backwoods of Texas searching for urban legends of murder end up as prisoners of a bizarre and sadistic backwater family of serial killers.

title: Verity
description: Struggling writer Lowen Ashleigh is hired as a ghostwriter for renowned author Verity Crawford under mysterious circumstances, but her assignment takes a dark turn after discovering chilling autobiographical notes. Faced with a series of deadly family secrets, Lowen struggles to separate fiction from reality, while also blurring the lines with Verity’s husband, Jeremy.

title: Daisies
description: Our screening on Thursday 8 October will be introduced by art historian and Fashion in Film Festival director Marketa Uhlirova. A…

title: Digger (15) (AD)
description: Academy Award-winning filmmaker Alejandro G Iñárritu ( Birdman ) returns with his original feature starring Tom Cruise as the most powerful man in the world.

title: Knife: The Attempted Murder of Salman Rushdie (15) (AD)
description: Whilst recovering in hospital from a devastating assassination attempt, renowned author Salman Rushdie looks back at his life and career, in this deeply personal documentary.

title: The Day She Returns
description: Hong Sangsoo returns to themes of aging and the creative pursuit, centering on a middle-aged actress whom we come to know through three spellbinding conversations during a press tour for her first film after years of retirement. Preceded by Kleber Mendonça Filho’s South of Tehran.

title: Making Marie Antoinette
description: Tickets Are Only Available via BFI London Film Festival Website from Tuesday 17 September 2026 10:00am: Click Here To Book Eleanor Coppola’s documentary on the making of Marie Antoinette is a rousing love letter to filmic craft and the joys and complexities of leading an artistic life. Drawn from over 80 hours of footage, Coppola’s insightful eye is complimented by her production diaries (voiced by Diane Lane) which form the narrative spine of this profound exploration of creativity, the unique pressures placed on female artists and maternal love. The beauty of her words gives pause, not only to the ambitious artistry onscreen, but the historical character at the centre of this fiction. This screening will be presented with Descriptive Subtitles.

title: Shaun the Sheep: The Beast of Mossy Bottom
description: The new adventure sees the residents of Mossy Bottom Farm looking forward to Halloween - until the clumsy Farmer trashes the Flock's beloved pumpkin patch. When Shaun turns mad scientist to fix the problem, things rapidly spiral out of control, leading to a wild beast roaming the woods.

title: The History of Concrete
description: Fri, Sep 18: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Edy Modica (actress, comedian, filmmaker), after 4:40 show! Fri, Sep 18: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Rachel Kaly (comedian, writer, actor), after 7:15 show! Sun, Sep 20: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Sarah Sherman after 2:10 show! Following the finale of his TV show, filmmaker John Wilson searches for a new creative outlet. After attending a workshop on how to write and sell a Hallmark movie, he attempts to apply the same formula to a documentary about concrete.

title: UNZIPPED
description: “Isaac Mizrahi as he conceived and contorted the way through to his fall 1994 show, [dashing] around a deserted SoHo with pal Sandra Bernhard; [meeting] with Naomi Campbell, Linda Evangelista, and baby Kate Moss for fittings; and [racing] uptown to an audience with Eartha Kitt... Hair-raising deadlines, delirious Bette Davis impressions, and the hostile but exhilarating act of executing a designer’s vision come together in a work that set the bar for all fashion films after.” – Vogue

title: Peking Opera Blues
description: Set in the newly established, vulnerable Republican China of 1913, Peking Opera Blues is a fizzily exuberant, chaotically colorful espionage thriller/screwball romance/slapstick social satire/costume drama pageant that bends genres and genders at will, wending together the stories of three irrepressible female protagonists—played by Sally Yeh, Brigitte Lin, and Cherie Chung, respectively here as a would-be star of the all-male Peking Opera stage, a warlord’s headstrong daughter, and a courtesan who’s copped a case of stolen jewels. Frenetic, filled with whiplash-inducing tonal shifts, frightfully enjoyable and, in the opinion of Quentin Tarantino, “one of the greatest films ever made.” Part of Don't Play with Fire: The Films of Tsui Hark

title: Digger
description: Academy Award-winning filmmaker Alejandro G. Iñárritu returns with his original film Digger, starring Tom Cruise. The most powerful man in the world (Cruise) embarks on a frantic mission to prove he is humanity’s savior before the disaster he’s unleashed destroys everything. This wildly hilarious satire was shot entirely in VistaVision.

title: Free Leonard Peltier
description: Sun, Oct 4: Q &A w/ dirs. Jesse Short Bull and David France after 1:15 show!

title: COMBAT BREATHING: READ MY DESIRE, PART 1
description: READ MY DESIRE, PART 1 Social orders are resisted and overturned not merely because the dominant classes create unlivable conditions for the dominated classes, but also because the dominated classes actively and transgenerationally imagine, prefigure, and desire the realization of alternative social relations that cannot be accommodated by the present order. Such disruptive, exorbitant, and irrepressible desires – often structurally designated as queer – are the focus of this program. “Read My Desire” invokes the work of philosopher Joan Copjec and echoes her formulations that desire precisely emerges from the divisions within the subject which cannot be reduced to social identity or captured by historical regimes. Bringing together historical and contemporary works to explore cinema’s desire-producing capacity as well as the often-elided place of desire, love, eroticism, and sensuality in social movements and associated streams of cultural production, the program traverses multiple geographies and genres, including sci-fi, music video, mythical fable, narrative drama, parodic documentary, and experimental film. The selected works by Marlon Riggs, Valentin Noujaïm, Michelle Parkerson, Peng Zuqiang, Jumana Manna, and Naomi Rincon Gallardo theorize the function of desire in reorienting the horizons of liberation struggles and affirming subjectivities at continual risk of erasure. Marlon Riggs ANTHEM 1991, 9 min, DCP “Every time we kiss we confirm the new world coming.” This is one among many of the defiant phrases voiced in Marlon Riggs’s experimental and agitational music video, which politicizes black male homoeroticism through its African rhythm-informed combination of socially charged images, symbols, dance, text, and spoken poetry. Produced during an era marked by state-backed cultural repression, neoliberalization, and an escalating HIV epidemic, Riggs’s audiovisual manifesto calls on its viewers to “pervert the language” – an act it reflexively performs through its appropriation of a popular and desire-inducing commercial form for the ends of black queer revolution. Valentin Noujaïm OCEANIA 2024, 24 min, 16mm-to-DCP Set in the apartment complex of a quiet French suburb, Valentin Noujaïm’s short film revolves around the entwined personal and socio-political yearnings of its teenage diasporic protagonist, Najib. Upon learning of the passing of an elderly Algerian neighbor from his mother, Najib takes the keys to the deceased man’s apartment only to discover a world of unanswered questions, from letters penned by a former lover to archival videos of pan-African cultural festivals, and other ephemera. An ode to the often-unconscious drives of desire, OCEANIA gestures toward the oblique modes by which past struggles are continually carried on but also transformed by newer generations. Michelle Parkerson ODDS AND ENDS 1993, 28 min, DCP ODDS AND ENDS is a pioneering work of science fiction that capaciously mobilizes the speculative dimensions of the genre to center black lesbian militancy and futurity. The campy intergalactic fable unfolds in the year 2096 – by way of striking allegorical correspondences with the conditions of the fascistic present – in which a cast of black women warriors wage a battle against “ultra-right-wing clones” who seek their annihilation. Michelle Parkerson’s new-age short uncovers psychic and fleshly sites of desire and sexuality within revolutionary movements through its lead character, Lieutenant Loz Wayard, a courageous young amazon, who learns the price of passion when her beloved Sephra takes on the ultimate sacrifice for the struggle. Total running time: ca. 65 min. Introduced by Carlos Motta.

title: A Well for the Thirsty
description: Completed in 1965 but suppressed by Soviet authorities until its eventual release in 1987, Yuri Ilyenko’s debut feature is a cryptic, visionary work that chronicles the interiority of an old peasant who is beset by memories and apparitions as he prepares for death.

title: Sixteen Moments of My Life
description: Ingrid Caven, best known as Rainer Werner Fassbinder’s longtime theater and screen collaborator, looms large in every shot of this mesmerizing concert film by Albert Serra (Afternoons of Solitude, NYFF62), shot in Paris in 2025.

title: Off-Circuit: The Seasons
description: Weaving accounts of rural workers and field notes of a couple of archaeologists, amateur footage and scientific drawings, legends, poems and songs, Maureen Fazendeiro's The Seasons is a journey through the real history and the tales of a region in southern Portugal, Alentejo, and a portrait of the people who have lived there.

title: BASIC INSTINCT
description:
A volatile San Francisco homicide detective is drawn into a murder investigation in which the prime suspect, bestselling novelist Catherine Tramell, appears to have written the crime before it happened. Cool, wealthy and completely unruffled, Catherine turns interrogation into seduction, pulling Nick Curran into a tightening web of sex, obsession and violence.
Paul Verhoeven’s gleaming, ice-cold erotic thriller is Hollywood excess at its most shameless and controlled - a lurid game of authorship and appetite, driven by Sharon Stone’s star-making performance, Jan de Bont’s cobalt cinematography and Jerry Goldsmith’s serpentine score. Few studio films have made danger look this luxurious.

title: Heart of the Beast
description: After a harrowing plane crash, Special Forces officer James Belmont (Brad Pitt) and his combat dog, Odin, find themselves stranded deep in the Alaskan wilderness. Together, they are forced into a brutal fight for survival against the elements. From acclaimed filmmaker David Ayer, Heart of the Beast is an intense adventure thriller that explores the unbreakable bond between a man and his best friend as they face their greatest battle yet.

title: Iron Monkey (少年黃飛鴻之鐵馬騮)
Girls Like Girls
description: Based on writer/director Hayley Kiyoko's hit single and best-selling novel of the same name and featuring all-new music from Kiyoko, GIRLS LIKE GIRLS is a heartfelt coming-of-age story set over the course of one sun-drenched summer, where new-girl-in-town Coley falls in love for the first time while learning to accept herself along the way.

title: FATHERLAND
description: Set in the summer of 1949 amidst the rubble of a defeated Germany in the aftermath of World War II, Fatherland centers on the relationship between the Nobel Prize–winning novelist Thomas Mann (Zischler) and his daughter Erika Mann (Hüller) -actress, writer, and rally driver. Returning home after sixteen years of exile in the US, Thomas Mann must face not only a divided fatherland, but also a deep fissure within his own family, one that is both politically charged and emotionally challenging. As father and daughter embark on a fictionalized road trip across a torn Germany- still visibly scarred by battle and simultaneously in denial of its evils and culpability- they travel from US-dominated Frankfurt in the west to Soviet controlled Weimar in the east. Pawlikowski and Handloegten’s screenplay uses the Mann’s own fractured relationship as the vehicle to examine a country at the crossroads of history, facing an impending moral crisis. Cinematographer Łukasz Żal’s hauntingly stark black-and-white visuals skillfully capture Zischler and Hüller’s masterfully restrained performances.

title: DOWNBEAT / "Dropping Off"
description: An aspiring musician gigging as a rideshare driver struggles to navigate the bizarre request of a mourning passenger.

title: André Leon Talley: Style is Forever
description: André Leon Talley was a trailblazing fashion icon whose influence spanned nearly five decades. This documentary explores his legacy of inclusivity, elegance, and the fearless pursuit of authenticity. Interviews with Anna Wintour, Tom Ford and Diane von Furstenberg, among others, as well as never-before-seen footage, reveal Talley’s personal and professional challenges and remarkable triumphs.

title: DIGGER
description: The most powerful man in the world embarks on a frantic mission to prove he is humanity’s saviour from a disaster he's caused... Tom Cruise stars as oil tycoon DIGGER in this darkly comic satire of power, ego and self-preservation from Academy Award-winning director Alejandro G. Iñárritu. Shot entir...
