title: WALESA: MAN OF HOPE
description: It felt inevitable that Wajda would make a film dramatizing the incredible life of Lech Wałęsa, who rose from being a shipyard electrician and participant in the 1970 strikes at Gdansk to the leader of the Solidarity Movement a decade later, and then the country’s president and a Nobel Peace Prize winner. Walesa’s story, and the rousing film that Wajda made, is the perfect conclusion to the trilogy including MAN OF MARBLE and MAN OF IRON, which seem now to foreshadow Wałęsa’s rise. True to form, Wajda avoids cliches and gives us an unvarnished, complex portrait, brilliantly interweaving dramatic scenes with documentary footage.

title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother 35mm
description: Latif is a devoutly religious hitman who struggles to balance work, faith, and fatherhood. When his wife dies, he embarks on a desperate journey across Houston in search of breast milk for his infant daughter, all while dodging sex traffickers, an evangelical militia, and his own demons.

title: Big Trouble in Little China
description: John Carpenter’s San Francisco-set, supernatural spin on Hollywood’s Chinatown tropes populates the storied neighborhood with mystical beings. Kurt Russell is antihero Jack Burton, an outsider who’s clueless without his Chinese American friend Wang Chi (Dennis Dun). Teaming up to save Wang’s fiancé from the vicious Lords of Death, the pair embarks on a curiously supernatural adventure through the street of this historic Bay Area district. Originally written as a period Western, this cult favorite is an off-kilter, distinctly Carpenterian take on traditional action films, buoyed with the filmmaker’s signature wry comedy. —Adapted from a note written by Arthur Dong.
director: John Carpenter PRODUCED BY: Larry J. Franco

title: VIKA KIRCHENBAUER PGM 1
description: We enter this program with a salacious direct address-cum-invitation in PLEASE RELAX NOW, as Kirchenbauer seduces the viewer from a black box void, stretching the edges of imagination. In LIKE RATS LEAVING A SINKING SHIP, Kirchenbauer layers psychiatric assessments to consider the coherency of a biography, and assess the ways in which individual memory is puppeted by state apparatuses. Both SHE WHOSE BLOOD IS CLOTTING IN MY UNDERWEAR and MOOD MANAGEMENT again push the viewer’s capacity to render a coherent picture of actions, generating a half-constructed image which lends itself only then to a projection. Both works are guided by Kirchenbauer’s music project, COOL FOR YOU. Through essay and material vignettes, UNTITLED SEQUENCE OF GAPS explores light outside of the visible spectrum to consider violence as it attaches to different kinds of visibility and invisibility. To tickle is a form of touch, an intimate act carried out to delight, to excite, or to torment. In THE ISLAND OF PERPETUAL TICKLING (III), Kirchenbauer surrenders to this metaphoric and literal tickle. Noting that it is impossible to tickle oneself, her task requires assistance. PLEASE RELAX NOW (2014, 12 min, DCP) LIKE RATS LEAVING A SINKING SHIP (2012, 24.5 min, DCP) SHE WHOSE BLOOD IS CLOTTING IN MY UNDERWEAR (2016, 3.5 min, DCP) MOOD MANAGEMENT 2017, 2 min, DCPUNTITLED SEQUENCE OF GAPS (2020, 12.5 min, DCP) THE ISLAND OF PERPETUAL TICKLING (III) (2018, 13 min, DCP) Total running time: ca. 75 min. Filmmaker Vika Kirchenbauer in person for both screenings!

title: Pink Palace: THE WASP WOMAN + Shorts
description: Pink Palace in conjunction with Lobotomy Room (devoted to Bad Movies for Bad People), presents The Wasp Woman (tagline: “A beautiful woman by day – a lusting queen wasp by night!”). Directed by wildly influential and prolific high potentate of low-budget cinema Roger Corman. Screening with supportin...

title: MY UNDESIRABLE FRIENDS: PART II – EXILE: Chapters 1-3
description: When Russia shuts down all independent media, a group of young dissident journalists must flee Moscow so they can keep reporting and not go to prison. In her riveting follow-up to last year’s awards-sweeping MY UNDESIRABLE FRIENDS — LAST AIR IN MOSCOW, Julia Loktev follows these courageous, sharply funny women (and a few men) as they fan out across a dozen countries, to Istanbul, Tbilisi, Prague, Vienna, Amsterdam, New York, and beyond. Over the course of four years, they continue to report the truth to Russians from exile, covering their country’s war crimes, even as they face death threats and are declared extremists and terrorists—as they find new meanings of family, friendship, love, and home far from the country to which they may never return. (Viewers can follow EXILE without first seeing LAST AIR IN MOSCOW.)

title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

title: Paprika
description: The fourth and final film by Kon takes place in a not-too-distant future in which therapists, using a new technology called DC Mini, are able to record the dreams of psychiatric patients. All well and good, until a raid on the lab leads to the loss of the DC Mini prototype and a bleed between the troubled subconscious images and reality, leading to a race-against-time to stop bedlam from breaking out in the streets. An admitted inspiration for Christopher Nolan’s Inception (2010), though far more visually extravagant in its vibrant, psychedelia-inflected imaginings, which climax in a thrilling, terrifying dream apocalypse burst from Kon’s fervid imagination. Part of A Cyberpunk Canon

title: UNZIPPED
description: “Isaac Mizrahi as he conceived and contorted the way through to his fall 1994 show, [dashing] around a deserted SoHo with pal Sandra Bernhard; [meeting] with Naomi Campbell, Linda Evangelista, and baby Kate Moss for fittings; and [racing] uptown to an audience with Eartha Kitt... Hair-raising deadlines, delirious Bette Davis impressions, and the hostile but exhilarating act of executing a designer’s vision come together in a work that set the bar for all fashion films after.” – Vogue

title: FILIPIÑANA
description: 17-year-old Isabel navigates the opulent pavilions and lush green landscapes of Dr. Palanca’s luxury golf course as a newly-hired “tee girl.” Meticulously composed, highly stylized, and guided by precisely choreographed movement and deadpan delivery, FILIPIÑANA unfolds through the gradual accumulation of everyday encounters between staff and the wealthy clients of this secluded country club on the outskirts of Manila. When she attempts to return a lost golf club, Isabel uncovers a dark underbelly beneath the club’s pristine surfaces, in this sweltering, pastel-colored fairy tale of class division, institutional patriarchy, and invisible violence.

title: COMBAT BREATHING: READ MY DESIRE, PART 2
description: READ MY DESIRE, PART 2 Social orders are resisted and overturned not merely because the dominant classes create unlivable conditions for the dominated classes, but also because the dominated classes actively and transgenerationally imagine, prefigure, and desire the realization of alternative social relations that cannot be accommodated by the present order. Such disruptive, exorbitant, and irrepressible desires – often structurally designated as queer – are the focus of this program. “Read My Desire” invokes the work of philosopher Joan Copjec and echoes her formulations that desire precisely emerges from the divisions within the subject which cannot be reduced to social identity or captured by historical regimes. Bringing together historical and contemporary works to explore cinema’s desire-producing capacity as well as the often-elided place of desire, love, eroticism, and sensuality in social movements and associated streams of cultural production, the program traverses multiple geographies and genres, including sci-fi, music video, mythical fable, narrative drama, parodic documentary, and experimental film. The selected works by Marlon Riggs, Valentin Noujaïm, Michelle Parkerson, Peng Zuqiang, Jumana Manna, and Naomi Rincon Gallardo theorize the function of desire in reorienting the horizons of liberation struggles and affirming subjectivities at continual risk of erasure. Peng Zuqiang SIGHT LEAK 2022, 12 min, 16mm & Super-8mm-to-DCP Peng Zuqiang’s SIGHT LEAK takes as its departure point Roland Barthes’s visit to China in 1973, using the French theorist’s published travel notes and his renowned writing on love and desire as source texts for exploring the objective and subjective machinations of class and looking. Shot on black-and-white film, SIGHT LEAK brims with minimal haptic images, from framed close-ups of body parts to natural and urban landscapes sensuously sculpted by plays of light and shadow. In the film, Peng’s camera trails behind a local tourist who travels through different spaces and gatherings, seemingly never looking at anyone, yet always silently looking at someone. Counterposing foreign and local projections – whether they be filmic, ideological, or psychic – SIGHT LEAK subtly alludes to the problematics of homoerotic imperial (mis)recognition while holding out the possibility for desire to produce non-normative, subterranean collectivities. Jumana Manna BLESSED BLESSED OBLIVION 2010, 21 min, DCP This early work by Jumana Manna offers a portrait of masculine performativity in East Jerusalem, as manifested in gyms, body shops, and hairdressing parlors. Inspired by Kenneth Anger’s SCORPIO RISING (1963), the video employs visual collage and a dynamic musical soundtrack as ironic commentary. Anger’s depiction of leather-clad bikers serves as a counterpoint to the social scene Manna portrays in BLESSED BLESSED OBLIVION, that of stereotyped male “thug” culture in Palestine. Close-up fragments construct an eroticized and parodic montage of bodies, cars, and locations, intersected by snippets of often-humorous dialogue and a monologue about the art of a car wash. Psychologizing the characters while also being seduced by them, Manna’s conflicted desires mirror those of her male protagonist who drifts from abject rants to declamations of heroic poetry and unashamed self-praise. Naomi Rincon Gallardo PATLACHE ANT NEST 2025, 21 min, DCP PATLACHE ANT NEST, the latest work by Naomi Rincon Gallardo, is a fable inspired by the image and description of an ambiguous figure called Patlache who appears in the Florentine Codex, a sixteenth-century colonial ethnographic research document about Mesoamerica created by a Spanish missionary priest. The Patlache was described in racially coded and gender disruptive terms – as a filthy woman with a penis and body hair who practices lesbian love. Merging camp DIY aesthetics and surreal, indigenous forms of storytelling, Gallardo mythically rearticulates the archival capture of this figure in PATLACHE ANT NEST with a cast of costumed characters representing toothed vaginas, leafcutter ants, and a cactus. Over the course of the film, the Patlache character transforms into a dome-like architectural structure bearing an entrance that leads to an underground, patriarchy-free dwelling of lesbian sociality and flourishing. Total running time: ca. 60 min. Introduced by Omar Alsayyed.

title: The History of Concrete
description: A filmmaker applies lessons from a Hallmark movie writing workshop to pitch a documentary about concrete.

title: The Dreamed Adventure
description: Winner of the Cannes Jury Prize, Valeska Grisebach’s quietly thrilling new film about a middle-aged archaeologist searching for a disappeared former flame at the fragile boundaries of Eastern and Western Europe gradually shifts into a wide-ranging crime saga. Bulgaria’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: The Devil's Rejects
description: The murderous, backwoods Firefly family take to the road to escape the vengeful Sheriff Wydell, who is not afraid of being as ruthless as his target.

title: Valie Export Shorts Program
description: A provocative program of short films by Export whose work, focused in her words, on “the body and moreover the female body,” can be viewed as both parallel to and a response against that of the male-dominated Viennese Actionists. Featuring the confrontational and mock-erotic Self-Portrait with Head; Touch Cinema, a document of Export’s taboo-busting performance piece; Man & Woman & Animal, an “assertion and affirmation of female sexuality and its independence from male values and pleasures” [Joanna Kierman]; Syntagma, a frenzied study of the fragmented female form; and Lust, per the director “a continuation of my previous work with the body as a vehicle for social codes. ” Self-Portrait with Head (Valie Export, 1966/1967, 4 mins) Touch Cinema (Valie Export, 1968, 2 mins) Man & Woman & Animal (Valie Export, 1970/1973, 8 mins) ....Remote.....Remote..... (Valie Export, 1973, 10 mins) Syntagma (Valie Export, 1984, 20 mins) Lust (Valie Export, 1986, 12 mins) Part of Valie Export: Tap Touch Burn

title: Bitter Christmas
description: The incomparable Pedro Almodóvar explores the artist’s tenuous relationship with fiction and reality in this film about an actress writing a script inspired by the lives of those around her—which is itself the invention of an Almodóvar-like filmmaker.

title: Bucking Fastard
description: The oddball brilliance of Werner Herzog—returning to NYFF for the first time since 1982’s Fitzcarraldo (NYFF20)—is in full effect in this tale of two sisters (Kate and Rooney Mara, in total sync) who live by their own social and emotional standards and rules.

title: Goodbye South, Goodbye
description: One of Hou Hsiao-hsien’s unassailable 1990s masterpieces and a staggering, mesmerizing generational portrait, Goodbye South, Goodbye follows the plots and schemes of a small group of young men and women in the age of get-rich-quick late-capitalism.

title: Cotton Queen
description: In a cotton-farming village in Sudan, teenage Nafisa is raised on heroic tales of battling British colonisers told by her grandmother, the village matriarch Al-Sit. But when a young businessman arrives from abroad with a new development plan and genetically engineered cotton, Nafisa becomes the centre of a power play to determine the future of the village. Awakening to her own strength, Nafisa sets out to save the cotton fields – and herself. Neither she nor her community will ever be the same again.

title: Call Your Bluff [Shorts Programme]
description: Tickets Are Only Available via BFI London Film Festival Website from Tuesday 17 September 2026 10:00am: Click Here To Book Whether it’s cutting your own hair, winning the lottery, looking for love or livening up a dull day at work, these uk shorts will cover all your comedy needs. FILMS IN THE PROGRAMME: A Twist of Hate Director- Maddy Shenai UK - 2026 - 9min Newlyweds encounter an unusual lawyer who probes their motivations for love. Date Night Director- Tanya Reynolds UK - 2026 - 16min Danielle and Harry's latest attempt at kinky roleplay shines a discomforting light on what they really want from life. Laundreams Director - Amber Gadd, Evie Ward-Drummond USA - 2026 - 15min In an empty laundrette manned by 20-year-olds Minnie and Leah, nothing ever happens and nothing ever changes. Micro Bangs Director - Iris Breward UK - 2026 - 5min A woman starts to spiral as she considers a drastic haircut. Sweet Bitter Sweet Director - Nicolee Tsin UK - 2025 - 9min After moving to London, a young Chinese woman searches for love while working at a bakery. The Devil Is In Me Director - Tia Salisbury UK - 2026 - 11min In late 18th-century England, a nightmarish teenager and a rookie reverend lock horns over Sunday school attendance. A Kind of Purity Director - Theo Shivdasani UK - 2026 - 15min At an art gallery, a disillusioned assistant's pretence of normality is pushed to breaking point when a sudden act takes place. How To Hide It Director - Ramla Ali, Richard A. Moore UK - 2025 - 13min After winning the lottery, a woman faces tension between dreams of a better life and her deeply held beliefs.

description: Left destitute by ruthless family members, two sisters navigate scandal, heartbreak, and strict social etiquette while searching for their perfect romantic matches.

title: Hanabi
description: In this diaristic journey through the combustible heart of contemporary Japan, filmmaker Ana Vaz uses Yoko Hasuke’s essay “Journal of a Radioactive Brain” as the inspiration and anchor for a freeform inquiry into living amidst natural and manmade disasters. Special Mention winner at the 2026 Locarno Film Festival.

title: Digger (15) (AD)
description: Academy Award-winning filmmaker Alejandro G Iñárritu ( Birdman ) returns with his original feature starring Tom Cruise as the most powerful man in the world.

title: Tony (15) (AD)
description: A 19-year-old Anthony Bourdain travels to Provincetown and stumbles into the chaotic world of a restaurant kitchen, carving out a slice of a summer that will shape the course of his life.

title: Digger
description: The most powerful man in the world embarks on a frantic mission to prove he is humanity's saviour before the disaster he’s unleashed destroys everything.

title: Verity
description: Struggling writer Lowen Ashleigh is hired as a ghostwriter for renowned author Verity Crawford under mysterious circumstances, but her assignment takes a dark turn after discovering chilling autobiographical notes. Faced with a series of deadly family secrets, Lowen struggles to separate fiction from reality, while also blurring the lines with Verity’s husband, Jeremy.

title: Begotten
description: BEGOTTEN has no characters in the ordinary sense. Its final credits name three principal figures: God Killing Himself. Mother Earth. Son of Earth – Flesh on Bone. The entire film is what those names do to each other and to the earth. God Killing Himself tears open his body and dies. Mother Earth rises from what remains and takes his seed into herself. She gives birth to Son of Earth Flesh on Bone. He is cast into a barren world, seized by the Nomads, tortured, killed, and briefly returned to life by his mother.The Nomads destroy her too. The Robed Figures gather what remains of mother and son, grind their bodies down, and return them to the soil. The ground flowers.

title: Girls Like Girls
description: Based on writer/director Hayley Kiyoko's hit single and best-selling novel of the same name and featuring all-new music from Kiyoko, GIRLS LIKE GIRLS is a heartfelt coming-of-age story set over the course of one sun-drenched summer, where new-girl-in-town Coley falls in love for the first time while learning to accept herself along the way.

title: Red Rocks
description: In Bruno Dumont’s drama of danger, purity, and freedom, a group of children between the ages of 5 and 7 enact a kind of pre-preadolescent Romeo and Juliet, complete with rival gangs and puppy love, in a coastal French Riviera town.

title: Sense And Sensibility
description: An irresistible new take on Jane Austen’s iconic Sense and Sensibility: a charming, witty, and deeply relatable story of love and sisterhood starring Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles. Sisters Elinor and Marianne Dashwood must leave their Sussex estate following the sudden loss of their wealthy father and are forced to move in with a distant relative. The two sisters attempt to find security and happiness whilst navigating their vastly different approaches to love.

title: Heart of the Beast
description: After a harrowing plane crash, Special Forces officer James Belmont (Brad Pitt) and his combat dog, Odin, find themselves stranded deep in the Alaskan wilderness. Together, they are forced into a brutal fight for survival against the elements. From acclaimed filmmaker David Ayer, Heart of the Beast is an intense adventure thriller that explores the unbreakable bond between a man and his best friend as they face their greatest battle yet.

title: Resident Evil
description: In this sci-fi horror action reboot, a hapless medical courier fights for his life amid an outbreak of a deadly mutagenic virus in an isolated mountain town.

title: BAGWORM / "Shadow Daddy"
description: When a mysterious dream sparks an unexpected conversation, a boyfriend and girlfriend spiral into revealing the insecurities lurking beneath their relationship.

title: V/H/S/Mixtape
description: Thu, Oct 8: Extended intro by filmmaker Ernest Dickerson at the9:30 show! Featuring all-new segments from legendary filmmaker Ernest Dickerson, hip-hop icon RZA, visionary director David Moreau, and acclaimed filmmaker Renee Zhan, whose segment includes original puppets by Jim Henson’s Creature Shop. V/H/S/MIXTAPE also features original music video interludes directed by acclaimed filmmaker and musician Flying Lotus, alongside a brand-new music video from debut filmmaker Tobias Forge, creating a genre-bending mixtape experience unlike anything the franchise has attempted before. Adding to the chaos, legendary shock-metal pioneers GWAR also make a featured appearance, further cementing the film’s celebration of horror, music, and cult cinema.
director: Ernest Dickerson, Flying Lotus, Tobias Forge, David Moreau, RZA, Renee Zhan

title: FINAL FLESH
description:
As a nuclear catastrophe approaches, the suburban Pollard family confronts extinction through four increasingly deranged episodes involving bodily transformation, domestic ritual and the possibility of rebirth. Their fractured story unfolds like a transmission from another dimension, performed with total sincerity by actors who appear to inhabit a world whose logic is only barely connected to our own.
FINAL FLESH began as a collection of absurd scripts written by Vernon Chatman, co-creator of Wonder Showzen, then anonymously commissioned from four separate custom-fetish video companies whose performers believed every word was genuine. Edited together into a single feature, the result is an uncanny collision of conceptual comedy, outsider performance and apocalyptic science fiction. Hilarious, unsettling and almost impossible to categorise, it feels less like a conventional film than an artefact recovered from a parallel civilisation.

title: Sympathy for Mr. Vengeance
description: Fired from his factory job, Ryu (Shin Ha-kyun), a gentle deaf-mute man desperately trying to scrape together funds for his sister’s kidney transplant, falls in with a plan, hatched by his anarchist activist girlfriend (Bae Doona), to kidnap the daughter of the wealthy industrialist who fired him and ransom her for the necessary cash—and in so doing sets off on a path that terminates in an explosion of shockingly visceral violence. A brutal, claustrophobic film of escalating desperation, illustrating with grim logic how an ordinary man can be pushed into acts of extraordinary retaliation, with Bae’s performance bringing some welcome levity to the affair, even as her character acts as the catalyst for catastrophe to come. Introduction by LEENALCHI and a post-screening Q&A with composer Jang Young Gyu moderated by Goran Topalovic, October 3rd Part of Composed by Jang Young Gyu

title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

title: Ghost in the Shell: 30th Anniversary Remaster
description: “My codename is Project 2501, and I am a life form that was born in a sea of information.” In the year 2029, the world looks like a hybridization of Hong Kong, Tokyo, and New York, yielding to entropy and technocracy. Cyborg Major Kusanagi, a perfect specimen of human-brained computer engineering is on the case to track and destroy an omnipotent entity known as The Puppet Master—a hacker? a virus?—who threatens world order. Her physical and existential journey deftly detailed by Oshii’s animation, combining traditional hand-drawn cells and computer-generated graphics, creating a haunting, awe-inspiring magnum opus. Part of A Cyberpunk Canon

title: The History of Concrete
description: A filmmaker applies lessons from a Hallmark movie writing workshop to pitch a documentary about concrete.

title: Throne of Blood             / Ugetsu
description: A vivid, visceral Macbeth adaptation, Throne of Blood , directed by Akira Kurosawa, sets Shakespeare’s definitive tale of ambition and duplicity in a ghostly, fog-enshrouded landscape in feudal Japan. As a hardened warrior who rises savagely to power, Toshiro Mifune gives a remarkable, animalistic performance, as does Isuzu Yamada as his ruthless wife. Throne of Blood fuses classical Western tragedy with formal elements taken from Noh theater to create an unforgettable cinematic experience. (Janus Films)

title: The Disciple
description: Dutch Moroccan fanboy Tarik Azzougarh spends over a decade working to meet and befriend his heroes, the genre-defining hip-hop group Wu-Tang Clan and its iconic spiritual leader, RZA. After joining their movement, he becomes the architect of one of their most talked-about and controversial albums, “Once Upon a Time in Shaolin,” whose radical concept continues to reverberate throughout the music industry. What unfolds is a twisting coming-of-age tale of boyhood dreams, relentless determination and the downfall of flying too close to the sun.

title: THE PRINCESS BRIDE
description: “As... you... wish...” Farmboy Westley turned the Dread Pirate Roberts must face the Cliffs of Insanity, Rodents of Unusual Size, and torture in the Pit of Despair in order to rescue his true love Buttercup, finding help along the way from the vengeance-seeking Inigo Montoya and the giant Fezzik. This beloved adaptation of William Goldman’s novel features an all-star ensemble cast, including Mandy Patinkin, Chris Sarandon, Christopher Guest, Wallace Shawn, Billy Crystal, Carol Kane, and Peter Falk.

title: Fjord
description: Tue, Oct 6: Sneak preview + Q&A with director Cristian Mungiu and co-star Sebastian Stan after the 6:15 show! Tues, Oct 6: Extended intro with director Cristian Mungiu and co-star Sebastian Stan at the 8:15 show! From two-time Palme d’Or winner Cristian Mungiu, a Norwegian woman and her devout Romanian husband relocate with their five children to a remote, close-knit, coastal town. Their teenage children form a fast bond with a neighboring family as unease begins to simmer around their rigid beliefs. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice.

title: Other Mommy
description: Bela, an 8-year-old girl living in a home with marital problems, confronts a sinister entity that comes out of her closet. The presence, whom she calls "Other Mommy," becomes increasingly threatening to her and her family.

title: The Exorcist (Extended Cut)
description: One of the most profitable horror movies ever made, this tale of an exorcism is based loosely on actual events. When young Regan (Linda Blair) starts acting odd -- levitating, speaking in tongues -- her worried mother (Ellen Burstyn) seeks medical help, only to hit a dead end. A local priest (Jason Miller), however, thinks the girl may be seized by the devil. The priest makes a request to perform an exorcism, and the church sends in an expert (Max von Sydow) to help with the difficult job.

title: Remake
description: In Remake , filmmaker Ross McElwee turns his lens on the passage of time and the uneasy space between documenting life and understanding it. The film traces McElwee’s relationship with his son Adrian, and the fragile bond the camera created between them while Adrian was alive, and now that he’s gone. Drawing from decades of footage, some shot by Ross, some by Adrian, the film becomes a layered excavation of memory and image making. Threaded through is the ghost of another project: a stalled effort by Hollywood to fictionalize McElwee’s 1986 classic, Sherman’s March . What emerges is a work shaped by absence and propelled forward by a father’s love for his son.

title: MY UNDESIRABLE FRIENDS: PART II – EXILE: Chapters 1-3
description: When Russia shuts down all independent media, a group of young dissident journalists must flee Moscow so they can keep reporting and not go to prison. In her riveting follow-up to last year’s awards-sweeping MY UNDESIRABLE FRIENDS — LAST AIR IN MOSCOW, Julia Loktev follows these courageous, sharply funny women (and a few men) as they fan out across a dozen countries, to Istanbul, Tbilisi, Prague, Vienna, Amsterdam, New York, and beyond. Over the course of four years, they continue to report the truth to Russians from exile, covering their country’s war crimes, even as they face death threats and are declared extremists and terrorists—as they find new meanings of family, friendship, love, and home far from the country to which they may never return. (Viewers can follow EXILE without first seeing LAST AIR IN MOSCOW.)

title: Don't Look Now
description: After the death of their child, a couple moves to Venice, where the husband has an assignment of restoring a church. There, they meet a sister who claims their kid is trying to warn them of a danger.

title: All of a Sudden
description: Virginie Efira and Tao Okamoto shared the Best Actress prize at Cannes for Academy Award–winning director Ryûsuke Hamaguchi’s (Drive My Car, NYFF59) radiant new film about a nursing home director promoting a radical new care program. Japan’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: A Well for the Thirsty
description: Completed in 1965 but suppressed by Soviet authorities until its eventual release in 1987, Yuri Ilyenko’s debut feature is a cryptic, visionary work that chronicles the interiority of an old peasant who is beset by memories and apparitions as he prepares for death.

title: UNZIPPED
description: “Isaac Mizrahi as he conceived and contorted the way through to his fall 1994 show, [dashing] around a deserted SoHo with pal Sandra Bernhard; [meeting] with Naomi Campbell, Linda Evangelista, and baby Kate Moss for fittings; and [racing] uptown to an audience with Eartha Kitt... Hair-raising deadlines, delirious Bette Davis impressions, and the hostile but exhilarating act of executing a designer’s vision come together in a work that set the bar for all fashion films after.” – Vogue

title: THE LEOPARD MAN
description: When a supposedly tame black leopard escapes from a New Mexico nightclub, young girls start to die horribly. While the police desperately search for the beast, nightclub singer Kiki Walkerand her manager Jerry Manning start to suspect that someone or something far worse is responsible for the killings. Something is stalking the small town, something with an overwhelming compulsion to kill and kill again…

title: Sixteen Moments of My Life
description: Ingrid Caven, best known as Rainer Werner Fassbinder’s longtime theater and screen collaborator, looms large in every shot of this mesmerizing concert film by Albert Serra (Afternoons of Solitude, NYFF62), shot in Paris in 2025.

title: Late Fame
description: Willem Defoe plays Ed Saxberger, a forgotten New York poet, who works in the post office. After an eager and flattering young admirer appears on his doorstep, Saxberger is beckoned into a coterie of twentysomething admirers who anoint him as a rediscovered genius. Intoxicated by the attention — and by the alluring presence of Gloria, the group’s “tragic heroine” — Saxberger gradually reckons with the authenticity of his newfound poetic circle. Kent Jones's thoughtful, witty film is a wistful yet unromantic look at a lost idea of downtown New York.

title: MAN OF MARBLE
description: An aggressive documentary filmmaker fights present-day 1970s government censorship as she seeks the truth about bricklayer Matuesz Birkut, a state-manufactured proletariat hero during the Soviet-controlled 1950s. Fourteen years in the making, MAN OF MARBLE is a film-within-a-film that blends documentary, pseudo-documentary, and fictional techniques that inevitably draw comparison to CITIZEN KANE. Like Orson Welles’ masterpiece, MAN OF MARBLE is a reflection on national history and mythology and also on the very nature of filmmaking. It also turned out to prophesize the worker strikes of 1980 and the rise of the Solidarity movement.

title: The Lair of the White Worm
description: When an archaeologist uncovers a strange skull in a foreign land, the residents of a nearby town begin to disappear, leading to further inexplicable occurrences.

title: Digger
description: Academy Award-winning filmmaker Alejandro G. Iñárritu returns with his original film Digger, starring Tom Cruise. The most powerful man in the world (Cruise) embarks on a frantic mission to prove he is humanity’s savior before the disaster he’s unleashed destroys everything. This wildly hilarious satire was shot entirely in VistaVision.

title: Little Shop Of Horrors (1986)
description: Frank Oz’s film update of the Roger Corman classic via the off-Broadway musical hit is a delightfully deranged multi-genre mashup of biting humor and fun-filled horror, featuring killer songs from composer Alan Menken and writer Howard Ashman. When nerdy florist Seymour (Rick Moranis) finds unlikely life advice from a mysterious plant, his world is turned upside down because this leafy oversized carnivore has strange cravings and is very, very hungry. A stellar Ellen Greene reprises her role from the theatrical production as the sweet-natured Audrey, the object of Seymour’s affections, while the Four Tops’ Levi Stubbs energetically voices Audrey II, the flytrap-like fiend for flesh cleverly controlled by a talented team of puppeteers. With Steve Martin as a sadistic dentist and a fantastic feast of comedy star cameos.

title: The Terminator
description: Too many sequels and an incalculable cultural impact later, it’s sometimes forgotten what a hot and nasty little movie Cameron’s original Terminator was, dropping peak-physique Schwarzenegger into a sleazy Los Angeles of leather bars, punk rockers, and skid rows, where he quickly proceeds to killing cops by the score and tracking down mother-to-be of humankind’s savior Linda Hamilton. Working for the very last time with budget constraints, Cameron—and FX gurus Stan Winston and Gene Warren Jr.—deliver the goods and how, in a grimy lil’ chef d’oeuvre that gave us Cyberdine, Skynet, and a whole lexicon for discussing extinction-level singularity events. Part of A Cyberpunk Canon

title: The Taking of Pelham One Two Three
description: Lower East Side native Walter Matthau wears perhaps the broadest tie in film history as a grousing Transit Authority lieutenant who gets an unlikely shot at heroism when a group of criminals take a downtown 6 train hostage and demand a million dollars from the flat-broke city. Engineered with perfect pace and verve by the underrated Sargent, with growly, jowly Matthau at his hangdog best. “Featuring one of the grittiest New Yorkers ever seen on film: the ruddy-cheeked wino who, despite the commotion on her hijacked 6 train, sleeps through the entire ordeal.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue Introduction by Genevieve Yue and Erika Balsom, with a book signing following the screening, on Saturday, October 3rd Part of Trains: Local Routes

title: Barrio Triste
description: In an impoverished neighborhood of 1980s Medellín, a group of disaffected teens steal a TV reporter’s camera to document their lives. Piercing the derelict landscape’s oppressive atmosphere with disarming reflections on dreams and death, their understanding of reality and hope begins to erode as reports of mysterious lights falling from the sky coincide with temporal and spatial distortions. In his striking feature debut, long-time Bad Bunny collaborator Stillz captures an intimate, formally daring portrait of Colombia's forgotten youth. Barrio Triste is heightened by a restless, intense debut score from Arca, whose fluid soundscapes anchor the film's vision. Navigating the thin line between desperation and the supernatural, Stillz delivers a beautiful, unclassifiable piece of contemporary cinema.

title: There's No Business Like Show Business
description: The Donahue clan, led by husband and wife Molly and Terry (Ethel Merman and Dan Dailey), navigate the ups and downs of show biz, from their beginnings in Vaudeville to the Great Depression, in this musical comedy with songs by Irving Berlin. The family’s close bond is further tested with the arrival of the talented and driven Vicky Parker (Marilyn Monroe). Costume designer Travilla played an integral role in shaping Marilyn Monroe’s public image on- and off-screen. Together they famously produced looks that evaded censorship while still courting controversy. His designs for her showgirl characters are of particular note.
director: Walter Lang PRODUCED BY: Sol C. Siegel

title: The Uprising
description: Andrew Garfield stars as the legendary leader of a ferocious rebellion against the tyranny of King Richard II. As war burns across England, he forms an army of the people to face the King’s might in a fight for justice and survival.

Three sisters experience love and heartbreak after they're forced to leave their family estate with their widowed mother and move to a humble cottage...

title: Manhunter (4K Restoration)
description: In celebration of the 40th anniversary of Michael Mann’s Manhunter , Mann’s final cut of the film returns in a newly restored 4K version. FBI criminal profiler Will Graham is called out of early retirement to assist on a deadly case involving a murderer known as the “Tooth Fairy.” After enlisting the help of imprisoned serial killer Dr. Hannibal Lecktor, Graham and the FBI are soon entangled in a menacing cat-and-mouse game.

title: The Shining [UK Version]
description: Jack Torrance (Jack Nicholson) becomes winter caretaker at the isolated Overlook Hotel in Colorado, hoping to cure his writer's block. He settles in along with his wife, Wendy (Shelley Duvall), and his son, Danny (Danny Lloyd), who is plagued by psychic premonitions. As Jack's writing goes nowhere and Danny's visions become more disturbing, Jack discovers the hotel's dark secrets and begins to unravel into a homicidal maniac hell-bent on terrorizing his family.

title: Suicide Note
description: Shot largely in New York between 1976 and 1984, this newly restored, seldom-screened film from critic and artist Fred Camper is a fragmentary, diaristic work, capturing a cluttered and melancholic world on silent Super 8 Ektachrome reversal film.

title: The Craft
description: After transferring to a Los Angeles high school, Sarah (Robin Tunney) finds that her telekinetic gift appeals to a group of three wannabe witches, who happen to be seeking a fourth member for their rituals. Bonnie (Neve Campbell), Rochelle (Rachel True) and Nancy (Fairuza Balk), like Sarah herself, all have troubled backgrounds, which combined with their nascent powers lead to dangerous consequences. When a minor spell causes a fellow student to lose her hair, the girls grow power-mad.

title: The Social Reckoning
description: Explores Facebook's internal practices, spread of false information, impact on teen mental health, and connection to January 6 Capitol events.

title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

title: The Social Reckoning (15) (AD)
description: In this companion piece to The Social Network , screenwriter Aaron Sorkin returns to the Metaverse with a tale of the whistleblower who started the social media reckoning we're seeing play out today.

title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother 35mm
description: Latif is a devoutly religious hitman who struggles to balance work, faith, and fatherhood. When his wife dies, he embarks on a desperate journey across Houston in search of breast milk for his infant daughter, all while dodging sex traffickers, an evangelical militia, and his own demons.

title: The Man I Love
description: Ira Sachs’s finely detailed period drama about an emotionally complicated cabaret star and performance artist (Oscar winner Rami Malek) living with AIDS in 1980s New York is a reminder that art and imagination are keys to human survival in the darkest times.

title: WISE BLOOD
description:
Returning from military service to a transformed American South, Hazel Motes arrives in a small Georgia city determined to reject the religious convictions that shaped his childhood. Proclaiming himself the founder of the "Church Without Christ", he embarks on a furious campaign against belief, attracting a succession of eccentric followers, opportunists, and would-be prophets. As Hazel's crusade against faith grows increasingly obsessive, his attempts to escape spiritual certainty lead him toward acts of self-destruction that mirror the fervour he claims to oppose.
Adapted from Flannery O'Connor's 1952 novel, Wise Blood occupies a distinctive place within John Huston's later work, combining Southern Gothic, black comedy, and religious allegory. Filmed in Georgia near O'Connor's home territory and closely preserving the novel's dialogue and structure, the film translates her world of preachers, charlatans, and spiritual seekers into a landscape where belief and disbelief become equally consuming forces. Anchored by Brad Dourif's remarkable performance, Wise Blood explores evangelical culture, American individualism, and the uneasy relationship between modernity and faith, resulting in one of the most unusual literary adaptations of the 1970s.

title: FILIPIÑANA
description: 17-year-old Isabel navigates the opulent pavilions and lush green landscapes of Dr. Palanca’s luxury golf course as a newly-hired “tee girl.” Meticulously composed, highly stylized, and guided by precisely choreographed movement and deadpan delivery, FILIPIÑANA unfolds through the gradual accumulation of everyday encounters between staff and the wealthy clients of this secluded country club on the outskirts of Manila. When she attempts to return a lost golf club, Isabel uncovers a dark underbelly beneath the club’s pristine surfaces, in this sweltering, pastel-colored fairy tale of class division, institutional patriarchy, and invisible violence.

title: Digger (15) (AD)
description: Academy Award-winning filmmaker Alejandro G Iñárritu ( Birdman ) returns with his original feature starring Tom Cruise as the most powerful man in the world.

title: The History of Concrete
description: Fri, Sep 18: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Edy Modica (actress, comedian, filmmaker), after 4:40 show! Fri, Sep 18: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Rachel Kaly (comedian, writer, actor), after 7:15 show! Sun, Sep 20: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Sarah Sherman after 2:10 show! Following the finale of his TV show, filmmaker John Wilson searches for a new creative outlet. After attending a workshop on how to write and sell a Hallmark movie, he attempts to apply the same formula to a documentary about concrete.

title: Girls Like Girls
description: Based on writer/director Hayley Kiyoko's hit single and best-selling novel of the same name and featuring all-new music from Kiyoko, GIRLS LIKE GIRLS is a heartfelt coming-of-age story set over the course of one sun-drenched summer, where new-girl-in-town Coley falls in love for the first time while learning to accept herself along the way.

title: Tommy
description: After a series of traumatic childhood events, a psychosomatically deaf, dumb and blind boy becomes a master pinball player and the object of a religious cult.

title: The History of Concrete
description: A filmmaker applies lessons from a Hallmark movie writing workshop to pitch a documentary about concrete.

title: 9 to 5
description: Vidiots remembers its forever Goddess Dolly Parton with a special screening of the iconic 9 to 5 .

title: TAKE ME HOME
description: The American Cinematheque is thrilled to announce a limited engagement of TAKE ME HOME, Liz Sargent’s feature length version of the 2024 PROOF Film Festival Grand Jury Prize winner. From an award-winning short film to a world premiere at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival with the feature is an inspirational journey, and we wish the team the best as they bring this moving film around the world.

title: MY UNDESIRABLE FRIENDS: PART II – EXILE: Chapters 4-5
description: When Russia shuts down all independent media, a group of young dissident journalists must flee Moscow so they can keep reporting and not go to prison. In her riveting follow-up to last year’s awards-sweeping MY UNDESIRABLE FRIENDS — LAST AIR IN MOSCOW, Julia Loktev follows these courageous, sharply funny women (and a few men) as they fan out across a dozen countries, to Istanbul, Tbilisi, Prague, Vienna, Amsterdam, New York, and beyond. Over the course of four years, they continue to report the truth to Russians from exile, covering their country’s war crimes, even as they face death threats and are declared extremists and terrorists—as they find new meanings of family, friendship, love, and home far from the country to which they may never return. (Viewers can follow EXILE without first seeing LAST AIR IN MOSCOW.)

title: The Lost Children of Tuam
description: In rural Ireland, amateur historian Catherine Corless begins researching a former institution for unmarried mothers and their children, uncovering a shocking hidden history of loss. Based on the true story, and featuring a powerful performance from Monica Dolan, THE LOST CHILDREN OF TUAM is a deeply moving portrait of one woman’s fight for justice.

title: Once Upon a Time in China II(黃飛鴻之二：男兒當自強)
description: Once Upon a Time in China II (黃飛鴻之二：男兒當自強). 1992. Hong Kong. Directed by Tsui Hark. Screenplay by Tsui, Chan Tin-suen, Cheung Tan. Martial arts direction by Yuen Woo-ping. With Jet Li, Donnie Yen. DCP courtesy Janus Films. In Cantonese; English subtitles. 112 min. Tsui Hark’s Once Upon a Time in China II shifts focus from foreign imperialism to China’s internal political fractures. Jet Li returns as legendary folk hero Wong Fei-hung, who becomes entangled with a fanatical sect and a ruthless imperial officer (Donnie Yen). Yuen Woo-ping grounds his award-winning choreography in traditional Southern kung fu while infusing it with Peking Opera theatricality and gravity-defying fantasy. The result is a series of astonishing encounters, including Wong’s signature “shadowless kick” and the climactic duel between Li and Yen—a ferocious clash of wet-cloth whip and bamboo staff that ranks among the most celebrated fight scenes in martial arts cinema.

title: Shaun the Sheep: The Beast of Mossy Bottom
description: The new adventure sees the residents of Mossy Bottom Farm looking forward to Halloween - until the clumsy Farmer trashes the Flock's beloved pumpkin patch. When Shaun turns mad scientist to fix the problem, things rapidly spiral out of control, leading to a wild beast roaming the woods.

title: THE PROMISED LAND
description: The rise of the industrial era and the capitalist boom it engendered are at the core of Wajda’s epic adaptation of the novel by 1924 Nobel Prize winner W. S. Reymont. The film charts the rise and fall of three ambitious tycoons, Karol, a Polish nobleman, Maks, a German hoping to improve on the fate of his father who ran a failing old-time mill, and Moryc, who appears to be disdained except for his valuable connections. Exposing the ways that workers are exploited for the sake of financial growth, the film builds to a powerful climax that connects it to economic conflicts that were simmering in Poland at the time it was made.

title: The Age of Innocence
description: One breathtaking composition follows another in Scorsese’s adaptation of Edith Wharton’s Pulitzer Prize–winning masterpiece about social mores (and taboos) amongst New York’s viperous moneyed classes in late 19th-century New York, brought to life by an all-star lineup of craftspeople including cinematographer Michael Ballhaus, editor Thelma Schoonmaker, production designer Dante Ferretti, and composer Elmer Bernstein. In front of the camera there are Daniel Day-Lewis and Michelle Pfeiffer suffering beautifully as wealthy lawyer Newland Archer and Countess Ellen Olenska, the divorced pariah whom he yearns for, and Winona Ryder as Archer’s fiancée and, eventually, wife—outwardly a winsome innocent, but a cunning, cutthroat strategist where affairs of the heart are concerned. It was, Ryder stated during a recent appearance on (of all things) Hot Ones, “The role of a lifetime.” Part of Winona Ryder Analogue Youth

title: Cotton Queen
description: In a cotton-farming village in Sudan, teenage Nafisa is raised on heroic tales of battling British colonisers told by her grandmother, the village matriarch Al-Sit. But when a young businessman arrives from abroad with a new development plan and genetically engineered cotton, Nafisa becomes the centre of a power play to determine the future of the village. Awakening to her own strength, Nafisa sets out to save the cotton fields – and herself. Neither she nor her community will ever be the same again.

title: Cameron Winter at Carnegie
description: Paul Thomas Anderson turns a revelatory, stripped-down set by Brooklyn’s own Cameron Winter into a smashing cinematic concert, shot on 16mm and 35mm with a perfect mix of intimate images of Winter and of the cavernous space.

title: Extra Geography
description: Set in an English boarding school, Extra Geography follows two teenage girls as they grapple with all the challenges of girlhood: friendship, boys, studies, growing up and their summer project, "to fall in love".

title: Socrates
description: Beginning in the mid-’60s and ending with his death in 1977, Rossellini committed himself to producing a series of films, telefilms, and serial works that would together constitute a narrative of human progress and the history of ideas from aleolithic to present times. Socrates, initiating a tetralogy of works on epoch-defining thinkers, sets its scene in an Athens humbled by Sparta and increasingly irritated by the prickly, prodding philosopher in their midst, finally determined to silence him. Using out-of-vogue in-camera effects to transform an ancient Spanish village into Athens, probing scenes with his customized, remote-controlled Pancinor zoom, and employing a dirge-like electronic score by Mario Nascimbene, Rossellini gives us a singular vision of antiquity, one that’s downright avant-garde. Part of Classical Cinema

title: Comédie Française
description: The Comédie-Française is one of France’s most revered arts institutions, and the oldest still-performing theatre company in the world. There is one golden rule: the play is NEVER cancelled.  Unfortunately for theatre producer Nina (Pauline Clément), everything is unravelling just three hours before the premiere of her first production – an ambitious retelling of Shakespeare’s Macbeth. Her lead actor is stuck on a train, tensions are exploding, passions flaring, equipment breaking down and egos are clashing. With panic setting in and the clock ticking Nina must hold things together at all costs. Will the show go on? France’s hit summer comedy and the runaway winner of four awards at the Alpe d’Huez comedy Film Festival, Comédie Française is a delicious behind-the-scenes farce which is unafraid to poke fun at the highbrow reputation of French theatre. Featuring a cast of real-life members of the Comédie-Française company, this is a gleeful, knowing parody and a sheer delight.

title: Phenomena
description: A young girl, with an amazing ability to communicate with insects, is transferred to an exclusive Swiss boarding school, where her unusual capability might help solve a string of murders.

title: The Uprising
description: Andrew Garfield stars as the legendary leader of a ferocious rebellion against the tyranny of King Richard II. As war burns across England, he forms an army of the people to face the King’s might in a fight for justice and survival.

title: Digger
description: The most powerful man in the world embarks on a frantic mission to prove he is humanity's saviour before the disaster he’s unleashed destroys everything.

title: Sense and Sensibility (U) (AD)
description: An irresistible new take on Jane Austen ’s iconic Sense and Sensibility : a charming, witty and deeply relatable story of love and sisterhood, starring Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles .

title: Digger
description: The most powerful man in the world embarks on a frantic mission to prove he is humanity's saviour before the disaster he’s unleashed destroys everything.

title: 14th
description: Ava DuVernay follows her epochal 2016 documentary 13th with a thrillingly expansive sequel of sorts, which passionately and persuasively details how the tenets of the 14th Amendment, ratified post–Civil War, are now under systematic attack.

title: L'Innocente
description: In his final film, Luchino Visconti offers a poison-pill variation on the theme that consumed his career—the moral decay of the soul-sick aristocracy—while achieving a masterful synthesis of stylistic splendor and emotional intensity.

title: A Nightmare On Elm Street
description: In Wes Craven's classic slasher film, several Midwestern teenagers fall prey to Freddy Krueger (Robert Englund), a disfigured midnight mangler who preys on the teenagers in their dreams -- which, in turn, kills them in reality. After investigating the phenomenon, Nancy (Heather Langenkamp) begins to suspect that a dark secret kept by her and her friends' parents may be the key to unraveling the mystery, but can Nancy and her boyfriend Glen (Johnny Depp) solve the puzzle before it's too late?

title: Sense and Sensibility
description: Left destitute by ruthless family members, two sisters navigate scandal, heartbreak, and strict social etiquette while searching for their perfect romantic matches.

title: Dead Ringers
description: This screening will be introduced by Video Bazaar. In one of Cronenberg’s most renowned and psychologically intense thrillers, twin brothers switch…

title: Fjord
description: Tue, Oct 6: Sneak preview + Q&A with director Cristian Mungiu and co-star Sebastian Stan after the 6:15 show! Tues, Oct 6: Extended intro with director Cristian Mungiu and co-star Sebastian Stan at the 8:15 show! From two-time Palme d’Or winner Cristian Mungiu, a Norwegian woman and her devout Romanian husband relocate with their five children to a remote, close-knit, coastal town. Their teenage children form a fast bond with a neighboring family as unease begins to simmer around their rigid beliefs. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice.

title: CORRUPTION
description:
Williams receives a mysterious briefcase that grants immense power, but only if he renounces love. Drawn into a shadowy warehouse filled with disturbing sexual tableaux, he descends deeper into a hallucinatory world of control, desire, and moral decay.
A bleak and surreal blend of porn, horror, and art-film, Corruption uses stark visuals and minimal plot to craft a disorienting, unsettling journey through human depravity and obsession.
CONTAINS HARDCORE SCENES. ADULTS ONLY!

title: The Disciple
description: Dutch Moroccan fanboy Tarik Azzougarh spends over a decade working to meet and befriend his heroes, the genre-defining hip-hop group Wu-Tang Clan and its iconic spiritual leader, RZA. After joining their movement, he becomes the architect of one of their most talked-about and controversial albums, “Once Upon a Time in Shaolin,” whose radical concept continues to reverberate throughout the music industry. What unfolds is a twisting coming-of-age tale of boyhood dreams, relentless determination and the downfall of flying too close to the sun.

title: Verity
description: Struggling writer Lowen Ashleigh is hired as a ghostwriter for renowned author Verity Crawford under mysterious circumstances, but her assignment takes a dark turn after discovering chilling autobiographical notes. Faced with a series of deadly family secrets, Lowen struggles to separate fiction from reality, while also blurring the lines with Verity’s husband, Jeremy.

title: THE SCOUT
description: Director González-Nasser spent six years working as a location scout. In this luminous directorial debut, she brings us into a day in the life of a young scout tasked with finding the perfect interiors for a television pilot. Sofía (Mimi Davila) moves in and out of other people’s intimate spaces and quotidian lives, tweaking her personality just enough to connect while struggling to find balance between her professional and personal worlds. With a mounting stack of parking tickets and the impertinent commentaries of her crew, she faces a series of small-yet-paralyzing obstacles that render her day increasingly exhausting. Through a constellation of quiet but poignant vignettes, the film offers an original view into the invisible labor of TV production, unfolding as an alternative symphony of a New York grappling with gentrification and a growing erosion of empathy.

title: Hanabi
description: In this diaristic journey through the combustible heart of contemporary Japan, filmmaker Ana Vaz uses Yoko Hasuke’s essay “Journal of a Radioactive Brain” as the inspiration and anchor for a freeform inquiry into living amidst natural and manmade disasters. Special Mention winner at the 2026 Locarno Film Festival.

description: In this companion piece to The Social Network , screenwriter Aaron Sorkin returns to the Metaverse with a tale of the whistleblower who started the social media reckoning we're seeing play out today.

The Clouds of Odessa Director - Luca Arcangeli Italy - 2026 - 13min A Ukrainian director thinks about the film, a love story, that she would have liked to make but that she may never be able to. Fantasies of a Rescue Dummy Director - Adrian Maganza U.K - 2025 - 7min Everyone forgets the rescue dummy that's left at the bottom of a swimming pool.

title: UNZIPPED
description: “Isaac Mizrahi as he conceived and contorted the way through to his fall 1994 show, [dashing] around a deserted SoHo with pal Sandra Bernhard; [meeting] with Naomi Campbell, Linda Evangelista, and baby Kate Moss for fittings; and [racing] uptown to an audience with Eartha Kitt... Hair-raising deadlines, delirious Bette Davis impressions, and the hostile but exhilarating act of executing a designer’s vision come together in a work that set the bar for all fashion films after.” – Vogue

title: Her Private Hell
description: From filmmaker Nicolas Winding Refn ( Drive , Only God Forgives , The Neon Demon ), Her Private Hell is a hypnotic moodscape enshrined in pink mist. Set against a surrealist, futuristic metropolis, the story follows Elle (Sophie Thatcher), a rising movie star preparing to shoot a space odyssey alongside her ex-lover turned stepmother (Havana Rose Liu). Elsewhere in the haze, an American GI (Charles Melton) wanders the desolate streets on a desperate search for his daughter. As an enigmatic and sinister figure known only as the Leather Man stalks the city's shadows, their lives begin to converge, dissolving the boundaries between past and present, memory and fate. Driven by his trademark neon cinematography, striking atmospheric dread, and an intoxicating orchestral score by legendary composer Pino Donaggio, Her Private Hell is a breathtaking, kaleidoscopic experience designed to mesmerise and seduce.

title: THE SOCIAL RECKONING
description: A companion piece to the hit film The Social Network, Sorkin’s original screenplay is based on the events that gave rise to the Wall Street Journal’s shocking exposé The Facebook Files. The film is inspired by the true story of how Frances Haugen (Madison), a young Facebook engineer, enlists the hel...

description: An American drama of uncommon intelligence, humor, and grace, the latest from writer-director Tony Gilroy (Michael Clayton) stars Pedro Pascal in a career-best performance as a cellist picking up the pieces of a fractured life.

title: Drunken Master (醉拳)
description: Drunken Master (醉拳). 1978. Hong Kong. Directed by Yuen Woo-ping. Martial arts direction by Yuen Woo-ping, Hsu Hsia. With Jackie Chan, Yuen Siu-tien. DCP. Courtesy Swank Motion Pictures. In Cantonese; English subtitles. 110 min. Building on the runaway success of Snake in the Eagle’s Shadow (1978), Drunken Master, released the same year, reunited director Yuen Woo-ping and Jackie Chan, establishing kung fu comedy as a major genre and hastening Chan’s unstoppable ascendence. Chan stars as a mischievous young Wong Fei-hung, the legendary kung fu master who has inspired countless movies and television series. Yuen’s father, Yuen Siu-tien, once again plays opposite Chan as his kung fu teacher, subjecting the reluctant pupil to an unforgiving regimen of “drunken boxing.” Yuen’s action choreography transforms seemingly clumsy movements into dazzling feats of precision and athleticism. Chan’s extraordinary physical gifts and impeccable comic timing reach exhilarating heights in the film’s breathtaking fight scenes, securing his place as one of the screen’s most original action stars.
