It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

title: FILIPIÑANA
description: 17-year-old Isabel navigates the opulent pavilions and lush green landscapes of Dr. Palanca’s luxury golf course as a newly-hired “tee girl.” Meticulously composed, highly stylized, and guided by precisely choreographed movement and deadpan delivery, FILIPIÑANA unfolds through the gradual accumulation of everyday encounters between staff and the wealthy clients of this secluded country club on the outskirts of Manila. When she attempts to return a lost golf club, Isabel uncovers a dark underbelly beneath the club’s pristine surfaces, in this sweltering, pastel-colored fairy tale of class division, institutional patriarchy, and invisible violence.

title: The Immigrant
description: Marion Cotillard has one of her greatest roles as Ewa, a Polish Catholic immigrant newly arrived in Ellis Island, trying to find the means to free her sister from quarantine in a c. 1921 New York City that’s full of lures and snares, among them Joaquin Phoenix’s smalltime pimp and tinhorn impresario and Jeremy Renner’s Bowery illusionist. A richly textured film of disarming depths of feeling from Gray, whose beguiling closing shot resonates long after the credits roll. “We effectively destroyed the film negative with various techniques,” said Darius Khondji, “to achieve the desired emotional aesthetic of that era.” Part of Radical Chiaroscuro: The Work of Darius Khondji

title: THE GOOD, THE BAD AND THE UGLY
description: The Man With No Name and Tuco are gunmen who admire each other professionally but dislike each other personally. Encountering a group of dying soldiers, Tuco learns the location of the graveyard where a Confederate treasure is buried, while the Man With No Name learns the identity of the exact grave. Joined by mercenary drifter Sentenza, they cross the desert, each of the desperadoes knowing part of the secret and each focusing his squinty eyes on the $200,000 bounty.

title: A Long Winter
description: High in the stark Mountain West, Mikey (Fred Hechinger) watches as his family slowly comes undone in Andrew Haigh’s (All of Us Strangers, NYFF61) beautiful yet forbidding 1950s-set tale of disappearance and growth, adapted from a Colm Tóibín story.

title: I Rarely Wake Up Dreaming
description: A timely and tender account of internal and external transformations, German filmmaker Isabelle Stever’s striking drama centers on a young queer couple navigating unprecedented waters in Ukraine during the height of the Russia invasion.

title: The History of Concrete
description: Fri, Sep 18: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Edy Modica (actress, comedian, filmmaker), after 4:40 show! Fri, Sep 18: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Rachel Kaly (comedian, writer, actor), after 7:15 show! Sun, Sep 20: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Sarah Sherman after 2:10 show! Following the finale of his TV show, filmmaker John Wilson searches for a new creative outlet. After attending a workshop on how to write and sell a Hallmark movie, he attempts to apply the same formula to a documentary about concrete.

title: Girls Like Girls
description: Based on writer/director Hayley Kiyoko's hit single and best-selling novel of the same name and featuring all-new music from Kiyoko, GIRLS LIKE GIRLS is a heartfelt coming-of-age story set over the course of one sun-drenched summer, where new-girl-in-town Coley falls in love for the first time while learning to accept herself along the way.

title: The History of Concrete
description: A filmmaker applies lessons from a Hallmark movie writing workshop to pitch a documentary about concrete.

title: Teen Witch
description: Top That! Behold the magic, the music, the hairspray, the tutus, and the rap battles of this camptastic spectacle of 80s awesomeness! Louise is a teenage nerd with dreams of popularity, romance, and style that always seem to elude her. But when she happens upon the witch Madame Serena (played by Poltergeist ‘s Zelda Rubinstein), she discovers she’s about to come into her magical powers upon her 16th birthday. But even as all her dreams come true, she’s finding out that magic isn’t always enchanting. Sing along to such bizarro songs as I Like Boys, Top That , and Most Popular Girl as this campy and over-the-top musicalamity casts its spell on you.

title: THE FROG AND THE WATER
description: Young Stefan ‘Buschi’ Busch (Detlefsen) lives in an assisted group home in Cologne, where his structured daily routine leaves little room for surprises. Nevertheless, he longs for change. Setting out on his own in an unexpected act of self-determination, Buschi seizes the chance to leave an organized outing and casually joins a Japanese tour group. Having lived his entire life without speaking, Buschi discovers new ways to express himself and connect with others on this unusual trip. Along the way, a tentative, silent friendship develops between Buschi and the Japanese traveler Hideo Kitamura (Kanji), a man on his own personal journey. As this extraordinary road trip unfolds across Germany, Switzerland, and Japan, a bond develops between these unlikely friends that transcends words. Stuber, Kuppel, and Yamato’s screenplay provides the perfect roadmap for award-winning performances by Kanji and Detlefsen in this most unlikely of off-beat road movies.

title: Battle Royale (18) + Introduction
description: Revisit the landmark of Asian Extreme Cinema, with an introduction by lead actor Tatsuya Fujiwara.

title: The Lost Children of Tuam
description: In rural Ireland, amateur historian Catherine Corless begins researching a former institution for unmarried mothers and their children, uncovering a shocking hidden history of loss. Based on the true story, and featuring a powerful performance from Monica Dolan, THE LOST CHILDREN OF TUAM is a deeply moving portrait of one woman’s fight for justice.

title: Kill Bill: Volume 1
description: Kill Bill: Volume 1. 2003. USA. Directed by Quentin Tarantino. Screenplay by Tarantino, Uma Thurman. Martial arts advisor Yuen Woo-ping. Sword fight choreography by Tetsuro Shimaguchi. With Thurman, Daryl Hannah, Vivica A. Fox, David Carradine. 35mm. In English, Japanese, French; English subtitles. 111 min. Quentin Tarantino’s Kill Bill is an exuberant revenge saga in which a former assassin awakens from a coma and sets out to hunt down the squad of killers who betrayed her. A lifelong devotee of Hong Kong kung fu, Japanese samurai films, and 1970s exploitation cinema, Tarantino turns the film into a delirious tour through the genres he loves, from Shaw Brothers martial arts to spaghetti Westerns and anime. Tarantino brought in Yuen Woo-ping, whose months-long fight camp prepared the stellar cast for hand-to-hand combat and fluid wirework, while sword-fight choreographer Tetsuro Shimaguchi contributed to the design of the blood-soaked katana duels. Blending Asian martial traditions with American grindhouse aesthetics, Kill Bill is a triumph of hyper-stylized action cinema.

title: The Illiac Passion
description: Markopoulos corralled together the underground’s haute monde—Taylor Mead, Gerard Malanga, Jack Smith, Gregory Battcock and, in the role of Poseidon, Andy Warhol—for his radical reinterpretation of Aeschylus’s Prometheus Bound, in which the filmmaker can be heard on the soundtrack reciting Thoreau’s translation of the source text betwixt snatches of Bartók’s Cantata Profana. A rebel posing a direct challenge to Zeus’s absolute authority, Prometheus was a figure of fascination for Markopoulos, who saw in the outlaw Titan something of a kindred spirit. Hence his vainglorious description of The Illiac Passion: “Metamorphosis of the filmmaker. Passions of the filmmaker. Out of his breast the free flowing blood of the creation of a motion picture which depicts the passions of mankind and of everyman in general.” Part of Classical Cinema

title: Shaun the Sheep: The Beast of Mossy Bottom
description: The new adventure sees the residents of Mossy Bottom Farm looking forward to Halloween - until the clumsy Farmer trashes the Flock's beloved pumpkin patch. When Shaun turns mad scientist to fix the problem, things rapidly spiral out of control, leading to a wild beast roaming the woods.

title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother 35mm
description: Latif is a devoutly religious hitman who struggles to balance work, faith, and fatherhood. When his wife dies, he embarks on a desperate journey across Houston in search of breast milk for his infant daughter, all while dodging sex traffickers, an evangelical militia, and his own demons.

title: Bird in Hand
description: Writer/Director Melody C. Roscher in person after the Friday, October 9th screening!

title: The Firemen's Ball
description: Our screening on Saturday 10 October will be introduced by Czech film expert Peter Hames and followed by a discussion group…

title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

title: Cotton Queen
description: In a cotton-farming village in Sudan, teenage Nafisa is raised on heroic tales of battling British colonisers told by her grandmother, the village matriarch Al-Sit. But when a young businessman arrives from abroad with a new development plan and genetically engineered cotton, Nafisa becomes the centre of a power play to determine the future of the village. Awakening to her own strength, Nafisa sets out to save the cotton fields – and herself. Neither she nor her community will ever be the same again.

title: UNZIPPED
description: “Isaac Mizrahi as he conceived and contorted the way through to his fall 1994 show, [dashing] around a deserted SoHo with pal Sandra Bernhard; [meeting] with Naomi Campbell, Linda Evangelista, and baby Kate Moss for fittings; and [racing] uptown to an audience with Eartha Kitt... Hair-raising deadlines, delirious Bette Davis impressions, and the hostile but exhilarating act of executing a designer’s vision come together in a work that set the bar for all fashion films after.” – Vogue

title: ASHES AND DIAMONDS
description: In the spring of 1945, weary and disillusioned by the war against the Nazis that has just ended, uncertain about a future under Communist rule, two resistance fighters are under orders to assassinate the incoming district leader. One of the fighters, the brooding Maciek, played by Zbigniew Cybulski (often called “the Polish James Dean”), falls in love with a local barmaid, and is suddenly torn about how to move forward. As Wajda said about ASHES AND DIAMONDS, almost universally regarded as his masterpiece, “I have tried to reveal to movie audiences the complicated and difficult world of a generation to which I myself belong.” This anguished, romantic, and deeply personal film is an all-time favorite of both Francis Ford Coppola and Martin Scorsese, who placed it as #3 on his top ten list for Sight and Sound.

title: Le jour où… (The Day When)
description: Le jour où… (The Day When). 1997. Switzerland. Directed by Chantal Akerman. 2K restoration by the Royal Film Archive of Belgium — CINEMATEK and Fondation Chantal Akerman; courtesy Waka Films. In French; English subtitles. 7 min. Sud (South). 1999. Belgium/France. Directed by Chantal Akerman. DCP courtesy Icarus Films. 70 min. Chantal Akerman, drawn to the American South by William Faulkner and James Baldwin, arrived in Jasper, Texas, on the one-year anniversary of the gruesome lynching of James Byrd Jr. by white supremacists. With imagery from what was meant to be a location-scouting trip, Sud interweaves interviews, footage of Byrd’s funeral, and prolonged tracking shots retracing the road on which Byrd, chained to a pickup truck, met his senseless and brutal death. “Chantal and I often listened to Billie Holiday’s ‘Strange Fruit’ during the editing process,” Claire Atherton recalls. “We even considered putting the song in the film. Ultimately, we didn’t even try…. What guided me during the construction of Sud was Chantal’s extreme attention to the present. We never show or describe the past, but it is dredged up by the present…. It’s about the violence of the world and the way history haunts landscapes to become a part of our gaze.” Sud is preceded by The Day When, produced for an omnibus project on the occasion of the Locarno Film Festival’s 50th anniversary in 1997. In a comical interlude, Akerman makes herself dizzy with the circular movement of her camera and the sound of her own voice. “The day I decided to think about the future of cinema, I told myself I wouldn’t live to see it,” she says. “I asked myself if the future is always in front of us. So I looked ahead; then I turned around.”

title: Sense and Sensibility (U) (AD)
description: An irresistible new take on Jane Austen ’s iconic Sense and Sensibility : a charming, witty and deeply relatable story of love and sisterhood, starring Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles .

title: Digger
description: The most powerful man in the world embarks on a frantic mission to prove he is humanity's saviour before the disaster he’s unleashed destroys everything.

title: Serial Mom
description: Beverly is the perfect happy homemaker, along with her doting husband and two children, but this nuclear family just might explode when her fascination with serial killers collides with her ever-so-proper code of ethics.

title: VACANCES
description: FILMMAKER IN PERSON! A strange and unusual mixture of warts-and-all family portraiture, subtle exposé of class and privilege, and minimalist depiction of a particular setting that’s rendered with an almost miraculously tactile sense of presence, photographer and filmmaker Victoria Hely-Hutchinson’s VACANCES is a deceptively unassuming film. Filmed over the course of a decade at the property in Provence inhabited by Hely-Hutchinson’s outrageously uninhibited grandmother, a bohemian Austro-Hungarian countess and family matriarch, VACANCES grew out of Hely-Hutchinson’s 2016 short film of the same name, and is something of a filmic complement to her autobiographical 2023 book, “I Left My Grandmother’s House”. The documentary delves, with a grace and open-endedness that belies its analytical bite, into both the bigger-than-life personality of “granny” as well as the sometimes strained dynamics among the rest of the family, including Hely-Hutchinson’s grandfather, mother, and siblings. Unique in suggesting by turns cinema vérité, reality TV, chamber theater, and the minimalism of landscape cinema, VACANCES is a profoundly singular work – a film whose technique is nearly invisible, but which sneaks up on you with its trenchant perceptions, layered meanings, and emotional and filmic complexity. “This time-lapse film, shot over a period of ten years, follows members of several generations of a wealthy aristocratic family with Austro-Hungarian roots. The entire film is set in a Provençal villa, whose social heart is the swimming pool, around which the women gather to exchange various observations and, surreptitiously, gossip. The center of the family is the aging matriarch, who likes to talk about her extravagant, promiscuous life, but at the same time commands all the attention and authority of those around her. However, her influence gradually weakens with each passing generation.” –JI.HLAVA INTERNATIONAL DOCUMENTARY FILM FESTIVAL

title: The Uprising
description: Andrew Garfield stars as the legendary leader of a ferocious rebellion against the tyranny of King Richard II. As war burns across England, he forms an army of the people to face the King’s might in a fight for justice and survival.

title: Possession
description: The film will be introduced by writer and historian Susan Jonusas on the 18th of September and by writer Stephen Thrower…

title: Mermaids
description: It’s 1963, and different-drummer single mother Cher has decided to move from Oklahoma to smalltown Massachusetts, uprooting her two daughters, nine-year-old Kate and Catholicism-obsessed 15-year-old Rachel (Winona Ryder, who provides the narration). What follows includes JFK assassination trauma, a pregnancy scare, mother-daughter sexual competition, and one miraculous rescue, with devastating dynamic duo Cher and Ryder pushing one another to histrionic heights. Part of Winona Ryder Analogue Youth

title: The Dreamed Adventure
description: Winner of the Cannes Jury Prize, Valeska Grisebach’s quietly thrilling new film about a middle-aged archaeologist searching for a disappeared former flame at the fragile boundaries of Eastern and Western Europe gradually shifts into a wide-ranging crime saga. Bulgaria’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: Possession
description: After Anna (Isabelle Adjani) reveals to her husband, Mark (Sam Neill), that she is having an affair, she leaves him and their son. Mark is devastated, and seeks out Heinrich (Heinz Bennent), the man who cuckolded him, only to receive a beating. After a series of violent confrontations between Mark and Anna, Mark hires a private investigator to follow her. Anna descends into madness, and it's soon clear that she is hiding a much bigger secret -- one that is both inexplicable and shocking.

title: SHARKY'S MACHINE
description:
A tough Atlanta vice detective becomes obsessed with bringing down a powerful pimp connected to a wider web of crime and corruption. As his investigation deepens, he pushes beyond the limits of the law, risking his career and safety in a relentless pursuit that pulls him further into danger.
Less about flashy action than slow-burn obsession, the film settles into the rhythms of surveillance, stakeouts, and creeping paranoia. Its sense of place is key, capturing a city simmering beneath the surface, while the central performance anchors the story in a mix of weariness, fixation, and quiet intensity.

title: Digger

title: The Diary of a Chambermaid
description: Radu Jude brilliantly explores Europe’s modern-day power and class dynamics through the trenchant story of a young Romanian woman working for a well-to-do family in Bordeaux, while her own young daughter misses her back home.

title: The Social Reckoning (15) (AD)
description: In this companion piece to The Social Network , screenwriter Aaron Sorkin returns to the Metaverse with a tale of the whistleblower who started the social media reckoning we're seeing play out today.

title: Sense and Sensibility
description: Left destitute by ruthless family members, two sisters navigate scandal, heartbreak, and strict social etiquette while searching for their perfect romantic matches.

title: Fjord
description: Tue, Oct 6: Sneak preview + Q&A with director Cristian Mungiu and co-star Sebastian Stan after the 6:15 show! Tues, Oct 6: Extended intro with director Cristian Mungiu and co-star Sebastian Stan at the 8:15 show! From two-time Palme d’Or winner Cristian Mungiu, a Norwegian woman and her devout Romanian husband relocate with their five children to a remote, close-knit, coastal town. Their teenage children form a fast bond with a neighboring family as unease begins to simmer around their rigid beliefs. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice.

title: The Disciple
description: Dutch Moroccan fanboy Tarik Azzougarh spends over a decade working to meet and befriend his heroes, the genre-defining hip-hop group Wu-Tang Clan and its iconic spiritual leader, RZA. After joining their movement, he becomes the architect of one of their most talked-about and controversial albums, “Once Upon a Time in Shaolin,” whose radical concept continues to reverberate throughout the music industry. What unfolds is a twisting coming-of-age tale of boyhood dreams, relentless determination and the downfall of flying too close to the sun.

title: Verity
description: Struggling writer Lowen Ashleigh is hired as a ghostwriter for renowned author Verity Crawford under mysterious circumstances, but her assignment takes a dark turn after discovering chilling autobiographical notes. Faced with a series of deadly family secrets, Lowen struggles to separate fiction from reality, while also blurring the lines with Verity’s husband, Jeremy.

title: Bucking Fastard
description: The oddball brilliance of Werner Herzog—returning to NYFF for the first time since 1982’s Fitzcarraldo (NYFF20)—is in full effect in this tale of two sisters (Kate and Rooney Mara, in total sync) who live by their own social and emotional standards and rules.

title: UNZIPPED

title: Her Private Hell
description: From filmmaker Nicolas Winding Refn ( Drive , Only God Forgives , The Neon Demon ), Her Private Hell is a hypnotic moodscape enshrined in pink mist. Set against a surrealist, futuristic metropolis, the story follows Elle (Sophie Thatcher), a rising movie star preparing to shoot a space odyssey alongside her ex-lover turned stepmother (Havana Rose Liu). Elsewhere in the haze, an American GI (Charles Melton) wanders the desolate streets on a desperate search for his daughter. As an enigmatic and sinister figure known only as the Leather Man stalks the city's shadows, their lives begin to converge, dissolving the boundaries between past and present, memory and fate. Driven by his trademark neon cinematography, striking atmospheric dread, and an intoxicating orchestral score by legendary composer Pino Donaggio, Her Private Hell is a breathtaking, kaleidoscopic experience designed to mesmerise and seduce.

title: THE SOCIAL RECKONING
description: A companion piece to the hit film The Social Network, Sorkin’s original screenplay is based on the events that gave rise to the Wall Street Journal’s shocking exposé The Facebook Files. The film is inspired by the true story of how Frances Haugen (Madison), a young Facebook engineer, enlists the hel...

title: The Social Reckoning
description: Explores Facebook's internal practices, spread of false information, impact on teen mental health, and connection to January 6 Capitol events.

title: Tony (15) (AD)
description: A 19-year-old Anthony Bourdain travels to Provincetown and stumbles into the chaotic world of a restaurant kitchen, carving out a slice of a summer that will shape the course of his life.

title: MY UNDESIRABLE FRIENDS: PART II – EXILE: Chapters 1-3
description: When Russia shuts down all independent media, a group of young dissident journalists must flee Moscow so they can keep reporting and not go to prison. In her riveting follow-up to last year’s awards-sweeping MY UNDESIRABLE FRIENDS — LAST AIR IN MOSCOW, Julia Loktev follows these courageous, sharply funny women (and a few men) as they fan out across a dozen countries, to Istanbul, Tbilisi, Prague, Vienna, Amsterdam, New York, and beyond. Over the course of four years, they continue to report the truth to Russians from exile, covering their country’s war crimes, even as they face death threats and are declared extremists and terrorists—as they find new meanings of family, friendship, love, and home far from the country to which they may never return. (Viewers can follow EXILE without first seeing LAST AIR IN MOSCOW.)

title: Earth
description: Dovzhenko’s final silent feature, which depicts a clash between reactionary landowning peasants and modernizing paupers bringing the first tractor to their corner of the Ukrainian countryside, has by now spawned nearly a century of debate: is it a propagandist paean to the collectivization project in Stalin’s first Five-Year Plan, which would have catastrophic results in the Ukrainian Famine of 1932-33, or, as certain Soviet censors suspected, an on-the-sly celebration of a Ukrainian folk culture grounded in an ancient connection between the peasants and the soil they’ve so long tilled, threatened with impending erasure? What is not up for question is that Earth is among the greatest of films from the silent film canon, its distinct synthesis of Eisenstein, Pudovkin, and Vertov making it something like a summation of what had come before it, while its lyric ode to the natural world and those that live with it in harmony blazes a trail for the Ukrainian Poetic Cinema of the future to follow. 35mm print courtesy of the Filmoteka Narodowa, Warsaw Live musical accompaniment by Fima Chupakhin, piano & synths, and Julian Kytasty, bandura & vocals on Saturday, October 10th Part of Oleksandr Dovzhenko: Earth and Empire

title: Kill Bill: Volume 2
description: Kill Bill: Volume 2. 2004. USA. Directed by Quentin Tarantino. Screenplay by Tarantino, Uma Thurman. Martial Arts Advisor Yuen Woo-ping. With Thurman, David Carradine, Gordon Liu Chia-hui. 35mm. In English, Cantonese, Mandarin, Spanish; English subtitles. 137 min. Originally conceived as a single film, the four-hour-plus Kill Bill was split into two volumes released six months apart. Volume 2 completes the Bride’s (Uma Thurman) quest for revenge, turning inward from the operatic violence of the first installment to focus on the history, training, and emotional bonds that shaped her. Yuen Woo-ping’s choreography anchors the transformation, revealing in flashbacks her brutal training under kung fu master Pai Mei, played by legendary Shaw Brothers star Gordon Liu Chia-hui (The 36th Chamber of Shaolin, The Eight Diagram Pole Fighter). Combining Yuen’s traditional martial discipline with Quentin Tarantino’s Western aesthetic, Volume 2 delivers a character-focused resolution to the Bride’s journey.

title: AFTERIMAGE
description: Released the year that he died at 90, Wajda’s AFTERIMAGE is the perfect coda to a career devoted to depicting the struggle between repressive governments and the free individual. Based on the life of avant-garde painter Wladysław Strzeminski, who was a target of post-War Stalinist forces, which banned abstract art in favor of state-sponsored Socialist Realism, AFTERIMAGE is a classically made drama with a commanding performance by long-time Wajda actor Bogusław Linda as the artist. Of his compulsion to make a film about Strzemiński, Wajda said, “It’s good to see what happens when art is supervised, controlled, influenced by authority and censorship.”

title: Nightborn
description: Tickets Are Only Available via BFI London Film Festival Website from Tuesday 17 September 2026 10:00am: Click Here To Book A couple’s dream of idyllic family life in the Finnish woods is shattered by the arrival of their nightmarish new baby, in Hanna Bergholm’s riotously gory folk horror. Drawing deeply from the wells of folk horror and psychological post-natal angst, director Bergholm pits Seidi Haarla and Rupert Grint’s new parents against their hairy, howling offspring, which displays a taste for raw meat over milk. Gruesome and bloody, it’s also chock-full of self-aware humour that surely guarantees the film’s place as a future cult classic. English and Finnish Language with some English subtitles Content warning: Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury and harm towards children.

title: First They Came for My College
description: When Florida Governor Ron DeSantis stages a coup at New College, the state’s beloved public honors college, students and professors confront a new reality: their campus is ground zero in an unprecedented nationwide assault on academic freedom and diversity.

title: André Leon Talley: Style is Forever
description: André Leon Talley was a trailblazing fashion icon whose influence spanned nearly five decades. This documentary explores his legacy of inclusivity, elegance, and the fearless pursuit of authenticity. Interviews with Anna Wintour, Tom Ford and Diane von Furstenberg, among others, as well as never-before-seen footage, reveal Talley’s personal and professional challenges and remarkable triumphs.

title: A LAND WITHIN
description: Alto Adige/Südtirol/South Tyrol, 1961. A series of separatist bomb attacks shakes the northern Italian region with a German-speaking minority. Paul (Prenn), a farmer’s son and free spirit, dreams of escaping his little village to study painting in Munich. When his hardliner older brother, Anton (Rupp), is exposed as one of the bombers and is forced to flee, he leaves the farm, his wife Anna (Schwarz) and young son Thomas (Carli) behind. Reluctantly, Paul stays to support the family, but as ethnic tensions and police repression in the village grow, he is drawn into a downward spiral of violence and toxic masculinity. As events spin out of control, Paul must choose between his dream and standing up against his brother. In

title: HOPE
description: In the remote South Korean village of Hope Harbor, police chief Bum-seok (Hwang Jung- min) and officer Sung-ae (Hoyeon) are called to find a mysterious creature that has wreaked havoc on the village. In the nearby forest, a coterie of hunters, including Sung- ki (Zo In-Sung) set out to track the bea...

title: D’est (From the East)
description: D’est (From the East). 1993. Belgium/France. Directed by Chantal Akerman. 2K restoration by the Royal Film Archive of Belgium — CINEMATEK and Fondation Chantal Akerman; DCP courtesy Icarus Films. No dialogue. 115 min. Filmed from East Germany to Moscow between the summer and deep winter of 1993, Chantal Akerman’s dispatch from the newly collapsed Soviet Union captures “everything that touched me” through deliberately paced tracking shots, circular pans, and domestic scenes. A travelogue through landscapes and overcrowded urban centers—whose interminable tableaux of train and bus queues become a sobering metaphor of historic upheaval—D’est chronicles everyday Poles, Ukrainians, Germans, and Russians staring down an uncertain future. Claire Atherton recalls editing this landmark film: “It was like a composition, both in the musical and visual sense. We were sculpting in time and space, looking for the right rhythm. We were editing in the same way Chantal had shot the film, following our intuition, without trying to understand. We said simple things to each other about color, clashes, ruptures, night and day, exterior and interior, violence, softness, the sound of footsteps in the snow or of tires screeching on icy roads…. Words only appeared a year later, like echoes to the images, when we were editing the installation D’est, au bord de la fiction (1995). These words became those of the installation’s 25th screen, spoken by Chantal: ‘Yesterday, today, and tomorrow, there were, there will be, there are at this very moment, / people whom history, which no longer even has a capital H, whom history has struck down.’”

description: Latif is a devoutly religious hitman who struggles to balance work, faith, and fatherhood. When his wife dies, he embarks on a desperate journey across Houston in search of breast milk for his infant daughter, all while dodging sex traffickers, an evangelical militia, and his own demons.

title: House
description: Hoping to find a sense of connection to her late mother, Gorgeous takes a trip to the country to visit her aunt at their ancestral house. She invites her six friends, Prof, Melody, Mac, Fantasy, Kung Fu, and Sweet, to join her. The girls soon discover that there is more to the old house than meets the eye.

title: WALKER / EL PATRULLERO
description: The life of American lawyer and journalist William Walker, who named himself president of Nicaragua during the 1850s.

title: PLAYING WITH FIRE: AN ECOSEXUAL EMERGENCY
description: Following their two previous films – GOODBYE GAULEY MOUNTAIN: AN ECOSEXUAL LOVE STORY (2014) and WATER MAKES US WET: AN ECOSEXUAL ADVENTURE (2019) – Annie Sprinkle and Beth Stephens bring us the third chapter in their climate crisis trilogy: PLAYING WITH FIRE: AN ECOSEXUAL EMERGENCY. With the climate crisis worsening with each passing season, the artist/activist duo sound the alarm by enlisting a collective of artists, elders, witches, neighbors, and friends, to examine the ways we can support the health of our dear Earth. Partially narrated by Boulder Creek’s mythical white peacock Albert and culminating in a ceremonial Wedding to Fire in the Redwoods, PLAYING WITH FIRE is a powerful portrait of queer resilience but also a reckoning with the power of fire, with its capacity to heal and its potential to destroy. Co-sponsored by Climate Film Festival and Queer New York International Arts Festival. Annie Sprinkle & Beth Stephens will be here in person for both screenings, and will present a ten-minute performative introduction before each show, “Ecosex 101”! On Saturday, Sprinkle & Stephens will appear for a post-screening discussion and Q&A led by Barbara Carellas, author of “The Book of Ecstasy”, and on Sunday, Angelo Madsen (director of A BODY TO LIVE IN) will lead a Q&A. Viewers are encouraged to dress up in the themes of fire and ecosex. After the Saturday screening, all are welcome to join a reception in the lobby. Beth and Annie will honor two legends of golden age adult entertainment and the co-founders of the first pornstar support group, Club 90. Veronica Vera is turning 80 and Veronica Hart is turning 70. Birthday cake will be served, and signed books and merch will be available for purchase.

title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

title: The Foul King
description: Already a well-established presence in South Korean music, with an ability to work with equal facility in a variety of idioms (experimental, rock, folk, et. al.), Jang got his start in film composing the distinctive score for Kim’s eccentric, unpredictable, and entirely endearing underdog sports comedy, a barbed commentary on suffocating white-collar culture starring Song Kang-ho (Parasite) as mild-mannered bank clerk Dae-ho, mercilessly pushed around in the office and generally ground down by life… until he gains a new measure of self-worth by beginning to moonlight as a masked “heel” wrestler, his signature move: finding ingenious new ways to cheat in the ring. Part of Composed by Jang Young Gyu

title: UNZIPPED
description: “Isaac Mizrahi as he conceived and contorted the way through to his fall 1994 show, [dashing] around a deserted SoHo with pal Sandra Bernhard; [meeting] with Naomi Campbell, Linda Evangelista, and baby Kate Moss for fittings; and [racing] uptown to an audience with Eartha Kitt... Hair-raising deadlines, delirious Bette Davis impressions, and the hostile but exhilarating act of executing a designer’s vision come together in a work that set the bar for all fashion films after.” – Vogue

title: FILIPIÑANA
description: 17-year-old Isabel navigates the opulent pavilions and lush green landscapes of Dr. Palanca’s luxury golf course as a newly-hired “tee girl.” Meticulously composed, highly stylized, and guided by precisely choreographed movement and deadpan delivery, FILIPIÑANA unfolds through the gradual accumulation of everyday encounters between staff and the wealthy clients of this secluded country club on the outskirts of Manila. When she attempts to return a lost golf club, Isabel uncovers a dark underbelly beneath the club’s pristine surfaces, in this sweltering, pastel-colored fairy tale of class division, institutional patriarchy, and invisible violence.

title: The History of Concrete
description: A filmmaker applies lessons from a Hallmark movie writing workshop to pitch a documentary about concrete.

title: Sense and Sensibility (U) (AD)
description: An irresistible new take on Jane Austen ’s iconic Sense and Sensibility : a charming, witty and deeply relatable story of love and sisterhood, starring Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles .

title: The Enchanted Desna
description: The third film made by Solntseva from a script by her late husband and creative collaborator, The Enchanted Desna—an intimate epic in the magic-realist vein filmed on 70mm Sovscope and boasting state-of-the-art stereophonic sound—draws on Dovzhenko’s memories of his childhood on the banks of the Desna River in Chernihiv Oblast, moving freely between pre-revolutionary bucolic idyll, the horrors of World War II, and contemporary-set scenes. Winner of a Special Jury Prize at the San Sebastián Film Festival, Jean-Luc Godard’s favorite film of 1965 and, per critic Jonathan Rosenbaum, “among the most ravishingly beautiful and poetic spectacles ever made.” DCP courtesy of Berkeley Art Museum and Pacific Film Archive, scanned from a 35mm print in their collection. Part of Oleksandr Dovzhenko: Earth and Empire

title: Suicide Note
description: Shot largely in New York between 1976 and 1984, this newly restored, seldom-screened film from critic and artist Fred Camper is a fragmentary, diaristic work, capturing a cluttered and melancholic world on silent Super 8 Ektachrome reversal film.

title: The Social Reckoning (15) (AD)
description: In this companion piece to The Social Network , screenwriter Aaron Sorkin returns to the Metaverse with a tale of the whistleblower who started the social media reckoning we're seeing play out today.

title: The Uprising
description: Andrew Garfield stars as the legendary leader of a ferocious rebellion against the tyranny of King Richard II. As war burns across England, he forms an army of the people to face the King’s might in a fight for justice and survival.

title: The Social Reckoning
description: A companion piece to the hit film The Social Network, Sorkin’s original screenplay is based on the events that gave rise to the Wall Street Journal’s shocking exposé The Facebook Files. The film is inspired by the true story of how Frances Haugen (Madison), a young Facebook engineer, enlists the help of Jeff Horwitz (White), a Wall Street Journal reporter, to go on a dangerous journey that ends up blowing the whistle on the social network’s most guarded secrets.

title: Nadja
description: In 1993, invited by David Lynch to come up with a low-budget genre movie, Michael Almereyda ( Tesla , Experimenter , Hamlet ) came up with a moody, postmodern reimagining of the Dracula myth which draws inspiration from Dracula’s Daughter (1936) and André Breton’s surrealist novel Nadja . The film follows estranged vampire twins Nadja (Elina Löwensohn) and Edgar (a young Jared Harris) as they reunite following their father’s death by the flamboyantly unhinged Dr. Van Helsing, played with relish by Peter Fonda. The film’s striking visuals combine high-contrast black-and-white 35mm cinematography with the hallucinatory grain of Pixelvision video is now newly restored in 4K.

title: Digger (15) (AD)
description: Academy Award-winning filmmaker Alejandro G Iñárritu ( Birdman ) returns with his original feature starring Tom Cruise as the most powerful man in the world.

title: The Shining [UK Version]
description: Jack Torrance (Jack Nicholson) becomes winter caretaker at the isolated Overlook Hotel in Colorado, hoping to cure his writer's block. He settles in along with his wife, Wendy (Shelley Duvall), and his son, Danny (Danny Lloyd), who is plagued by psychic premonitions. As Jack's writing goes nowhere and Danny's visions become more disturbing, Jack discovers the hotel's dark secrets and begins to unravel into a homicidal maniac hell-bent on terrorizing his family.

title: BITTER MOON
description:
On a luxury cruise to Istanbul, buttoned-up British husband Nigel becomes fascinated by the beautiful Mimi and her bitter, wheelchair-bound husband Oscar. Night after night, Oscar draws him deeper into the story of their affair: a delirious descent from erotic obsession into humiliation, cruelty and mutual destruction.
Roman Polanski turns a holiday romance into a poisonous black comedy of sexual warfare, with Hugh Grant, Kristin Scott Thomas, Peter Coyote and Emmanuelle Seigner circling one another through a fog of lust, jealousy and very bad decisions.

title: Digger
description: The most powerful man in the world embarks on a frantic mission to prove he is humanity's saviour before the disaster he’s unleashed destroys everything.

title: The Lost Children of Tuam
description: In rural Ireland, amateur historian Catherine Corless begins researching a former institution for unmarried mothers and their children, uncovering a shocking hidden history of loss. Based on the true story, and featuring a powerful performance from Monica Dolan, THE LOST CHILDREN OF TUAM is a deeply moving portrait of one woman’s fight for justice.

title: LOTNA
description: Perhaps the most personally meaningful of Wajda’s World War II movies, LOTNA was likely inspired by the director’s admiration for his father, a Polish cavalry officer who was killed during the Katyń massacre in 1940. LOTNA is a beautiful white horse, given as a gift by a wealthy landowner to a Polish cavalry troop in the fateful year of 1939. As the Germans attack with planes and tanks, the underequipped Polish army relies on archaic resources, such as the cavalry. Symbolic and at times surreal, the film was controversial at the time of its release for suggesting Polish foolhardiness in the face of the Nazi threat.

title: Verity
description: Struggling writer Lowen Ashleigh is hired as a ghostwriter for renowned author Verity Crawford under mysterious circumstances, but her assignment takes a dark turn after discovering chilling autobiographical notes. Faced with a series of deadly family secrets, Lowen struggles to separate fiction from reality, while also blurring the lines with Verity’s husband, Jeremy.

title: Crimes of Passion
description: Fashion designer Joanna Crane leads a double life. By night she is China Blue, a prostitute who’s attracted the attention of a sexually frustrated private detective, and a psychopathic priest in possession of a murderous sex toy.

title: The Man I Love
description: Ira Sachs’s finely detailed period drama about an emotionally complicated cabaret star and performance artist (Oscar winner Rami Malek) living with AIDS in 1980s New York is a reminder that art and imagination are keys to human survival in the darkest times.

title: LFF: I Plant My Hand in the Garden
Hot Spot
description: Tickets Are Only Available via BFI London Film Festival Website from Tuesday 17 September 2026 10:00am: Click Here To Book The new film from the acclaimed director of The Silent Twins is a daring and distinctive sci-fi thriller set in a near-future society ruled by sentient AI. Djonny, a vibrantly dressed private eye, is called to solve a mysterious murder case, only to discover a rebel group capable of undermining the digital overlord led by Rana, who may or may not be a cyber witch. Agnieszka Smoczynska creates a hypnotic, dystopian world that lures you in with its breathtaking aesthetics and hallucinatory images. English, Japanese Language and Polish Language with some English Subtitles Content Warning: Contains flashing images

title: The Social Reckoning
description: Explores Facebook's internal practices, spread of false information, impact on teen mental health, and connection to January 6 Capitol events.

title: Resident Evil
description: In this sci-fi horror action reboot, a hapless medical courier fights for his life amid an outbreak of a deadly mutagenic virus in an isolated mountain town.

title: Bitter Christmas
description: The incomparable Pedro Almodóvar explores the artist’s tenuous relationship with fiction and reality in this film about an actress writing a script inspired by the lives of those around her—which is itself the invention of an Almodóvar-like filmmaker.

title: Fjord
description: Tue, Oct 6: Sneak preview + Q&A with director Cristian Mungiu and co-star Sebastian Stan after the 6:15 show! Tues, Oct 6: Extended intro with director Cristian Mungiu and co-star Sebastian Stan at the 8:15 show! From two-time Palme d’Or winner Cristian Mungiu, a Norwegian woman and her devout Romanian husband relocate with their five children to a remote, close-knit, coastal town. Their teenage children form a fast bond with a neighboring family as unease begins to simmer around their rigid beliefs. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice.

title: Pulse
description: After college student Taguchi (Kenji Mizuhashi) commits suicide, a number of young adults living in Tokyo witness terrifying visions transferred across the Internet. As more people disappear throughout the city, the Internet becomes a breeding ground for malevolent spirits. Three seemingly disconnected stories follow Michi (Kumiko Asô), Ryosuke (Haruhiko Katô) and Harue (Koyuki) as they attempt to solve the mystery behind the ghostly visions that are seeping beyond their computer monitors.

title: Akira
description: The post-apocalypse as playground for wayward youth. Street gangs ride up and down the highways, and it’s all fun and games until the city gets blown up. Again. The second banana gets big for his boots, and I mean BIG. You know it, you love it. A pounding soundtrack, the best drawn visuals money can buy and an ending for the ages.

title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

title: BATMAN & ROBIN
description: Superstars George Clooney and Arnold Schwarzenegger face off as the coolest–and the cruelest–villain to ever stalk Gotham City comes after its courageous caped crusaders, Batman & Robin. When the evil Mr. Freeze (Schwarzenegger) teams up with toxic Poison Ivy (Uma Thurman) to freeze Gotham City and destroy its residents, the end appears near for superheroes Batman (George Clooney) and Robin (Chris O’Donnell). But with the arrival of Batgirl (Alicia Silverstone), the dynamic duo becomes a transcendent trio in this fourth episode of the blockbuster theatrical series.

title: The Wailing
description: As country bumpkin police sergeant Kwak Do-won investigates a series of murders that appear to be connected to a strange, sense-deranging sickness that’s going around, local villagers fix the blame on a Japanese drifter suspected of being an evil spirit in Na’s atmospheric tale of demons, shamans, exorcisms, and animated corpses, steeped in ancient east Asian folklore and Christian symbolism. A sporadically hilarious, brilliantly plotted work of insinuating, creeping terror that turns shopworn horror tropes inside out to create something entirely unpredictable and genuinely disturbing. “Korean cinema has a new genre maestro… A supremely unsettling evocation.” —The Guardian Introduction by composer Jang Young Gyu on Saturday, October 3rd Part of Composed by Jang Young Gyu

title: High and Low
description: Kurosawa’s formal genius and rare humanism are on full display in this white-knuckle thriller—source of an upcoming remake by Spike Lee—which transposes the materials of an Ed McBain novel to contemporary Japan, starring Toshiro Mifune as a rich industrialist thrown into a nerve-shredding situation after, first believing his son has been kidnapped, discovering that his chauffeur’s child was taken by accident. Boasting nigh-constant visual invention, geometric precision of framing, an inventive narrative structure, and a bevy of staggering set pieces—the train hand-off! the down-and-dirty G.I. bar!—High & Low is a virtuoso work that’s also a deeply moral one, exploring the meaning of “justice” in a society defined by vast economic disparity. “High and Low has one of the most iconic train scenes of all time. And though it’s only one of many segments, the entire, wildly careening film has the feeling of a train in the slow-motion throes of derailment.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue Part of Trains: Local Routes

title: All About Lily Chou-Chou
description: Staff pick by Richard For kids around the world, music is often the only salvation when the pain and anxiety of teenage life becomes too much to bear. Yuichi (Hayato Ichihara) is in the 8th grade and he worships Lily Chou-Chou, a Bjork-like chanteuse whose epic music is lush and transcendent. Yuichi only lives for Lily Chou-Chou’s big Tokyo concert, where the lies and violence can be washed away by the presence of his goddess and her powerful music. But fate has yet another obstacle in store for Lily’s devoted fan.

title: Evil Dead 2
description: After playing a recording of the Book of the Dead found in a seemingly abandoned cabin in the woods and unleashing an evil force that possesses his girlfriend, Ash (Bruce Campbell) is forced into a macabre battle for his life. When four strangers appear in the midst of his mad scramble for survival, more and more possessions and gory deaths pile up.

title: The Exorcist
description: SOMETHING ALMOST BEYOND COMPREHENSION IS HAPPENING TO A GIRL ON THIS STREET, IN THIS HOUSE… AND A MAN HAS BEEN SENT FOR AS A LAST RESORT. When 12-year-old Regan MacNeil falls ill, she becomes violent and puzzles doctors with the personality of a horrifying entity. Desperate for answers, Regan’s movie-star mother Chris seeks the help of two priests: one who has lost his faith, and an exorcist. Winner of 1973 Oscars for Best Adapted Screenplay and Best Sound Mixing, THE EXORCIST remains one of the most shocking and gripping movies in the history of cinema.

title: Let’s Scare Jessica to Death
description: Something is after Jessica. Something very cold, very wet… and very dead. Recently released from a mental institution, a young woman hopes for a return to normal life but soon finds her sanity unraveling after moving into a rundown farmhouse. Hypnotically atmospheric and unforgettably unsettling, Let’s Scare Jessica to Death is a ‘70s masterwork of mood-drenched horror.

title: The Blair Witch Project
description: Three film students travel to Maryland to make a student film about a local urban legend... The Blair Witch. The three went into the woods on a two day hike to find the Blair Witch, and never came back. One year later, the students film and video were found in the woods. The footage was compiled and made into a movie. The Blair Witch Project.

title: Begotten
description: BEGOTTEN has no characters in the ordinary sense. Its final credits name three principal figures: God Killing Himself. Mother Earth. Son of Earth – Flesh on Bone. The entire film is what those names do to each other and to the earth. God Killing Himself tears open his body and dies. Mother Earth rises from what remains and takes his seed into herself. She gives birth to Son of Earth Flesh on Bone. He is cast into a barren world, seized by the Nomads, tortured, killed, and briefly returned to life by his mother.The Nomads destroy her too. The Robed Figures gather what remains of mother and son, grind their bodies down, and return them to the soil. The ground flowers.

title: A Nightmare on Elm Street 3: Dream Warriors             / The Blob (1988)
description: Sleep can’t protect the youth of Westin Hills Psychiatric Hospital when a knife-gloved night slasher invades terrified teen dreams and turns their nightmares into deadly reality. But their new therapist has her own tortured history with the dream demon and together they may be able to finally rid the world of Freddy in what may be the ultimate Elm Street sequel.

title: The History of Concrete
description: A filmmaker applies lessons from a Hallmark movie writing workshop to pitch a documentary about concrete.

title: The Birds
description: A wealthy San Francisco socialite pursues a potential boyfriend to a small Northern California town that slowly takes a turn for the bizarre when birds of all kinds suddenly begin to attack people.

title: At Night
description: An expansive and provocative work of rich nocturnal beauty, British experimental filmmaker Beatrice Gibson’s feature is a shapeshifting, feminist meditation on the mind and body that follows an array of women over the course of one night in Paris. Winner of Best Emerging Director at the 2026 Locarno Film Festival.

title: Behemoth!
description: An American drama of uncommon intelligence, humor, and grace, the latest from writer-director Tony Gilroy (Michael Clayton) stars Pedro Pascal in a career-best performance as a cellist picking up the pieces of a fractured life.

title: A Day in the Life of Jo
description: Contemporary suburban Athens becomes the site of astronomical, ethereal beauty in Greek filmmaker Jacqueline Lentzou’s audacious film, which glances at the ephemerality of life with humor and poignancy as it charts a consequential day for 15-year-old Jo. Winner of Orizzonti Award for Best Director at the 2026 Venice Film Festival.

title: The Disciple
description: Dutch Moroccan fanboy Tarik Azzougarh spends over a decade working to meet and befriend his heroes, the genre-defining hip-hop group Wu-Tang Clan and its iconic spiritual leader, RZA. After joining their movement, he becomes the architect of one of their most talked-about and controversial albums, “Once Upon a Time in Shaolin,” whose radical concept continues to reverberate throughout the music industry. What unfolds is a twisting coming-of-age tale of boyhood dreams, relentless determination and the downfall of flying too close to the sun.

title: Sense And Sensibility
description: An irresistible new take on Jane Austen’s iconic Sense and Sensibility: a charming, witty, and deeply relatable story of love and sisterhood starring Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles. Sisters Elinor and Marianne Dashwood must leave their Sussex estate following the sudden loss of their wealthy father and are forced to move in with a distant relative. The two sisters attempt to find security and happiness whilst navigating their vastly different approaches to love.

title: Members' Screening: Digger (15) (AD)
description: Academy Award-winning filmmaker Alejandro G Iñárritu ( Birdman ) returns with his original feature starring Tom Cruise as the most powerful man in the world.

title: Digger
description: Academy Award-winning filmmaker Alejandro G. Iñárritu returns with his original film Digger, starring Tom Cruise. The most powerful man in the world (Cruise) embarks on a frantic mission to prove he is humanity’s savior before the disaster he’s unleashed destroys everything. This wildly hilarious satire was shot entirely in VistaVision.

Tues, Oct 6: Extended intro with director Cristian Mungiu and co-star Sebastian Stan at the 8:15 show! title: The Age of Innocence
description: One breathtaking composition follows another in Scorsese’s adaptation of Edith Wharton’s Pulitzer Prize–winning masterpiece about social mores (and taboos) amongst New York’s viperous moneyed classes in late 19th-century New York, brought to life by an all-star lineup of craftspeople including cinematographer Michael Ballhaus, editor Thelma Schoonmaker, production designer Dante Ferretti, and composer Elmer Bernstein. In front of the camera there are Daniel Day-Lewis and Michelle Pfeiffer suffering beautifully as wealthy lawyer Newland Archer and Countess Ellen Olenska, the divorced pariah whom he yearns for, and Winona Ryder as Archer’s fiancée and, eventually, wife—outwardly a winsome innocent, but a cunning, cutthroat strategist where affairs of the heart are concerned. It was, Ryder stated during a recent appearance on (of all things) Hot Ones, “The role of a lifetime.” Part of Winona Ryder Analogue Youth

title: Once Upon a Time in China
description: No one wields a ’Scope frame with quite the same flexibility and dynamism as Hark, and the spectacular, Sergio Leone–inspired Once Upon a Time in China—perhaps the crucial film of the 1990s wuxia revival—shows Hark at his most flamboyant, keeping up with the human whirlwind that is Jet Li, here in the role of physician, martial artist, and 19th-century Cantonese folk hero Wong Fei-hung, who’s pitted against unscrupulous gangsters, human traffickers from the West, and his inconvenient feelings for “13th Aunt” Rosamund Kwan. Showstopping set pieces come fast and furious en route to a shoot-the-works shipboard finale; a monumental work of kinetic cinema. Part of Don't Play with Fire: The Films of Tsui Hark

title: The Loneliest Man in Town
description: Vienna meets the Mississippi Delta in Tizza Covi and Rainer Frimmel’s delightful and poignant portrait of Austria’s preeminent blues musician, Al Cook, who discovers that he must evacuate his beloved apartment, set for demolition.

title: Relaxed Screening: Whisper of the Heart (U)
description: Pure Studio Ghibli magic unfolds as a bookish 14-year-old follows a cat to find the person who has borrowed all the same books as her from the library in this touching coming-of-age story.

title: Heart of the Beast
description: After a harrowing plane crash, Special Forces officer James Belmont (Brad Pitt) and his combat dog, Odin, find themselves stranded deep in the Alaskan wilderness. Together, they are forced into a brutal fight for survival against the elements. From acclaimed filmmaker David Ayer, Heart of the Beast is an intense adventure thriller that explores the unbreakable bond between a man and his best friend as they face their greatest battle yet.

title: Paw Patrol 3: The Dino Movie
description: The Paw Patrol lands on a mysterious dinosaur island after a storm, where they meet Rex, a stranded pup. When Humdinger's reckless mining triggers a volcano, the team faces their biggest rescue mission yet to save the island Sunday 2nd Aug 11am Charity Screening All proceeds from this performance will be donated to MEDICINEMA Cinema-based healthcare programmes inside hospitals

title: MY UNDESIRABLE FRIENDS: PART II – EXILE: Chapters 1-3
description: When Russia shuts down all independent media, a group of young dissident journalists must flee Moscow so they can keep reporting and not go to prison. In her riveting follow-up to last year’s awards-sweeping MY UNDESIRABLE FRIENDS — LAST AIR IN MOSCOW, Julia Loktev follows these courageous, sharply funny women (and a few men) as they fan out across a dozen countries, to Istanbul, Tbilisi, Prague, Vienna, Amsterdam, New York, and beyond. Over the course of four years, they continue to report the truth to Russians from exile, covering their country’s war crimes, even as they face death threats and are declared extremists and terrorists—as they find new meanings of family, friendship, love, and home far from the country to which they may never return. (Viewers can follow EXILE without first seeing LAST AIR IN MOSCOW.)

title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

title: Bad Apples
description: A struggling primary school teacher begins to make some questionable decisions after one of her students is injured.

title: Red Rocks
description: In Bruno Dumont’s drama of danger, purity, and freedom, a group of children between the ages of 5 and 7 enact a kind of pre-preadolescent Romeo and Juliet, complete with rival gangs and puppy love, in a coastal French Riviera town.

title: The Red Shoes
description: In this classic drama, Vicky Page (Moira Shearer) is an aspiring ballerina torn between her dedication to dance and her desire to love. While her imperious instructor, Boris Lermontov (Anton Walbrook), urges to her to forget anything but ballet, Vicky begins to fall for the charming young composer Julian Craster (Marius Goring). Eventually Vicky, under great emotional stress, must choose to pursue either her art or her romance, a decision that carries serious consequences.

title: Coyote vs. Acme
description: A story set in the ACME warehouse, the manufacturer of anything and everything used by the Looney Tunes characters.

title: Brother Bear
description: When an impulsive boy named Kenai is magically transformed into a bear, he must literally walk in another’s footsteps until he learns some valuable life lessons. His courageous and often zany journey introduces him to a forest full of wildlife, including the lovable bear cub Koda, hilarious moose Rutt and Tuke, woolly mammoths and rambunctious rams.

title: The Fox
description: Tickets Are Only Available via BFI London Film Festival Website from Tuesday 17 September 2026 10:00am: Click Here To Book A talking fox, voiced by Olivia Colman, persuades a hunter to transform his cheating wife into an ideal spouse, in this gleefully outrageous, shape-shifting comedy. As revenge for adultery, who wouldn’t take a talking fox’s advice to throw your cheating partner into a magical outback hole with transformative powers? Dario Russo’s sly, irreverent black comedy mercilessly satirises our baser animal instincts, and is played straight by a terrifically committed cast that includes Jai Courtney and Emily Browning, alongside the vocal talents of Colman and the late, great Sam Neill.

title: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma
description: After years of slapdash sequels and waning fandom, the Camp Miasma slasher franchise is handed over to an enthusiastic young director (Hannah Einbinder, Hacks) for resurrection. But when she visits the original movie’s star (Gillian Anderson, The X-Files, Sex Education), a now-reclusive actress shrouded in mystery, the two women fall into a blood-soaked world of desire, fear, and delirium.

title: UNZIPPED
description: “Isaac Mizrahi as he conceived and contorted the way through to his fall 1994 show, [dashing] around a deserted SoHo with pal Sandra Bernhard; [meeting] with Naomi Campbell, Linda Evangelista, and baby Kate Moss for fittings; and [racing] uptown to an audience with Eartha Kitt... Hair-raising deadlines, delirious Bette Davis impressions, and the hostile but exhilarating act of executing a designer’s vision come together in a work that set the bar for all fashion films after.” – Vogue

title: The History of Concrete
description: Fri, Sep 18: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Edy Modica (actress, comedian, filmmaker), after 4:40 show! Fri, Sep 18: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Rachel Kaly (comedian, writer, actor), after 7:15 show! Sun, Sep 20: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Sarah Sherman after 2:10 show! Following the finale of his TV show, filmmaker John Wilson searches for a new creative outlet. After attending a workshop on how to write and sell a Hallmark movie, he attempts to apply the same formula to a documentary about concrete.

title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day
description: A forgotten Peter Parker lives alone as a full-time Spider-Man until mounting pressure triggers a dangerous change and a powerful new enemy emerges.

title: Mezzanine presents: Edvard Munch
description: We are thrilled to present a rare 35mm screening of the theatrical version of Peter Watkins’ masterpiece, one of the greatest films about art and art-making, in tribute to the late filmmaker (1935-2025). Known for its highly original style, Watkins’ biopic of the great Norwegian artist uses the tropes of a documentary film—direct-to-camera interviews, contrapuntal voice-over and vérité zooms—while employing non-professional actors, creating an utterly modern exploration of Munch’s ascension into the art world of the late 19th century.

title: Sky Hopinka Presents ORPHEUS
description: Jean Cocteau’s update of the Orpheus myth depicts a famous poet (Jean Marais), scorned by the Left Bank youth, and his love for both his wife, Eurydice (Marie Déa), and a mysterious princess (Maria Casarès). Seeking inspiration, the poet follows the princess from the world of the living to the land of the dead, through Cocteau’s famous mirrored portal. Orpheus ’s peerless visual poetry and dreamlike storytelling represent the legendary Cocteau at the height of his powers.

title: THE SCOUT
description: Director González-Nasser spent six years working as a location scout. In this luminous directorial debut, she brings us into a day in the life of a young scout tasked with finding the perfect interiors for a television pilot. Sofía (Mimi Davila) moves in and out of other people’s intimate spaces and quotidian lives, tweaking her personality just enough to connect while struggling to find balance between her professional and personal worlds. With a mounting stack of parking tickets and the impertinent commentaries of her crew, she faces a series of small-yet-paralyzing obstacles that render her day increasingly exhausting. Through a constellation of quiet but poignant vignettes, the film offers an original view into the invisible labor of TV production, unfolding as an alternative symphony of a New York grappling with gentrification and a growing erosion of empathy.

title: THE PROMISED LAND
description: The rise of the industrial era and the capitalist boom it engendered are at the core of Wajda’s epic adaptation of the novel by 1924 Nobel Prize winner W. S. Reymont. The film charts the rise and fall of three ambitious tycoons, Karol, a Polish nobleman, Maks, a German hoping to improve on the fate of his father who ran a failing old-time mill, and Moryc, who appears to be disdained except for his valuable connections. Exposing the ways that workers are exploited for the sake of financial growth, the film builds to a powerful climax that connects it to economic conflicts that were simmering in Poland at the time it was made.

title: A Statement
description: In 1980, a group of environmental activists, scientists, and policymakers convened to discuss an alarming government study on climate change. Tom McCarthy (Spotlight) re-creates this historical moment with a brilliant ensemble cast including Paul Rudd, Amy Ryan, Paul Giamatti, John Turturro, and more.

title: Off-Circuit: The Seasons
description: Weaving accounts of rural workers and field notes of a couple of archaeologists, amateur footage and scientific drawings, legends, poems and songs, Maureen Fazendeiro's The Seasons is a journey through the real history and the tales of a region in southern Portugal, Alentejo, and a portrait of the people who have lived there.

title: The Disciple (Open Captioning)
description: Dutch Moroccan fanboy Tarik Azzougarh spends over a decade working to meet and befriend his heroes, the genre-defining hip-hop group Wu-Tang Clan and its iconic spiritual leader, RZA. After joining their movement, he becomes the architect of one of their most talked-about and controversial albums, “Once Upon a Time in Shaolin,” whose radical concept continues to reverberate throughout the music industry. What unfolds is a twisting coming-of-age tale of boyhood dreams, relentless determination and the downfall of flying too close to the sun.

title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother 35mm
description: Latif is a devoutly religious hitman who struggles to balance work, faith, and fatherhood. When his wife dies, he embarks on a desperate journey across Houston in search of breast milk for his infant daughter, all while dodging sex traffickers, an evangelical militia, and his own demons.

title: André Leon Talley: Style is Forever
description: André Leon Talley was a trailblazing fashion icon whose influence spanned nearly five decades. This documentary explores his legacy of inclusivity, elegance, and the fearless pursuit of authenticity. Interviews with Anna Wintour, Tom Ford and Diane von Furstenberg, among others, as well as never-before-seen footage, reveal Talley’s personal and professional challenges and remarkable triumphs.

title: The Social Reckoning
description: A companion piece to the hit film The Social Network, Sorkin’s original screenplay is based on the events that gave rise to the Wall Street Journal’s shocking exposé The Facebook Files. The film is inspired by the true story of how Frances Haugen (Madison), a young Facebook engineer, enlists the help of Jeff Horwitz (White), a Wall Street Journal reporter, to go on a dangerous journey that ends up blowing the whistle on the social network’s most guarded secrets.

title: First They Came for My College
description: When Florida Governor Ron DeSantis stages a coup at New College, the state’s beloved public honors college, students and professors confront a new reality: their campus is ground zero in an unprecedented nationwide assault on academic freedom and diversity.

title: Extra Geography
description: Set in an English boarding school, Extra Geography follows two teenage girls as they grapple with all the challenges of girlhood: friendship, boys, studies, growing up and their summer project, "to fall in love".

title: The Valley of the Bees
description: Our screening on Sunday 11 October will be introduced by writer, lecturer, and Czech cinema expert, Peter Hames. Set in a…

title: Other Mommy
description: Bela, an 8-year-old girl living in a home with marital problems, confronts a sinister entity that comes out of her closet. The presence, whom she calls "Other Mommy," becomes increasingly threatening to her and her family.

title: The Dark Crystal
description: A lavish and stunningly visualized fantasy of mystical adventure and magical imagination! On another world, in another time, a Gelfling embarks on a prophetic quest to restore balance and truth in the universe by finding the missing shard of The Dark Crystal . Jim Henson and Frank Oz use their brilliant puppetry skills to craft a dazzling fairy tale that’s wondrous, poetic, and beautifully haunting – and unlike anything else the big screen has ever seen.

title: Aliens
description: Ellen Ripley, the only survivor of the commercial spaceship Nostromo, is awakened from a half-century of suspended animation only to find herself returning to the last place she ever wanted to go— the planet where she first encountered the alien that slaughtered her crewmates. Writer-director James Cameron’s action-packed continuation of Ridley Scott’s 1979 sci-fi horror classic won Oscars for its sound effects editing and visual effects and received nominations for its film editing, sound, James Horner’s tense score, and Sigourney Weaver’s steely yet vulnerable performance as Ripley. The art direction of production designer Peter Lamont and set decorator Crispian Sallis also garnered a nomination, making a seamless visual connection with the original film while creating a variety of imaginative yet utterly convincing new designs.

title: DANCES WITH WOLVES
description: During the Civil War, a lone lieutenant at a Union outpost (Kevin Costner) in the Dakota territories develops tenuous but satisfying relationships with a cautious wolf and a proud Sioux tribe.

title: TIME AND WATER
description: Renowned Icelandic poet and author Andri Snær Magnason is chasing something elusive. As the glacial ice of his homeland melts, he constructs a time capsule to hold onto this moment and send it to the future, before everything he loves slips away. Using his own collected archives, his grandparents’ photographs and films, as well as traditional songs and folktales, Andri interlaces his family’s story with that of the land around him. From Academy Award-nominated director Sara Dosa, TIME AND WATER is a universal reflection on the power of home and what it means to be alive amid profound epochal change.

title: Black History Month: HYENAS + Intro
description: Dramaan Drameh is a respected, convivial shopkeeper in the tiny village of Colobane. When a forgotten act of cruelty committed thirty years in his past comes back to haunt him, the young girl he impregnated and abandoned returns seeking revenge.  This screening will feature an introduction.  HYENAS ...

title: Qui a tué Ali Ziri? 2015. Directed by Luc Decaster
Shaun the Sheep: The Beast of Mossy Bottom
description: The new adventure sees the residents of Mossy Bottom Farm looking forward to Halloween - until the clumsy Farmer trashes the Flock's beloved pumpkin patch. When Shaun turns mad scientist to fix the problem, things rapidly spiral out of control, leading to a wild beast roaming the woods.

title: Digger (15) (AD)
description: Academy Award-winning filmmaker Alejandro G Iñárritu ( Birdman ) returns with his original feature starring Tom Cruise as the most powerful man in the world.
