title: Sense and Sensibility (U) (AD)
description: An irresistible new take on Jane Austen ’s iconic Sense and Sensibility : a charming, witty and deeply relatable story of love and sisterhood, starring Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles .

title: Heil Jupiter!
description: This dreamlike astonishment from Carlos Reygadas (Silent Light, NYFF45) suggests a world balanced on the edge of the corporeal and the mythic—a work of feral cinematic expression that contrasts elemental pleasure and authoritarian brutality.

title: The Uprising
description: Andrew Garfield stars as the legendary leader of a ferocious rebellion against the tyranny of King Richard II. As war burns across England, he forms an army of the people to face the King’s might in a fight for justice and survival.

title: Antigone
description: Brecht’s adaptation of Sophocles’s Antigone—concerning the title character’s rebellion against the uncle, King Creon, who has condemned her to death—is performed in its entirety in Straub and Huillet’s final film set in the ancient world, which recalls their 1975 Moses und Aron in its antiquarian setting: the ruins of a Greek theatre in Segesta, Sicily. Part of Classical Cinema

title: UNZIPPED
description: “Isaac Mizrahi as he conceived and contorted the way through to his fall 1994 show, [dashing] around a deserted SoHo with pal Sandra Bernhard; [meeting] with Naomi Campbell, Linda Evangelista, and baby Kate Moss for fittings; and [racing] uptown to an audience with Eartha Kitt... Hair-raising deadlines, delirious Bette Davis impressions, and the hostile but exhilarating act of executing a designer’s vision come together in a work that set the bar for all fashion films after.” – Vogue

title: Fjord (Open Captioning)
description: Tue, Oct 6: Sneak preview + Q&A with director Cristian Mungiu and co-star Sebastian Stan after the 6:15 show! Tues, Oct 6: Extended intro with director Cristian Mungiu and co-star Sebastian Stan at the 8:15 show! Please note that there are additional showtimes of FJORD that screen without open captions (on-screen display of dialogue and sounds). For those showtimes, click here. From two-time Palme d’Or winner Cristian Mungiu, a Norwegian woman and her devout Romanian husband relocate with their five children to a remote, close-knit, coastal town. Their teenage children form a fast bond with a neighboring family as unease begins to simmer around their rigid beliefs. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice.

title: Once Upon a Time in China II
description: No one wields a ’Scope frame with quite the same flexibility and dynamism as Hark, and the spectacular, Sergio Leone–inspired Once Upon a Time in China II shows Hark at his most inspired, keeping up with the human whirlwind that is Jet Li, here returning to the role of physician, martial artist, and 19th-century Cantonese folk hero Wong Fei-hung. Traveling to Canton for a medical conference, Wong finds a city in chaos, with the anti-western White Lotus Cult seeking to snuff out foreign influence by any means necessary, and government forces—including officer Donnie Yen—resorting to violent measures against Dr. Sun Yat-sen’s republican revolutionaries. Unrelenting, utterly dazzling, pedal-to-the-metal action cinema. Part of Don't Play with Fire: The Films of Tsui Hark

title: Dao
description: French Senegalese filmmaker Alain Gomis’s (Félicité, NYFF55) ecstatic epic plunges headfirst into two separate yet intrinsically interconnected ceremonies—a memorial in Guinea-Bissau and a wedding in Paris—which Gomis cuts between with kinetic abandon.

title: Digger
description: The most powerful man in the world embarks on a frantic mission to prove he is humanity's saviour before the disaster he’s unleashed destroys everything.

title: WOMEN IN ANIMATION PGM 1: ANIMATED ANIMALS
description: Bessie Mae Kelley FLOWER FAIRIES (1921, 5 min, 35mm-to-DCP, silent. Restored and distributed by Manitou Productions Inc.) Dave Fleischer EDUCATED FISH (1937, 7.5 min, 35mm. Uncredited animator: Lillian Friedman. Preserved by the Academy Film Archive and UCLA Film & Television Archive in cooperation with Paramount Pictures.) Hermína Týrlová & Ladislav Zástěra FERDA THE ANT / FERDA MRAVENEC (1944, 10 min, 16mm-to-DCP. Courtesy of the Czech National Film Archive.) Mary Ellen Bute COLOR RHAPSODIE (1948, 6 min, 35mm. Made with Ted Nemeth. Preserved by Anthology Film Archives, with assistance from Cineric, Inc.) Brian Borthwick & John Halas THE OWL AND THE PUSSYCAT (1952, 6 min, 35mm-to-DCP. Produced by Joy Batchelor & John Halas.) Tex Avery CRAZY MIXED UP PUP (1954, 6 min, 35mm-to-DCP. Animator: Laverne Harding.) Mort & Millie Goldsholl INTERGALACTIC ZOO (1964, 2.5 min, 16mm-to-DCP) Evelyn Lambart THE HOARDER (1969, 7.5 min, 35mm-to-DCP) Sara Petty FURIES (1977, 3 min, 16mm) Sally Cruikshank FROM YOUR HEAD (1996, 2 min, 35mm. Print courtesy of the Academy Film Archive.) Total running time: ca. 65 min. The program will be introduced by Rachael Guma and by writer, scholar, and filmmaker Mindy Johnson!

title: A. Rimbaud
description: The improbable life of French poet Arthur Rimbaud unfolds with all the shock and playfulness of his poetry.

title: Wild Horse Nine
description: Tickets Are Only Available via BFI London Film Festival Website from Tuesday 17 September 2026 10:00am: Click Here To Book Martin McDonagh continues to mine the absurdities and complexities of male relationships in a film that brims with energy and is sure to delight. On the cusp of dictator Augusto Pinochet taking power in Chile, a trio of CIA agents snipe and bicker as they await the ‘go’ date on their part in yet another military coup. However, against the stunning natural beauty and mysterious ancient artefacts of Easter Island, their plan starts to unravel. John Malkovich’s peerless performance chimes beautifully with co-stars Sam Rockwell and Steve Buscemi, who together bring McDonagh’s brilliantly acerbic and witty script hilariously to life. English and Spanish Language with English Subtitles This screening will be presented with Descriptive Subtitles and will have Audio Description available on request. Content Warning: Contains scenes of drug use and graphic violence or injury.

title: THE SOCIAL RECKONING
description: A companion piece to the hit film The Social Network, Sorkin’s original screenplay is based on the events that gave rise to the Wall Street Journal’s shocking exposé The Facebook Files. The film is inspired by the true story of how Frances Haugen (Madison), a young Facebook engineer, enlists the hel...

title: The Social Reckoning (15) (AD)
description: In this companion piece to The Social Network , screenwriter Aaron Sorkin returns to the Metaverse with a tale of the whistleblower who started the social media reckoning we're seeing play out today.

title: The Social Reckoning
description: Explores Facebook's internal practices, spread of false information, impact on teen mental health, and connection to January 6 Capitol events.

title: FILIPIÑANA
description: 17-year-old Isabel navigates the opulent pavilions and lush green landscapes of Dr. Palanca’s luxury golf course as a newly-hired “tee girl.” Meticulously composed, highly stylized, and guided by precisely choreographed movement and deadpan delivery, FILIPIÑANA unfolds through the gradual accumulation of everyday encounters between staff and the wealthy clients of this secluded country club on the outskirts of Manila. When she attempts to return a lost golf club, Isabel uncovers a dark underbelly beneath the club’s pristine surfaces, in this sweltering, pastel-colored fairy tale of class division, institutional patriarchy, and invisible violence.

title: Annie
description: Vidiots remembers the great Tim Curry with a special screening of the musical bonanza Annie for Tim Curry lovers of all ages!

title: Suspiria [1977]
description: Suzy (Jessica Harper) travels to Germany to attend ballet school. When she arrives, late on a stormy night, no one lets her in, and she sees Pat (Eva Axén), another student, fleeing from the school. When Pat reaches her apartment, she is murdered. The next day, Suzy is admitted to her new school, but has a difficult time settling in. She hears noises, and often feels ill. As more people die, Suzy uncovers the terrifying secret history of the place.

title: MYSTERY DOJO: SURPRISE KUNG FU MATINEES
description:
Enter the 36 Chambers of Grindhouse Cinema, with these Sunday mystery martial-arts matinees that harken back to the glory days of 42nd Street.
Expect deep-cut chopsocky plucked from the 70s and 80s screening on both digital and VHS - with bone-crushing bashers from the genre that mixed Chinese folklore and fantasy, spaghetti westerns, melodrama, Japanese samurai films and American genre cinema into an electrifying combo that inspired both the future of action films - and hip hop.
These Kung Fu flicks became an international sensation in the 1970s, particularly at the Grindhouse cinemas that proliferated in impoverished inner-cities. Here were movies in which working-class heroes stood up to oppression, speaking loud and clear to the marginalised underclasses around the world.
Bring the ruckus!

title: The History of Concrete
description: Fri, Sep 18: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Edy Modica (actress, comedian, filmmaker), after 4:40 show! Fri, Sep 18: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Rachel Kaly (comedian, writer, actor), after 7:15 show! Sun, Sep 20: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Sarah Sherman after 2:10 show! Following the finale of his TV show, filmmaker John Wilson searches for a new creative outlet. After attending a workshop on how to write and sell a Hallmark movie, he attempts to apply the same formula to a documentary about concrete.

title: Comédie Française
description: The Comédie-Française is one of France’s most revered arts institutions, and the oldest still-performing theatre company in the world. There is one golden rule: the play is NEVER cancelled.  Unfortunately for theatre producer Nina (Pauline Clément), everything is unravelling just three hours before the premiere of her first production – an ambitious retelling of Shakespeare’s Macbeth. Her lead actor is stuck on a train, tensions are exploding, passions flaring, equipment breaking down and egos are clashing. With panic setting in and the clock ticking Nina must hold things together at all costs. Will the show go on? France’s hit summer comedy and the runaway winner of four awards at the Alpe d’Huez comedy Film Festival, Comédie Française is a delicious behind-the-scenes farce which is unafraid to poke fun at the highbrow reputation of French theatre. Featuring a cast of real-life members of the Comédie-Française company, this is a gleeful, knowing parody and a sheer delight.

title: Girls Like Girls
description: Based on writer/director Hayley Kiyoko's hit single and best-selling novel of the same name and featuring all-new music from Kiyoko, GIRLS LIKE GIRLS is a heartfelt coming-of-age story set over the course of one sun-drenched summer, where new-girl-in-town Coley falls in love for the first time while learning to accept herself along the way.

title: The History of Concrete
description: A filmmaker applies lessons from a Hallmark movie writing workshop to pitch a documentary about concrete.

title: Everytime
description: After a shocking accident befalls a teenage girl in Berlin, her mother, younger sister, and boyfriend drift into a state of suspended grief in Sandra Wollner’s atmospheric, constantly surprising new film, winner of the Cannes Un Certain Regard Prize. Germany’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: Short Films from Sky Hopinka
description: “Kunįkaga Remember Red Banks, Kunįkaga Remembers the Welcoming Song,” 2014, Dir. Sky Hopinka, 9 Mins, USA

title: MY UNDESIRABLE FRIENDS: PART II – EXILE: Chapters 4-5
description: When Russia shuts down all independent media, a group of young dissident journalists must flee Moscow so they can keep reporting and not go to prison. In her riveting follow-up to last year’s awards-sweeping MY UNDESIRABLE FRIENDS — LAST AIR IN MOSCOW, Julia Loktev follows these courageous, sharply funny women (and a few men) as they fan out across a dozen countries, to Istanbul, Tbilisi, Prague, Vienna, Amsterdam, New York, and beyond. Over the course of four years, they continue to report the truth to Russians from exile, covering their country’s war crimes, even as they face death threats and are declared extremists and terrorists—as they find new meanings of family, friendship, love, and home far from the country to which they may never return. (Viewers can follow EXILE without first seeing LAST AIR IN MOSCOW.)

title: PLAYING WITH FIRE: AN ECOSEXUAL EMERGENCY
description: Following their two previous films – GOODBYE GAULEY MOUNTAIN: AN ECOSEXUAL LOVE STORY (2014) and WATER MAKES US WET: AN ECOSEXUAL ADVENTURE (2019) – Annie Sprinkle and Beth Stephens bring us the third chapter in their climate crisis trilogy: PLAYING WITH FIRE: AN ECOSEXUAL EMERGENCY. With the climate crisis worsening with each passing season, the artist/activist duo sound the alarm by enlisting a collective of artists, elders, witches, neighbors, and friends, to examine the ways we can support the health of our dear Earth. Partially narrated by Boulder Creek’s mythical white peacock Albert and culminating in a ceremonial Wedding to Fire in the Redwoods, PLAYING WITH FIRE is a powerful portrait of queer resilience but also a reckoning with the power of fire, with its capacity to heal and its potential to destroy. Co-sponsored by Climate Film Festival and Queer New York International Arts Festival. Annie Sprinkle & Beth Stephens will be here in person for both screenings, and will present a ten-minute performative introduction before each show, “Ecosex 101”! On Saturday, Sprinkle & Stephens will appear for a post-screening discussion and Q&A led by Barbara Carellas, author of “The Book of Ecstasy”, and on Sunday, Angelo Madsen (director of A BODY TO LIVE IN) will lead a Q&A. Viewers are encouraged to dress up in the themes of fire and ecosex. After the Saturday screening, all are welcome to join a reception in the lobby. Beth and Annie will honor two legends of golden age adult entertainment and the co-founders of the first pornstar support group, Club 90. Veronica Vera is turning 80 and Veronica Hart is turning 70. Birthday cake will be served, and signed books and merch will be available for purchase.

title: Sense And Sensibility
description: An irresistible new take on Jane Austen’s iconic Sense and Sensibility: a charming, witty, and deeply relatable story of love and sisterhood starring Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles. Sisters Elinor and Marianne Dashwood must leave their Sussex estate following the sudden loss of their wealthy father and are forced to move in with a distant relative. The two sisters attempt to find security and happiness whilst navigating their vastly different approaches to love.

title: The Lost Children of Tuam
description: In rural Ireland, amateur historian Catherine Corless begins researching a former institution for unmarried mothers and their children, uncovering a shocking hidden history of loss. Based on the true story, and featuring a powerful performance from Monica Dolan, THE LOST CHILDREN OF TUAM is a deeply moving portrait of one woman’s fight for justice.

title: Wing Chun (詠春)
description: Wing Chun (詠春). 1994. Hong Kong. Directed by Yuen Woo-ping. Action direction by Yuen Woo-ping. With Michelle Yeoh, Donnie Yen, Yuen King-tan. DCP courtesy Hong Kong Film Archive, Leisure and Cultural Services Department. In Cantonese; English subtitles. 96 min. Michelle Yeoh stars as Yim Wing-chun, the legendary folk hero credited with creating her namesake martial art, who uses her formidable skills to defend her town from ruthless bandits. Boldly subverting traditional gender norms within kung fu cinema, Yeoh delivers a radiant performance, seamlessly blending masterly authority with endearing comedic vulnerability amid chaotic romantic mix-ups with Donnie Yen. Director Yuen Woo-ping enriches the story through inventive, prop-focused wirework—most memorably during the legendary “Tofu Fight,” in which Yeoh deflects heavy broadsword strikes with graceful footwork while preserving a delicate tray of bean curd. The result is a delightfully entertaining milestone in Hong Kong action cinema.

title: Shaun the Sheep: The Beast of Mossy Bottom
description: The new adventure sees the residents of Mossy Bottom Farm looking forward to Halloween - until the clumsy Farmer trashes the Flock's beloved pumpkin patch. When Shaun turns mad scientist to fix the problem, things rapidly spiral out of control, leading to a wild beast roaming the woods.

title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother 35mm
description: Latif is a devoutly religious hitman who struggles to balance work, faith, and fatherhood. When his wife dies, he embarks on a desperate journey across Houston in search of breast milk for his infant daughter, all while dodging sex traffickers, an evangelical militia, and his own demons.

title: Digger
description: The most powerful man in the world embarks on a frantic mission to prove he is humanity's saviour before the disaster he’s unleashed destroys everything.

title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

title: Bird in Hand
description: Writer/Director Melody C. Roscher in person after the Friday, October 9th screening!

title: UNZIPPED
description: “Isaac Mizrahi as he conceived and contorted the way through to his fall 1994 show, [dashing] around a deserted SoHo with pal Sandra Bernhard; [meeting] with Naomi Campbell, Linda Evangelista, and baby Kate Moss for fittings; and [racing] uptown to an audience with Eartha Kitt... Hair-raising deadlines, delirious Bette Davis impressions, and the hostile but exhilarating act of executing a designer’s vision come together in a work that set the bar for all fashion films after.” – Vogue

title: KORCZAK
description: Janusz Korczak was a renowned doctor, teacher, and author who ran a Jewish orphanage in the Warsaw Ghetto, and ultimately sacrificed his life to stay with them until his deportation to Treblinka. With a bracingly unsentimental script by Agnieszka Holland, and stunning black-and-white cinematography by Robby Müller intercut with actual archival footage, Wajda recreates life in the ghetto in vivid detail. Wajda fought for years to get this film made, claiming “Jewish themes in Polish culture have been virtually banned for twenty years.”

title: Tous les enfants sauf un (All the Children but One)
Once Upon a Time in China III
description: In Jet Li’s third outing as the legendary Wong Fei-hung, master of both inflicting pain and relieving it, Wong and Rosamund Kwan’s “13th Aunt” travel from Foshan to Beijing to meet with his father, there finding preparations underway for a colorful competition to crown a “Lion Dance King” and learning of a plot to assassinate statesman and court favorite Li Hongzhang. With leadership at home slipping into self-involved venality and foreign powers licking their chops at the prospect of dividing China up amongst themselves, Wong will have to hold the line one more time—and as one has come to expect of the series, the results are nothing short of spectacular. Part of Don't Play with Fire: The Films of Tsui Hark

title: Arsenal
description: The film that made Dovzhenko’s international reputation, Arsenal depicts—in thrillingly innovative, lyric cinematic language—a 1918 episode in the Russian Civil War, a worker’s uprising at Kyiv’s Arsenal Factory, and its brutal military suppression, in the midst of fighting between Bolshevik forces and the Central Rada of the Ukrainian People’s Republic, in whose ranks Dovzhenko may have served for a time. One of a quartet of films commissioned by Soviet authorities to celebrate the 10th anniversary of the October Revolution and, of the four, the most ambivalent, showing an understanding, in turns, of both the universalist, workers-of-the-world-unite Bolshevik cause and a Ukrainian nationalism rooted in soul and soil. 35mm print courtesy of the Filmoteka Narodowa, Warsaw Live musical accompaniment by Fima Chupakhin, piano & synths on Sunday, October 11th Part of Oleksandr Dovzhenko: Earth and Empire

title: Sense and Sensibility (U) (AD)
description: An irresistible new take on Jane Austen ’s iconic Sense and Sensibility : a charming, witty and deeply relatable story of love and sisterhood, starring Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles .

title: THE SOCIAL RECKONING
description: A companion piece to the hit film The Social Network, Sorkin’s original screenplay is based on the events that gave rise to the Wall Street Journal’s shocking exposé The Facebook Files. The film is inspired by the true story of how Frances Haugen (Madison), a young Facebook engineer, enlists the hel...

title: The Social Reckoning (15) (AD)
description: In this companion piece to The Social Network , screenwriter Aaron Sorkin returns to the Metaverse with a tale of the whistleblower who started the social media reckoning we're seeing play out today.

title: Onibaba
description: While her son, Kichi, is away at war, a woman and her daughter-in-law survive by killing samurai who stray into their swamp, then selling whatever valuables they find. Both are devastated when they learn that Kichi has died, but his wife soon begins an affair with a neighbor who survived the war, Hachi. The mother disapproves and, when she can’t steal Hachi for herself, tries to scare her daughter-in-law with a mysterious mask from a dead samurai.

title: VACANCES
description: FILMMAKER IN PERSON! A strange and unusual mixture of warts-and-all family portraiture, subtle exposé of class and privilege, and minimalist depiction of a particular setting that’s rendered with an almost miraculously tactile sense of presence, photographer and filmmaker Victoria Hely-Hutchinson’s VACANCES is a deceptively unassuming film. Filmed over the course of a decade at the property in Provence inhabited by Hely-Hutchinson’s outrageously uninhibited grandmother, a bohemian Austro-Hungarian countess and family matriarch, VACANCES grew out of Hely-Hutchinson’s 2016 short film of the same name, and is something of a filmic complement to her autobiographical 2023 book, “I Left My Grandmother’s House”. The documentary delves, with a grace and open-endedness that belies its analytical bite, into both the bigger-than-life personality of “granny” as well as the sometimes strained dynamics among the rest of the family, including Hely-Hutchinson’s grandfather, mother, and siblings. Unique in suggesting by turns cinema vérité, reality TV, chamber theater, and the minimalism of landscape cinema, VACANCES is a profoundly singular work – a film whose technique is nearly invisible, but which sneaks up on you with its trenchant perceptions, layered meanings, and emotional and filmic complexity. “This time-lapse film, shot over a period of ten years, follows members of several generations of a wealthy aristocratic family with Austro-Hungarian roots. The entire film is set in a Provençal villa, whose social heart is the swimming pool, around which the women gather to exchange various observations and, surreptitiously, gossip. The center of the family is the aging matriarch, who likes to talk about her extravagant, promiscuous life, but at the same time commands all the attention and authority of those around her. However, her influence gradually weakens with each passing generation.” –JI.HLAVA INTERNATIONAL DOCUMENTARY FILM FESTIVAL

title: Digger
description: Academy Award-winning filmmaker Alejandro G. Iñárritu returns with his original film Digger, starring Tom Cruise. The most powerful man in the world (Cruise) embarks on a frantic mission to prove he is humanity’s savior before the disaster he’s unleashed destroys everything. This wildly hilarious satire was shot entirely in VistaVision.

title: EXTRA GEOGRAPHY
description: Set in an English boarding school, EXTRA GEOGRAPHY follows two teenage girls as they grapple with all the challenges of girlhood: friendship, boys, studies, growing up and their summer project, "to fall in love".  “Extra Geography joins the ranks of instant greats like “Lady Bird,” “Booksmart” and “...

title: The Uprising
description: Andrew Garfield stars as the legendary leader of a ferocious rebellion against the tyranny of King Richard II. As war burns across England, he forms an army of the people to face the King’s might in a fight for justice and survival.

title: Haruki Murakami in Conversation + Tony Takitani (U)
description: We are honoured to welcome the celebrated Japanese author on stage to read aloud from his book The City and Its Uncertain Walls (2023) and discuss his work with interviewer Simon McBurney.

title: The Liberation
description: Tickets Are Only Available via BFI London Film Festival Website from Tuesday 17 September 2026 10:00am: Click Here To Book In Guy Nattiv’s tense, probing film, two young women attempt to extract their mother from a cult, but find themselves susceptible to its mysterious leader. Carrie Coon has never been better than she is as Rita, who lives an ‘ordinary’ life as a bank teller, wife and mother. But beneath the veneer of this seemingly ordinary life, she hides the deep trauma of being a holocaust survivor. When she falls into the orbit of the seductive Ricki (a compelling Lily James), Rita finds the space to heal. But at what cost to her family?

title: Digger
description: The most powerful man in the world embarks on a frantic mission to prove he is humanity's saviour before the disaster he’s unleashed destroys everything.

title: THE SCOUT
description: Director González-Nasser spent six years working as a location scout. In this luminous directorial debut, she brings us into a day in the life of a young scout tasked with finding the perfect interiors for a television pilot. Sofía (Mimi Davila) moves in and out of other people’s intimate spaces and quotidian lives, tweaking her personality just enough to connect while struggling to find balance between her professional and personal worlds. With a mounting stack of parking tickets and the impertinent commentaries of her crew, she faces a series of small-yet-paralyzing obstacles that render her day increasingly exhausting. Through a constellation of quiet but poignant vignettes, the film offers an original view into the invisible labor of TV production, unfolding as an alternative symphony of a New York grappling with gentrification and a growing erosion of empathy.

title: Black Swan
description: Nina, a ballerina, gets the chance to play the White Swan, Princess Odette. But she finds herself slipping into madness when Thomas, the artistic director, decides that Lily might fit the role better.

title: ALLIGATOR
description:
Flushed into the sewers as a baby, Ramón survives by feeding on laboratory animals pumped full of experimental growth hormones. Twelve years later he is enormous, ravenous and heading for the surface, leaving weary detective David Madison and a reptile expert to confront the city’s least plausible urban legend.
Lewis Teague and screenwriter John Sayles deliver the rare
Jaws
imitation with teeth: a grubby, funny and surprisingly sharp monster movie, powered by Robert Forster’s deadpan charm and a magnificent thirty-six-foot rubber alligator.

title: Sense and Sensibility
description: Left destitute by ruthless family members, two sisters navigate scandal, heartbreak, and strict social etiquette while searching for their perfect romantic matches.

title: Fjord
description: Tue, Oct 6: Sneak preview + Q&A with director Cristian Mungiu and co-star Sebastian Stan after the 6:15 show! Tues, Oct 6: Extended intro with director Cristian Mungiu and co-star Sebastian Stan at the 8:15 show! From two-time Palme d’Or winner Cristian Mungiu, a Norwegian woman and her devout Romanian husband relocate with their five children to a remote, close-knit, coastal town. Their teenage children form a fast bond with a neighboring family as unease begins to simmer around their rigid beliefs. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice.

title: The Disciple
description: Dutch Moroccan fanboy Tarik Azzougarh spends over a decade working to meet and befriend his heroes, the genre-defining hip-hop group Wu-Tang Clan and its iconic spiritual leader, RZA. After joining their movement, he becomes the architect of one of their most talked-about and controversial albums, “Once Upon a Time in Shaolin,” whose radical concept continues to reverberate throughout the music industry. What unfolds is a twisting coming-of-age tale of boyhood dreams, relentless determination and the downfall of flying too close to the sun.

title: Verity
description: Struggling writer Lowen Ashleigh is hired as a ghostwriter for renowned author Verity Crawford under mysterious circumstances, but her assignment takes a dark turn after discovering chilling autobiographical notes. Faced with a series of deadly family secrets, Lowen struggles to separate fiction from reality, while also blurring the lines with Verity’s husband, Jeremy.

title: VIKA KIRCHENBAUER PGM 1
description: We enter this program with a salacious direct address-cum-invitation in PLEASE RELAX NOW, as Kirchenbauer seduces the viewer from a black box void, stretching the edges of imagination. In LIKE RATS LEAVING A SINKING SHIP, Kirchenbauer layers psychiatric assessments to consider the coherency of a biography, and assess the ways in which individual memory is puppeted by state apparatuses. Both SHE WHOSE BLOOD IS CLOTTING IN MY UNDERWEAR and MOOD MANAGEMENT again push the viewer’s capacity to render a coherent picture of actions, generating a half-constructed image which lends itself only then to a projection. Both works are guided by Kirchenbauer’s music project, COOL FOR YOU. Through essay and material vignettes, UNTITLED SEQUENCE OF GAPS explores light outside of the visible spectrum to consider violence as it attaches to different kinds of visibility and invisibility. To tickle is a form of touch, an intimate act carried out to delight, to excite, or to torment. In THE ISLAND OF PERPETUAL TICKLING (III), Kirchenbauer surrenders to this metaphoric and literal tickle. Noting that it is impossible to tickle oneself, her task requires assistance. PLEASE RELAX NOW (2014, 12 min, DCP) LIKE RATS LEAVING A SINKING SHIP (2012, 24.5 min, DCP) SHE WHOSE BLOOD IS CLOTTING IN MY UNDERWEAR (2016, 3.5 min, DCP) MOOD MANAGEMENT 2017, 2 min, DCPUNTITLED SEQUENCE OF GAPS (2020, 12.5 min, DCP) THE ISLAND OF PERPETUAL TICKLING (III) (2018, 13 min, DCP) Total running time: ca. 75 min. Filmmaker Vika Kirchenbauer in person for both screenings!

title: Sixteen Moments of My Life
description: Ingrid Caven, best known as Rainer Werner Fassbinder’s longtime theater and screen collaborator, looms large in every shot of this mesmerizing concert film by Albert Serra (Afternoons of Solitude, NYFF62), shot in Paris in 2025.

title: The Music Lovers
description: Composer, conductor and teacher Peter Ilych Tchaikovsky struggles against his homosexual tendencies by marrying, but unfortunately, he chooses wacky nymphomaniac Nina, whom he is unable to satisfy.

title: UNZIPPED
description: “Isaac Mizrahi as he conceived and contorted the way through to his fall 1994 show, [dashing] around a deserted SoHo with pal Sandra Bernhard; [meeting] with Naomi Campbell, Linda Evangelista, and baby Kate Moss for fittings; and [racing] uptown to an audience with Eartha Kitt... Hair-raising deadlines, delirious Bette Davis impressions, and the hostile but exhilarating act of executing a designer’s vision come together in a work that set the bar for all fashion films after.” – Vogue

title: The Social Reckoning
description: Explores Facebook's internal practices, spread of false information, impact on teen mental health, and connection to January 6 Capitol events.

title: Artificial
description: Anchored by brilliant lead performances by Andrew Garfield and Yura Borisov, Luca Guadagnino’s thrilling, funny, and very human drama propels audiences through the two decades of machine learning research that have brought us to our current AI crisis point.

title: Goodbye South, Goodbye
description: One of Hou Hsiao-hsien’s unassailable 1990s masterpieces and a staggering, mesmerizing generational portrait, Goodbye South, Goodbye follows the plots and schemes of a small group of young men and women in the age of get-rich-quick late-capitalism.

title: Cotton Queen
description: In a cotton-farming village in Sudan, teenage Nafisa is raised on heroic tales of battling British colonisers told by her grandmother, the village matriarch Al-Sit. But when a young businessman arrives from abroad with a new development plan and genetically engineered cotton, Nafisa becomes the centre of a power play to determine the future of the village. Awakening to her own strength, Nafisa sets out to save the cotton fields – and herself. Neither she nor her community will ever be the same again.

title: The Lost Children of Tuam
description: In rural Ireland, amateur historian Catherine Corless begins researching a former institution for unmarried mothers and their children, uncovering a shocking hidden history of loss. Based on the true story, and featuring a powerful performance from Monica Dolan, THE LOST CHILDREN OF TUAM is a deeply moving portrait of one woman’s fight for justice.

title: The History of Concrete
description: Fri, Sep 18: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Edy Modica (actress, comedian, filmmaker), after 4:40 show! Fri, Sep 18: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Rachel Kaly (comedian, writer, actor), after 7:15 show! Sun, Sep 20: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Sarah Sherman after 2:10 show! Following the finale of his TV show, filmmaker John Wilson searches for a new creative outlet. After attending a workshop on how to write and sell a Hallmark movie, he attempts to apply the same formula to a documentary about concrete.

title: Other Mommy
description: Bela, an 8-year-old girl living in a home with marital problems, confronts a sinister entity that comes out of her closet. The presence, whom she calls "Other Mommy," becomes increasingly threatening to her and her family.

title: American Psycho
description: I have to return some videotapes … Patrick Bateman is your average 1980s Wall Street executive, from his expensive designer suits, to his dinner reservations, to his business card, to his well-educated beautiful fiance, all up to the penchant for mergers and acquisitions, or is it murders and executions? Adapted from Bret Easton Ellis’ notorious novel, American Psycho continues to make you laugh and shriek in equal measures as it steers you through the disquieting mind as it unravels into madness. So turn up the Huey Lewis, don your Armani dinner jacket, and get ready to have a psycho good time!

title: SID AND NANCY / REPO MAN
description: A harrowing look at the bizarre, self-destructive and curiously compelling relationship between Sid Vicious of the Sex Pistols and Nancy Spungen, an American groupie. Docu-realism laced with allegorical dream images.

title: BLUE HERON
description: In the late 1990s, eight-year-old Sasha and her family relocate to a new home on Vancouver Island, but their fresh start is interrupted by increasingly dangerous behavior from the eldest son, Jeremy. At wit’s end, their parents are presented with a shattering choice. Award-winning director Sophy Romvari’s feature debut is a lyrical and profound testament to the things we carry with us, masterfully chronicling the haze of a languid summer and the hyaline clarity of the moments that defined it.

title: GLORIA
description: Kid averse ex-moll Gena Rowlands gets stuck with an 8-year-old when her neighbor, mob accountant/FBI informant Buck Henry, gets noisily rubbed out. Then it’s a road movie for the smart-mouthed twerp and smartly suited, heat-packing Rowlands (Best Actress Oscar® nomination).

title: Shchors
description: A biopic of the “Red Commander of the Ukraine,” Bolshevik commander Mykola Shchors, starring Yevgeny Samoylov in the title role, Shchors was personally commissioned by Joseph Stalin himself, and its production was a fraught one for Dovzhenko, whose health suffered grievously from the make-or-break pressure he faced to toe the line. The eventual results pleased the General Secretary—Dovzhenko would be awarded his first of two Stalin Prizes in 1941—though the film endures less for its vigorous, saber-rattling hagiography than the moments of ineffable poetry with which it’s embroidered, rooted as always in a deep sense of Ukrainian cultural tradition and relish in the natural world. “As in all [Dovzhenko’s] best work, Shchors leaves in the memory burning images of death and of passionate life” —Jay Leyda 35mm print courtesy of the Filmoteka Narodowa, Warsaw Part of Oleksandr Dovzhenko: Earth and Empire

title: MY UNDESIRABLE FRIENDS: PART II – EXILE: Chapters 4-5
description: When Russia shuts down all independent media, a group of young dissident journalists must flee Moscow so they can keep reporting and not go to prison. In her riveting follow-up to last year’s awards-sweeping MY UNDESIRABLE FRIENDS — LAST AIR IN MOSCOW, Julia Loktev follows these courageous, sharply funny women (and a few men) as they fan out across a dozen countries, to Istanbul, Tbilisi, Prague, Vienna, Amsterdam, New York, and beyond. Over the course of four years, they continue to report the truth to Russians from exile, covering their country’s war crimes, even as they face death threats and are declared extremists and terrorists—as they find new meanings of family, friendship, love, and home far from the country to which they may never return. (Viewers can follow EXILE without first seeing LAST AIR IN MOSCOW.)

title: A Bittersweet Life
description: A mob enforcer (Lee Byung-hun, No Other Choice) with a sterling record of loyal service finds himself fighting for his life after sparing the life of his boss’s straying mistress (Shin Min-a) in Kim’s drum-tight neo-noir thriller, unusually grounded by both emotional stakes and a sense of real physical danger in the action set pieces, choreographed for the widescreen with much panache. Jang’s second collaboration with Kim, after The Foul King, earned him and collaborator (and Peach Present collective bandmate) Dalparan Best Music honors from the Busan Film Critics Association, responding to the composers’ sophisticated melange of samba, flamenco, solo cello, and electronic elements. Part of Composed by Jang Young Gyu

title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother 35mm
description: Latif is a devoutly religious hitman who struggles to balance work, faith, and fatherhood. When his wife dies, he embarks on a desperate journey across Houston in search of breast milk for his infant daughter, all while dodging sex traffickers, an evangelical militia, and his own demons.

title: Prince of Darkness
description: Quantum physics Professor Howard Birack (Victor Wong) tasks his students with their most unusual assignment yet when a Catholic priest (Donald Pleasence) uncovers a strange and ancient substance in a monastery. As the young scientists investigate, dark entities descend upon the church, bringing representatives of Satan to the Earthly plane. John Carpenter wrote, directed, and co-scored Prince of Darkness as the second chapter in his Apocalypse Trilogy, which begins with The Thing (1982), and finishes with In the Mouth of Madness (1995).
director: John Carpenter PRODUCED BY: Larry J. Franco

title: LEGEND
description: LEGEND, from director Ridley Scott, is a visually stunning fantasy-adventure in which pure good and evil battle to the death amidst spectacular surroundings. Set in a timeless mythical forest inhabited by fairies, goblins, unicorns and mortals, this fantastic story stars Tom Cruise as a mystical forest dweller, chosen by fate, to undertake a heroic quest. He must save the beautiful Princess Lily (Mia Sara) and defeat the demonic Lord of Darkness (Tim Curry), or the world will be plunged into a never-ending ice age.

title: HOPE
description: In the remote South Korean village of Hope Harbor, police chief Bum-seok (Hwang Jung- min) and officer Sung-ae (Hoyeon) are called to find a mysterious creature that has wreaked havoc on the village. In the nearby forest, a coterie of hunters, including Sung- ki (Zo In-Sung) set out to track the bea...

title: The Social Reckoning
description: A companion piece to the hit film The Social Network, Sorkin’s original screenplay is based on the events that gave rise to the Wall Street Journal’s shocking exposé The Facebook Files. The film is inspired by the true story of how Frances Haugen (Madison), a young Facebook engineer, enlists the help of Jeff Horwitz (White), a Wall Street Journal reporter, to go on a dangerous journey that ends up blowing the whistle on the social network’s most guarded secrets.

title: Digger (15) (AD)
description: Academy Award-winning filmmaker Alejandro G Iñárritu ( Birdman ) returns with his original feature starring Tom Cruise as the most powerful man in the world.

title: 28 Days Later
description: Twenty-eight days after a killer virus was accidentally unleashed from a British research facility, a small group of London survivors are caught in a desperate struggle to protect themselves from the infected. Carried by animals and humans, the virus turns those it infects into homicidal maniacs — and it’s absolutely impossible to contain.

title: EXTRA GEOGRAPHY
description: Set in an English boarding school, EXTRA GEOGRAPHY follows two teenage girls as they grapple with all the challenges of girlhood: friendship, boys, studies, growing up and their summer project, "to fall in love".  “Extra Geography joins the ranks of instant greats like “Lady Bird,” “Booksmart” and “...

title: FILIPIÑANA
description: 17-year-old Isabel navigates the opulent pavilions and lush green landscapes of Dr. Palanca’s luxury golf course as a newly-hired “tee girl.” Meticulously composed, highly stylized, and guided by precisely choreographed movement and deadpan delivery, FILIPIÑANA unfolds through the gradual accumulation of everyday encounters between staff and the wealthy clients of this secluded country club on the outskirts of Manila. When she attempts to return a lost golf club, Isabel uncovers a dark underbelly beneath the club’s pristine surfaces, in this sweltering, pastel-colored fairy tale of class division, institutional patriarchy, and invisible violence.

title: Ha-Chan, Shake Your Booty!
description: Tickets Are Only Available via BFI London Film Festival Website from Tuesday 17 September 2026 10:00am: Click Here To Book Recently widowed Haru rediscovers her love for ballroom dancing, only to find herself attracted to her new instructor, in this zany, toe-tapping film. Haru (an excellent Rinko Kikuchi) loves ballroom dancing. But after tragedy strikes, she retreats into isolation. Her concerned friends convince her to return to the studio, where she soon becomes infatuated with a new instructor. With Haru throwing caution to the wind, director Josef Kubota Wladyka delivers an exploration of grief that is bold, surprisingly playful and crowd-pleasing. English and Japanese Language with some English subtitles

title: VIKA KIRCHENBAUER PGM 2
description: In the second program of our 2-part retrospective devoted to Vika Kirchenbauer, we dive deeper into the politics of labor in contemporary art, as the artist offers us a WELCOME ADDRESS, directly calling into question the art economy’s coded-progressive positioning of difference and diversity as symbolic cultural currency. Considering the foul, late-stage capitalist “Experience Economy,” YOU ARE BORING troubles the nature of looking. THE CAPACITY FOR ADEQUATE ANGER positions still images from the artist’s presumable childhood archive, gaps of nothingness, and the essay form to offer a critique of the production of contemporary art in the face of upward mobility, mapping subjectivity and political agency. To close this program with a thorough and considered look at the complicit role of artists and art institutions, COMPASSION AND INCONVENIENCE takes us back to 18th century London to trace the first public exhibitions of contemporary art, when materiality intersects with ideology via Liberalism and Enlightenment, taking to task the economic and colonial interests that define/d the “pursuit of refinement.” WELCOME ADDRESS (2017, 9 min, DCP) YOU ARE BORING! (2015, 14 min, DCP) THE CAPACITY FOR ADEQUATE ANGER (2021, 15 min, DCP) COMPASSION AND INCONVENIENCE (2024, 30 min, DCP) Total running time: ca. 75 min. Filmmaker Vika Kirchenbauer in person for both screenings!

title: The History of Concrete
description: A filmmaker applies lessons from a Hallmark movie writing workshop to pitch a documentary about concrete.

title: Extra Geography
description: Set in an English boarding school, Extra Geography follows two teenage girls as they grapple with all the challenges of girlhood: friendship, boys, studies, growing up and their summer project, "to fall in love".

title: WALKING THE EDGE
description:
After her husband and young son are murdered during a brutal home invasion, Christine Holloway sets out to find the men responsible. Her search brings her to Jason Walk, a weary Los Angeles cab driver and small-time numbers runner who reluctantly agrees to help. Together they move through the city’s nocturnal underworld, drawing ever closer to sadistic gang leader Brusstar and his crew.
Directed by Norbert Meisel, WALKING THE EDGE is a lean, hard-edged revenge thriller built around the unlikely pairing of Robert Forster and Nancy Kwan, with cult favourite Joe Spinell at his most menacing. Shot on the streets of Los Angeles, the film combines urban grit, melancholy and sudden violence, gradually turning its damaged central characters into a formidable vigilante partnership.

title: The Social Reckoning (15) (AD)
description: In this companion piece to The Social Network , screenwriter Aaron Sorkin returns to the Metaverse with a tale of the whistleblower who started the social media reckoning we're seeing play out today.

title: One More Time
description: New York avant-garde legend André Gregory, now in his nineties, teams up with actors Larry Pine and Gerry Bamman to film a reading of Samuel Beckett’s Endgame in this enormously moving document of an inextinguishable creative spark, executive produced by Martin Scorsese.

title: Nadja
description: In 1993, invited by David Lynch to come up with a low-budget genre movie, Michael Almereyda ( Tesla , Experimenter , Hamlet ) came up with a moody, postmodern reimagining of the Dracula myth which draws inspiration from Dracula’s Daughter (1936) and André Breton’s surrealist novel Nadja . The film follows estranged vampire twins Nadja (Elina Löwensohn) and Edgar (a young Jared Harris) as they reunite following their father’s death by the flamboyantly unhinged Dr. Van Helsing, played with relish by Peter Fonda. The film’s striking visuals combine high-contrast black-and-white 35mm cinematography with the hallucinatory grain of Pixelvision video is now newly restored in 4K.

title: The Uprising
description: Andrew Garfield stars as the legendary leader of a ferocious rebellion against the tyranny of King Richard II. As war burns across England, he forms an army of the people to face the King’s might in a fight for justice and survival.

title: The History of Concrete

John Wilson, moderated by Rachel Kaly (comedian, writer, actor), after 7:15 show! Sun, Sep 20: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Sarah Sherman after 2:10 show! title: Digger
description: The most powerful man in the world embarks on a frantic mission to prove he is humanity's saviour before the disaster he’s unleashed destroys everything.

title: Perfect Blue
description: A young Japanese singer is encouraged by her agent to quit singing and pursue an acting career, beginning with a role in a murder mystery TV show. Our 11th October performance of Perfect Blue will be preceded by the European Premiere of brand-new short film, IDOLS. Idols | South Korea, Japan, UK | 20 min. Dir. by Matt Halsall Kim Min-ha (Hojo Shin) has always dreamed of the spotlight. Now, nearing 30, she’s still chasing a K-pop debut while everyone else sees only her uncanny resemblance to superstar Park Hye-mi (Hojo Shin)—the woman she believes is living the life that should have been hers. Matt Halsall’s slick, darkly funny short turns that obsession into an increasingly unhinged psychological thriller. IDOLS made its world premiere at Fantasia before being selected for Sitges, Beyond Fest and Tokyo’s Yami International Film Festival.

title: The Lost Children of Tuam
description: In rural Ireland, amateur historian Catherine Corless begins researching a former institution for unmarried mothers and their children, uncovering a shocking hidden history of loss. Based on the true story, and featuring a powerful performance from Monica Dolan, THE LOST CHILDREN OF TUAM is a deeply moving portrait of one woman’s fight for justice.

title: Verity
description: Struggling writer Lowen Ashleigh is hired as a ghostwriter for renowned author Verity Crawford under mysterious circumstances, but her assignment takes a dark turn after discovering chilling autobiographical notes. Faced with a series of deadly family secrets, Lowen struggles to separate fiction from reality, while also blurring the lines with Verity’s husband, Jeremy.

title: The Lair of the White Worm
description: When an archaeologist uncovers a strange skull in a foreign land, the residents of a nearby town begin to disappear, leading to further inexplicable occurrences.

title: The Social Reckoning
description: Explores Facebook's internal practices, spread of false information, impact on teen mental health, and connection to January 6 Capitol events.

title: Resident Evil
description: In this sci-fi horror action reboot, a hapless medical courier fights for his life amid an outbreak of a deadly mutagenic virus in an isolated mountain town.

title: 14th
description: Ava DuVernay follows her epochal 2016 documentary 13th with a thrillingly expansive sequel of sorts, which passionately and persuasively details how the tenets of the 14th Amendment, ratified post–Civil War, are now under systematic attack.

title: Making Marie Antoinette
description: Sofia Coppola’s dynamic craftsmanship in creating her personal vision for 2006’s Marie Antoinette (NYFF44) is on full display in this video diary shot by her mother, Eleanor Coppola, on the film’s set in Versailles in 2005. Preceded by Kleber Mendonça Filho’s South of Tehran.

title: Fjord
description: Tue, Oct 6: Sneak preview + Q&A with director Cristian Mungiu and co-star Sebastian Stan after the 6:15 show! Tues, Oct 6: Extended intro with director Cristian Mungiu and co-star Sebastian Stan at the 8:15 show! From two-time Palme d’Or winner Cristian Mungiu, a Norwegian woman and her devout Romanian husband relocate with their five children to a remote, close-knit, coastal town. Their teenage children form a fast bond with a neighboring family as unease begins to simmer around their rigid beliefs. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice.

title: TAKE ME HOME
description: The American Cinematheque is thrilled to announce a limited engagement of TAKE ME HOME, Liz Sargent’s feature length version of the 2024 PROOF Film Festival Grand Jury Prize winner. From an award-winning short film to a world premiere at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival with the feature is an inspirational journey, and we wish the team the best as they bring this moving film around the world.

title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

title: The Foul King
description: Already a well-established presence in South Korean music, with an ability to work with equal facility in a variety of idioms (experimental, rock, folk, et. al.), Jang got his start in film composing the distinctive score for Kim’s eccentric, unpredictable, and entirely endearing underdog sports comedy, a barbed commentary on suffocating white-collar culture starring Song Kang-ho (Parasite) as mild-mannered bank clerk Dae-ho, mercilessly pushed around in the office and generally ground down by life… until he gains a new measure of self-worth by beginning to moonlight as a masked “heel” wrestler, his signature move: finding ingenious new ways to cheat in the ring. Part of Composed by Jang Young Gyu

title: The Terminator
description: Too many sequels and an incalculable cultural impact later, it’s sometimes forgotten what a hot and nasty little movie Cameron’s original Terminator was, dropping peak-physique Schwarzenegger into a sleazy Los Angeles of leather bars, punk rockers, and skid rows, where he quickly proceeds to killing cops by the score and tracking down mother-to-be of humankind’s savior Linda Hamilton. Working for the very last time with budget constraints, Cameron—and FX gurus Stan Winston and Gene Warren Jr.—deliver the goods and how, in a grimy lil’ chef d’oeuvre that gave us Cyberdine, Skynet, and a whole lexicon for discussing extinction-level singularity events. Part of A Cyberpunk Canon

title: A Nightmare on Elm Street 3: Dream Warriors             / The Blob (1988)
description: Sleep can’t protect the youth of Westin Hills Psychiatric Hospital when a knife-gloved night slasher invades terrified teen dreams and turns their nightmares into deadly reality. But their new therapist has her own tortured history with the dream demon and together they may be able to finally rid the world of Freddy in what may be the ultimate Elm Street sequel.

title: Possible Love
description: The lives of two married couples from different social strata collide in Lee Chang-dong’s brilliantly unfolding narrative about economic precarity, in which a laid-off factory worker and his wife become the camera subjects for a documentary filmmaker. Winner of the Silver Lion at the 2026 Venice Film Festival and South Korea’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: The Disciple
description: Dutch Moroccan fanboy Tarik Azzougarh spends over a decade working to meet and befriend his heroes, the genre-defining hip-hop group Wu-Tang Clan and its iconic spiritual leader, RZA. After joining their movement, he becomes the architect of one of their most talked-about and controversial albums, “Once Upon a Time in Shaolin,” whose radical concept continues to reverberate throughout the music industry. What unfolds is a twisting coming-of-age tale of boyhood dreams, relentless determination and the downfall of flying too close to the sun.

title: Sense And Sensibility
description: An irresistible new take on Jane Austen’s iconic Sense and Sensibility: a charming, witty, and deeply relatable story of love and sisterhood starring Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles. Sisters Elinor and Marianne Dashwood must leave their Sussex estate following the sudden loss of their wealthy father and are forced to move in with a distant relative. The two sisters attempt to find security and happiness whilst navigating their vastly different approaches to love.

title: 2026 Spotlight Shorts
description: This shorts program includes the world premiere of Kleber Mendonça Filho’s South of Tehran, Kamal Aljafari’s Masao Adachi Takes a Passport Photo, the world premiere of Camilo Restrepo’s A Stolen Movie, Jia Zhangke’s Torino Shadow, and the world premiere of Morgan Fisher’s Screening Room. Note: Screening Room will be included only at screenings in the Walter Reade Theater.
director: Kleber Mendonça Filho, Kamal Aljafari, Camilo Restrepo, Jia Zhangke, Morgan Fisher

title: Comédie Française
description: The Comédie-Française is one of France’s most revered arts institutions, and the oldest still-performing theatre company in the world. There is one golden rule: the play is NEVER cancelled.  Unfortunately for theatre producer Nina (Pauline Clément), everything is unravelling just three hours before the premiere of her first production – an ambitious retelling of Shakespeare’s Macbeth. Her lead actor is stuck on a train, tensions are exploding, passions flaring, equipment breaking down and egos are clashing. With panic setting in and the clock ticking Nina must hold things together at all costs. Will the show go on? France’s hit summer comedy and the runaway winner of four awards at the Alpe d’Huez comedy Film Festival, Comédie Française is a delicious behind-the-scenes farce which is unafraid to poke fun at the highbrow reputation of French theatre. Featuring a cast of real-life members of the Comédie-Française company, this is a gleeful, knowing parody and a sheer delight.

title: Joy of Joys
description: This exuberant yet sobering documentary from Jonathan Glazer (The Zone of Interest)—with the help of London schoolkids equipped with cameras—goes behind the scenes at Abbey Road to capture the recording of a charity album from War Child Records, which aids children in conflict zones. The screening on Sept. 30 will be followed by an extended Q&A with Glazer.

title: Mulholland Dr.
description: A dark-haired woman (Laura Elena Harring) is left amnesiac after a car crash. She wanders the streets of Los Angeles in a daze before taking refuge in an apartment. There she is discovered by Betty (Naomi Watts), a wholesome Midwestern blonde who has come to the City of Angels seeking fame as an actress. Together, the two attempt to solve the mystery of Rita's true identity. The story is set in a dream-like Los Angeles, spoilt neither by traffic jams nor smog.

title: The Little Mermaid
description: This sprightly interpretation of Hans Christian Anderson’s story was eyed by Disney as far back as the days of Snow White and the Seven Dwarves, finally surfacing in 1989. There’s a hot crustacean band, sure, but also a keening grasp of the angst, loneliness, and longing in Anderson’s tale, encapsulated in Ariel’s dream of being “Part of Your World,” a highlight of Alan Mencken and Howard Ashman's superlative songbook. Part of It Started With A Mouse: Hand-Drawn Classics on 35

title: Everybody Digs Bill Evans
description: Winner of the Silver Bear for Best Director at the 2026 Berlin Film Festival, Everybody Digs Bill Evans is a biographical drama film about the famous jazz pianist and composer Bill Evans. In 1961, Bill Evans is playing with what he considers the perfect musical trio until tragedy strikes in the premature death of his bass player, Scott LaFaro – his musical soulmate. Traumatised by grief, Evans stops playing for the first time since his childhood. A tug-of-war between personal torment and the seemingly safer haven of familial love will see Evans oscillate between New York and suburbia, his genius always bubbling beneath the surface. The screening on Friday 11th September will be followed by a Q&A with director Grant Gee and actor Valene Kane

title: Goodbye, Dragon Inn
description: The Fu-Ho Grand, a movie palace in Taipei, is closing its doors. Its valedictory screening: King Hu’s 1967 wuxia epic Dragon Inn, playing to a motley smattering of spectators, including two stars of Hu’s original opus, Miao Tien and Shih Chun, watching their younger selves with tears in their eyes.

title: Possession
description: After Anna (Isabelle Adjani) reveals to her husband, Mark (Sam Neill), that she is having an affair, she leaves him and their son. Mark is devastated, and seeks out Heinrich (Heinz Bennent), the man who cuckolded him, only to receive a beating. After a series of violent confrontations between Mark and Anna, Mark hires a private investigator to follow her. Anna descends into madness, and it's soon clear that she is hiding a much bigger secret -- one that is both inexplicable and shocking.

title: Parent and Baby: The Social Reckoning
description:
Join us for an exclusive screening to come along to with your baby (Under 2), with lower volume, subtitles and slightly raised lighting for a more relaxed feel so your little ones can be as loud as they want!

A companion piece to the hit film The Social Network, Sorkin’s original screenplay is based on the events that gave rise to the Wall Street Journal’s shocking exposé The Facebook Files. The film is inspired by the true story of how Frances Haugen (Madison), a young Facebook engineer, enlists the help of Jeff Horwitz (White), a Wall Street Journal reporter, to go on a dangerous journey that ends up blowing the whistle on the social network’s most guarded secrets.

title: André Leon Talley: Style is Forever
description: André Leon Talley was a trailblazing fashion icon whose influence spanned nearly five decades. This documentary explores his legacy of inclusivity, elegance, and the fearless pursuit of authenticity. Interviews with Anna Wintour, Tom Ford and Diane von Furstenberg, among others, as well as never-before-seen footage, reveal Talley’s personal and professional challenges and remarkable triumphs.

title: What Can't Be Mentioned
description: Jackie (Tallie Medel) is a social worker in training picking at the knots of her own unresolved issues in microbudget maestro Dan Sallitt’s sequel to his notorious-yet-gentle 2012 taboo-buster The Unspeakable Act. Preceded by Nathan Silver’s Sounds From Home.

title: Manhunter (4K Restoration)
description: In celebration of the 40th anniversary of Michael Mann’s Manhunter , Mann’s final cut of the film returns in a newly restored 4K version. FBI criminal profiler Will Graham is called out of early retirement to assist on a deadly case involving a murderer known as the “Tooth Fairy.” After enlisting the help of imprisoned serial killer Dr. Hannibal Lecktor, Graham and the FBI are soon entangled in a menacing cat-and-mouse game.

title: Other Mommy
description: Bela, an 8-year-old girl living in a home with marital problems, confronts a sinister entity that comes out of her closet. The presence, whom she calls "Other Mommy," becomes increasingly threatening to her and her family.

title: Double Freedom
description: Argentinean director Lisandro Alonso expands upon his remarkable first feature, La Libertad (NYFF39), with a contemplative, elegantly crafted sequel again following charismatic woodcutter Misael (Misael Saavedra), who must now take in his mentally unstable sister.

title: Tender Loving Care
description: Mike Leigh’s portrayal of overwhelmed, resilient lives in post-Brexit England should be received as one of his signature works, a film with a leveling sense of humor about the difficulty of asking for—and accepting—help in a world that continually lets us down.

title: An Autumn's Tale
description: Newly arrived in New York City from Hong Kong and unhappily reunited with boyfriend Danny Chan, Jennifer (Cherie Chung) finds a guide to this strange new world in the person of distant relation Samuel Pang, aka “Sampan” (Chow Yun-fat, at his most goofily charming)… and the prospect, possibly, of something more. A time capsule of ’80s NYC—particularly Chinatown—and a perfectly delightful blend of odd-couple romance and amiable comedy from Cheung and longtime collaborator Alex Law, who took home Best Screenplay honors at the 7th Hong Kong Film Awards for his work here. (Lowell Lo’s heartstring-tugging score was, alas, robbed.) Part of The Leaves Are Falling

title: Tokyo Melody
description: In 1984, American-born, Paris-based artist Elizabeth Lennard traveled to Japan to make a film for French television about Ryuichi Sakamoto, pop star, solo artist, film actor, and film score composer. The result, shot over the course of a frenetic week, was Tokyo Melody, a mosaic work whose structure appears to have been determined by the multi-faceted nature of its subject’s creative practice: at various points we see Sakamoto snapping photographs, cruising through Tokyo on foot or via limousine, performing onstage with Yellow Magic Orchestra, pottering around his house, and in the studio for the recording of his Illustrated Musical Encyclopedia. Made not so long after his collaboration with Nagisa Ōshima on Merry Christmas, Mr. Lawrence, Lennard’s scintillating film, now in a new 4K restoration, captures a pivotal juncture in an extraordinary life. Introduction by composer Paul Grimstad on Saturday, September 26th Part of Sakamoto on Screen Portraits of an Artist

description: Weaving accounts of rural workers and field notes of a couple of archaeologists, amateur footage and scientific drawings, legends, poems and songs, Maureen Fazendeiro's The Seasons is a journey through the real history and the tales of a region in southern Portugal, Alentejo, and a portrait of the people who have lived there.

title: Classic Matinee: AMAZING GRACE
description: For our October Classic Matinee, and to mark Black History Month, we celebrate the Queen of Soul with AMAZING GRACE , the extraordinary concert film capturing Aretha Franklin at the height of her powers. Filmed over two nights at Los Angeles’ New Temple Missionary Baptist Church in 1972, Franklin jo...

title: Alien (Theatrical Cut)
description: In deep space, the crew of the commercial starship Nostromo is awakened from their cryo-sleep capsules halfway through their journey home to investigate a distress call from an alien vessel. The terror begins when the crew encounters a nest of eggs inside the alien ship. An organism from inside an egg leaps out and attaches itself to one of the crew, causing him to fall into a coma.

title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother 35mm
description: Latif is a devoutly religious hitman who struggles to balance work, faith, and fatherhood. When his wife dies, he embarks on a desperate journey across Houston in search of breast milk for his infant daughter, all while dodging sex traffickers, an evangelical militia, and his own demons.

title: Ryuichi Sakamoto: Coda
description: A precious glimpse into the creative process of the late synth-pop star, film composer, and activist Ryuichi Sakamoto, Schible’s deeply affecting film picks up with its introspective subject as he returns to music-making after having been diagnosed with cancer, channeling his new awareness of his mortality into his latest work. Part of Sakamoto on Screen Portraits of an Artist

title: The Only Living Pickpocket
description: In Noah Segan’s elegant love letter to New York, John Turturro delivers a star performance of effortless command and charisma as an aging petty thief from the Bronx who is thrust into a borough-hopping race against time.

title: The Craft
description: After transferring to a Los Angeles high school, Sarah (Robin Tunney) finds that her telekinetic gift appeals to a group of three wannabe witches, who happen to be seeking a fourth member for their rituals. Bonnie (Neve Campbell), Rochelle (Rachel True) and Nancy (Fairuza Balk), like Sarah herself, all have troubled backgrounds, which combined with their nascent powers lead to dangerous consequences. When a minor spell causes a fellow student to lose her hair, the girls grow power-mad.

title: Sense And Sensibility
description: An irresistible new take on Jane Austen’s iconic Sense and Sensibility: a charming, witty, and deeply relatable story of love and sisterhood starring Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles. Sisters Elinor and Marianne Dashwood must leave their Sussex estate following the sudden loss of their wealthy father and are forced to move in with a distant relative. The two sisters attempt to find security and happiness whilst navigating their vastly different approaches to love.

title: The Music Lovers
description: Composer, conductor and teacher Peter Ilych Tchaikovsky struggles against his homosexual tendencies by marrying, but unfortunately, he chooses wacky nymphomaniac Nina, whom he is unable to satisfy.

title: The Wedding Banquet
description: Before scaling Brokeback Mountain, Taiwanese American director Lee made this indie breakout about Wai Tung (Winston Chao, in his film debut), a gay man happily living in Manhattan with his partner who stages a sham marriage between himself and a penniless immigrant artist from mainland China in his building (May Chin) in order to please his traditionally minded parents—only to be appalled when they insist on throwing the “newlyweds” a whopper of a wedding party. A tender, emotionally grounded, sharply observed comedy of clashing cultures that’s made all the more poignant by its function as a time capsule of ’90s NYC. Part of Jiā: Histories of Home

title: 9 Temples to Heaven
description: A Thai family accompanies its ailing matriarch on a pilgrimage to nine separate Buddhist temples all in one day in this contemplative spiritual journey from Apichatpong Weerasethakul’s longtime assistant director, Sompot Chidgasornpongse. Thailand’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: Club Kid
description: Jordan Firstman’s wildly funny and remarkably assured feature debut about a washed-up thirtysomething New York scenester who discovers he has a 10-year-old British son swerves from irreverent satire to genuine pathos.

title: Digger
description: Academy Award-winning filmmaker Alejandro G. Iñárritu returns with his original film Digger, starring Tom Cruise. The most powerful man in the world (Cruise) embarks on a frantic mission to prove he is humanity’s savior before the disaster he’s unleashed destroys everything. This wildly hilarious satire was shot entirely in VistaVision.

title: Barrio Triste
description: In an impoverished neighborhood of 1980s Medellín, a group of disaffected teens steal a TV reporter’s camera to document their lives. Piercing the derelict landscape’s oppressive atmosphere with disarming reflections on dreams and death, their understanding of reality and hope begins to erode as reports of mysterious lights falling from the sky coincide with temporal and spatial distortions. In his striking feature debut, long-time Bad Bunny collaborator Stillz captures an intimate, formally daring portrait of Colombia's forgotten youth. Barrio Triste is heightened by a restless, intense debut score from Arca, whose fluid soundscapes anchor the film's vision. Navigating the thin line between desperation and the supernatural, Stillz delivers a beautiful, unclassifiable piece of contemporary cinema.

title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

description: Andrew Garfield stars as the legendary leader of a ferocious rebellion against the tyranny of King Richard II. As war burns across England, he forms an army of the people to face the King’s might in a fight for justice and survival.

description: Director Marine Atlan’s exceptionally accomplished feature debut turns a high school trip to Naples for a group of French teenagers into a revelatory experience, capturing the intimacies of her youthful characters with pinpoint emotional precision.

title: The Social Reckoning
description: A companion piece to the hit film The Social Network, Sorkin’s original screenplay is based on the events that gave rise to the Wall Street Journal’s shocking exposé The Facebook Files. The film is inspired by the true story of how Frances Haugen (Madison), a young Facebook engineer, enlists the help of Jeff Horwitz (White), a Wall Street Journal reporter, to go on a dangerous journey that ends up blowing the whistle on the social network’s most guarded secrets.

title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, The Devils lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color and Warner Bros. Sound. Following the sold-out LFF performance on 12th October, Ken Russell's THE DEVILS will screen daily from 30th October. Screenings from both 35mm and Digital. 35mm performances will be noted next to the time. If there is no note next to the time, the performance is Digital.

title: The Disciple
description: Dutch Moroccan fanboy Tarik Azzougarh spends over a decade working to meet and befriend his heroes, the genre-defining hip-hop group Wu-Tang Clan and its iconic spiritual leader, RZA. After joining their movement, he becomes the architect of one of their most talked-about and controversial albums, “Once Upon a Time in Shaolin,” whose radical concept continues to reverberate throughout the music industry. What unfolds is a twisting coming-of-age tale of boyhood dreams, relentless determination and the downfall of flying too close to the sun.

title: Invasion of the Body Snatchers (1956)
description: * ON SALE 23rd SEPT * In the sleepy Californian town of Santa Mira, strange happenings are afoot. Dr. Miles Bennell finds residents experiencing an epidemic of mass hysteria, imagining their relatives replaced by detached, emotionless copies. As Bennell gets closer to the horrifying truth - that the substitutions are part of an extraterrestrial invasion scheme and the copies are emerging from giant seed pods - the 'pod people' begin to close in.

title: Nadja
description: In 1993, invited by David Lynch to come up with a low-budget genre movie, Michael Almereyda ( Tesla , Experimenter , Hamlet ) came up with a moody, postmodern reimagining of the Dracula myth which draws inspiration from Dracula’s Daughter (1936) and André Breton’s surrealist novel Nadja . The film follows estranged vampire twins Nadja (Elina Löwensohn) and Edgar (a young Jared Harris) as they reunite following their father’s death by the flamboyantly unhinged Dr. Van Helsing, played with relish by Peter Fonda. The film’s striking visuals combine high-contrast black-and-white 35mm cinematography with the hallucinatory grain of Pixelvision video is now newly restored in 4K.

title: Other Mommy
description: Bela, an 8-year-old girl living in a home with marital problems, confronts a sinister entity that comes out of her closet. The presence, whom she calls "Other Mommy," becomes increasingly threatening to her and her family.
