title: KNEEJERK PRESENTS: I AM A SEX ADDICT
description:
On the eve of his third marriage, filmmaker Caveh Zahedi looks back over the compulsions, affairs and visits to sex workers that wrecked his previous relationships. Speaking directly to the camera, he reconstructs his worst decisions with actors, former partners and a disarming willingness to expose his own vanity. Confession repeatedly tips into comedy, then circles back towards consequences that cannot be laughed away.
Part memoir, part documentary and part elaborately staged act of self-incrimination, I Am a Sex Addict turns the confessional film inside out. Zahedi’s cheerful candour is both seductive and suspect, forcing the audience to question whether honesty can become another form of selfishness. Awkward, formally playful and often painfully funny, it is less a story of redemption than an uncomfortably intimate portrait of a man trying to make art from the damage he has caused.
Presented by Kneejerk

title: Penelope & Jane: A Polar Love Story
description: One Night Only Introduced by Director Ashley Francis-Roy In 1910, Captain Robert Falcon Scott set out aboard the Terra Nova, embarking on one of the most famous expeditions in the history of polar exploration. It's an epic tale of courage, endurance and sacrifice, deeply embedded in our national consciousness. But beneath the familiar retelling lies something more intimate - a story of secrecy, friendship and love. When polar-history obsessive Allegra Rosenberg uncovers the private diary of Terra Nova officer Harry Pennell, she discovers extraordinary declarations of his feelings for a fellow officer, Edward Atkinson. Pennell describes himself as "violently in love" and they share affectionate nicknames in a remarkable correspondence that offers a new perspective on the men behind Scott's legendary expedition. Now, following in Scott's footsteps across Antarctica, Allegra investigates a relationship that challenges our assumptions about masculinity, affection and sexuality in the early 20th century. Directed by Bafta-winner Ashley Francis-Roy, this film combines remarkable archive footage, contemporary interviews, and scripted drama to pose questions about how history is open to interpretation and which parts are all too easily erased. Were Pennell and Atkinson lovers, friends, or something harder to define? Against the breathtaking backdrop of Antarctic exploration, Penelope & Jane: A Polar Love Story uncovers a deeply human story hidden within one of Britain's greatest adventures.

title: The Lost Children of Tuam
description: In rural Ireland, amateur historian Catherine Corless begins researching a former institution for unmarried mothers and their children, uncovering a shocking hidden history of loss. Based on the true story, and featuring a powerful performance from Monica Dolan, THE LOST CHILDREN OF TUAM is a deeply moving portrait of one woman’s fight for justice.

title: The Man I Love
description: Ira Sachs’s finely detailed period drama about an emotionally complicated cabaret star and performance artist (Oscar winner Rami Malek) living with AIDS in 1980s New York is a reminder that art and imagination are keys to human survival in the darkest times.

title: Comédie Française
description: The Comédie-Française is one of France’s most revered arts institutions, and the oldest still-performing theatre company in the world. There is one golden rule: the play is NEVER cancelled.  Unfortunately for theatre producer Nina (Pauline Clément), everything is unravelling just three hours before the premiere of her first production – an ambitious retelling of Shakespeare’s Macbeth. Her lead actor is stuck on a train, tensions are exploding, passions flaring, equipment breaking down and egos are clashing. With panic setting in and the clock ticking Nina must hold things together at all costs. Will the show go on? France’s hit summer comedy and the runaway winner of four awards at the Alpe d’Huez comedy Film Festival, Comédie Française is a delicious behind-the-scenes farce which is unafraid to poke fun at the highbrow reputation of French theatre. Featuring a cast of real-life members of the Comédie-Française company, this is a gleeful, knowing parody and a sheer delight.

title: BERLIN HERO
description: Berlin, 2019: The 30th Anniversary of the Fall of the Berlin Wall is approaching, but former East German Railway worker “Micha” Hartung (Hübner) is focused on saving his failing video store, not on the past. When tabloid journalist Landmann (Ullrich) uncovers a report from the Stasi archives linking Micha to a mass escape of GDR citizens via the city’s Friedrichstraße Station in 1984, he moves to secure the rights to the story. Denying his role at first, Micha bends the facts, confirming the report in exchange for the cash royalty. Suddenly, Micha is a media sensation. After Paula (Paul), who was a child on that train, sees Micha on TV, she travels to thank him. Upon meeting, Paula thinks she’s found her “Berlin Hero,” and Micha has found the woman of his dreams. Still, it is only a matter of time before the web of lies and half-truths unravels, jeopardizing the couple’s happiness and the country’s understanding of the past. Based on Maxim Leo’s eponymous novel, featuring an extraordinary cast including Charly Hübner, Leonie Benesch, Thorsten Merten, Becker himself, and his long-time ensemble, Christiana Paul, Jürgen Vogel, and Daniel Brühl, Wolfgang Becker’s final film is a heart-warming, honest comedy about the nature of truth.

title: Oedipus Rex
description: Seeking source materials from which to forge a new “primal cinema,” Pasolini delved into the storehouse of mythic heritage. Taking on Sophocles’s Oedipus Rex, he begins with a prologue set in prewar Italy, and goes on to defy expectation throughout, depicting Oedipus (Franco Citti), unknowingly betrothed to biological mother Silvana Mangano, as a victim of his own ignorant innocence, here far from an unambiguously positive virtue. Pasolini’s first film in color, featuring costumes and art direction that evoke an almost science fiction vision of the ancient world, and a showy role for Carmelo Bene, then-reigning bad boy of Italian stage and screen. Part of Classical Cinema

description: An alien entity inhabits the earthly form of a seductive young woman who combs the Scottish highways in search of the human prey it is here to plunder. It lures its isolated and forsaken male victims into an otherworldly dimension where they are stripped and consumed. But life in all its complexity starts to change the alien. It begins to see itself as 'she', as human, with tragic and terrifying consequences.

title: Rogue Trooper
description: Tickets Are Only Available via BFI London Film Festival Website from Tuesday 17 September 2026 10:00am: Click Here To Book Duncan Jones brings the beloved 2000 AD comic strip to life with an all-guns-blazing sci-fi animation, about a soldier in a dystopian future who is sent on an impossible mission. Biochipped genetic soldiers, whose personalities can be downloaded should they fall on the battlefield, fight a futile, violent war across a chemically toxic landscape. Time is of the essence for their mission, but a raft of horrors await them. Fast and funny, Rogue Trooper is skilfully directed by Jones (Moon and Source Code), who gives this terrific British indie the feel of a Hollywood blockbuster.

title: Her Private Hell
description: From filmmaker Nicolas Winding Refn ( Drive , Only God Forgives , The Neon Demon ), Her Private Hell is a hypnotic moodscape enshrined in pink mist. Set against a surrealist, futuristic metropolis, the story follows Elle (Sophie Thatcher), a rising movie star preparing to shoot a space odyssey alongside her ex-lover turned stepmother (Havana Rose Liu). Elsewhere in the haze, an American GI (Charles Melton) wanders the desolate streets on a desperate search for his daughter. As an enigmatic and sinister figure known only as the Leather Man stalks the city's shadows, their lives begin to converge, dissolving the boundaries between past and present, memory and fate. Driven by his trademark neon cinematography, striking atmospheric dread, and an intoxicating orchestral score by legendary composer Pino Donaggio, Her Private Hell is a breathtaking, kaleidoscopic experience designed to mesmerise and seduce.

title: Se7en
description: Nearing-retirement veteran Detective Morgan Freeman and new transfer Brad Pitt track a serial killer with an advanced sense of stagecraft through a sickly, perpetually sodden city of peeling lead paint and lost souls in Fincher’s tour de force, easily one of the most stylistically influential films of the 1990s. “The look of Se7en … came out of this tight working ‘cell’ we created between David, myself, the production designer Arthur Max, and the costume designer Michael Kaplan. The four of us would meet together to discuss the art direction and visual scope of the movie, and we did several sessions like that to establish a unified plan… There was something [about Robert Frank’s photos in The Americans] that interested me, which was related to the grittiness of them, the blandness, the loneliness of a past era and the texture of death.” —Darius Khondji Part of Radical Chiaroscuro: The Work of Darius Khondji

description: The incomparable Pedro Almodóvar explores the artist’s tenuous relationship with fiction and reality in this film about an actress writing a script inspired by the lives of those around her—which is itself the invention of an Almodóvar-like filmmaker.

description: After an impulsive hookup, a Parisian photographer (Niels Schneider) finds that he has somehow swapped bodies with a German actress (Léa Seydoux). Arthur Harari treats this wild metaphysical gambit with the utmost sincerity in this uncanny supernatural drama.

title: Heathers
description: “Dear Diary: My teen-angst bullshit now has a body count.” A caustic rejoinder to John Hughes’s ’80s Brat Pack pictures, Lehmann’s savage suburban satire brought out the sociopathic side of Christian Slater’s too-cool outlaw persona, casting him as J.D., the motorcycle-riding new arrival at Ohio’s Westerburg High School who recruits Winona Ryder’s at-first pliable Veronica Chandler into his increasingly unhinged plans to humble their class’s ruling clique of three terrible popular girls named Heather. Clearly having a ball with Daniel Waters’s imminently quotable, coal-black screenplay, Ryder gives more than a few line-readings for the ages here; just try to keep “What’s your damage?” out of your vocabulary after viewing. Part of Winona Ryder Analogue Youth

title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

title: LADY IN THE WATER
description: Apartment building superintendent Cleveland Heep rescues what he thinks is a young woman from the pool he maintains. When he discovers that she is actually a character from a bedtime story who is trying to make the journey back to her home, he works with his tenants to protect his new friend from the creatures that are determined to keep her in our world.

title: The History of Concrete
description: A filmmaker applies lessons from a Hallmark movie writing workshop to pitch a documentary about concrete.

title: The Town That Dreaded Sundown             / The Evictors
description: A hooded killer terrorizes the moonlit streets of Texarkana, Arkansas and ‘70s genre staple Andrew Prine and cowboy star Ben Johnson are powerless to stop him. This ripped-from-the-headlines heart stopper was Charles B. Pierce’s terrifying follow-up to his smash hit The Legend of Boggy Creek . The legendary filmmaking personality could do it all: direct, act, produce & write. He came up with Dirty Harry’s signature line “go ahead, make my day” and was a set decorator on MacGyver. But The Town That Dreaded Sundown is his regional horror masterpiece, a haunting recreation of the brutal true-to-life, still-unsolved 1946 murders. Filmed on the actual blood-stained streets and using real Texarkana residents, the movie is a cold-hearted procedural, a nightmare-inducing proto-Unsolved Mysteries where an unhappy ending has already been assured.

title: Sense And Sensibility
description: An irresistible new take on Jane Austen’s iconic Sense and Sensibility: a charming, witty, and deeply relatable story of love and sisterhood starring Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles. Sisters Elinor and Marianne Dashwood must leave their Sussex estate following the sudden loss of their wealthy father and are forced to move in with a distant relative. The two sisters attempt to find security and happiness whilst navigating their vastly different approaches to love.

title: The Disciple
description: Dutch Moroccan fanboy Tarik Azzougarh spends over a decade working to meet and befriend his heroes, the genre-defining hip-hop group Wu-Tang Clan and its iconic spiritual leader, RZA. After joining their movement, he becomes the architect of one of their most talked-about and controversial albums, “Once Upon a Time in Shaolin,” whose radical concept continues to reverberate throughout the music industry. What unfolds is a twisting coming-of-age tale of boyhood dreams, relentless determination and the downfall of flying too close to the sun.

title: Comédie Française
description: The Comédie-Française is one of France’s most revered arts institutions, and the oldest still-performing theatre company in the world. There is one golden rule: the play is NEVER cancelled.  Unfortunately for theatre producer Nina (Pauline Clément), everything is unravelling just three hours before the premiere of her first production – an ambitious retelling of Shakespeare’s Macbeth. Her lead actor is stuck on a train, tensions are exploding, passions flaring, equipment breaking down and egos are clashing. With panic setting in and the clock ticking Nina must hold things together at all costs. Will the show go on? France’s hit summer comedy and the runaway winner of four awards at the Alpe d’Huez comedy Film Festival, Comédie Française is a delicious behind-the-scenes farce which is unafraid to poke fun at the highbrow reputation of French theatre. Featuring a cast of real-life members of the Comédie-Française company, this is a gleeful, knowing parody and a sheer delight.

From two-time Palme d’Or winner Cristian Mungiu, a Norwegian woman and her devout Romanian husband relocate with their five children to a remote, close-knit, coastal town. Their teenage children form a fast bond with a neighboring family as unease begins to simmer around their rigid beliefs. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice.

title: Queen at Sea
description: Starring Juliette Binoche, Tom Courtenay and Anna Calder-Marshall, Queen at Sea received its world premiere in competition at the Berlin International Film Festival earlier this year, where it won both the Silver Bear Jury Prize and the Silver Bear for Best Supporting Performance for both Courtenay and Calder-Marshall. The film follows Amanda (Binoche) and her stepfather, Martin (Courtney), at odds over a moral quandary involving Amanda’s mother, Leslie (Calder-Marshall). In the advanced stages of dementia, they quarrel over whether Leslie has lost all ability to make critical decisions in her own best interests, and, if so, who is responsible – a spouse, a child, an institution – for making such a determination? As Amanda and Martin are forced to make increasingly difficult choices, the repercussions spiral out of their control.

title: Late Fame
description: Willem Defoe plays Ed Saxberger, a forgotten New York poet, who works in the post office. After an eager and flattering young admirer appears on his doorstep, Saxberger is beckoned into a coterie of twentysomething admirers who anoint him as a rediscovered genius. Intoxicated by the attention — and by the alluring presence of Gloria, the group’s “tragic heroine” — Saxberger gradually reckons with the authenticity of his newfound poetic circle. Kent Jones's thoughtful, witty film is a wistful yet unromantic look at a lost idea of downtown New York.

title: The Thing
description: In remote Antarctica, a group of American research scientists are disturbed at their base camp by a helicopter shooting at a sled dog. When they take in the dog, it brutally attacks both human beings and canines in the camp and they discover that the beast can assume the shape of its victims. A resourceful helicopter pilot (Kurt Russell) and the camp doctor (Richard Dysart) lead the camp crew in a desperate, gory battle against the vicious creature before it picks them all off, one by one.

title: Cosi Fan Tutte
description: The Met: Live in HD season kicks off with Mozart’s satirical comedy of fickle young love, one of the composer’s most sublime creations.

title: Suspiria [1977]
description: Suzy (Jessica Harper) travels to Germany to attend ballet school. When she arrives, late on a stormy night, no one lets her in, and she sees Pat (Eva Axén), another student, fleeing from the school. When Pat reaches her apartment, she is murdered. The next day, Suzy is admitted to her new school, but has a difficult time settling in. She hears noises, and often feels ill. As more people die, Suzy uncovers the terrifying secret history of the place.

title: The Social Reckoning
description: A companion piece to the hit film The Social Network, Sorkin’s original screenplay is based on the events that gave rise to the Wall Street Journal’s shocking exposé The Facebook Files. The film is inspired by the true story of how Frances Haugen (Madison), a young Facebook engineer, enlists the help of Jeff Horwitz (White), a Wall Street Journal reporter, to go on a dangerous journey that ends up blowing the whistle on the social network’s most guarded secrets.

title: Remake
description: In Remake , filmmaker Ross McElwee turns his lens on the passage of time and the uneasy space between documenting life and understanding it. The film traces McElwee’s relationship with his son Adrian, and the fragile bond the camera created between them while Adrian was alive, and now that he’s gone. Drawing from decades of footage, some shot by Ross, some by Adrian, the film becomes a layered excavation of memory and image making. Threaded through is the ghost of another project: a stalled effort by Hollywood to fictionalize McElwee’s 1986 classic, Sherman’s March . What emerges is a work shaped by absence and propelled forward by a father’s love for his son.

title: Happy Together
description: Hong Kong cinema superstars Tony Leung and Leslie Cheung play a pair of lovers living out the waning days of their relationship as expatriates in Buenos Aires. Lusty tango bars, the salsa music of the La Boca sidewalks, and a hypnotic visit to the nearby Iguazu Falls give further dimension to the tensions growing between the two. Winner of the Best Director prize at the 1997 Cannes Film Festival, Wong’s Happy Together is a stunning display of filmmaking style and a touching story of love on the brink of dissolution. Part of Like the Wind: Lensed by Christopher Doyle

title: Paprika
description: The fourth and final film by Kon takes place in a not-too-distant future in which therapists, using a new technology called DC Mini, are able to record the dreams of psychiatric patients. All well and good, until a raid on the lab leads to the loss of the DC Mini prototype and a bleed between the troubled subconscious images and reality, leading to a race-against-time to stop bedlam from breaking out in the streets. An admitted inspiration for Christopher Nolan’s Inception (2010), though far more visually extravagant in its vibrant, psychedelia-inflected imaginings, which climax in a thrilling, terrifying dream apocalypse burst from Kon’s fervid imagination. Part of A Cyberpunk Canon

As they spend time together, they develop feelings for each other, but their relationship remains chaste and unspoken, reflecting societal constraints and their own moral compass.

title: Jennifer's Body
description: "She's evil… and not just high school evil.” A demon possesses high-school It-girl Jennifer (Megan Fox) after she is kidnapped and sacrificed in a failed occult ritual. Bloodthirsty, she seeks revenge through any man who crosses her path, but is challenged when her best friend, Needy (Amanda Seyfried), won´t stand idly by as the body-count rises. Campy, funny, horrific and truly impressive. After initially receiving mixed critical reception, Jennifer´s Body has become a horror and teen cult-classic as queer and female audiences have reclaimed the title. Ahead of its time, the film is still referenced in Halloween costumes, fan-theories, and video edits as audiences are hungrier than ever for the iconic maneater, Jennifer Check! Jennifer´s Body is featured as part of MANEATERS, a season exploring the female supernatural on screen. The season is presented with the National Film and Television School’s Film Studies, Programming and Curation MA.

title: André Leon Talley: Style is Forever
description: André Leon Talley was a trailblazing fashion icon whose influence spanned nearly five decades. This documentary explores his legacy of inclusivity, elegance, and the fearless pursuit of authenticity. Interviews with Anna Wintour, Tom Ford and Diane von Furstenberg, among others, as well as never-before-seen footage, reveal Talley’s personal and professional challenges and remarkable triumphs.

title: The Magnificent Butcher (林世榮)
description: The Magnificent Butcher (林世榮). 1979. Hong Kong. Directed by Yuen Woo-ping. Martial arts direction by Yuen Woo-ping, Sammo Hung. With Sammo Hung, Kwan Tak-hing, Yuen Biao. DCP courtesy Janus Films. In Cantonese; English subtitles. 108 min. Yuen Woo-ping’s The Magnificent Butcher stars Sammo Hung as Lam Sai-wing, the boisterous disciple of legendary martial-arts master Wong Fei-hung (Kwan Tak-hing), who becomes embroiled in a deadly feud while his teacher is away. Following the remarkable success of Drunken Master (1978), Yuen further developed his exuberant fusion of kung fu and comedy, while giving Hung a defining showcase for his extraordinary agility and impeccable comedic touch. Co-choreographed by Yuen and Hung, the action turns martial-arts virtuosity into physical comedy without sacrificing technical precision. Kwan’s appearance as Wong Fei-hung also provides a memorable meeting of two generations of kung fu cinema.

title: Invisible Adversaries
description: Export’s terrifyingly intimate, at times downright assaultive feature debut plunges the viewer into the unraveling psyche of Anna (Susanne Widl), a photographer whose conviction that extraterrestrials called “Hyksos” are in the process of hastening civilization-wide decline leads to schizophrenic episodes—imagined in blistering montage—and a devastating crack-up with her partner, played by artist and new media theoretician Peter Weibel. “A tour de force of cinematic invention… Reveals a prodigious talent at work… Some of the most audacious and amazing experiments since Cocteau… A modern Blood of the Poet… Export brings a fresh and intelligent sensibility, characteristically self-referential.” —Gene Youngblood, Expanded Cinema Introduction by filmmaker Lynne Sachs on Saturday, October 3rd Part of Valie Export: Tap Touch Burn

title: Ghost in the Shell: 30th Anniversary Remaster
description: “My codename is Project 2501, and I am a life form that was born in a sea of information.” In the year 2029, the world looks like a hybridization of Hong Kong, Tokyo, and New York, yielding to entropy and technocracy. Cyborg Major Kusanagi, a perfect specimen of human-brained computer engineering is on the case to track and destroy an omnipotent entity known as The Puppet Master—a hacker? a virus?—who threatens world order. Her physical and existential journey deftly detailed by Oshii’s animation, combining traditional hand-drawn cells and computer-generated graphics, creating a haunting, awe-inspiring magnum opus. Part of A Cyberpunk Canon

title: Cotton Queen
description: In a cotton-farming village in Sudan, teenage Nafisa is raised on heroic tales of battling British colonisers told by her grandmother, the village matriarch Al-Sit. But when a young businessman arrives from abroad with a new development plan and genetically engineered cotton, Nafisa becomes the centre of a power play to determine the future of the village. Awakening to her own strength, Nafisa sets out to save the cotton fields – and herself. Neither she nor her community will ever be the same again.

title: The Uprising
description: Andrew Garfield stars as the legendary leader of a ferocious rebellion against the tyranny of King Richard II. As war burns across England, he forms an army of the people to face the King’s might in a fight for justice and survival.

title: Funeral Parade presents A Nightmare on Elm Street 2: Freddy's Revenge
description: Just in time for Spooky Season, Funeral Parade is proud to present A Nightmare on Elm Street 2: Freddy’s Revenge, a queer-coded slasher classic. The man of your dreams is BACK! That’s right, Freddy Krueger has returned to stalk Elm Street once again – and this time he’s enlisting teenager Jesse Walsh to help carry out his evil deeds. Freddy intends to possess Jesse’s body in order to take his bloody revenge on the teenage population of Springwood, Ohio. Will Jesse be able to resist him? A Nightmare on Elm Street 2: Freddy’s Revenge has become infamous for its homoerotic subtext and features an iconic performance from Mark Patton as slasher cinema’s first male “scream queen”. With intro from film curator Sarah Cleary.

title: Yi Yi
description: The last work of a master filmmaker who died far too young, the gentle, restrained, and terribly humane Yi Yi observes the interplay between three generations of an upper middle-class Taipei family. Comic when dealing in the foibles of its excellent ensemble cast and the mores of the urban bourgeoise, yet also possessed throughout by an air of unmistakable melancholy and lingering regret at missed opportunities, this feeling made all the deeper when one considers the great films Yang might still have produced. A work of epic length that avoids even a hint of bombast, dedicated instead to working its way into the hidden, niche spaces of everyday people’s emotional lives, it’s a film as rich and as sad as life itself. Part of Jiā: Histories of Home

title: Gothic
description: Living on an estate on the shores of Lake Geneva, Lord Byron is visited by Percy and Mary Shelley. Together with Byron’s lover Claire Clairmont, and aided by hallucinogenic substances, they devise an evening of ghoulish tales. However, when confronted by horrors, ostensibly of their own creation, it becomes difficult to tell apparition from reality.

title: VACANCES
description: FILMMAKER IN PERSON! A strange and unusual mixture of warts-and-all family portraiture, subtle exposé of class and privilege, and minimalist depiction of a particular setting that’s rendered with an almost miraculously tactile sense of presence, photographer and filmmaker Victoria Hely-Hutchinson’s VACANCES is a deceptively unassuming film. Filmed over the course of a decade at the property in Provence inhabited by Hely-Hutchinson’s outrageously uninhibited grandmother, a bohemian Austro-Hungarian countess and family matriarch, VACANCES grew out of Hely-Hutchinson’s 2016 short film of the same name, and is something of a filmic complement to her autobiographical 2023 book, “I Left My Grandmother’s House”. The documentary delves, with a grace and open-endedness that belies its analytical bite, into both the bigger-than-life personality of “granny” as well as the sometimes strained dynamics among the rest of the family, including Hely-Hutchinson’s grandfather, mother, and siblings. Unique in suggesting by turns cinema vérité, reality TV, chamber theater, and the minimalism of landscape cinema, VACANCES is a profoundly singular work – a film whose technique is nearly invisible, but which sneaks up on you with its trenchant perceptions, layered meanings, and emotional and filmic complexity. “This time-lapse film, shot over a period of ten years, follows members of several generations of a wealthy aristocratic family with Austro-Hungarian roots. The entire film is set in a Provençal villa, whose social heart is the swimming pool, around which the women gather to exchange various observations and, surreptitiously, gossip. The center of the family is the aging matriarch, who likes to talk about her extravagant, promiscuous life, but at the same time commands all the attention and authority of those around her. However, her influence gradually weakens with each passing generation.” –JI.HLAVA INTERNATIONAL DOCUMENTARY FILM FESTIVAL

title: Nadja
description: In 1993, invited by David Lynch to come up with a low-budget genre movie, Michael Almereyda ( Tesla , Experimenter , Hamlet ) came up with a moody, postmodern reimagining of the Dracula myth which draws inspiration from Dracula’s Daughter (1936) and André Breton’s surrealist novel Nadja . The film follows estranged vampire twins Nadja (Elina Löwensohn) and Edgar (a young Jared Harris) as they reunite following their father’s death by the flamboyantly unhinged Dr. Van Helsing, played with relish by Peter Fonda. The film’s striking visuals combine high-contrast black-and-white 35mm cinematography with the hallucinatory grain of Pixelvision video is now newly restored in 4K.

title: SWEET BABY CHARLIE aka THE SADIST
description:
A trio of schoolteachers traveling by car through rural California stop at a junkyard for help, only to encounter a young man and his unstable girlfriend. What begins as a minor inconvenience quickly turns into a hostage situation, as the couple reveal themselves to be violent fugitives with a taste for sadistic control and escalating cruelty.
Shot in stark black and white by Vilmos Zsigmond early in his career, the film traps its characters in a pressure cooker of intimidation and unpredictability. Its stripped-down setting and relentless focus on power imbalance give it a raw, early blueprint feel for later home-invasion and exploitation cinema. Watch out for an incredible and demonic leading performance by Arch Hall, Jr.

title: Hadestown: The Musical
description: The live theater capture of the hit musical Hadestown, which won eight Tony Awards in 2019 including Best Musical and the 2020 Grammy Award for Best Musical Theater Album, featuring the five original principals of the Broadway company. The genre-defying new musical blends modern American folk music with New Orleans-inspired jazz to reimagine a sweeping ancient tale. Following two intertwining love stories — that of young dreamers Orpheus and Eurydice, and that of King Hades and his wife Persephone —Hadestowninvites audiences on a hell-raising journey to the underworld and back.

title: The Lost Children of Tuam
description: In rural Ireland, amateur historian Catherine Corless begins researching a former institution for unmarried mothers and their children, uncovering a shocking hidden history of loss. Based on the true story, and featuring a powerful performance from Monica Dolan, THE LOST CHILDREN OF TUAM is a deeply moving portrait of one woman’s fight for justice.

title: Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon(臥虎藏龍)
description: Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon (臥虎藏龍). 2000. Taiwan/Hong Kong/USA. Directed by Ang Lee. Screenplay by Wang Hui Ling, James Schamus, Tsai Kuo Jung, based on the book by Wang Du Lu. Action choreography by Yuen Woo-ping. With Chow Yun Fat, Michelle Yeoh, Zhang Ziyi, Cheng Pei-pei, Chang Chen. 4K DCP courtesy Sony Pictures Classics. In Mandarin; English subtitles. 120 min. Ang Lee’s groundbreaking Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon reimagines the wuxia tradition as an elegant fusion of martial arts, romance, and philosophical drama. When a legendary sword is stolen, two seasoned warriors (Chow Yun Fat and Michelle Yeoh) pursue a young martial artist (Zhang Ziyi) whose rebellious spirit draws her into a world of love, duty, and danger. Yuen Woo-ping’s choreography transforms combat into an extension of character and emotion. Bridging grounded martial discipline with poetic, dance-like wirework, he staged some of the most memorable combat sequences ever filmed, including an iconic duel balanced high atop a swaying bamboo forest. The film became an unprecedented international phenomenon and earned 10 Academy Award nominations, winning four, including Best Foreign Language Film.

title: The Yellow Sea
description: Jang and Lee Byung-hoon’s propulsive score sets a fire under Na’s unrelenting man-on-the-run thriller that burns hotter with each passing minute. Debt-strapped down-on-his-luck cabbie Gu-nam (Ha Jung-woo), an ethnic Korean living and working in China, agrees to take a contract killing gig from a local gangster (Kim Yoon-seok) that will take him across the Yellow Sea and into South Korea—and in short order finds himself scrambling to keep ahead of cops, crooks, and a bevy of other characters who’d like nothing more than to see his head on a skewer. “Contains two of the most mindbogglingly choreographed, thrillingly extended pursuit scenes—one on foot and one in cars—that I’ve ever seen.” —Amy Taubin, Film Comment Part of Composed by Jang Young Gyu

title: MAŁ̣NI - TOWARDS THE OCEAN, TOWARDS THE SHORE
description: A poetic, experimental debut feature circling the origin of the death myth from the Chinookan people in the Pacific Northwest, MAŁ̣NI – TOWARDS THE OCEAN, TOWARDS THE SHORE follows two people as they wander through their surrounding nature, the spirit world and something much deeper inside. At its center are Sweetwater Sahme and Jordan Mercier, who take separate paths contemplating their afterlife, rebirth and death. Probing questions about humanity’s place on earth and other worlds, Sky Hopinka’s film will have audiences thinking (and dreaming) about it long after.

title: AVATARS: THE DOMINATRIX SLEEPS TONIGHT
description: Taking the avatar of the dominatrix as its starting point, this short film program gathers together various films made – across a 40-year period – by or in collaboration with those who have experience in the leathersex scene. As an avatar of working sex, the figure of the dominatrix is elusive in so far as she uses the theater of the scene of “violation” to both pursue and obfuscate her desires. Though cinema longs to unmask the dominatrix to witness her “true” self, this program instead finds pleasure in the artifice of the scene wherein various characters find themselves at the mercy of the seductive and controlling gaze of the dominatrix. The shorts here range from documentary exercises of sadism, like Ione Wang’s WHEN I LOOK AT YOU, I SEE ME, to the electric pop-music video work of Beth B’s THE DOMINATRIX SLEEPS TONIGHT, made for the band Dominatrix. Shorts by Azian Nurudin and Michelle Handelman from the late 1980s and early 1990s invite a reconsideration of race, power, and aesthetics through their respectively overlooked and censored films, while M.M. Serra and Maria Beatty’s work demonstrates the aesthetic bliss that emerges from submitting to the fantasies of a powerful woman. Azian Nurudin NANCY’S NIGHTMARE (1988, 5 min, digital) Michelle Handelman CATSCAN (1989, 6 min, Super-8mm-to-digital. Made with with Monte Cazazza.) M.M. Serra & Jennifer Reeves DARLING INTERNATIONAL (1999, 22 min, 16mm-to-digital) Maria Beatty THE BLACK GLOVE (1996, 30 min, digital) Beth B THE DOMINATRIX SLEEPS TONIGHT (1984, 4 min, video) Ione Wang WHEN I LOOK AT YOU, I SEE ME (2024, 7 min, digital) Total running time: ca. 80 min.

title: When There Is No More Music to Write, and OtherRoman Stories
Elephant Gym: More Real Than Dreams
description: Elephant Gym successfully completed a world tour spanning 60 cities across 23 countries. However, behind this achievement lay an unseen crisis of disbandment, along with hidden conflicts and struggles. What does it truly mean to be a band? The film was first screened in October 2025 at the Kaohsiung Film Festival, one of Taiwan’s leading film festivals, and will also be shown in theaters in both Japan and Taiwan.

title: Naza
description: In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them. We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA ’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence. — Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

title: The History of Concrete
description: A filmmaker applies lessons from a Hallmark movie writing workshop to pitch a documentary about concrete.

title: The Shining [UK Version]
description: Jack Torrance (Jack Nicholson) becomes winter caretaker at the isolated Overlook Hotel in Colorado, hoping to cure his writer's block. He settles in along with his wife, Wendy (Shelley Duvall), and his son, Danny (Danny Lloyd), who is plagued by psychic premonitions. As Jack's writing goes nowhere and Danny's visions become more disturbing, Jack discovers the hotel's dark secrets and begins to unravel into a homicidal maniac hell-bent on terrorizing his family.

description: The screening on the September 1st will be introduced by Garden Cinema team member, writer, and filmmaker Sarah Grice. Subsequent screenings…

description: Fri, Sep 18: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Edy Modica (actress, comedian, filmmaker), after 4:40 show! Fri, Sep 18: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Rachel Kaly (comedian, writer, actor), after 7:15 show! Sun, Sep 20: Q&A with dir. John Wilson, moderated by Sarah Sherman after 2:10 show! Following the finale of his TV show, filmmaker John Wilson searches for a new creative outlet. After attending a workshop on how to write and sell a Hallmark movie, he attempts to apply the same formula to a documentary about concrete.

title: Sense and Sensibility (U) (AD)
description: An irresistible new take on Jane Austen ’s iconic Sense and Sensibility : a charming, witty and deeply relatable story of love and sisterhood, starring Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles .

title: Her Private Hell
description: From filmmaker Nicolas Winding Refn ( Drive , Only God Forgives , The Neon Demon ), Her Private Hell is a hypnotic moodscape enshrined in pink mist. Set against a surrealist, futuristic metropolis, the story follows Elle (Sophie Thatcher), a rising movie star preparing to shoot a space odyssey alongside her ex-lover turned stepmother (Havana Rose Liu). Elsewhere in the haze, an American GI (Charles Melton) wanders the desolate streets on a desperate search for his daughter. As an enigmatic and sinister figure known only as the Leather Man stalks the city's shadows, their lives begin to converge, dissolving the boundaries between past and present, memory and fate. Driven by his trademark neon cinematography, striking atmospheric dread, and an intoxicating orchestral score by legendary composer Pino Donaggio, Her Private Hell is a breathtaking, kaleidoscopic experience designed to mesmerise and seduce.

title: Digger (15) (AD)
description: Academy Award-winning filmmaker Alejandro G Iñárritu ( Birdman ) returns with his original feature starring Tom Cruise as the most powerful man in the world.

title: Digger
description: The most powerful man in the world embarks on a frantic mission to prove he is humanity's saviour before the disaster he’s unleashed destroys everything.

title: The Social Reckoning (15) (AD)
description: In this companion piece to The Social Network , screenwriter Aaron Sorkin returns to the Metaverse with a tale of the whistleblower who started the social media reckoning we're seeing play out today.

title: Queer Edward II
description: Tickets Are Only Available via BFI London Film Festival Website from Tuesday 17 September 2026 10:00am: Click Here To Book This all-archival tour de force takes us behind the scenes of Derek Jarman’s Edward II, set against the backdrop of the anti-LGBTQIA+ legislation of 1980s Britain. This all-archival tour de force takes us behind the scenes of Derek Jarman’s Edward II, set against the backdrop of the anti-LGBTQIA+ legislation of 1980s Britain. In 1991, Jarman started production on Edward II, just as queer life in the UK was under renewed threat from the British government. Seamus McGarvey captured all the drama on set in a previously unseen treasure trove of behind-the-scenes footage. Queer Edward II masterfully reanimates this archive as a vigorous and radical reflection on the power of art as protest.

title: EXTRA GEOGRAPHY
description: Set in an English boarding school, EXTRA GEOGRAPHY follows two teenage girls as they grapple with all the challenges of girlhood: friendship, boys, studies, growing up and their summer project, "to fall in love".  “Extra Geography joins the ranks of instant greats like “Lady Bird,” “Booksmart” and “...

title: The Lost Children of Tuam
description: In rural Ireland, amateur historian Catherine Corless begins researching a former institution for unmarried mothers and their children, uncovering a shocking hidden history of loss. Based on the true story, and featuring a powerful performance from Monica Dolan, THE LOST CHILDREN OF TUAM is a deeply moving portrait of one woman’s fight for justice.

title: NATURAL ENEMIES
description:
Paul Steward, the editor of a scientific journal, wakes after a sleepless night convinced that his life has become an empty failure. Having decided to murder his wife, their children and then himself, he spends the day revisiting his past and indulging his long-suppressed desires before returning home.
A bleak, confrontational psychological drama starring Hal Holbrook and Louise Fletcher, Jeff Kanew’s debut feature turns a midlife crisis into an unsettling portrait of despair, alienation and domestic violence.

title: Verity
description: Struggling writer Lowen Ashleigh is hired as a ghostwriter for renowned author Verity Crawford under mysterious circumstances, but her assignment takes a dark turn after discovering chilling autobiographical notes. Faced with a series of deadly family secrets, Lowen struggles to separate fiction from reality, while also blurring the lines with Verity’s husband, Jeremy.

title: Tommy
description: After a series of traumatic childhood events, a psychosomatically deaf, dumb and blind boy becomes a master pinball player and the object of a religious cult.

title: Other Mommy
description: Bela, an 8-year-old girl living in a home with marital problems, confronts a sinister entity that comes out of her closet. The presence, whom she calls "Other Mommy," becomes increasingly threatening to her and her family.

title: The Social Reckoning
description: Explores Facebook's internal practices, spread of false information, impact on teen mental health, and connection to January 6 Capitol events.

title: The Social Reckoning
description: A companion piece to the hit film The Social Network, Sorkin’s original screenplay is based on the events that gave rise to the Wall Street Journal’s shocking exposé The Facebook Files. The film is inspired by the true story of how Frances Haugen (Madison), a young Facebook engineer, enlists the help of Jeff Horwitz (White), a Wall Street Journal reporter, to go on a dangerous journey that ends up blowing the whistle on the social network’s most guarded secrets.

title: Resident Evil
description: In this sci-fi horror action reboot, a hapless medical courier fights for his life amid an outbreak of a deadly mutagenic virus in an isolated mountain town.

title: SEDUCTION: THE CRUEL WOMAN
description: In SEDUCTION: THE CRUEL WOMAN, Wanda is a dominatrix and gallerist who invites patrons to witness her scenes with her submissives. Inspired by the Marquis de Sade’s “Venus in Furs”, writer-directors Monika Treut and Elfi Mikesch spin Sade’s tale of power, apathy, and pleasure to foreground the role the spectator (both imagined and real) plays in enabling these violating acts to occur.

title: Fjord
description: Tue, Oct 6: Sneak preview + Q&A with director Cristian Mungiu and co-star Sebastian Stan after the 6:15 show! Tues, Oct 6: Extended intro with director Cristian Mungiu and co-star Sebastian Stan at the 8:15 show! From two-time Palme d’Or winner Cristian Mungiu, a Norwegian woman and her devout Romanian husband relocate with their five children to a remote, close-knit, coastal town. Their teenage children form a fast bond with a neighboring family as unease begins to simmer around their rigid beliefs. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice.

title: The Double
description: Inspired by the Dostoyevsky novella of the same title, Ayoade’s noir-inflected sophomore feature gives a dead game Jesse Eisenberg not one but two juicy parts as both a mousy, long-overlooked office drone, Simon James, and his new colleague, the cocksure and charismatic James Simon, who no one other than Simon seems to notice is in fact Simon’s doppelgänger, and who briskly sets about invading every aspect of Simon’s life. The bleakly comic story of a man struggling to get the upper hand over himself, with Eisenberg, in his virtuoso double role, getting more than capable backup from a supporting cast that includes Mia Wasikowska, Wallace Shawn, and Cathy Moriarty. Part of The Office of Emptiness

title: Women on the Verge of a Nervous Breakdown
description: Capping an incredible eight-year creative partnership with Almodóvar, repeat collaborator Carmen Maura here plays voice actress Pepa, who, abandoned by her lover, has resolved to kill herself by downing a batch of gazpacho laced with sleeping pills. That’s just the start of the orgy of unhinged behavior that makes up Almodóvar’s gaudy, cheeky screwball melodrama about Shiite terrorist cells and romance on the rocks, a camp romp celebration of emotional excess that has all the makings of an obscure cult classic, yet improbably became the highest-grossing Spanish film of all time upon release, and did its part in putting co-star Antonio Banderas on the international stage. Part of Among Friends

title: MONSTER HOUSE
description: Even for a 12-year old, D.J. Walters has a particularly overactive imagination. He is convinced that his haggard and crabby neighbor Horace Nebbercracker, who terrorizes all the neighborhood kids, is responsible for Mrs. Nebbercracker’s mysterious disappearance. Any toy that touches Nebbercracker’s property promptly disappears, swallowed up by the cavernous house in which Horace lives. D.J. has seen it with his own eyes! But no one believes him, not even his best friend, Chowder. What everyone does not know is D.J. is not imagining things. Everything he’s seen is absolutely true and it’s about to get much worse than anything D.J could have imagined.

title: The History of Concrete

title: Who Killed Teddy Bear?             / In the Cut
description: An unforgettable descent into sleazy mid-60s NYC, Who Killed Teddy Bear? is a staggering psycho-sexual thriller determined to smash every previously untouchable Hollywood taboo in the rulebook. Juliet Prowse plays a discotheque DJ on the receiving end of a series of increasingly obscene phone calls. As violence from the mysterious stalker tumbles into real life, who could be the madman responsible: the nightclub manager with sapphic desires (Elaine Stritch), the creepy cop with a damaged past (Jan Murray), or the club’s shy busboy hiding dark family secrets (Sal Mineo)? Teddy Bear is ripe for rediscovery, raw and unflinching, with a charged Mineo at his fiery best.

title: LFF: My Undesirable Friends: Part II — Exile
Perfect Blue
description: A young Japanese singer is encouraged by her agent to quit singing and pursue an acting career, beginning with a role in a murder mystery TV show. Our 11th October performance of Perfect Blue will be preceded by the European Premiere of brand-new short film, IDOLS. Idols | South Korea, Japan, UK | 20 min. Dir. by Matt Halsall Kim Min-ha (Hojo Shin) has always dreamed of the spotlight. Now, nearing 30, she’s still chasing a K-pop debut while everyone else sees only her uncanny resemblance to superstar Park Hye-mi (Hojo Shin)—the woman she believes is living the life that should have been hers. Matt Halsall’s slick, darkly funny short turns that obsession into an increasingly unhinged psychological thriller. IDOLS made its world premiere at Fantasia before being selected for Sitges, Beyond Fest and Tokyo’s Yami International Film Festival.

title: Late Fame
description: Willem Defoe plays Ed Saxberger, a forgotten New York poet, who works in the post office. After an eager and flattering young admirer appears on his doorstep, Saxberger is beckoned into a coterie of twentysomething admirers who anoint him as a rediscovered genius. Intoxicated by the attention — and by the alluring presence of Gloria, the group’s “tragic heroine” — Saxberger gradually reckons with the authenticity of his newfound poetic circle. Kent Jones's thoughtful, witty film is a wistful yet unromantic look at a lost idea of downtown New York.

title: Halloween (1978)
description: Fifteen years after murdering his sister on Halloween Night 1963, Michael Myers escapes from a mental hospital and returns to the small town of Haddonfield, Illinois to kill again.

title: Cosi Fan Tutte
description: The Met: Live in HD season kicks off with Mozart’s satirical comedy of fickle young love, one of the composer’s most sublime creations.

title: Remake
description: In Remake , filmmaker Ross McElwee turns his lens on the passage of time and the uneasy space between documenting life and understanding it. The film traces McElwee’s relationship with his son Adrian, and the fragile bond the camera created between them while Adrian was alive, and now that he’s gone. Drawing from decades of footage, some shot by Ross, some by Adrian, the film becomes a layered excavation of memory and image making. Threaded through is the ghost of another project: a stalled effort by Hollywood to fictionalize McElwee’s 1986 classic, Sherman’s March . What emerges is a work shaped by absence and propelled forward by a father’s love for his son.

title: Inland Empire
description: An actress's perception of reality becomes increasingly distorted as she finds herself falling for her co-star in a remake of an unfinished Polish production that was supposedly cursed.

title: The Texas Chain Saw Massacre
description: When Sally (Marilyn Burns) hears that her grandfather's grave may have been vandalized, she and her paraplegic brother, Franklin (Paul A. Partain), set out with their friends to investigate. After a detour to their family's old farmhouse, they discover a group of crazed, murderous outcasts living next door. As the group is attacked one by one by the chainsaw-wielding Leatherface (Gunnar Hansen), who wears a mask of human skin, the survivors must do everything they can to escape. * The first 35 customers to have tickets scanned in each of these performances will recieve an exclusive limited edition " I SURVIVED THE TEXAS CHAINSAW MASSACRE" badge. A replica of one's we gave out back in 1976 when we were the first cinema to debut this iconic film.

title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother 35mm
description: Latif is a devoutly religious hitman who struggles to balance work, faith, and fatherhood. When his wife dies, he embarks on a desperate journey across Houston in search of breast milk for his infant daughter, all while dodging sex traffickers, an evangelical militia, and his own demons.

title: Barrio Triste
description: In an impoverished neighborhood of 1980s Medellín, a group of disaffected teens steal a TV reporter’s camera to document their lives. Piercing the derelict landscape’s oppressive atmosphere with disarming reflections on dreams and death, their understanding of reality and hope begins to erode as reports of mysterious lights falling from the sky coincide with temporal and spatial distortions. In his striking feature debut, long-time Bad Bunny collaborator Stillz captures an intimate, formally daring portrait of Colombia's forgotten youth. Barrio Triste is heightened by a restless, intense debut score from Arca, whose fluid soundscapes anchor the film's vision. Navigating the thin line between desperation and the supernatural, Stillz delivers a beautiful, unclassifiable piece of contemporary cinema.

title: The Uprising
description: Andrew Garfield stars as the legendary leader of a ferocious rebellion against the tyranny of King Richard II. As war burns across England, he forms an army of the people to face the King’s might in a fight for justice and survival.

title: Mikey and Nicky
description: Our performance on 14th October is presented with an introduction by Christina Newland Elaine May crafted a gangster film like no other in the nocturnal odyssey Mikey and Nicky, capitalising on the chemistry between frequent collaborators John Cassavetes and Peter Falk by casting them together as small-time mobsters whose lifelong relationship has turned sour. Set over the course of one night, this restless drama finds Nicky (Cassavetes) holed up in a hotel after the boss he stole money from puts a hit out on him. Terrified, he calls on Mikey (Falk), the one person he thinks can save him. Scripted to match the live-wire energy of its stars—alongside supporting players Ned Beatty, Joyce Van Patten, and Carol Grace—and inspired by real-life characters from May’s own childhood, this unbridled portrait of male friendship turned tragic is an unsung masterpiece of American cinema. Our performance on 14th October is featured as part of Gangsters Have Feelings Too, a season exploring the sensitive gangster film. The season is presented with the National Film and Television School’s Film Studies, Programming and Curation MA.

title: CECIL B. DEMENTED
description:
Cecil B. Demented follows an underground filmmaker who leads a radical group of devoted cinephiles determined to wage war against mainstream Hollywood. During a movie premiere, the group kidnaps a famous but frustrated actress and forces her to star in their guerrilla film, which they shoot illegally across the city while evading the authorities and studio security.
Blending dark comedy with anarchic satire, Cecil B. Demented celebrates rebellious filmmaking and critiques the commercialization of cinema. The film portrays its band of self proclaimed film terrorists as both fanatics and passionate artists, using outrageous stunts, confrontations, and film culture references to champion independent creativity over corporate entertainment.

title: Cotton Queen
description: In a cotton-farming village in Sudan, teenage Nafisa is raised on heroic tales of battling British colonisers told by her grandmother, the village matriarch Al-Sit. But when a young businessman arrives from abroad with a new development plan and genetically engineered cotton, Nafisa becomes the centre of a power play to determine the future of the village. Awakening to her own strength, Nafisa sets out to save the cotton fields – and herself. Neither she nor her community will ever be the same again.

title: BIRD IN HAND
description: Inspired by Roscher’s own biracial experience, BIRD IN HAND follows the newly engaged Bird Rowe (Alisha Wainwright) as she returns to her rural hometown to plan the wedding with her narcissistic hippie mother Carlotta (Christine Lahti). Bird also has a hidden agenda, one that leads her to her mother’s new neighbors, a misguided couple on a mission to ‘rebrand’ a plantation. Truth, lies and fantasy collide against that backdrop, leading to a surprising climax as tender as it is funny.

title: Candyman
description: Sweets for the sweet …Undisputedly one of the best horror films of the 1990s (and arguably of all time), this creepy classic will still chill you to the bone. Let the hypnotic Philip Glass score draw you into a haunting and menacing nightmare about gentrification and systemic racism, perfectly helmed by Tony Todd’s iconic performance. Helen (Virginia Madsen) is a grad student on the hunt for the definitive scoop of a local urban legend for her thesis project. What she finds is a monster that preys on the projects and seduces her into his antebellum mythology. A pitch-perfect masterpiece of horror, say his name five times and join us for terror in Cabrini Green!

title: It Gets Worse
description: Tickets Are Only Available via BFI London Film Festival Website from Tuesday 17 September 2026 10:00am: Click Here To Book Leo Reich’s new series turns the struggles of young Londoners into its playground, mining a generation’s problems for biting, clever comedy. Ethan, Abi and Sam, inseparable friends in their mid-20s, are forced into real adulthood when eviction looms. Razor-sharp and witty, It Gets Worse skewers a generation stuck between housing crisis, humiliating jobs and messy relationships, while savouring the joy of youth in one of the buzziest cities in the world. It’s anchored by standout performances from the three leads, alongside unforgettable cameos from the likes of Lena Dunham and Andrew Scott.

title: BUMPKIN SOUP
description: A country girl named Akiko (Yoriko Doguchi, known for her collaborations with the late Kishin Shinoyama) visits a college in Tokyo in search of her hometown sweetheart. In the course of finding him, she runs into various odd inhabitants of the college campus – blasé intellectuals, sex-crazed co-eds, a psychology professor in search of the theory of shame (played by award-winning director Juzo Itami) and of course her sweetheart Yoshioka, who has become an elusive campus nobody. An early pink film from Kiyoshi Kurosawa, the award-winning director of CURE and TOKYO SONATA.

title: Who Killed Teddy Bear?             / In the Cut
description: An unforgettable descent into sleazy mid-60s NYC, Who Killed Teddy Bear? is a staggering psycho-sexual thriller determined to smash every previously untouchable Hollywood taboo in the rulebook. Juliet Prowse plays a discotheque DJ on the receiving end of a series of increasingly obscene phone calls. As violence from the mysterious stalker tumbles into real life, who could be the madman responsible: the nightclub manager with sapphic desires (Elaine Stritch), the creepy cop with a damaged past (Jan Murray), or the club’s shy busboy hiding dark family secrets (Sal Mineo)? Teddy Bear is ripe for rediscovery, raw and unflinching, with a charged Mineo at his fiery best.

title: The Story of Documentary Film (The 1990s)
description: Tickets Are Only Available via BFI London Film Festival Website from Tuesday 17 September 2026 10:00am: Click Here To Book This fascinating chapter from Mark Cousins’ epic essay on the history of documentary chronicles a decade of formal reinvention and mainstream success. Cousins, the creator of the groundbreaking The Story of Film: A New Generation and Women Make Film, trains his distinctive film-historian lens on the evolution of documentary. The result is a rich tapestry of landmark works and underappreciated gems. In this illuminating chapter, he guides us through the 1990s, a decade of filmmakers exploring bodies, spirituality, labour, war and politics, against the backdrop of rising commercial interest in the form.

title: Birth
description: It took Anna (Nicole Kidman) 10 years to recover from the death of her husband, Sean, but now she's on the verge of marrying her boyfriend, Joseph (Danny Huston), and finally moving on. However, on the night of her engagement party, a young boy named Sean (Cameron Bright) turns up, saying he is her dead husband reincarnated. At first she ignores the child, but his knowledge of her former husband's life is uncanny, leading her to believe that he might be telling the truth.

title: Queen at Sea
description: Starring Juliette Binoche, Tom Courtenay and Anna Calder-Marshall, Queen at Sea received its world premiere in competition at the Berlin International Film Festival earlier this year, where it won both the Silver Bear Jury Prize and the Silver Bear for Best Supporting Performance for both Courtenay and Calder-Marshall. The film follows Amanda (Binoche) and her stepfather, Martin (Courtney), at odds over a moral quandary involving Amanda’s mother, Leslie (Calder-Marshall). In the advanced stages of dementia, they quarrel over whether Leslie has lost all ability to make critical decisions in her own best interests, and, if so, who is responsible – a spouse, a child, an institution – for making such a determination? As Amanda and Martin are forced to make increasingly difficult choices, the repercussions spiral out of their control.

title: Manhunter (4K Restoration)
description: In celebration of the 40th anniversary of Michael Mann’s Manhunter , Mann’s final cut of the film returns in a newly restored 4K version. FBI criminal profiler Will Graham is called out of early retirement to assist on a deadly case involving a murderer known as the “Tooth Fairy.” After enlisting the help of imprisoned serial killer Dr. Hannibal Lecktor, Graham and the FBI are soon entangled in a menacing cat-and-mouse game.

title: The Unknown
description: Tickets Are Only Available via BFI London Film Festival Website from Tuesday 17 September 2026 10:00am: Click Here To Book Mesmerising, stimulating and unsettling, Niels Schneider and Léa Seydoux star in this body-swap tale that grapples with the existential implications of being trapped inside someone else’s physical being. David, a withdrawn photographer, meets a mysterious woman at a party. The two share a sexual encounter, only for David to wake up the morning after in the woman’s body. Arthur Harari’s (co-writer of Anatomy of a Fall) vertiginous, occasionally harrowing and ultimately rewarding ride eschews straightforward resolution in favour of a reflection on the aftermath of severing the link between body and mind. French Language with English subtitles

As Jack's writing goes nowhere and Danny's visions become more disturbing, Jack discovers the hotel's dark secrets and begins to unravel into a homicidal maniac hell-bent on terrorizing his family.

When a minor spell causes a fellow student to lose her hair, the girls grow power-mad.

title: REPORT TO THE COMMISSIONER
description:
A veteran New York City police officer dies during a botched undercover operation, leaving his inexperienced replacement to uncover what really happened. As the investigation unfolds, she becomes entangled in the city’s bureaucratic pressures, internal corruption, and the psychological toll of policing a system that resists transparency.
The film unfolds as a tense urban crime procedural, but its focus steadily shifts toward the emotional strain of its protagonist and the institutional forces surrounding her. Its New York setting is used less for spectacle and more as a dense, procedural environment where ambiguity and moral compromise dominate.

title: The Lost Children of Tuam

title: Outpost
description: Join us in the microcinema for Joe Lo Truglio’s nail-biting nightmare of the darkness that lurks in the woods and inside us. In his directorial debut feature, veteran comedian and actor Joe Lo Truglio displays his darker side with this satisfying slow burn of isolation, PTSD, and pyschosis. After a violent attack, a woman searches for strength in the solitude of a lookout job, but is overwhelmed by something darker. With a phenomenal cast and a slow and steadily unhinged descent into madness and feminine rage, culminating in a gory and hallucinatory climax, you won’t want to skip this trip to the nature…of revenge!

title: The Greg Proops Film Club Presents LET'S SCARE JESSICA TO DEATH
description: Jessica goes to the Connecticut countryside for some rest following her release from an institution where she has just recovered from a nervous breakdown. She arrives with her husband and friend, but the three find little relaxation. Instead, they become entangled in a creepy tale of the supernatural which involves murder, an attempted drowning, a séance, disappearing bodies, vampires and constant torment for Jessica. Her marriage is strained, she hears voices and she can’t escape the mental turbulence which haunts her – for there really is something after Jessica.

title: KEN RUSSELL'S THE DEVILS
description: An enduring masterpiece of cinema starring Oliver Reed and Vanessa Redgrave, KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption – and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is the uncut and unfiltered theatrical experience that Russell always envisioned – and the first time the film will be presented restored and in 4K.

title: The Devils
description: Ken Russell’s infamous adaptation of Aldous Huxley’s novel, about the apparent possession of a group of nuns after one (Vanessa Redgrave) accuses a priest (Oliver Reed) of collaborating with the devil, is at long last available in its full, uncensored splendor.

title: The Witches of Eastwick
description: Have a hell of a good time with Jack Nicholson, Michelle Pfeiffer, Susan Sarandon, and of course Cher in this devilishly sexy comedy based on the John Updike novel. Three single women in a picturesque Rhode Island village have their wishes granted — at a cost — when a mysterious and flamboyant man arrives in their lives and promises to grant them supernatural powers even as he charms each of them with his own. Now that they have their own powers, it’s time to turn the tables on their sinister seducer. With an iconic cast, fiercely funny dialogue, and tons of witchy fun, you’ll want to gather up your coven and get ready for all the sexy and savage sorcery!

title: NARROW ROOMS: LES FANTÔMES DU HARD + FISTULE
description: Most kinky queers in NYC know all about the Mineshaft, the legendary, long-shuttered NYC sex club in the Meatpacking District that was in operation from 1976 to 1985. But across the Atlantic, France’s first “hard” gay BDSM sex club was also called Mineshaft, and it has remained a sacred space for BDSM and fetish sex in Marseille since its opening in 1967. In this pair of short experimental documentaries, director Lazare Lazarus and friends excavate the archive left by the Mineshaft’s founder Jean-Pierre Fouque. Chapter 1 tells the story of the squatters who took over Fouque’s apartment after his death in 2022 and discovered his archive, while illuminating aspects of the club owner’s life – his lovers, political views, activism, and more. Chapter 2, co-directed with Lupa Charon Gateff, is more of a found-footage experimental porno mixtape, using the Mineshaft’s archive of hardcore gay porn and BDSM videotapes to take us into the dungeons of Europe, both real and imagined. These two shorts will be followed by Emre Busse’s FISTULE, which invites the audience into a realm where an anal fissure serves as a dramatic springboard, exposing the absurdity of societal norms with a mix of tragedy, camp, and sexuality. If you’re a fan of the films of Liz Purchell (ASK ANY BUDDY), Ryan A. White (RAW! UNCUT! VIDEO!), and Yann Gonzalez (KNIFE + HEART), you’ll find much to enjoy in this month’s program. Lazare Lazarus LES FANTÔMES DU HARD, CHAPTER 1 2023, 35 min, DCP. In French with English subtitles. Lazare Lazarus & Lupa Charon Gateff LES FANTÔMES DU HARD, CHAPTER 2 2024, 24 min, DCP. In French with English subtitles. Emre Busse FISTULE 2026, 17 min, DCP Total running time: ca 80 min.

title: Late Fame
description: Willem Defoe plays Ed Saxberger, a forgotten New York poet, who works in the post office. After an eager and flattering young admirer appears on his doorstep, Saxberger is beckoned into a coterie of twentysomething admirers who anoint him as a rediscovered genius. Intoxicated by the attention — and by the alluring presence of Gloria, the group’s “tragic heroine” — Saxberger gradually reckons with the authenticity of his newfound poetic circle. Kent Jones's thoughtful, witty film is a wistful yet unromantic look at a lost idea of downtown New York.

title: The History of Concrete
description: Tickets Are Only Available via BFI London Film Festival Website from Tuesday 17 September 2026 10:00am: Click Here To Book Having attended a Hallmark movie workshop, John Wilson applies his learnings to a documentary about concrete, albeit with a dryly funny and deceptively understated tone. After finding himself with too much time on his hands, documentarian Wilson attends a workshop on how to make Hallmark romcoms. It inspires him to apply the formula to a film investigating the story of concrete. Infused with Wilson’s trademark curiosity and wit, the film project introduces him to a variety of unusual people and places. The result is a wry and humane meditation on the modern world. These screenings will be presented with Descriptive Subtitles.

Based on the true story, and featuring a powerful performance from Monica Dolan, THE LOST CHILDREN OF TUAM is a deeply moving portrait of one woman’s fight for justice.

title: Verity
description: Struggling writer Lowen Ashleigh is hired as a ghostwriter for renowned author Verity Crawford under mysterious circumstances, but her assignment takes a dark turn after discovering chilling autobiographical notes. Faced with a series of deadly family secrets, Lowen struggles to separate fiction from reality, while also blurring the lines with Verity’s husband, Jeremy.

title: Weapons
description: When all but one child from the same class mysteriously vanish on the same night at exactly the same time, a community is left questioning who or what is behind their disappearance.

title: BAD LIEUTENANT
description:
A corrupt New York City police lieutenant spirals through a world of drugs, gambling, and moral decay, abusing his authority while sinking deeper into self-destruction. When a brutal crime shocks the community, he becomes obsessed with the case, confronting questions of guilt, redemption, and faith as his own life unravels.
Abel Ferrara’s film is raw and confrontational, driven by an intense central performance and an unflinching look at addiction and spiritual crisis. Its loose, almost documentary-like style gives the story a sense of immediacy, pushing the character’s descent into something deeply uncomfortable and difficult to shake.

title: The Social Reckoning
description: Explores Facebook's internal practices, spread of false information, impact on teen mental health, and connection to January 6 Capitol events.

title: The Social Reckoning
description: A companion piece to the hit film The Social Network, Sorkin’s original screenplay is based on the events that gave rise to the Wall Street Journal’s shocking exposé The Facebook Files. The film is inspired by the true story of how Frances Haugen (Madison), a young Facebook engineer, enlists the help of Jeff Horwitz (White), a Wall Street Journal reporter, to go on a dangerous journey that ends up blowing the whistle on the social network’s most guarded secrets.

title: Supernatural             / Terror Aboard
description: Finding himself a hot commodity after the success of his Bela Lugosi favorite White Zombie , director Victor Halperin moved to Paramount for his next scare outing, Supernatural . What should have been a casting coup with loaned-out-from-Fox star Carole Lombard reportedly made neither the actress or the director happy. Nevertheless, Lombard is great as Roma, a woman who inherits a fortune after her brother dies, then immediately becomes the target of a fake medium, Bavian (Alan Dinehart), who promises a spiritual reunion. Coincidentally, triple murderess Ruth Rogen (Vivienne Osbourne) is fried in the electric chair and the prison releases her body to a scientist (H. B. Warner) for research. Once he attempts to resuscitate her, the electric current releases her soul to immediately possess Roma. Roma’s beau (Randolph Scott) is alarmed at her abrupt change. Forced to believe in the transference, he does his best to free her before Ruth’s spirit can avenge herself on her enemies – especially spiritualist Bavian.

title: Too Many Beasts
description: Tickets Are Only Available via BFI London Film Festival Website from Tuesday 17 September 2026 10:00am: Click Here To Book In this deliciously unhinged mash-up of rural thriller and dark comedy, enormous wild boars create havoc in a small French town. Farmers and hunters are openly at war in the rural town of Sérieux. Wild boars are ruining crops and putting everyone on edge. When a local farmer mysteriously disappears, gendarme Fulda is put on the case. As he reluctantly teams up with psychologist Stéphane, the investigation gradually spirals out of control, and so does this offbeat and absurdly funny comedy. French Language with English subtitles

title: Okja
description: The titular beast is a gentle, lumbering, lovable “super pig” created by big agribusiness, peacefully raised in the South Korean countryside by young Mija (Ahn Seo-hyun) before being spirited off to the US, sweeping both pet and owner into a conflict between animal rights activists and mercenary corporate forces. A dark science fiction fable, its impressive ensemble cast includes Tilda Swinton, Paul Dano, and Jake Gyllenhaal. “[Okja] represents a departure toward a different type of image, a different texture and look: something very blue and metallic, with lots of compressed cityscapes and a bit of gold in the flesh tones… [Visual effects supervisor Erik de Boer] sat in with us [during the color grading] where we took every single shot of Okja in the film and treated each one individually for aspects of color and light.” —Darius Khondji Part of Radical Chiaroscuro: The Work of Darius Khondji

title: Critters
description: The battle began in another galaxy. It’s about to end in the Brown’s backyard. When a pack of pint-sized, piranha-teethed alien furballs land in small town Grover’s Bend, they’ll mischievously munch through everything they can. Now a farming family will have to put up the fight of their lives, with the aid of a pair of intergalactic bounty hunters, if they’re going to survive their encounter with these calamitous critters in one of the decade’s most entertaining creature feature horror comedies.

title: Strangers on a Train
description: “Criss cross.” Hitchcock’s adaptation of Highsmith’s 1951 page-turner kicks off with a casual encounter that reads like a same-sex pickup, as tennis star Guy Haines (Farley Granger) inadvertently agrees to “swap murders” with preening rich kid Bruno Anthony (Robert Walker, in a career performance), and continues through some of the finest set pieces of Hitch’s career: a tennis match at Forest Hills, Bruno stalking his prey through a vulgar county fair, and an out-of-control carousel. “In Hitchcock, the people you meet on trains can spell romance, adventure, or, in the case of Strangers on a Train’s Guy Haines, a colossal headache! Tip: beware anyone wearing spectator shoes.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue Part of Trains: Local Routes

title: Mouse
description: Tickets Are Only Available via BFI London Film Festival Website from Tuesday 17 September 2026 10:00am: Click Here To Book Katherine Mallen Kupferer and Sophie Okonedo excel in this moving drama about facing up to life in the aftermath of a tragedy. Lifelong friends Callie and Minnie are like ying and yang: one loud and popular, the other shy and quiet. Abruptly forced out from her friend’s shadow, it’s finally time for Minnie to figure out who she is on her own terms. Kupferer and Okonedo’s performances drive this beautiful film that’s guaranteed to have audiences alternating between crying and laughing out loud.

title: Alien (Theatrical Cut)
description: In deep space, the crew of the commercial starship Nostromo is awakened from their cryo-sleep capsules halfway through their journey home to investigate a distress call from an alien vessel. The terror begins when the crew encounters a nest of eggs inside the alien ship. An organism from inside an egg leaps out and attaches itself to one of the crew, causing him to fall into a coma.

title: ROMANCE X
description:
A schoolteacher enters into an emotionally detached relationship with a man who refuses physical intimacy, leading her to pursue a series of increasingly explicit encounters outside the relationship in an attempt to understand her own desires and frustrations. As she moves through different sexual experiences, questions of control, vulnerability, and emotional fulfillment begin to dominate her life.
Catherine Breillat approaches the material with a confrontational directness that treats sexuality as both psychological terrain and philosophical inquiry. Rather than building toward conventional eroticism, the film maintains a cool, analytical tone that turns intimacy into a site of emotional exposure, imbalance, and self-examination.
