title: Socrates
description: Beginning in the mid-’60s and ending with his death in 1977, Rossellini committed himself to producing a series of films, telefilms, and serial works that would together constitute a narrative of human progress and the history of ideas from aleolithic to present times. Socrates, initiating a tetralogy of works on epoch-defining thinkers, sets its scene in an Athens humbled by Sparta and increasingly irritated by the prickly, prodding philosopher in their midst, finally determined to silence him. Using out-of-vogue in-camera effects to transform an ancient Spanish village into Athens, probing scenes with his customized, remote-controlled Pancinor zoom, and employing a dirge-like electronic score by Mario Nascimbene, Rossellini gives us a singular vision of antiquity, one that’s downright avant-garde. Part of Classical Cinema

title: Midnight in Paris
description: Screenwriter, would-be novelist, and romantic-at-heart Owen Wilson, on vacation in the City of Lights with level-headed fiancée Rachel McAdams, sets out on his own one night after a wine tasting and finds himself suddenly in the Jazz Age Paris of Fitzgerald and Hemingway, Dali and Picasso—an invigorating draught of bohemian freedom that sets our protagonist to seriously interrogating his life choices. “We talked about pushing the color even more in the period scenes, in order to distinguish them from the present-day ones. The Paris of today would be normal and generic, bland and desaturated, and when you entered the Paris of the 1920s the colors would be more warm, lush and flamboyant, with lots of brown and gold and red.” —Darius Khondji Part of Radical Chiaroscuro: The Work of Darius Khondji

title: By Design
description: Upon seeing a gorgeous chair in a showroom, Camille (Juliette Lewis) realises that she truly envies the life of this perfect piece of furniture. If only she could be someone’s favourite thing. When she and the chair swap forms, Camille learns that she is better liked as an inanimate object than she was as a person: her mother (Betty Buckley) finds her to be a better listener, and her best friends (Samantha Mathis and Robin Tunney) enjoy a newfound, friction-free rapport. As the chair, Camille is unable to speak or move and winds up in the hands of Olivier (Mamoudou Athie), a minimalist bachelor who gradually becomes romantically fixated on his elegant new possession. Narrated by Melanie Griffith, this modern fable celebrates the messiness of female interiority with deadpan humour, surrealist flourishes, and interpretative dance numbers. An absurdist spin on the body-swap comedy, By Design is a bold new work from singular filmmaker Amanda Kramer.

title: Tokyo: The Last War
description: In 1945, after the horrific fire-bombings of the Pacific War levels Japan to the ground, the government consults spiritual psychics to aid them in winning the war. Unfortunately, the souls’ resentment and agony of the victims culminate together to revive the evil Onmyoji, Yasunori Kato. Only a young, psychically imbued priests’ apprentice will dare fight the evil magician.

title: Godzilla Minus Zero
description: Tickets Are Only Available via BFI London Film Festival Website from Tuesday 17 September 2026 10:00am: Click Here To Book The sequel to Takashi Yamazaki’s acclaimed 2023 film is a true cinematic spectacle that’s sure to grip fans of Godzilla, as well as newcomers to the franchise. Japan, 1949. Pilot Kōichi, his wife Noriko and adoptive daughter Akiko are attempting from recover from Godzilla’s recent attacks. But just as everything seems settled, a new danger emerges. Meanwhile, at the bottom of the sea, something is stirring. The first Japanese film to be shot for IMAX, Godzilla Minus Zero combines high-octane thrills with more than a little heart. Japanese Language with English subtitles

title: Halloween (1978) + Halloween II (1981) • Double Feature
description: HALLOWEEN (1978): Fifteen years after murdering his sister on Halloween Night 1963, Michael Myers escapes from a mental hospital and returns to the small town of Haddonfield, Illinois to kill again. HALLOWEEN II (1981): After failing to kill stubborn survivor Laurie and taking a bullet or six from former psychiatrist Dr. Sam Loomis, Michael Myers has followed Laurie to the Haddonfield Memorial Hospital, where she’s been admitted for Myers’ attempt on her life. The institution proves to be particularly suited to serial killers, however, as Myers cuts, stabs and slashes his way through hospital staff to reach his favourite victim. Presented with a 10-15 minute break between features

description:
While hiding in her lover Terry’s apartment, Sylvia witnesses a violent attack from his bedroom window. To protect their affair, Terry tells the police that he saw it himself - a gallant lie that collapses under scrutiny and places both the witness and the surviving victim in mortal danger.
Before
L.A. Confidential
, Curtis Hanson fashioned this deliciously contrived Hitchcockian neo-noir, casting Steve Guttenberg against type alongside Isabelle Huppert and Elizabeth McGovern in a tightening web of voyeurism, guilt and murder.

description: Directed by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, two of the co-directors of the 2024 Oscar-winning documentary No Other Land , Naza reveals the systems behind Israel’s bombing of Gaza and its mass killing of Palestinian civilians. Winner of Special Jury Prize at the 2026 Venice Film Festival.

title: Minority Report
description: Based on a Philip K. Dick short story, Spielberg’s wheeling, virtuoso science-fiction thriller stars Tom Cruise as an investigator of “PreCrime” who specializes in arresting criminals before they’ve done the deed in near-future Washington, DC. They’re still working on the jetpacks, but the film’s vision of a world run on touchscreens and bombarded with targeted advertising already looks frightfully prescient.

title: Paris Was a Woman
description: Drawing on newly discovered home movies and a rich bounty of archival materials, Schiller’s trailblazing documentary, now marking its 30th anniversary, offers up a vibrant and vivacious evocation of the community of female artists and culturati of all stripes—among their number Gertrude Stein, Alice B. Toklas, Djuna Barnes, and Colette—who called Paris’s Left Bank home in the first decades of the previous century. A film that acts on the viewer like a tonic draught of fresh air, Paris Was a Woman is an enthralling evocation of one of the most storied periods in the history of the City of Light and of an anything-goes bohemian enclave that fostered both personal and creative liberation. New 4k Restoration created by IndieCollect in association with Women’s Film Preservation Fund A Zeitgeist Films release Q&A with filmmakers Greta Schiller and Andrea Weiss moderated by broadcast journalist Laura Flanders on Friday, October 16th Q&A with filmmakers Greta Schiller and Andrea Weiss moderated by Jane Gaines, Founder of Columbia University’s Women Film Pioneers Project, on Saturday, October 17th Introduction by Sandra Schulberg, President of IndieCollect, on Sunday, October 18th Book signing of Paris Was A Woman with author Andrea Weiss following all three screenings

title: MULTI-MEDIA RESOURCE CENTER PGM 1: CONFESSIONS AND SEX HISTORIES
description: The openness and non-judgement that characterized the National Sex Forum meant that the films it produced depicted not only sex acts without scripting or simulation, but also frank discussions of participants’ sexual desires and experiences. Most straightforward in its treatment of these discussions is WARDELL POMEROY TAKES A SEX HISTORY, in which the titular doctor and former Alfred Kinsey collaborator interviews sexologist-in-training Janice Epp on her past relationships, sexual preferences, childhood awareness of puberty, present-day masturbation habits, and other aspects of her sexual identity. In this program, SEX HISTORY is accompanied by three more erotic portraits, each of them both candid and playful. Betty Brown & Rikki Ripp SEXUAL FANTASY PARTY (1973, 12 min, SD-video-to-DCP) Honey Lee Cottrell SWEET DREAMS (1979, 14 min, 16mm-to-DCP. Featuring Patrick Califia.) Laird Sutton WARDELL POMEROY TAKES A SEX HISTORY (1977, 35 min, 16mm) Curt McDowell CONFESSIONS (1972, 11 min, 16mm) Total running time: ca. 75 min. Introduced by film historian and programmer Elizabeth Purchell.

description: Set against the backdrop of mass protests in Paris, Case 137 follows Stéphanie, a meticulous internal affairs investigator working on the case of a teenager severely wounded by police fire. As she searches for the truth her inquiry collides with institutional resistance and pressure mounts as the case takes a personal turn when she discovers the victim is from her hometown.

title: The Idiot(s)
description: Tickets Are Only Available via BFI London Film Festival Website from Tuesday 17 September 2026 10:00am: Click Here To Book Aimee Lou Wood and Johnny Flynn are superb as Anna and Fyodor Dostoevsky in Małgorzata Szumowska and Michał Englert’s acerbic and joyful period film. Anna Dostoevsky loves her husband Fyodor. Fyodor loves his wife, but he also loves gambling and booze. Living in self-imposed exile in Germany, Fyodor’s biggest obstacle to creative progress is himself. Anna tries desperately to rid him of his procrastination so he can deliver a new novel and they can avoid destitution. Sending up the myth of the male genius, The Idiot(s) is also a beautiful love story about the writer and the wife that saved him. English and French Language with English subtitles

title: MULTI-MEDIA RESOURCE CENTER PGM 2: ACTIVE PARTNERS
description: ACTIVE PARTNERS: FOUR FILMS ON SEX AND DISABILITY Reflecting on the National Sex Forum (NSF) and Multi-Media Resource Center (MMRC), Ted McIlvenna often said that his proudest achievement was his work producing films on the sexuality of people with disabilities. These films dealt frankly with a subject seldom addressed either in erotic and sexually explicit cinema or in educational media about physical disability. They used a combination of candid narration and explicit visuals to explore the possibilities of sexual expression for disabled people, particularly those with able-bodied partners. The first two films in this program were directed by Laird Sutton for the NSF, while the latter two were produced by the University of Minnesota and San Francisco State University, and distributed by the MMRC. Laird Sutton JUST WHAT CAN YOU DO (1972, 23 min, 16mm) Laird Sutton TOUCHING (1972, 17 min, 16mm) Theodore M. Cole & Sandra S. Cole ARTIST’S FANTASY (1975, 15 min, 16mm) Marvin Silverman ACTIVE PARTNERS (1979, 8 min, 16mm) Total running time: ca. 70 min.

title: MYSTERY MOVIE
description:
Not for the easily offended, and strictly programmed for adult audiences only - our mystery films are eye-popping forays into the bold and bonkers world of psychotronic cinema. Expect the unacceptable.
Please consider yourself forewarned that these films may (and probably will) contain offensive and upsetting content. Do not attend if you are of a sensitive disposition.

title: Almost Famous
description: Before breaking into movies with his screenplay for Fast Times at Ridgemont High, Cameron Crowe was a teenage journalist with a regular byline in Rolling Stone magazine in the hedonistic early 1970s, and he draws from a deep well of memories of those pot-hazy days in his poignant-funny, semi-autobiographical Almost Famous, starring Patrick Fugit as a fresh-faced rock rag writer on the road with hesher idols Stillwater, Kate Hudson as road-warrior Stillwater superfan “Penny Lane,” and Philip Seymour Hoffman as an impassioned, opinionated, marvelously disheveled Lester Bangs. “In Almost Famous, a loose, affectionate look back on his earlier career as a teenage music journalist, Mr. Crowe has devoted a whole movie to the love of rock 'n' roll. The soul he lays open—a sweet, forgiving and generous one—is his own … He may be the least cynical director working in Hollywood today.” —A.O. Scott, The New York Times Introduction by Jon Caramanica and Joe Coscarelli of “Popcast” on Friday, October 16th Part of The New York Times presents Stop the Presses

title: The Terminator
description: Too many sequels and an incalculable cultural impact later, it’s sometimes forgotten what a hot and nasty little movie Cameron’s original Terminator was, dropping peak-physique Schwarzenegger into a sleazy Los Angeles of leather bars, punk rockers, and skid rows, where he quickly proceeds to killing cops by the score and tracking down mother-to-be of humankind’s savior Linda Hamilton. Working for the very last time with budget constraints, Cameron—and FX gurus Stan Winston and Gene Warren Jr.—deliver the goods and how, in a grimy lil’ chef d’oeuvre that gave us Cyberdine, Skynet, and a whole lexicon for discussing extinction-level singularity events. Part of A Cyberpunk Canon

title: BEGOTTEN
description: BEGOTTEN has no characters in the ordinary sense. Its final credits name three principal figures:  God Killing Himself. Mother Earth. Son of Earth — Flesh on Bone The entire film is what those names do to each other and to the earth. God Killing Himself tears open his body and dies. Mother Earth rises from what remains and takes his seed into herself. She gives birth to Son of Earth — Flesh on Bone. He is cast into a barren world, seized by the Nomads, tortured, killed and briefly returned to life by his mother. The Nomads destroy her too. The Robed Figures gather what remains of mother and son, grind their bodies down and return them to the soil. The ground flowers.

title: Akira
description: The post-apocalypse as playground for wayward youth. Street gangs ride up and down the highways, and it’s all fun and games until the city gets blown up. Again. The second banana gets big for his boots, and I mean BIG. You know it, you love it. A pounding soundtrack, the best drawn visuals money can buy and an ending for the ages.

title: From Dusk Till Dawn
description: George Clooney and Quentin Tarantino star as brothers on the lam from the law, hightailing it to Mexico with a kidnapped family in tow. But when they stop at an isolated strip club, they’ll have to try and survive From Dusk Till Dawn while battling the bar’s bloodthirsty denizens in Robert Rodriguez’s pulpy, stylish & hyper-violent cross-genre blast penned by its co-star. Featuring Harvey Keitel, Juliette Lewis & Salma Hayek plus an all-star cast of character actor greats including Cheech Marin, Fred Williamson, Danny Trejo and Tom Savini!

title: Wildwood
description: Tickets Are Only Available via BFI London Film Festival Website from Tuesday 17 September 2026 10:00am: Click Here To Book A forest inhabited by magical beings is the setting for this epic stop-motion saga from LAIKA Studios. When her baby brother is kidnapped by a large flock of crows, Prue hotfoots it to a local forest where a wondrous world of mystery and peril awaits. This breathtaking, hugely ambitious new film from LAIKA Studios (Coraline, Kubo and the Two Strings) is a masterpiece of stop-motion storytelling on an epic scale and quite unlike anything previously seen.

title: DOUBLE INDEMNITY
description: Barbara Stanwyck and Fred MacMurray star in this gripping film noir from director Billy Wilder. A calculating wife encourages her wealthy husband to sign a double indemnity policy proposed by smitten insurance agent Walter Neff. As the would-be lovers plot the unsuspecting husband’s murder, they are pursued by a suspicious claims manager (Edward G. Robinson). It’s a race against time to get away with the perfect crime in this heart-racing Academy Award-nominated masterpiece.

title: Okja
description: The titular beast is a gentle, lumbering, lovable “super pig” created by big agribusiness, peacefully raised in the South Korean countryside by young Mija (Ahn Seo-hyun) before being spirited off to the US, sweeping both pet and owner into a conflict between animal rights activists and mercenary corporate forces. A dark science fiction fable, its impressive ensemble cast includes Tilda Swinton, Paul Dano, and Jake Gyllenhaal. “[Okja] represents a departure toward a different type of image, a different texture and look: something very blue and metallic, with lots of compressed cityscapes and a bit of gold in the flesh tones… [Visual effects supervisor Erik de Boer] sat in with us [during the color grading] where we took every single shot of Okja in the film and treated each one individually for aspects of color and light.” —Darius Khondji Part of Radical Chiaroscuro: The Work of Darius Khondji

title: Scream
description: Wes Craven re-invented and revitalised the slasher-horror genre with this modern horror classic, which manages to be funny, clever and scary, as a fright-masked knife maniac stalks high-school students in middle-class suburbia. Craven is happy to provide both tension and self-parody as the body count mounts - but the victims aren't always the ones you'd expect.

title: Zvenygora
description: A hunt for the Scythian treasure trove of the title, a staple of Ukrainian folklore, becomes a jumping off point for a dizzying tour of a nation’s history, traditions, and fables, fleetly flitting between paeans to nature and man-made industry, a modern present and a mythic past, materialist fact and mystical fantasy. “My most interesting picture for me. I made it in one breath—a hundred days. Unusually complicated in structure, eclectic in form, the film gave me, a self-taught production worker, the fortuitous opportunity of trying myself out in every genre. It was a catalogue of all my creative abilities.” —Oleksandr Dovzhenko 35mm print courtesy of Austrian Filmmuseum, Vienna Original score and live musical accompaniment by medukha on Saturday, October 17th medukha features Asia Mieleszko on vocals, synth, accordion, piano, and drymba; Max Temnogorod on guitar and vocals; and Salina Kuo on guzheng. Part of Oleksandr Dovzhenko: Earth and Empire

title: Ken Russell's The Devils 35mm
description: An enduring masterpiece of cinema starring Oliver Reed and Vanessa Redgrave, THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption - and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. Fully restored and presented uncut and unfiltered as Russell always envisioned, the film screens from a stunning, brand new 35mm print.

title: Mad Monster Party?
description: Get ready for the wildest, cutest, stop-motion spooky soiree ever made when all your favorite monsters (and even a pint-sized Peter Lorre) get together to sing, dance, and get groovy in this Rankin and Bass animated classic! If you’ve been looking for the kiddo gateway to all the classic horror monsters, look no further than this adorable animated shindig from the people that animated all our favorite holidays! When Dr Frankenstein decides to retire from the monster-making business, he calls an international roster of monsters to a creepy convention to elect his successor. Everyone is there including Dracula, The Werewolf, The Creature, Dr Jekyll & Mr Hyde and many more. But Frankenstein’s title is not all that is at stake. The famous doctor has also discovered the secret of total destruction that must not fall into the wrong hands! Bring your little monster lovers, or your stop-motion stan besties for the party of the season!

title: SPANNING TIME
description: SPANNING TIME is a cinephilic love letter to the humble photobooth, drawing on one hundred years of cinema from around the world to illustrate the machine’s enduring and universal power both to freeze time and to transcend it. Created by film archivist and photobooth historian Brian Meacham, the film tells the story of these beloved machines, from their public debut in 1926, at the dawn of film’s sound era, to their return to popularity for a new generation a century later. Photobooths and cinema have grown up in parallel, and from silent comedies of the 1920s to American indies of the 1990s, from Hong Kong action to the French New Wave, the film illustrates the quiet power these machines have held for generations of friends, lovers, travelers, spies, convicts, exhibitionists and anyone else who needed a quick photo in the pre-selfie era. Through this encyclopedic collage made of selections from more than 150 films, both familiar and obscure, the versatile photobooth provides a space for privacy in public, creates lasting memories and becomes an unlikely hideout, time machine, even death chamber. Draw the curtain, raise the stool, insert a quarter and smile!

Paris Was a Woman
description: Drawing on newly discovered home movies and a rich bounty of archival materials, Schiller’s trailblazing documentary, now marking its 30th anniversary, offers up a vibrant and vivacious evocation of the community of female artists and culturati of all stripes—among their number Gertrude Stein, Alice B. Toklas, Djuna Barnes, and Colette—who called Paris’s Left Bank home in the first decades of the previous century. A film that acts on the viewer like a tonic draught of fresh air, Paris Was a Woman is an enthralling evocation of one of the most storied periods in the history of the City of Light and of an anything-goes bohemian enclave that fostered both personal and creative liberation. New 4k Restoration created by IndieCollect in association with Women’s Film Preservation Fund A Zeitgeist Films release Q&A with filmmakers Greta Schiller and Andrea Weiss moderated by broadcast journalist Laura Flanders on Friday, October 16th Q&A with filmmakers Greta Schiller and Andrea Weiss moderated by Jane Gaines, Founder of Columbia University’s Women Film Pioneers Project, on Saturday, October 17th Introduction by Sandra Schulberg, President of IndieCollect, on Sunday, October 18th Book signing of Paris Was A Woman with author Andrea Weiss following all three screenings

title: Scream 2
description: Sydney (Neve Campbell) and tabloid reporter Gale Weathers (Courteney Cox) survived the events of the first "Scream," but their nightmare isn't over. When two college students are murdered at a sneak preview of "Stab," a movie based on the events from the first film, it's clear a copycat killer is on the loose. Sydney and Gail, as well as fellow survivors Deputy Dewey (David Arquette) and Randy (Jamie Kennedy) have to find out who is behind this new murder spree, before they all end up dead.

title: Aerograd
description: Set in the Soviet Far East in the not-too-distant future, Dovzhenko’s film takes its title from a fictitious Siberian city that, as home to a strategically vital airfield, is targeted for conquest by the duplicitous forces of the Japanese Empire. A vision of technological utopianism and natural splendor, composed with dash and dynamism by cinematographer Eduard Tissé—a regular Eisenstein collaborator—in which the forces of the Revolution must contend with samurai saboteurs, counterrevolutionary kulaks, and rabble-rousing “Old Believer” Christians, pushing Soviet civilization into the wilds of the Pacific coast. Part spy thriller, part full-throated agitprop, part pantheistic bliss-out, and pure Dovzhenko. 35mm print courtesy of the Filmoteka Narodowa, Warsaw Part of Oleksandr Dovzhenko: Earth and Empire

title: Paper Tiger
description: Tickets Are Only Available via BFI London Film Festival Website from Tuesday 17 September 2026 10:00am: Click Here To Book James Gray goes back to his roots with this tense and atmospheric thriller, set in 1980s New York, which finds two brothers becoming embroiled with the Russian mafia. Irwin Pearl (Miles Teller, on top form) is an engineer and family man living in Queens. When his brother, a showboating ex-police officer (a magnetic Adam Driver), enlists him for a high paying job, things rapidly take a turn for the worse. Channelling the spirit of Sidney Lumet and Michael Mann, Gray’s own, distinctive directorial style is on full display in this instant classic of American crime cinema.

title: THE WITCHES OF EASTWICK
description: Academy Award winner Jack Nicholson stars as “the devil” opposite three witches played by superstar actresses Susan Sarandon, Academy Award winner Cher and Michelle Pfieffer in this offbeat thriller with a comic twist. In the quaint New England town of Eastwick, Alexandra, Jane and Sukie yearn to meet the man of their dreams. One rainy night, the women each express an overpowering need for just one dynamic male capable of challenging their liberated spirits, a man who could become their inspiration, their joy, their… everything. But take care with what you dream, for your dream may come true… as it does for the Witches of Eastwick.

title: IN THE REALM OF THE SENSES
description:
In 1930s Tokyo, former geisha Sada Abe begins an affair with Kichizo, the married proprietor of the inn where she works. Withdrawing from the world into rented rooms, the pair surrender themselves to an increasingly intense cycle of sex, jealousy and experimentation. Their mutual obsession gradually consumes every other part of their lives, carrying them towards an infamous and violent conclusion.
Based on the true story of Sada Abe, Nagisa Oshima’s IN THE REALM OF THE SENSES became an international sensation through its unprecedented combination of arthouse filmmaking and unsimulated sex. Produced as a French-Japanese collaboration to escape Japan’s censorship laws, the film was seized, banned and cut in numerous countries, while Oshima faced an obscenity trial at home. Fifty years later, it remains one of cinema’s most beautiful, confrontational and genuinely erotic studies of desire taken to its absolute limit.

title: The Insider
description: Mann’s white-knuckle drama of white-collar whistleblowing and callous boardroom skullduggery stars Russell Crowe as tobacco industry research scientist Dr. Jeffrey Wigand and his Heat star Al Pacino as the 60 Minutes producer desperate to get the good doctor to spill his secrets on air, leading to a clash of corporate titans between Brown & Williamson tobacco and CBS News. Media manipulation, profits over people, and businesses operating like rogue states—Mann didn’t invent the 21st century, but he sure saw it coming. “Once Hollywood had a favorite folk tale: that the lone truth teller battling political or corporate evil would triumph, however bitterly, when the facts became known. But in the chillingly contemporary world of The Insider it's not that simple. Almost every character in the story is compromised by business considerations. And in the film's vision of television news reporting, moral relativism is a big part of playing the game.” —Janet Maslin, The New York Times Q&A to follow with investigative journalist Lowell Bergman, portrayed by Al Pacino in the film, and Pulitzer Prize-winning reporter and podcast host Pablo Torre on Saturday, October 17th Part of The New York Times presents Stop the Presses

title: Stress Is Three
description: An automobile driving from Madrid to Almeria becomes a veritable pressure cooker in Saura’s formally audacious road movie. The passengers are a well-to-do industrialist, Fernando (Fernando Cebrián); his wife, Teresa (Chaplin, blonde and blasé); and Fernando’s architect colleague, Antonio (Juan Luis Galiardo), who Fernando is increasingly convinced has been having an affair with Teresa. Boasting some of the most blinding whites you’ll ever see in a black-and-white film, which only adds to its oneiric quality, the little-screened Stress is Three is an achievement on par with Saura and Chaplin’s very best, a withering critique of bourgeois hedonism and Spanish machismo ripe for rediscovery. Part of The Remembered Lives of G. Chaplin & C. Saura

title: EC: STRIKE
description: (STACHKA) Eisenstein’s interest in the Freudian father complex drives this psychological scenario in which non-actors step forward to acknowledge the viewer, illustrating Eisenstein’s desire to penetrate to the heart of cinema, sidestepping realism by ‘being real.’ Governmental restrictions made STRIKE the only completed film of a series intended to portray the road to revolution.

title: Scream 3
description: As bodies begin dropping around the set of 'STAB 3', a movie sequel based on the gruesome Woodsboro killings, Sidney Prescott and the other survivors are once again drawn into a game of a horror movie mayhem.

title: Look Back
description: Tickets Are Only Available via BFI London Film Festival Website from Thursday 1 October 2026 10:00am: Click Here To Book Spanning more than a decade, Hirokazu Koreeda’s tender coming-of-age story follows two girls who bond over their passion for and dream of becoming manga artists. Aspiring manga artist Fujino meets Kymoto, a shy admirer of her work. Seemingly opposites, they create the perfect team with their shared love of the form. But as their work draws praise and attention, they find themselves confronted with decisions that threaten their artistic collaboration. Koreeda’s striking love letter to friendship and the creative process offers keen insight into the craft. Content Warning: Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury.

title: MULTI-MEDIA RESOURCE CENTER PGM 3: GAY LIBERATION ON 16MM
description: From the late 1960s through the early 1980s, politically active gay and lesbian filmmakers like Arthur J. Bressan, Jr. and the Mariposa Film Group made didactic agitprop documentaries and narrative films on the liberation movement taking place in the streets around them. But alongside these works were smaller – in scope, length, and film gauge – and often more experimental works that shed light on the ideology of gay liberation in a less didactic mode. The two films in this program directed by Laird Sutton for the National Sex Forum take the form of casual, unstructured conversations between trios of gay men and lesbians. The others – which were, apart from FREEDOM DAY PARADE, distributed by the Multi-Media Resource Center – use documentary and satire to explore the concerns and culture of the gay liberation movement. Wakefield Poole FREEDOM DAY PARADE (1974, 11 min, 16mm-to-DCP) Laird Sutton GAY WOMEN SPEAK (1979, 15 min, 16mm. Featuring Phyllis Lyon.) Laird Sutton A GAY VIEW: MALE (1975, 17 min, 16mm) Jan Oxenberg A COMEDY IN SIX UNNATURAL ACTS (1975, 27 min, 16mm-to-DCP) Sharrie Farrell SANDY & MADELINE’S FAMILY (1973, 30 min, 16mm) Total running time: ca. 105 min.

title: Case 137
description: Set against the backdrop of mass protests in Paris, Case 137 follows Stéphanie, a meticulous internal affairs investigator working on the case of a teenager severely wounded by police fire. As she searches for the truth her inquiry collides with institutional resistance and pressure mounts as the case takes a personal turn when she discovers the victim is from her hometown.

title: Honeycomb
description: Married couple Teresa and Pedro (Chaplin and Per Oscarsson) live a life of antiseptic contentment in their chicly modern, minimalist home—that is until the delivery of a load of Teresa’s family’s furniture seems to jostle something loose in Teresa’s mind, leading her to press Pedro to join her in a series of “games” that have all the casual sadism of childhood in them, but also very real adult consequences. Saura’s first English-language feature is a harrowing vision of shifting power dynamics and mutually assured destruction played out in a conjugal hell, with Chaplin’s particular gift for radiating placid psychosis exercised to the fullest. Part of The Remembered Lives of G. Chaplin & C. Saura

title: LOST HIGHWAY
description: “We’ve met before, haven’t we?” A mesmerizing meditation on the mysterious nature of identity, LOST HIGHWAY, David Lynch’s seventh feature film, is one of the filmmaker’s most potent cinematic dreamscapes. Starring Patricia Arquette and Bill Pullman, the film expands the horizons of the medium, taking its audience on a journey through the unknown and the unknowable. As this postmodern noir detours into the realm of science fiction, it becomes apparent that the only certainty is uncertainty.

title: FRANKENHOOKER
description:
When a freak lawnmower accident reduces his fiancée Elizabeth to a collection of salvageable parts, amateur scientist Jeffrey Franken refuses to let death end their engagement. His plan is simple: find the perfect replacement body, assemble it piece by piece and bring Elizabeth back with a bolt of homemade electricity. Unfortunately, his search takes him into Times Square’s sex trade, and the resurrected woman who emerges has inherited more than one set of memories.
Frank Henenlotter’s delirious reworking of Frankenstein is a neon-pink mixture of gross-out horror, gutter comedy and unexpectedly tender romance. Patty Mullen’s electrically twitching performance is one of cult cinema’s great comic creations, while the film’s exploding bodies and handmade effects push bad taste into gleeful cartoon abstraction. Beneath the sleaze lies a warped warning about possession, reconstruction and the male urge to build the perfect woman.

title: EC: BATTLESHIP POTEMKIN
description: (BRONENOSETS POTEMKIN) “POTEMKIN used [Eisenstein’s] new set of rules to create what has been called the most perfect and concise example of film structure. Like STRIKE, [POTEMKIN] has no hero, only the masses, and no plot, only an incident plucked from the pre-history of the Revolution.” –Standish Lawder, EISENSTEIN AND CONSTRUCTIVISM “POTEMKIN was the first work to embody, in their most tangible form, various principles of construction peculiar to the medium: montage (or editing) and parallel action (the expansion of time through spatial manipulation); or, in sum, the purely formal deployment of objective action to create psychological dimensions. Eisenstein was not the first ‘film artist,’ but he was the first to be so pure, the first to use photography like painting in movement, photography like verbal imagery. As set down in his writings, his own theories inform us of this. Yet POTEMKIN must be seen to be believed.” –Parker Tyler

title: Broadcast News
description: Imagined by writer-director Brooks as a romantic comedy with a “new kind of heroine,” his follow-up to the wildly successful Terms of Endearment focuses on a love triangle between brilliant, career-driven television news producer Jane Craig (Holly Hunter); her conscientious but camera-shy colleague, Aaron (Albert Brooks); and telegenic station newcomer Tom (William Hurt), the two men competing for an anchor job and the attentions of the disarmingly intense Jane. “In his first film since his Oscar-winning Terms of Endearment, Mr. Brooks goes inside the offices and studios of the Washington bureau of a national television network to show us how things work. As exposes go, Broadcast News is gentle. It's far more amused than angry. Its wit is decently humane.” —Vincent Canby, The New York Times Introduction by Michael Barbaro of "The Daily" on Saturday, October 17th Part of The New York Times presents Stop the Presses

title: MULTI-MEDIA RESOURCE CENTER PGM 4: WOMEN’S LIB
description: THE PERSONAL AND THE POLITICAL: SEXUALITY, ROMANCE AND WOMEN’S LIB This program uses the cliché adage of second-wave feminism as a conceptual framework, bringing together films focused on individual and paired bodies with those concerned with the social and the political. Two playful Multi-Media Resource Center (MMRC) shorts that use visual and narrative tools to invert expectations of heterosexual gender performance are followed by films from the MMRC catalog (SELF-HEALTH, HOOKERS) and the Los Angeles underground (HIDDEN MEMORIES, I DON’T KNOW), departing in key ways from doctrinaire women’s liberation ideology. In these films, sexuality, romance, physical health, and communal solidarity are woven into a patchwork that renders women’s political and social identities more multifaceted than either dominant patriarchy or the mainstream feminist movement envisaged. Sam Joseph & Mariko Tse FIRST DATE (1977, 5 min, 8mm-to-DCP) Anne Severson I CHANGE I AM THE SAME (1969, 1 min, 16mm) Catherine Allen, Judy Irola, Allie Light, and Joan Musante SELF-HEALTH (1974, 23 min, 16mm-to-DCP) Jacqueline Frazier HIDDEN MEMORIES (1977, 10 min, 16mm-to-DCP) Penelope Spheeris I DON’T KNOW (1970, 20 min, 16mm-to-DCP) George Csicsery HOOKERS (1975, 25 min, 16mm) Total running time: ca. 90 min.

Returning as a ghost after a cruel betrayal results in her death, Eleanor and her sister deliver bloody vengeance on the man who took her life and murdered their father. Anna Biller, writer-director of The Love Witch, here delivers a rich visual feast. Gloriously shot on 35mm, this supernatural Gothic melodrama vibrantly brings 14th-century England to life.

title: By Design
description: Upon seeing a gorgeous chair in a showroom, Camille (Juliette Lewis) realises that she truly envies the life of this perfect piece of furniture. If only she could be someone’s favourite thing. When she and the chair swap forms, Camille learns that she is better liked as an inanimate object than she was as a person: her mother (Betty Buckley) finds her to be a better listener, and her best friends (Samantha Mathis and Robin Tunney) enjoy a newfound, friction-free rapport. As the chair, Camille is unable to speak or move and winds up in the hands of Olivier (Mamoudou Athie), a minimalist bachelor who gradually becomes romantically fixated on his elegant new possession. Narrated by Melanie Griffith, this modern fable celebrates the messiness of female interiority with deadpan humour, surrealist flourishes, and interpretative dance numbers. An absurdist spin on the body-swap comedy, By Design is a bold new work from singular filmmaker Amanda Kramer.

title: Medea (1988)
description: Based on an unfilmed screenplay by Carl Theodor Dreyer and, of course, Euripides’s tragedy of the same title, von Trier’s made-for-television film—save for two epiphanic eruptions—is uncharacteristically austere, the enfant terrible of Danish cinema making himself a medium for the Old Master’s vision, setting the source material in a pre-Christian Denmark. “An experimental film in the true sense of the word… Taking the greatest limitation of video—the medium’s lack of depth of field—Mr. von Trier turns it into a strength, flattening perspectives in a way that collapses his foreground characters into the tumultuous backgrounds (waves, wind-swept fields) that surround and dominate them.” —Dave Kehr, The New York Times Part of Classical Cinema

title: Akira
description: Iconic and game-changing, Akira is the definitive anime masterpiece! Katsuhiro Otomo’s landmark cyberpunk classic obliterated the boundaries of Japanese animation and forced the world to look into the future. Akira ‘s arrival shattered traditional thinking, creating space for future generations of ground-breaking movies.

title: Outpost
description: Join us in the microcinema for Joe Lo Truglio’s nail-biting nightmare of the darkness that lurks in the woods and inside us. In his directorial debut feature, veteran comedian and actor Joe Lo Truglio displays his darker side with this satisfying slow burn of isolation, PTSD, and pyschosis. After a violent attack, a woman searches for strength in the solitude of a lookout job, but is overwhelmed by something darker. With a phenomenal cast and a slow and steadily unhinged descent into madness and feminine rage, culminating in a gory and hallucinatory climax, you won’t want to skip this trip to the nature…of revenge!

title: HEY ARNOLD! THE MOVIE
description: A heartless industrialist has an evil plan: to level Arnold’s neighborhood and build a huge shopping mall. With time running out, someone needs to save the day. And that someone is Arnold.

title: Oldboy
description: Homer with a ball-peen hammer. Kidnapped and stuffed in a hole without explanation for 15 years of solitary confinement, when Oh Dae-su (Choi Min-sik) is suddenly let loose on the streets, he’s stone-cold pissed off and very, very dangerous. Winner of the Grand Prix at Cannes and an international pop phenomenon, Oldboy was a revenge thriller unlike any that had come before, featuring passages of pure bravura filmmaking (that one-shot hallway donnybrook!) and surreal sicko humor that’ll put you off of sushi for a while. “Put together with brutally uncompromising style [and] the cold-steel edge of a knife against your throat. A dark and thrillingly horrible adventure into the realms of the unthinkable.” —The Guardian Part of Classical Cinema

title: Blade Runner: The Final Cut
description: While so many special effects spectacles are lost in time like tears in the rain, Blade Runner remains the template for imagining the neon-wreathed downer of the future, every bit as influential in its vision as was Fritz Lang’s Metropolis over a half century before. Working from a novel by cult writer Philip K. Dick to create a film that would become the gold standard for sci-fi noir, director Scott shares credit here with “visual futurist” Syd Mead’s design concepts and synth pioneer Vangelis’s atmospheric score. Part of A Cyberpunk Canon

title: Ken Russell's The Devils 35mm
description: An enduring masterpiece of cinema starring Oliver Reed and Vanessa Redgrave, THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption - and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. Fully restored and presented uncut and unfiltered as Russell always envisioned, the film screens from a stunning, brand new 35mm print.

title: The Butterfly Effect
description: Change one thing. Change everything. Haunted by mysterious & traumatic childhood blackouts, a college psychology student discovers the ability to travel back to those personal points in time to alter the course of his life. But small changes could have huge consequences in this ambitious cult movie mind scrambler starring Ashton Kutcher and Amy Smart.

title: The Masque of the Red Death             / House of Usher
description: Death and debauchery reign in the castle of Prince Prospero, and when it reigns… it pours! Prospero has only one excuse for his diabolical deeds – the devil made him do it! But when a mysterious, uninvited guest crashes his pad during a masquerade ball, there’ll be hell to pay as the party atmosphere turns into a danse macabre! (MGM)

title: Abbott and Costello Meet Frankenstein
description: The Wolf Man tries to warn a dimwitted porter that Dracula wants his brain for Frankenstein monster's body.The Wolf Man tries to warn a dimwitted porter that Dracula wants his brain for Frankenstein monster's body.

title: Autumn Sonata
description: Ingmar and Ingrid, Bergman and Bergman, together at last. Sweden’s most popular export before the Volvo, in her final screen role, plays a world-renowned concert pianist who returns home to reunite with her now-married daughter (Liv Ullmann), long a distant second to her mother’s career ambitions, the two women exhuming old resentments and struggling towards reconciliation over the course of an emotionally draining 24 hours. “So unrelenting, so harrowing, that I walked out of the theater on shaking legs. If you’re open to the experience that Bergman means to provide, you may leave the film muttering a wrung-out ‘Whew!’ followed quickly by an appreciative ‘Wow!’” —Richard Corliss, Time Magazine Part of The Leaves Are Falling

title: Members' Screening: The Social Reckoning (15) (AD)
description: In this companion piece to The Social Network , screenwriter Aaron Sorkin returns to the Metaverse with a tale of the whistleblower who started the social media reckoning we're seeing play out today.

title: My Neighbour Totoro [Dubbed]
description: From the legendary Studio Ghibli, creators of Spirited Away and Ponyo, and Academy Award-winning director Hayao Miyazaki, comes a classic tale of…

title: The Aristocats
description: A big-screen outing for this flight of feline fun from the Disney vaults, the last animated feature to be signed off on by Walt himself is a purr-fect Parisian period piece featuring a family of nose-in-the-air cats who, after being kidnapped away from the accustomed baronial splendor of their home, have to rely on the streetwise wiles of alley cat O’Malley to keep them safe. Featuring animation supremely attentive to the syntax of kitty motion and the vocal talents of Eva Gabor and Scatman Crothers who gets to lead on the boppin' classic “Everybody Wants to Be a Cat.” Part of It Started With A Mouse: Hand-Drawn Classics on 35

title: The Exorcist (Extended Cut)
description: One of the most profitable horror movies ever made, this tale of an exorcism is based loosely on actual events. When young Regan (Linda Blair) starts acting odd -- levitating, speaking in tongues -- her worried mother (Ellen Burstyn) seeks medical help, only to hit a dead end. A local priest (Jason Miller), however, thinks the girl may be seized by the devil. The priest makes a request to perform an exorcism, and the church sends in an expert (Max von Sydow) to help with the difficult job.

title: Escape to Witch Mountain
description: Aliens! Kid-psychics! Black Cats! And Puppets! Come see the magically witchy movie that made Kim Richards a star! Tia and Tony are two orphaned youngsters with extraordinary psychic powers and the cutest black cat. Lucas Deranian poses as their uncle in order to get the kids into the clutches of Deranian’s megalomaniacal boss, evil millionaire Aristotle Bolt, who wants to exploit them. Can they escape the clutches of the evil capitalists and use their powers for good? Bring your little spellcasters to this fantastical adventure for your whole family or coven!

title: By Design
description: Upon seeing a gorgeous chair in a showroom, Camille (Juliette Lewis) realises that she truly envies the life of this perfect piece of furniture. If only she could be someone’s favourite thing. When she and the chair swap forms, Camille learns that she is better liked as an inanimate object than she was as a person: her mother (Betty Buckley) finds her to be a better listener, and her best friends (Samantha Mathis and Robin Tunney) enjoy a newfound, friction-free rapport. As the chair, Camille is unable to speak or move and winds up in the hands of Olivier (Mamoudou Athie), a minimalist bachelor who gradually becomes romantically fixated on his elegant new possession. Narrated by Melanie Griffith, this modern fable celebrates the messiness of female interiority with deadpan humour, surrealist flourishes, and interpretative dance numbers. An absurdist spin on the body-swap comedy, By Design is a bold new work from singular filmmaker Amanda Kramer.

title: Black Church Bay
description: Tickets Are Only Available via BFI London Film Festival Website from Thursday 1 October 2026 10:00am: Click Here To Book In a sleepy Welsh fishing village, Barry’s life starts to unravel after an intimate encounter in this gripping mystery drama starring Tom Cullen and Joe Locke. Barry has always kept his personal life tightly under wraps. But as hidden truths come to light, he is no longer able to control the double life he leads. Barry must decide what lengths he will go to cover up his private life and ultimately his true self. Black Church Bay is a tense and thought-provoking drama that affirms Rhys Marc Jones as an exciting queer filmmaker. Content advice: Contains scenes of nudity and sex

Fully restored and presented uncut and unfiltered as Russell always envisioned, the film screens from a stunning, brand new 35mm print.

title: Little Women
description: Winona Ryder would receive an Academy Award nomination for Best Actress for her role as the headstrong, literary minded Jo March in Armstrong’s perfectly enchanting adaptation of Louisa May Alcott’s 1868 novel of the same name, about the travails of the March sisters of Concord, Massachusetts, and their various suitors. Made with sweet-spirited good humor and exacting attention to period detail, with Trini Alvarado, Samantha Mathis, Kirsten Dunst, and Claire Danes rounding out the March clan, and Eric Stoltz, Gabriel Byrne, and Christian Bale among the men drawn to the glow exuded by the March homestead. “Solid, warming, bountiful, brimful of high spirits, a glowing treat that belongs at the top of any holiday movie shopping list.” —Boston Globe

title: All the President's Men
description: “All the President’s Men had to be on my list because it inspired me and so many other journalists to serve as watchdog press, and because so many recent events are reminiscent of Nixon and Watergate.” —Kimberley Reed Robert Redford and Dustin Hoffman star as newsmen Carl Bernstein and Bob Woodward in Pakula’s riveting retelling of the startling series of true events whereby the assignment of two Washington Post reporters to investigate the suspiciously urgent Republican response to what appears to be just an amateurish break-in at the Democratic Party National headquarters at the Watergate Hotel would lead to the toppling of a president. The process of investigative journalism rendered as high drama, its unerring eye for realistic detail extending to a scrupulous reproduction of the Post’s newsroom floor." Q&A with Carl Bernstein and Maggie Haberman, White House correspondent for The New York Times, moderated by Natalie Kitroeff of “The Daily” on Sunday, October 18th Part of The New York Times presents Stop the Presses

title: Hadestown: The Musical
description: The live theater capture of the hit musical Hadestown, which won eight Tony Awards in 2019 including Best Musical and the 2020 Grammy Award for Best Musical Theater Album, featuring the five original principals of the Broadway company. The genre-defying new musical blends modern American folk music with New Orleans-inspired jazz to reimagine a sweeping ancient tale. Following two intertwining love stories — that of young dreamers Orpheus and Eurydice, and that of King Hades and his wife Persephone —Hadestowninvites audiences on a hell-raising journey to the underworld and back.

title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem

title: Something Wicked This Way Comes
description: What would you give a man who could make your deepest dreams come true? When a strange carnival comes to a small, idyllic town, not all is as it first seems. But can two boys unravel the mystery? Walt Disney Productions brings Ray Bradbury’s classic tale to life in one of the key gateway horror films of the ‘80s.

title: Dance Umbrella Sunday Shorts: Spaces of Encounter (15*)
description: A programme of shorts selected by Omar Rajeh , bringing together works that explore the relationship between body, memory and place, revealing the social, political and emotional landscapes we inhabit.

title: THE MAN WITH THE PLAN + Q&A
description: A young student, Flea (Sophie Jenkin), discovers the 1942 Beveridge Report and its comprehensive vision for a better society. Her fantastical journey takes her amongst Beveridge's Five Giants - Want, Disease, Squalor, Idleness and Ignorance - and through politicians, ineffective policies and missed ...

title: ONE, TWO, THREE
description:
C. R. MacNamara, a Coca-Cola executive stationed in West Berlin, is charged with looking after his boss’s visiting daughter. When she secretly marries a fervent young East German communist, Mac launches a frantic scheme to turn her new husband into an acceptable capitalist son-in-law before her parents arrive.
Billy Wilder’s breathless Cold War farce stars James Cagney at full speed, firing off rapid dialogue, political satire and escalating comic chaos against a divided Berlin.

title: The Thing
description: In remote Antarctica, a group of American research scientists are disturbed at their base camp by a helicopter shooting at a sled dog. When they take in the dog, it brutally attacks both human beings and canines in the camp and they discover that the beast can assume the shape of its victims. A resourceful helicopter pilot (Kurt Russell) and the camp doctor (Richard Dysart) lead the camp crew in a desperate, gory battle against the vicious creature before it picks them all off, one by one.

title: A Tribute to Treehouse of Horror
description: D’oh! Spooky season just got more animated as Vidiots and our friends at Stonecutters LA are saluting one of the longest running Halloweenie television legacies ever – the brilliantly whacked-out Treehouse of Horror from The Simpsons . Join us as we screen clips from some of the best segments of its 30+ year run, host trivia for the Simpsons geek in your life (with prizes!), and chat with some special surprise guests from the Simpsons extended family! Come dressed as your favorite four fingered Simpsons character, there will be a costume contest as well as a raffle . Don’t miss this one of a kind afternoon of trivia, treats, tricks, and your favorite dysfunctional cartoon family!

title: CLUE
description: Here is the murderously funny movie based on the world-famous Clue board game. Was it Colonel Mustard in the study with a gun? Miss Scarlet in the billiard room with the rope? Or was it Wadsworth the butler? Meet all the notorious suspects and discover all their foul play things. You’ll love their dastardly doings as the bodies and the laughs pile up before your eyes.

title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother
description: Tickets Are Only Available via BFI London Film Festival Website from Tuesday 17 September 2026 10:00am: Click Here To Book Bassam Tariq follows Mogul Mowgli (LFF 2020) with this gripping, inventive thriller, featuring a commanding central performance by Oscar winner Mahershala Ali. An assassin and father of three, Latif’s life is turned upside down when his wife dies. He struggles to balance his two very different worlds, but when a hit goes south and as forces close in around him, he sets off on a desperate journey to protect his children. Amid all the mayhem, Tariq’s stylish and exhilarating thriller offers a tender portrait of grief and fatherhood, and a testament to maintaining one’s faith. English and Arabic Language with English Subtitles This screening will be presented with Descriptive Subtitles and will have Audio Description available on request. Content Warning: Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury.

title: Art Cinema for Tots: How to Play a Film
description: Born out of a commitment to the idea that it’s never too early to introduce kids to the pleasures of movies made outside of the commercial mainstream—and the suspicion that young audiences are often more open-minded and curious than their elders when it comes to such matters—Metrograph presents the latest iteration of Art Cinema for Tots, a celebration of handcrafted, kid-friendly films that reconcile the smart and the silly. In this edition, join us for How to Play a Film, a suite of enchanting, adventurous shorts, including Abbas Kiarostami’s early pedagogical documentary Orderly or Disorderly; Baby, D.A. Pennebaker’s document of a trip to the Central Park Zoo, and Francis Alÿs’s Reel/Unreel, which observes the game-playing of a group of Kabul children. Director of Programming (and mom) Inge de Leeuw describes the experience: “The sound levels will be dimmed, and there will be a gentle light on, creating a relaxed atmosphere where young viewers feel at ease. They won’t be confined to their seats; they can move around, explore, and enjoy the wonder of the big screen. It will be a playful, interactive cinematic journey, designed with little explorers in mind. Orderly or Disorderly (Abbas Kiarostami, 1981, 17 mins) Baby (D.A. Pennebaker, 1954, 6 mins) REEL/UNREEL (Francis Alÿs, 2011, 20 mins) Each ticket includes free admission for one child, if you’d like to bring more than one child per ticket, please email [email protected] to book a seat. This is a general admission screening with no reserved seating. Part of Screen Time at Metrograph

title: PERDITA DURANGO
description: Here, Perez reimagines Isabella Rossellini’s melancholic character into a tightly-coiled woman on the edge — one in love with an even crazier Bardem, who’s casually into blood rituals, bank/grave-robbing, extortion and wholesale slaughter. Gandolfini is just awesome as the bumbling FBI agent on their trail. This thing rocks.

title: Naza
description: Directed by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, two of the co-directors of the 2024 Oscar-winning documentary No Other Land , Naza reveals the systems behind Israel’s bombing of Gaza and its mass killing of Palestinian civilians. Winner of Special Jury Prize at the 2026 Venice Film Festival.

title: Reality Bites
description: Arguably the most consciously “Gen X” movie ever made, Stiller’s shambolically charming directorial debut stars Ryder as Lelaina Pierce, a university valedictorian whose postgraduate malaise threatens to become a full-fledged identity crisis when she’s faced with the choice between two very different eligible suitors: corporate climber Michael (Stiller) and slack motherfucker Troy (Ethan Hawke), the latter a staple of the Houston, Texas open mic circuit. Featuring a pip of a soundtrack (Juliana Hatfield Three! Lisa Loeb and Nine Stories!), career-best supporting work from Janeane Garofalo, and cameo appearances by Lemonheads frontman Evan Dando and Ryder’s then-beau, Soul Asylum’s Dave Pirner. Be there or be a cob nobbler.

title: EC: OLD AND NEW
description: (STAROYE I NOVOYE) With OLD AND NEW, also known as THE GENERAL LINE, Eisenstein developed and perfected his theories of “mise-en-cadre,” using the montage of characters in the foreground and background to conjure meanings, and “overtonal montage,” bringing silent film to its zenith.

title: RETURN TO THE TATLER + VARIETY
description: As part of our anniversary celebrations, we take a detour into the Rio’s saucy 1970’s years as the Dalston Tatler, one of London’s highest grossing porn cinema clubs with an uncensored grindhouse programme and a full burlesque striptease extravaganza stage show.  We delve into the lurid stories and ...

title: The Shining [UK Version]
description: Jack Torrance (Jack Nicholson) becomes winter caretaker at the isolated Overlook Hotel in Colorado, hoping to cure his writer's block. He settles in along with his wife, Wendy (Shelley Duvall), and his son, Danny (Danny Lloyd), who is plagued by psychic premonitions. As Jack's writing goes nowhere and Danny's visions become more disturbing, Jack discovers the hotel's dark secrets and begins to unravel into a homicidal maniac hell-bent on terrorizing his family.

title: MULTI-MEDIA RESOURCE CENTER PGM 5: BROUGHTON EC+
description: James Broughton, prolific poet-filmmaker and member of Anthology’s own Essential Cinema Selection Committee, was one of many Bay Area experimental filmmakers whose work was distributed by the Multi-Media Resource Center. Generally advertised in the “Erotic Fantasy” section of the distributor’s catalogs, Broughton’s films were recontextualized by their inclusion, their sensuality and spirituality understood as components of a holistic understanding of sexuality for the sex educator or therapist. In this special edition of Anthology’s Broughton Essential Cinema program, three characteristic works of the filmmaker’s late 60s-early 70s output are preceded by a very special entry in the National Sex Forum filmography, in which Broughton himself is bathed and massaged by erotic masseur Kenneth Ray Stubbs. Laird Sutton JAMES (1979, 10 min, 16mm) James Broughton THE BED (1968, 19 min, 16mm) James Broughton NUPTIAE (1969, 14 min, 16mm) James Broughton THE GOLDEN POSITIONS (1970, 32 min, 16mm) Total running time: ca. 80 min.

title: Club Kid
description: Tickets Are Only Available via BFI London Film Festival Website from Tuesday 17 September 2026 10:00am: Click Here To Book A jaded New York club promoter finds his messy lifestyle upended by the discovery that he has a son, in Jordan Firstman’s hilarious feature directorial debut. A decade of drinking, drugs and clubs is finally starting to take its toll on Peter. The unexpected arrival of an infant son means it’s finally time for him to get his life together. How hard can it be? The perfect skewering of millennial malaise that is also deeply touching, it’s easy to see why Club Kid was one of the most talked-about films at Cannes this year. This screening will be presented with Descriptive Subtitles. Content Warning: Contains flashing images, scenes of drug use and sex, and themes of suicide.

title: Case 137
description: Set against the backdrop of mass protests in Paris, Case 137 follows Stéphanie, a meticulous internal affairs investigator working on the case of a teenager severely wounded by police fire. As she searches for the truth her inquiry collides with institutional resistance and pressure mounts as the case takes a personal turn when she discovers the victim is from her hometown.

title: Paris Was a Woman
description: Drawing on newly discovered home movies and a rich bounty of archival materials, Schiller’s trailblazing documentary, now marking its 30th anniversary, offers up a vibrant and vivacious evocation of the community of female artists and culturati of all stripes—among their number Gertrude Stein, Alice B. Toklas, Djuna Barnes, and Colette—who called Paris’s Left Bank home in the first decades of the previous century. A film that acts on the viewer like a tonic draught of fresh air, Paris Was a Woman is an enthralling evocation of one of the most storied periods in the history of the City of Light and of an anything-goes bohemian enclave that fostered both personal and creative liberation. New 4k Restoration created by IndieCollect in association with Women’s Film Preservation Fund A Zeitgeist Films release Q&A with filmmakers Greta Schiller and Andrea Weiss moderated by broadcast journalist Laura Flanders on Friday, October 16th Q&A with filmmakers Greta Schiller and Andrea Weiss moderated by Jane Gaines, Founder of Columbia University’s Women Film Pioneers Project, on Saturday, October 17th Introduction by Sandra Schulberg, President of IndieCollect, on Sunday, October 18th Book signing of Paris Was A Woman with author Andrea Weiss following all three screenings

title: Ivan
description: In making his first sound film, Dovzhenko proved himself every bit as much an innovator in the realm of the aural as he had been in that of the visual, creating a rich sonic tapestry in this melic ode to the construction of the Dnipro Hydroelectric Station and the men and women conscripted into its accomplishment, among them the eponymous Ukrainian villager. (Some critics, however, observed that Dovzhenko took a little too much pleasure in the doings of Ivan’s antagonist, a layabout kulak who refuses to bust his hump slaving away for the glory of the state.) As influential, arguably, as Earth before it, on the Ukrainian poetic cinema of the 1960s, and an achievement of towering stature. 35mm print courtesy of Austrian Filmmuseum, Vienna Part of Oleksandr Dovzhenko: Earth and Empire

title: Ken Russell's The Devils 35mm
description: An enduring masterpiece of cinema starring Oliver Reed and Vanessa Redgrave, THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption - and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. Fully restored and presented uncut and unfiltered as Russell always envisioned, the film screens from a stunning, brand new 35mm print.

title: SCHINDLER'S LIST
description: Winner of seven Academy Awards including Best Picture and Best Director, this incredible true story follows the enigmatic Oskar Schindler, who saved the lives of more than 1,100 Jews during the Holocaust. It is the triumph of one man who made a difference and the drama of those who survived one of the darkest chapters in human history because of what he did.

title: ROY'S WORLD: BARRY GIFFORD'S CHICAGO
description: Hailed as “William Faulkner by way of B-movie film noir, porn paperbacks and Sun Records rockabilly,” poet, author and screenwriter Barry Gifford has given the world more than forty works, including the Sailor and Lula novels that inspired David Lynch’s WILD AT HEART. Featuring Willem Dafoe, Matt Dillon and Lili Taylor, ROY’S WORLD: BARRY GIFFORD’S CHICAGO brilliantly brings to life Gifford’s autobiographical collection of stories, capturing a vanished 1950s Chicago through a jazzy, impressionistic combination of beguiling archive footage, animation and spoken word.

title: EC: OCTOBER
description: (OKTYABR) “An imaginary document projected on actual locations, OCTOBER is the Soviet equivalent of the Sistine Chapel – an artist commissioned by the state has represented the sacred origins of the universe. Woodrow Wilson had famously hailed D.W. Griffith’s THE BIRTH OF A NATION (1915) as ‘history written with lightning,’ but Eisenstein’s cosmic newsreel cum theoretical film poem goes beyond THE BIRTH OF A NATION, as well as his own BATTLESHIP POTEMKIN, in drafting the past to serve the requirements of the present. No less than the revolutionaries who made October, Eisenstein understood himself as history’s tool. Thus consecrated to the Bolshevik faith, his OCTOBER is a perfect tautology – it clarifies and improves on history in the service of objective historical necessity.” –J. Hoberman, THE RED ATLANTIS: COMMUNIST CULTURE IN THE ABSENCE OF COMMUNISM

title: MULTI-MEDIA RESOURCE CENTER PGM 6: EROTIC FANTASY
description: EROTIC FANTASY: BEESON AND BEYOND While the bulk of the National Sex Forum’s (NSF) in-house productions were directed by Laird Sutton, a Methodist minister like co-founder Ted McIlvenna, the organization’s more experimental output was mostly helmed by Constance (or Coni) Beeson. A photojournalist-turned-filmmaker, Beeson’s films on women’s sexuality were cited as inspirations by her contemporary Barbara Hammer. In this program, presented in chronological order, three Beeson films produced for the NSF, each depicting sexual encounters layered in double-exposure and pastoral imagery, are bookended by classic works of expressive erotic cinema that, though not distributed by the Multi-Media Resource Center, would be at home in its catalogs. José Rodriguez-Soltero JEROVI (1965, 11 min, 16mm. Preserved by Anthology Film Archives with support from the Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts.) Coni Beeson THE NOW (1970, 14 min, 16mm) Coni Beeson HOLDING (1971, 15 min, 16mm) Coni Beeson STAMEN (1972, 15 min, 16mm) Chick Strand FEVER DREAM (1979, 7 min, 16mm) Total running time: ca. 65 min.

title: Possession
description: After Anna (Isabelle Adjani) reveals to her husband, Mark (Sam Neill), that she is having an affair, she leaves him and their son. Mark is devastated, and seeks out Heinrich (Heinz Bennent), the man who cuckolded him, only to receive a beating. After a series of violent confrontations between Mark and Anna, Mark hires a private investigator to follow her. Anna descends into madness, and it's soon clear that she is hiding a much bigger secret -- one that is both inexplicable and shocking.

While filming over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the question that was asked by our grandpar...

title: THE DOLL
description:
“A study of erotic delusion”
Lonesome night watchman Lundgren works the graveyard shift at a Stockholm shopping mall and in desperation steals a mannequin to bring home to keep him company. One night the mannequin comes alive, fulfilling his darkest fantasy but also questioning his grasp on reality. As the chorus of nosy neighbours starts suspecting something untoward in his dingy attic flat, Lundgren’s life begins to unravel.
Arne Mattsson’s sprawling resumes spans over 60 films including a proto-giallo detective series, breezy folk comedies and pulpy-thrillers, but in his mid-career flurry of films he directed Vaxdockan aka The Doll: a darkly poetic arthouse-creeper. British censors were swift to ban it due to “indecency” giving it the infamous “BANNED IN ENGLAND” tagline, but it’s lurid marketing obscured what is a beautifully realised psycho-fairytale about urban alienation and agalmatophilia. With strange and intense performances by Per Oscarsson and (Bergman actress turned “Swedish Sin” icon) Gio Petré, this is undoubtedly the crown jewel of Mattsson’s oeuvre.
Programmed and introduced by Harry Thorfinn-George

title: Once Upon a Time in China
description: No one wields a ’Scope frame with quite the same flexibility and dynamism as Hark, and the spectacular, Sergio Leone–inspired Once Upon a Time in China—perhaps the crucial film of the 1990s wuxia revival—shows Hark at his most flamboyant, keeping up with the human whirlwind that is Jet Li, here in the role of physician, martial artist, and 19th-century Cantonese folk hero Wong Fei-hung, who’s pitted against unscrupulous gangsters, human traffickers from the West, and his inconvenient feelings for “13th Aunt” Rosamund Kwan. Showstopping set pieces come fast and furious en route to a shoot-the-works shipboard finale; a monumental work of kinetic cinema. Part of Don't Play with Fire: The Films of Tsui Hark

title: Poem of the Sea
description: Based on a script left behind by Dovzhenko at his death, Poem of the Sea was finally filmed by his widow, Solntseva, a formidable filmmaker in her own right, her stated intention to work wholly “in accordance with Dovzhenko’s artistic conception, putting aside every trace of my own individual vision.” A companion piece of sorts to Ivan, likewise dealing with the construction of a dam and its impact on the surrounding countryside—in particular one soon-to-be-submerged village, birthplace of one General Fedorchenko (Boris Livanov), whose arrival for a visit in its final days stirs long-dormant memories. The feat of civil engineering documented here is the Kakhovka Hydroelectric Power Plant, opened in 1956 and destroyed by Russian forces in 2023, with catastrophic ecological results. 35mm SovScope print courtesy of Austrian Filmmuseum, Vienna Part of Oleksandr Dovzhenko: Earth and Empire

title: The Debut
description: Tickets Are Only Available via BFI London Film Festival Website from Tuesday 17 September 2026 10:00am: Click Here To Book For LFF 2026’s curtain call, writer-director Jesse Eisenberg delivers a rapturous and raucously funny love letter to community theatre, featuring a luminous lead performance by Julianne Moore. Quiet housewife Mona has become a supporting role in her own life; her husband barely acknowledges her presence and their children are on the cusp of fleeing the nest. So when, on an impulse, she auditions for a local production of an original musical, Mona suddenly finds herself in the spotlight when she is cast in a leading role, as Miss Danielle. However, she is unprepared for the theatrical hurricane that is Jerry, her enigmatic director and the ‘biggest name in New Jersey community theatre’. As she continues to be creatively pushed by him, Mona finds herself going to extreme lengths to unlock her character. The Debut once again finds the perfect balance between humour and drama that Eisenberg delivered with his previous films A Real Pain (LFF 2024) and When You Finish Saving the World. It’s both sparklingly witty and laugh-out-loud funny, while every scene works to build on the emotional undercurrents and heartbreaking revelations that make the characters so credible. This time, Eisenberg’s talents even stretch to writing the songs for the fictional stage musical. Moore is in her element, giving one of her finest performances, while Paul Giamatti’s Jerry continues his run from The Holdovers as the master of dramedy. Ultimately, The Debut is an elegant and intelligent coming-of-older-age story about how it’s never too late to find our true selves, and the redemptive powers of community and art. Take your seats... It’s showtime! This screening will be presented with Descriptive Subtitles and will have Audio Description available on request.

title: BEGOTTEN
description: BEGOTTEN has no characters in the ordinary sense. Its final credits name three principal figures:  God Killing Himself. Mother Earth. Son of Earth — Flesh on Bone The entire film is what those names do to each other and to the earth. God Killing Himself tears open his body and dies. Mother Earth rises from what remains and takes his seed into herself. She gives birth to Son of Earth — Flesh on Bone. He is cast into a barren world, seized by the Nomads, tortured, killed and briefly returned to life by his mother. The Nomads destroy her too. The Robed Figures gather what remains of mother and son, grind their bodies down and return them to the soil. The ground flowers.

title: THE HEROIC TRIO
description:
Newborn babies are disappearing across a nameless city, abducted by the Invisible Woman and delivered to a monstrous underground master searching for an imperial heir. Standing in her way are Wonder Woman, a masked vigilante hiding her identity from her police-inspector husband, and Thief Catcher, a shotgun-wielding mercenary willing to work for whoever pays. As their shared histories emerge, the three women are drawn together against an enemy commanding an army of killers beneath the city.
Michelle Yeoh, Anita Mui and Maggie Cheung join forces in Johnnie To’s delirious collision of superhero fantasy, wuxia action, gothic horror and Hong Kong New Wave style. Produced and choreographed by Ching Siu-tung, THE HEROIC TRIO tears through motorcycle stunts, invisibility cloaks, flying blades, cannibalistic henchmen and spectacular wirework with the untamed invention of Hong Kong cinema at its early-1990s peak.

title: How Deep Is Your Love
description: Special Screening followed by Q & A with Director Eleanor Mortimer, producer Jacob Thomas, and Dr Muriel Rabone, co-producer and marine biologist. Far out on the open sea, an expedition vessel travels toward one of the most remote regions on Earth, the Clarion–Clipperton Zone, twelve days from the nearest land. Here, darkness, silence, and immense depths conceal an unexplored universe. How Deep Is Your Love follows a group of marine biologists trying to understand life in this unknown world, while grappling with the question of whether their presence risks harming what they seek to protect. A visually hypnotic and deeply absorbing journey in which every discovery reshapes our understanding of the planet. Eleanor Mortimer has created a nature documentary like no other. How Deep Is Your Love weaves awe-inspiring footage of this breathtaking realm with a looming sense of urgency as mankind’s progress threatens to upend these delicate eco-systems.

title: MY FATHER'S SHADOW

title: Cinematic Void Presents DR. BUTCHER, MD
description: DR. BUTCHER, M.D. sparked riots on 42nd Street, spawned a generation of VHS gorehounds and forever set an insane standard for Italian mad doctor/zombie/cannibal carnage worldwide. Ian McCulloch (ZOMBIE) and Alexandra Delli Colli (THE NEW YORK RIPPER) star in this blood orgy of gut-munching, eyeball-gouging and face-chopping originally known as ZOMBIE HOLOCAUST, which a notorious American distributor would then re-edit, re-title and re-release as a certified grindhouse masterpiece. As a bonus, this is one of the rare Italian cannibal movies that features zero onscreen animal violence.

title: MULTI-MEDIA RESOURCE CENTER PGM 7: PATTERN FILMS, PART 1
description: The majority of Laird Sutton’s work for the National Sex Forum (NSF) consisted of “pattern films,” so termed for their portrayal of a real couple’s (or individual’s, or group’s) sexual pattern. According to a 1979 NSF brochure, “actors are not used in these films; the participants are ordinary people behaving and responding sexually as they usually do…. The persons to be filmed are interviewed about their sexual patterns. Once sexual activity commences, no directions are given. Every effort is made to allow the individuals to feel at ease.” Reflecting their use in structured therapeutic sessions, this selection of pattern films is preceded by a short from the Multi-Media Resource Center’s “Humor and Mood Alteration” collection, meant to dispel unease ahead of these candid portraits. title: In the Mouth of Madness
description: Directed and scored by John Carpenter, and written by Michael De Luca, this love letter to the work of H. P. Lovecraft sees insurance investigator John Trent (Sam Neill) journey to a mysterious small town, unaware that he is entering the depths of insanity. Taking its name from Lovecraft’s 1936 novella At the Mountains of Madness , the final film in the Apocalypse Trilogy follows Trent as he tracks down horror novelist Sutter Cane (Jürgen Prochnow), who has gone missing after completing his latest book. Word spreads that anyone who reads an advance copy of the novel becomes a homicidal maniac, but Trent is convinced it is all a publicity stunt—until his investigation leads him to an eerie town identical to Cane’s work.

THE BRIDE OF FRANKENSTEIN (1935): Dr. Frankenstein and his monster both turn out to be alive after being attacked by an angry mob. Together, the two attempt to solve the mystery of Rita's true identity. The story is set in a dream-like Los Angeles, spoilt neither by traffic jams nor smog.

Ballard’s classic underground novel in 1996, and Westminster Council banned it from screening in central London, even though the film had been given an 18 cert from the BBFC. title: SHOGUN ASSASSIN
description:
After his wife is murdered by agents of a paranoid shogun, former executioner Ogami Ittō takes to the road with his young son Daigoro, pushing him through feudal Japan in a baby cart fitted with an alarming arsenal of hidden weapons. Pursued by ninja assassins and three fearsome Masters of Death, father and son carve a path through ambushes, betrayals and spectacular fountains of blood.
Created for American grindhouse audiences by re-editing and dubbing the first two Lone Wolf and Cub films, SHOGUN ASSASSIN transforms Kenji Misumi’s samurai epics into a lean, hallucinatory barrage of flashing blades, severed limbs and pulsing synthesiser music. Initially notorious in Britain for its extreme violence, the film became a midnight-movie classic whose influence can be felt everywhere from Wu-Tang Clan’s Liquid Swords to Quentin Tarantino’s Kill Bill.

title: By Design
description: Upon seeing a gorgeous chair in a showroom, Camille (Juliette Lewis) realises that she truly envies the life of this perfect piece of furniture. If only she could be someone’s favourite thing. When she and the chair swap forms, Camille learns that she is better liked as an inanimate object than she was as a person: her mother (Betty Buckley) finds her to be a better listener, and her best friends (Samantha Mathis and Robin Tunney) enjoy a newfound, friction-free rapport. As the chair, Camille is unable to speak or move and winds up in the hands of Olivier (Mamoudou Athie), a minimalist bachelor who gradually becomes romantically fixated on his elegant new possession. Narrated by Melanie Griffith, this modern fable celebrates the messiness of female interiority with deadpan humour, surrealist flourishes, and interpretative dance numbers. An absurdist spin on the body-swap comedy, By Design is a bold new work from singular filmmaker Amanda Kramer.

To crack the case, Steve must journey into the city’s nocturnal underworld of S&M and leather bars, hoping to catch the killer’s eye – but will he lose himself along the way? Controversial with both straight and gay audiences upon its initial release, Friedkin’s film still retains its power to shock and unsettle 45 years later.
