Winner of the Silver Lion at the 2026 Venice Film Festival and South Korea’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: O.V.A. Night
description: Brain Dead Studios presents our first-ever O.V.A. Night, a surprise screening of obscure anime rarely seen on the big screen.

title: Possible Love
description: Possible Love follows the intertwined relationship of two married couples facing different paths and hidden desires. Mi-ok (Jeon Do-yeon) lives quietly with her laid-off husband Ho-seok (Sul Kyung-gu) and their young son Cheol until a funeral brings them into the orbit of Ye-ji (Cho Yeo-jeong), a documentary filmmaker chronicling laid-off workers, and her husband Sang-woo (Zo In-sung) – a couple whose affluent lifestyle stands in sharp contrast to their own. When Mi-ok agrees to be filmed, she grows close to Ye-ji, and finds herself uneasily drawn to the unreadable Sang-woo. As their worlds collide, fractures begin to appear in their daily existence. Marking his first release in eight years, highly acclaimed director Lee Chang-dong ( Burning , Poetry , Secret Sunshine ) brings his signature nuance to Possible Love , capturing shifting emotions, conflicts, and contrasting outlooks that shape these relationships.

title: Fatherland
description: Oscar-nominated director Paweł Pawlikowski (Cold War, NYFF56) won Best Director at Cannes for his most potent film yet, following novelist Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler) and his daughter Erika Mann (Sandra Hüller) on a road trip across Germany in the aftermath of World War II. Poland’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: The Lost Boys
description: Teenage brothers Michael (Jason Patric) and Sam (Corey Haim) move with their mother (Dianne Wiest) to a small town in northern California. While the younger Sam meets a pair of kindred spirits in geeky comic-book nerds Edward (Corey Feldman) and Alan (Jamison Newlander), the angst-ridden Michael soon falls for Star (Jami Gertz) -- who turns out to be in thrall to David (Kiefer Sutherland), leader of a local gang of vampires. Sam and his new friends must save Michael and Star from the undead.

title: Doc N' Roll: Punk Brighton + Q&A
description: Beneath Brighton’s waves, a punk revolution erupted. The Piranhas, The Depressions and Peter & The Test Tube Babies turned humour, mischief and music into a fiercely communal movement, centred around The Vault - an underground burial crypt transformed into a legendary gig venue. Told through 15 year...

title: Off-Circuit: The Night is Fading Away
Blade
description: A half-mortal, half-immortal is out to avenge his mother's death and rid the world of vampires. The modern-day technologically advanced vampires he is going after are in search of his special blood type needed to summon an evil god who plays a key role in their plan to execute the human race.

title: THE ADDAMS FAMILY
description: When long-lost Uncle Fester reappears after twenty-five years in the Bermuda Triangle, Gomez and Morticia plan a celebration to wake the dead.

title: The Beyond             / Pieces
description: Woe be unto him who opens one of the seven gateways to Hell, because through that gateway, evil will invade the world. Italian horror icon Lucio Fulci unleashes his towering terror masterpiece, a fright-filled, gore-soaked fever dream that follows a young woman (frequent Fulci star Catriona MacColl), whose recently inherited old Louisianian hotel holds dark secrets. Long available only in an edited, incomplete version, The Beyond was beautifully restored & rereleased uncut in the late ‘90s by Grindhouse Releasing and Quentin Tarantino’s Rolling Thunder Pictures.

title: FFW: Maya Give Me a Title (U)
description: A gloriously zany and personal film from Michel Gondry told with DIY animation and heaps of charm.

title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, The Devils lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color and Warner Bros. Sound. Following the sold-out LFF performance on 12th October, Ken Russell's THE DEVILS will screen daily from 30th October. Screenings from both 35mm and Digital. 35mm performances will be noted next to the time. If there is no note next to the time, the performance is Digital.

title: Halloween (1978)
description: Fifteen years after murdering his sister on Halloween Night 1963, Michael Myers escapes from a mental hospital and returns to the small town of Haddonfield, Illinois to kill again.

title: JIGOKU
description: Shocking, outrageous and poetic, JIGOKU (HELL, a.k.a. THE SINNERS OF HELL ) is the most innovative creation from Nobuo Nakagawa, the father of the Japanese horror film. After a young theology student flees a hit-and-run accident, he is plagued by both his own guilt-ridden conscience and a mysterious, diabolical doppelgänger. But all possible escape routes lead straight to hell—literally. In the gloriously gory final third of the film, Nakagawa offers up his vision of the underworld in a tour de force of torture and degradation. A striking departure from traditional Japanese ghost stories, JIGOKU, with its truly eye-popping (and -gouging) imagery, created aftershocks that are still reverberating in contemporary world horror cinema.

title: The Fly (1986)
description: A big screen love story unlike anything you’ve ever seen, David Cronenberg’s ‘80s update of The Fly is as terrifyingly tragic as its ultra-gooey Oscar-winning special effects are jaw-droppingly grotesque. When an eccentric scientist (Jeff Goldblum) uses himself as a test subject, he soon discovers himself devolving into something not quite human, with disastrous consequences to the relationship with his reporter girlfriend (Geena Davis). Bringing his body horror fascination to the mainstream, Cronenberg crafts a gross-out masterpiece that targets the heart as well as the stomach.

title: An Autumn Afternoon
description: Ozu’s gorgeous 53rd and final feature is a return to a favorite theme, the poignant comedy of marriage, with beloved regular Chishu Ryu as a father giving away his daughter and preparing for another, final goodbye. Good Morning’s satire of creeping consumerism has become more bitter here, the feeling of incoming winter chill is sharper, the entire project imbued with a tang of regret—incidentally, the title literally translates to “The Taste of Autumn Mackerel.” Part of The Leaves Are Falling

title: The Thing
description: In remote Antarctica, a group of American research scientists are disturbed at their base camp by a helicopter shooting at a sled dog. When they take in the dog, it brutally attacks both human beings and canines in the camp and they discover that the beast can assume the shape of its victims. A resourceful helicopter pilot (Kurt Russell) and the camp doctor (Richard Dysart) lead the camp crew in a desperate, gory battle against the vicious creature before it picks them all off, one by one.

title: The Shining [UK Version]
description: Jack Torrance (Jack Nicholson) becomes winter caretaker at the isolated Overlook Hotel in Colorado, hoping to cure his writer's block. He settles in along with his wife, Wendy (Shelley Duvall), and his son, Danny (Danny Lloyd), who is plagued by psychic premonitions. As Jack's writing goes nowhere and Danny's visions become more disturbing, Jack discovers the hotel's dark secrets and begins to unravel into a homicidal maniac hell-bent on terrorizing his family.

title: Peppermint Frappé
description: Chaplin and Saura’s electric creative partnership began with this perverse play on Alfred Hitchcock’s (already quite perverse!) Vertigo, in which meek doctor José Luis López Vázquez becomes besotted with his childhood friend’s bride (Chaplin), and sets about making over a doting assistant (Chaplin, again) at the radiology clinic where he works into the image of the woman he yearns for but cannot have. A delirious and seriously deviant psychological thriller. “I got home quite late and turned on the television; a film in Spanish with subtitles, that I knew absolutely nothing about... It was hard for me to follow and understand but, at the same time, I was convinced it was the film of a great director. I watched the rest of the film glued to the TV set and when it was over I picked up a newspaper and saw that it was Peppermint Frappé.” —Stanley Kubrick Part of The Remembered Lives of G. Chaplin & C. Saura

title: The Nightmare Before Christmas
description: Get in the spooky spirit with a trip to the delightful nightmare world of Halloween Town with Jack Skellington and his gruesome band of ghoulfriends. Tired of the monotony of scaring humans every October 31 with the same old bag of tricks, Jack Skellington, the spindly king of Halloween Town, has a plan to kidnap Santa Claus and turn Christmas creepy. But as the winter holiday approaches, Jack’s rag-doll girlfriend, Sally, tries to foil his misguided plans and bring back Christmas merriment. A stop-motion delight for everyone with extraordinary animation, iconic songs, and a whole world of creepy creatures to fall in love with!

title: Rushmore
description: Extracurricular-mad but otherwise unpromising 15-year-old student Max Fisher (Jason Schwartzman) is too busy competing (or so he thinks) with sad sack industrialist Bill Murray for the affections of teacher Olivia Williams to survive “sudden death academic probation” in Anderson’s deeply funny, deeply melancholic—and very class-conscious—sophomore feature. A back-to-school perennial, all dressed up in prep school navy blue and the muted colors of north Texas autumn, positively thrumming with the upstart energy of British Invasion anthems. (“Anderson,” noted admirer Martin Scorsese, “has a fine sense of how music works against an image.”) An irresistible, disarmingly original, delicately wrought comic fable. Part of The Leaves Are Falling

title: TETSUO THE IRON MAN
description:
A man is mysteriously transformed into a grotesque hybrid of flesh and metal after a bizarre encounter with a scrap‑metal–obsessed stranger. As his body slowly fuses with machinery, he becomes increasingly violent and unrecognizable, spiraling into a nightmarish cycle of rage, obsession, and mechanical mutation.
Shinya Tsukamoto’s debut is a visceral, industrial horror experience, drenched in stark black-and-white visuals, rapid editing, and metallic sound design. The film’s relentless energy and body‑horror imagery create a feverish, almost hypnotic assault on the senses, establishing it as a landmark of Japanese cyberpunk cinema.

title: An American Werewolf in London
description: American tourists David and Jack are savagely attacked by an unidentified animal while hiking on the Yorkshire Moors. After retiring to the home of a beautiful nurse to recuperate, David soon begins experiencing disturbing changes to his body and mind.

title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, The Devils lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color and Warner Bros. Sound. Following the sold-out LFF performance on 12th October, Ken Russell's THE DEVILS will screen daily from 30th October. Screenings from both 35mm and Digital. 35mm performances will be noted next to the time. If there is no note next to the time, the performance is Digital.

title: Jennifer's Body
description: "She's evil… and not just high school evil.” A demon possesses high-school It-girl Jennifer (Megan Fox) after she is kidnapped and sacrificed in a failed occult ritual. Bloodthirsty, she seeks revenge through any man who crosses her path, but is challenged when her best friend, Needy (Amanda Seyfried), won´t stand idly by as the body-count rises. Campy, funny, horrific and truly impressive. After initially receiving mixed critical reception, Jennifer´s Body has become a horror and teen cult-classic as queer and female audiences have reclaimed the title. Ahead of its time, the film is still referenced in Halloween costumes, fan-theories, and video edits as audiences are hungrier than ever for the iconic maneater, Jennifer Check! Jennifer´s Body is featured as part of MANEATERS, a season exploring the female supernatural on screen. The season is presented with the National Film and Television School’s Film Studies, Programming and Curation MA.

title: Film Africa: DEAR AJAYI
description: In southwestern Nigeria in the 1990s, sisters Ade and Titi Ajayi live under the shadow of their late father, their lives shaped by very different ideas of duty, faith and freedom. Ade, a devout Christian and the family’s breadwinner, struggles to understand Titi, her younger sister and an aspiring s...

title: EC: NANOOK OF THE NORTH
description: Flaherty’s pioneering ethnographic film depicts the struggle for survival of Inuit hunter Nanook and his family. Though rife with staged scenes, anachronisms, and an indulgence in the myth of the “noble savage” (Nanook was in fact an Inuit man named Allakariallak, who hunted not with harpoons and spears but with a rifle), NANOOK OF THE NORTH is a work of great lyricism, simplicity of design, and genuine affection for its protagonists, and its force is undiminished almost 100 years after it was made.

title: Sans Soleil
description: Marker's voyage through memory, history, and video games is a free-flow of images shot largely in Japan (a cat temple, sacred phalluses, horror movies, sleeping subway riders, an animatronic JFK), with detours to Guinea-Bissau, Iceland, and, for an extended homage to Vertigo, San Francisco. An alien travelog? The world’s most profound home movie? There’s nothing quite like it in the history of cinema. “Some of Sans Soleil’s trains carry dozing commuters, others travel to distant planets. The film itself moves like a ride through an ever-shifting landscape, shuttling between dreams and waking, here and there.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue Part of Trains: Local Routes

title: Cría Cuervos
description: Taking its title from the Spanish proverb “Raise ravens and they will pick your eyes out,” Saura’s lauded allegorical masterwork, set during the twilight of Spain’s Franco dictatorship, stars Ana Torrent (also seen in Spirit of the Beehive, in the same series) as a traumatized eight-year-old, second of three sisters living with a domineering aunt in Madrid following the death of their parents, who feels herself to be drifting freely between the worlds of the living and the dead and is increasingly convinced she has the ability to snuff out her adult persecutors’ lives. “Both an uncanny drama of family dysfunction and a historical parable of the end of Franco-ism… [Geraldine] Chaplin and Torrent are both outstanding.” —The Guardian Part of The Remembered Lives of G. Chaplin & C. Saura

title: The Edges of Cinema: Book Launch + Little Boy
description: Join us to celebrate the publication of Erika Balsom's The Edges of Cinema: Essays on Twenty-First Century Film Culture with the London premiere of James Benning's little boy (2025). Recent years have seen a panic over the future of mainstream film. Yet in her new collection The Edges of Cinema , Balsom argues that film culture is at its most vital on the margins, where the moving image meets visual art, documentary brushes up against experimentalism, and curators are reshaping established histories. Bringing together a decade of selected essays and reviews, the book explores subjects ranging from computer-generated animation to the effects of digitisation, and from the status of observational cinema to a new golden age of repertory cinema, in order to make a case for the politics, provocations, and pleasures of a less ordinary cinema. To celebrate this publication, join us for the first London screening of little boy by James Benning, an artist and filmmaker central to the book. For some fifty years, Benning has chronicled American hegemony and counterhegemony through an expert manipulation of light and time, giving unconventional shape to histories of settlement, racial violence, land use, and unbelonging. In little boy – winner of the grand prize at Paris's Cinéma du Réel festival – he continues this investigation, using popular songs, political speeches, and architectural models to traverse decades of U.S. history. What are the rules governing the organisation of all these component parts? That is left for the viewer to discern. In Benning's words, little boy is "a film looking at the past to warn about the future, from a little boy’s point of view. A companion to American Dreams (lost and found) (1984).”

title: Practical Magic
description: Witchcraft feels good in a place like this. Spend the night with two witchy sisters as they fight for love and their family lineage in this cinematic comfort food classic. Magic is in their family tree and these two sisters are about to take a crash course in sorcery when one of their boyfriends dies unexpectedly. Now they’ve got the police and an evil spirit on their tail, and they must stick together to come out on top. Initially panned by critics, audiences have been falling in love with this witchy fairy-tale for over 25 years. Bring your sis or your bestie and let this magical movie cast its spell on you!

title: THE ROCKY HORROR PICTURE SHOW
description: In this cult classic, sweethearts Brad (Barry Bostwick) and Janet (Susan Sarandon), stuck with a flat tire during a storm, discover the eerie mansion of Dr. Frank-N-Furter (Tim Curry), a transvestite scientist. As their innocence is lost, Brad and Janet meet a houseful of wild characters, including a rocking biker (Meat Loaf) and a creepy butler (Richard O’Brien). Through elaborate dances and rock songs, Frank-N-Furter unveils his latest creation: a muscular man named “Rocky.”

title: CLASS OF NUKE ‘EM HIGH
director: Richard W. Haines, Michael Herz, and Lloyd Kaufman

title: Under the Silver Lake
description: Young and disenchanted Sam meets a mysterious and beautiful woman who’s swimming in his building’s pool one night. When she suddenly vanishes the next morning, Sam embarks on a surreal quest across Los Angeles to decode the secret behind her disappearance, leading him into the murkiest depths of mystery, scandal and conspiracy.

title: Hansan: Rising Dragon
description: he second installment of the epic Yi Sun-sin trilogy by director Kim Han-min stars Park Hae-il as the 48-year-old Yi Sun-sin, an admiral of the Joseon dynasty (1392-1910) venerated for seemingly miraculous victories over the Japanese naval forces during the Imjin War period. The film focuses on the 1592 Hansan Island battle against a fleet overseen by daimyo (feudal lord) Wakisaka Yasuharu, who plans to conquer the Joseon peninsula on a quest to devour the entire Ming Dynasty. Yi’s famously optimized Turtle battleship appears in grandiose, precisely executed glory under Yi’s orchestration. Spectacular visual compositions, complemented by remarkable visual effects and a magnificent score, come together to deliver one of most gratifying naval war scenes ever shown on the Korean big screen.

title: Peven Everett: Voice of a Generation (12A*) + Screen Talk
Sing-A-Long-A Rocky Horror Picture Show
description: The Campest Cult Classic of all time gets the Singalonga treatment it’s been SCREAMING for! Featuring the film, starring Tim Curry, Susan Sarandon, Meatloaf and Richard O’Brien, it’s the most outrageous, riotous, kitsch, wonderful romp ever. If you’ve done The Time Warp before, you’ll never have done it quite like this! The evening begins with your host leading a vocal warm-up before they show you how to use your free interactive props bag. Fancy dress is not obligatory but highly recommended! Please Note : The 15 rating we have placed upon this screening is due to the Adult content of the hosted pre-show which may not be suitable for those under 15. Please Note : This is a screening of the movie not a live stage show. Also this screening may contain sudden loud noises and flashing lights. For Sing-a-long-a Grease, Rocky Horror, Dirty Dancing and The Greatest Showman at the Prince Charles Cinema, London we can offer a discount for groups of 10+. Simply get in touch with us via email at [email protected] before buying so we can arrange!

title: The Trouble with Harry
description: The inconvenient corpse, imbued with a sense of tragedy and terror in Hitchcock’s Rope, is the source of borderline-surrealist farce in The Trouble with Harry, his adaptation of Jack Trevor Story’s novel of the same name, a darkly comic tale in which the residents of a small New England hamlet—exteriors were shot on location in Vermont, with the fall foliage radiant in Technicolor—try and repeatedly fail to dispose of a dead body that has appeared in their midst. A rare foray into comedy (albeit of the black variety) for Hitchcock, with Shirley MacLaine, Mildred Natwick, and Jerry “The Beaver” Mathers perfectly embodying a bevy of smalltown American “types.” Part of The Leaves Are Falling

title: EC: MAN OF ARAN
description: Flaherty’s third major film portrays the lives of a family of fisher folk on the Aran Islands off the coast of Galway, Ireland. Flaherty selected the location and subjects because of their isolation as the westernmost outpost of European civilization. In addition, the daily struggle between the islanders and the sea perfectly suited his interests and concerns. The scenes at sea are breathtaking. “His passionate devotion to the portrayal of human gesture and of a man’s fight for his family makes the film an incomparable account of human dignity. Better than anyone, Flaherty knew how to show the true face of Man.” –Georges Sadoul

title: News From Home
description: Akerman was 26 years old and living in New York City, away from her native Belgium and her mother, when she teamed with DP Babette Mangolte to film this diary/essay/poem in subway stations and on street corners, their images to eventually be paired with Akerman’s recitals of her mother’s fretful letters. Arguably this extraordinary filmmaker’s most perfect and poignant nonfiction work, both one of the greatest portraits of a city ever put on film and a troubling, touching depiction of maternal love. Screens in the English-language version. “Though Chantal Akerman’s voice can be heard throughout News from Home, her image is only briefly glimpsed, in a reflection on the train. We can’t quite see her, but others undoubtedly can—men, especially, gawk unashamedly, a reminder that the graffiti-covered subway of 1976 New York was often a place of danger and hostility.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue Part of Trains: Local Routes

title: The Texas Chain Saw Massacre
description: When Sally (Marilyn Burns) hears that her grandfather's grave may have been vandalized, she and her paraplegic brother, Franklin (Paul A. Partain), set out with their friends to investigate. After a detour to their family's old farmhouse, they discover a group of crazed, murderous outcasts living next door. As the group is attacked one by one by the chainsaw-wielding Leatherface (Gunnar Hansen), who wears a mask of human skin, the survivors must do everything they can to escape. * The first 35 customers to have tickets scanned in each of these performances will recieve an exclusive limited edition " I SURVIVED THE TEXAS CHAINSAW MASSACRE" badge. A replica of one's we gave out back in 1976 when we were the first cinema to debut this iconic film.

title: City of Masks
description: In this romantic thriller, a young actor begins rehearsals at a haunted theatre and catches the attention of the resident ghost.

title: Audition
description: Steering away from jump scares and cheap gore and into avenues of absolute torture and terror, Takashi Miike’s breakthrough nightmare is the kind of rare horror film that affects you viscerally and haunts you in your psyche. Juxtaposing the banality of daily life for a widower and his son with an intense level of brutality and nauseating imagery, Miike weaves an unforgettable masterpiece of the macabre. Not for the faint of heart, but simply a must-experience for any horror-phile, Audition is the kind of movie you never really recover from.

title: The Exorcist
description: When a mysterious entity possesses a young girl, her mother seeks the help of two Catholic priests to save her life.

title: Bram Stoker's Dracula
description: Coppola at his most boldly baroque, Gary Oldman wearing cinema’s most iconic updo, a puppyish young Keanu Reeves trying to make his way back to Winona Ryder, and Anthony Hopkins as vampire hunter Abraham Van Helsing—it’s all here in this opulent production which returns to the original Stoker text and draws out the piercing sexual ache and romantic longing implicit therein. Part of Winona Ryder Analogue Youth

title: Blade Runner: The Final Cut
description: While so many special effects spectacles are lost in time like tears in the rain, Blade Runner remains the template for imagining the neon-wreathed downer of the future, every bit as influential in its vision as was Fritz Lang’s Metropolis over a half century before. Working from a novel by cult writer Philip K. Dick to create a film that would become the gold standard for sci-fi noir, director Scott shares credit here with “visual futurist” Syd Mead’s design concepts and synth pioneer Vangelis’s atmospheric score. Part of A Cyberpunk Canon

title: From Dusk Till Dawn
description: George Clooney and Quentin Tarantino star as brothers on the lam from the law, hightailing it to Mexico with a kidnapped family in tow. But when they stop at an isolated strip club, they’ll have to try and survive From Dusk Till Dawn while battling the bar’s bloodthirsty denizens in Robert Rodriguez’s pulpy, stylish & hyper-violent cross-genre blast penned by its co-star. Featuring Harvey Keitel, Juliette Lewis & Salma Hayek plus an all-star cast of character actor greats including Cheech Marin, Fred Williamson, Danny Trejo and Tom Savini!

title: Trick 'r Treat
description: Five interwoven stories that occur on Halloween: An everyday high school principal has a secret life as a serial killer; a college virgin might have just met the guy for her; a group of teenagers pull a mean prank; a woman who loathes the night has to contend with her holiday-obsessed husband; and a mean old man meets his match with a demonic, supernatural trick-or-treater.

title: The Beyond             / Pieces
description: Woe be unto him who opens one of the seven gateways to Hell, because through that gateway, evil will invade the world. Italian horror icon Lucio Fulci unleashes his towering terror masterpiece, a fright-filled, gore-soaked fever dream that follows a young woman (frequent Fulci star Catriona MacColl), whose recently inherited old Louisianian hotel holds dark secrets. Long available only in an edited, incomplete version, The Beyond was beautifully restored & rereleased uncut in the late ‘90s by Grindhouse Releasing and Quentin Tarantino’s Rolling Thunder Pictures.

title: The Bride of Frankenstein
description: Mary Shelley reveals the main characters of her novel survived: Dr. Frankenstein, goaded by an even madder scientist, builds his monster a mate.

title: Perfect Blue
description: A young Japanese singer is encouraged by her agent to quit singing and pursue an acting career, beginning with a role in a murder mystery TV show. Our 11th October performance of Perfect Blue will be preceded by the European Premiere of brand-new short film, IDOLS. Idols | South Korea, Japan, UK | 20 min. Dir. by Matt Halsall Kim Min-ha (Hojo Shin) has always dreamed of the spotlight. Now, nearing 30, she’s still chasing a K-pop debut while everyone else sees only her uncanny resemblance to superstar Park Hye-mi (Hojo Shin)—the woman she believes is living the life that should have been hers. Matt Halsall’s slick, darkly funny short turns that obsession into an increasingly unhinged psychological thriller. IDOLS made its world premiere at Fantasia before being selected for Sitges, Beyond Fest and Tokyo’s Yami International Film Festival.

title: The Thing
description: In remote Antarctica, a group of American research scientists are disturbed at their base camp by a helicopter shooting at a sled dog. When they take in the dog, it brutally attacks both human beings and canines in the camp and they discover that the beast can assume the shape of its victims. A resourceful helicopter pilot (Kurt Russell) and the camp doctor (Richard Dysart) lead the camp crew in a desperate, gory battle against the vicious creature before it picks them all off, one by one.

title: Vidiots Annual “Unscary” Halloween
description: Vidiots invites you and all your little witches and goblins to our annual “Unscary” Halloween , a free, all-ages, sensory-friendly Halloween-themed community event.

title: The Witches
description: Accessible screening On the last Saturday of every month, the museum's Family Matinee is an accessible screening where we offer open captioning, keep the theater dimly lit, and maintain a lower volume for viewers who are neurodiverse. They walk among us, often appearing as ordinary women, but when one notices those purple eyes, gloved hands, and keen smell for children, it can mean only one thing: a witch. Luke, an orphaned 9-year-old, is vacationing in a seaside hotel with his grandma. So is an undercover witch convention. After the Grand High Witch turns Luke into a mouse, he finds himself scurrying to save the rest of the world’s children from a similar fate. This wicked tale, adapted from Roald Dahl’s children’s novel of the same name, features the work of Jim Henson’s Creature Shop in the iconic and terrifying reveal of the witches' true forms, and an unforgettable performance by Anjelica Huston as the Grand High Witch.
director: Nicolas Roeg PRODUCED BY: Mark Shivas

title: Shaun the Sheep: The Beast of Mossy Bottom
description: Shaun the Sheep: The Beast of Mossy Bottom sees the residents of Mossy Bottom Farm looking forward to Halloween – until the…

title: Saturday Afternoon Cartoons: Time for Halloween
description: Saturday Afternoon Cartoons is New York City’s prime theatrical showcase of early and classic animated cartoons, shown in vintage 16mm film prints from the personal archives of historian Tommy José Stathes. Beginning more than 25 years ago as a casual effort to find and see early cartoons that were unavailable on home video, Stathes’s collection has grown to become one of the largest of its kind. It includes many titles and ‘orphan films’ that are difficult to access or view elsewhere. Stathes joins Metrograph at the end of October with Time For Halloween, a spooky selection of vintage family-friendly animated shorts to usher in the holiday. Come enjoy a crop of musically inclined skeletons enjoying a midnight graveyard dance; a human artist innocently 'haunting' his cartoon canine companion for a laugh; a little boy telling his younger brother a ghost story by the fireplace; a famous flapper hosting a Halloween house party; and other amusing tales. Spanning the 1920s through the ’50s, this assortment showcases classic characters such as Casper the Friendly Ghost, Popeye, Betty Boop, and others. Featuring introduction and Q&A with Stathes on Saturday, October 31st Part of Screen Time at Metrograph

title: The Shining [UK Version]
description: Jack Torrance (Jack Nicholson) becomes winter caretaker at the isolated Overlook Hotel in Colorado, hoping to cure his writer's block. He settles in along with his wife, Wendy (Shelley Duvall), and his son, Danny (Danny Lloyd), who is plagued by psychic premonitions. As Jack's writing goes nowhere and Danny's visions become more disturbing, Jack discovers the hotel's dark secrets and begins to unravel into a homicidal maniac hell-bent on terrorizing his family.

title: Friday The 13th
description: A group of teenage camp counselors attempt to re-open an abandoned summer camp with a tragic past, but they are stalked by a mysterious, relentless killer.

title: Poltergeist
description: The Freelings’ suburban home becomes the center of paranormal activity that opens a portal to the ‘other side’. With help, they must cross over to get their daughter back.

title: THE HAUNTING
description: Paranormal researcher Richard Johnson leads a team of clairvoyants (Julie Harris, Claire Bloom) to determine if the notorious, bad karma-filled Hill House is truly haunted. What he doesn’t bargain for is intensely neurotic Harris developing an unhealthy sensitivity to the mansion’s evil-charged atmosphere. Based on Shirley Jackson’s novel The Haunting of Hill House , this is one of the all-time classics of the genre.

title: THE INNOCENTS
description: Deborah Kerr brilliantly plays a repressed governess convinced that ghosts haunt the mansion and grounds of her innocent young charges (Martin Stephens, Pamela Franklin). Jack Clayton’s gothic psychological thriller was inspired by Henry James’ “The Turn of the Screw” and adapted with the help of Truman Capote.

title: FFW: Singing in the Rain (U) + Intro
Beetlejuice
description: Tim Burton’s afterlife spooktacular is an energetic mix of goth fantasy and laugh-out-loud comedy! When two newlyweds (Geena Davis & Alec Baldwin) die in a car accident, they must haunt their recently departed home and scare away the obnoxious replacement residents (Jeffrey Jones & Catherine O’Hara), while befriending the new tenants’ teenage daughter (Winona Ryder). But they get more trouble than they bargained for when they recruit Michael Keaton’s rambunctious “bio-exorcist” Beetlejuice to help.

title: The Curse of Frankenstein
description: Cherished by no less a personage than Martin Scorsese for its “totally uncalled for” graphic violence, The Curse of Frankenstein was a watershed film for both Fisher and Hammer, earning 30 times its budget back in the US alone and establishing the studio as the world’s preeminent purveyor of Gothic horror. Awaiting the guillotine, Victor Frankenstein (Peter Cushing) ruminates on the catastrophic fallout of his attempt at creating an exemplary being from scavenged bits of the dead, which results in his cracked creation (Christopher Lee) going on a murderous rampage. Extravagantly colorful, generous with the gruesomeness, and performed with zest—all the hallmarks of Hammer in its prime are in place here, in a shining new 4K restoration. Part of Terence Fisher: Hammer's Master Smith

title: HACKNEY CHILDREN'S FILM FEST: THE LITTLE VAMPIRE
description: Hackney Children’s Film Festival | Sat 24 - Sat 31 October Tickets £5 or £3 with a Hackney Library Card A Rio Cinema Project  The kids have waited long enough! This October half term, the Rio brings Hackney its first ever Children's Film Festival, with a lively and enchanting film programme curated ...

title: THE NICKEL’S PSYCHOTRONIC HALLOWEEN MYSTERY MOVIE MASH - WEEKEND PASS
description:
Two days, eight mystery horror movies from around the world.
Across Halloween and the following day, The Nickel presents four deep-cut psychotronic horror films per day: forgotten exploitation, regional nightmares, video-era mutations, disreputable sleaze and eye-popping oddities that have slipped through the cracks of horror history.
Every title remains secret until showtime. Come for one day or sacrifice yourself to the entire weekend.
Films will screen at 2:00pm, 4:15pm, 6:30pm and 9pm on both Saturday 31st October and Sunday 1st November.
Costumes highly encouraged.
Artwork by
Jordan McLaughlin

title: THE NICKEL’S PSYCHOTRONIC HALLOWEEN MYSTERY MOVIE MASH - DAY ONE 31/10
description:
DAY ONE ONLY - 31/11
Presenting four deep-cut psychotronic horror films: forgotten exploitation, regional nightmares, video-era mutations, disreputable sleaze and eye-popping oddities that have slipped through the cracks of horror history.
Every title remains secret until showtime. Come for one day or sacrifice yourself to the entire weekend.
Films will screen at 2:00pm, 4:15pm, 6:30pm and 9pm on Saturday 31st October. Weekend passes and day tickets for Sunday the 1st November also available.
Costumes highly encouraged.
Artwork by
Jordan McLaughlin

title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, The Devils lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color and Warner Bros. Sound. Following the sold-out LFF performance on 12th October, Ken Russell's THE DEVILS will screen daily from 30th October. Screenings from both 35mm and Digital. 35mm performances will be noted next to the time. If there is no note next to the time, the performance is Digital.

title: THE BIRDS
description: Nothing equals THE BIRDS for sheer terror when Alfred Hitchcock unleashes his foul friends in one of his most shocking and memorable masterpieces. As beautiful blonde Melanie Daniels (Tippi Hedren) rolls into Bodega Bay in pursuit of eligible bachelor Mitch Brenner (Rod Taylor), she is inexplicably attacked by a seagull. Suddenly thousands of birds are flocking into town, preying on schoolchildren and residents in a terrifying series of attacks. Soon Mitch and Melanie are fighting for their lives against a deadly force that can’t be explained and can’t be stopped in one of Hollywood’s most horrific films of nature gone berserk.

title: Halloween (1978)
description: Fifteen years after murdering his sister on Halloween Night 1963, Michael Myers escapes from a mental hospital and returns to the small town of Haddonfield, Illinois to kill again.

title: Obsession
description: You’ve heard the whispers. You’ve seen the hype. Now experience the horror phenomenon that has audiences obsessed. Come see what everyone is talking about…or come back because you love this movie more than anything in the whole f***ing world!

title: Vera
description: A pioneering work of transmasc cinema inspired by the life of Brazilian poet Anderson Bigode Herzer starring Ana Beatriz Nogueira as Bauer, a trans man who struggles to overcome a painful early life via the embrace of art and the love of a sympathetic young librarian (Aida Leiner). “When Caden Mark Gardner and I co-curated Vera as part of the original Masc series in 2022, Caden did some amazing research on the film. Together we determined that it is one of the earliest (and also one of the best) portrayals in world cinema of a transmasculine character. And the film’s protagonist, Bauer (the film’s title is his dead name), shines through as an incredible transmasc hero. As he confidently proclaims to the powers that be, ‘I’m not what everyone thinks I am. You hear me? I’m different. I’m something else. Something else.’” —Series curator Jenni Olson, queer film historian and archivist Introduction by Jenni Olson on Sunday, October 25th Part of Jenni Olson Selects: Mini Masc

title: POLTERGEIST
description: A typical family in a quiet suburb of a normal California faces a frightening ordeal when its home is invaded by a poltergeist. Late one night, 10-year-old Carol Anne Freeling (Heather O’Rourke) hears a voice coming from inside the television set… At first, the spirits that invade the Freeling’s home seem like playful children. But then they turn angry. And when Carol Anne is pulled from this world into another, Steve and Diane Freeling (Craig T. Nelson and JoBeth Williams) turn to an exorcist (Zelda Rubinstein) in this horror classic from director Tobe Hooper and producer and screenwriter Steven Spielberg.​

title: DEATH BECOMES HER
description: Meryl Streep and Goldie Hawn star with Bruce Willis in Robert Zemeckis’ outrageously entertaining comedy about greed, vanity, sex, immortality, life… and death. Isabella Rossellini is a beautiful enchantress who changes their lives—and deaths—forever in this hilarious dark comedy with ground-breaking special effects.

title: Horror of Dracula
description: Christopher Lee joined Max Schreck and Bela Lugosi in the Screen Vampires Hall of Fame with this, his first appearance as a regally seductive Count Dracula, facing off for the first but far from the last time against Peter Cushing’s Doctor Van Helsing. An infusion of fresh blood—quite literally, in the sanguinary opening credits—for Bram Stoker’s well-thumbed tale of the macabre, by turns elegant and frightfully visceral. Along with The Curse of Frankenstein, Horror of Dracula was decisive in Hammer’s turn to Gothic horror, embraced by thrill-loving audiences around the world, though not the reviewer of the Daily Telegraph, who sniffed: “This British film has an X certificate. This is too good for it. There should be a new certificate—‘S’ for sadistic or just ‘D’ for disgusting.” Part of Terence Fisher: Hammer's Master Smith

title: The Edges of Cinema: Book Launch + Panel Discussion
Bride of Frankenstein
description: Openly queer film director James Whale’s gothic masterpiece weaves the artistic style of German Expressionism, a distinctly camp sensibility, and a story of otherness that resonates throughout history. One of the greatest artistic triumphs of the Universal monster empire, this all-time classic features electric performances by Boris Karloff and Elsa Lanchester. Bleak and beautiful, this may be your grandmother’s monster movie, but it’s still fresh and iconic enough to be yours too!

title: Film Africa: STRAWBERRIES
description: Two young women leave their native Morocco to work a season picking strawberries in southern Spain. Promised fair pay, they dream of a better future for themselves and their families. The bond they form with other female workers helps them endure harsh conditions until abuse and harassment shatter t...

title: Scream
description: Wes Craven re-invented and revitalised the slasher-horror genre with this modern horror classic, which manages to be funny, clever and scary, as a fright-masked knife maniac stalks high-school students in middle-class suburbia. Craven is happy to provide both tension and self-parody as the body count mounts - but the victims aren't always the ones you'd expect.

title: EC: HOLLIS FRAMPTON
description: ZORNS LEMMA (1970, 60 min, 16mm. Preserved by Anthology Film Archives.) “A major poetic work. Created and put together by a very clear eye-head, this original and complex abstract work moves beyond the letters of the alphabet, beyond words and beyond Freud. If you don’t understand it the first time you see it, don’t despair, see it again! When you finally ‘get it,’ a small light, possibly a candle, will light itself inside your forehead.” –Ernie Gehr & HAPAX LEGOMENA I: (nostalgia) (1971, 36 min, 16mm. Preserved by Anthology Film Archives, MoMA, and the NYU Moving Image Archiving and Preservation Program, with funding from the National Film Preservation Foundation.) “In (nostalgia) the time it takes for a photograph to burn (and thus confirm its two-dimensionality) becomes the clock within the film, while Frampton plays the critic, asynchronously glossing, explicating, narrating, mythologizing his earlier art, and his earlier life, as he commits them both to the fire of a labyrinthine structure; for Borges too was one of his earlier masters, and he grins behind the facades of logic, mathematics, and physical demonstrations which are the formal metaphors for most of Frampton’s films.” –P. Adams Sitney Total running time: ca. 100 min. CLICK HERE TO BOOK TICKETS NOW!

title: The Trouble with Harry
description: The inconvenient corpse, imbued with a sense of tragedy and terror in Hitchcock’s Rope, is the source of borderline-surrealist farce in The Trouble with Harry, his adaptation of Jack Trevor Story’s novel of the same name, a darkly comic tale in which the residents of a small New England hamlet—exteriors were shot on location in Vermont, with the fall foliage radiant in Technicolor—try and repeatedly fail to dispose of a dead body that has appeared in their midst. A rare foray into comedy (albeit of the black variety) for Hitchcock, with Shirley MacLaine, Mildred Natwick, and Jerry “The Beaver” Mathers perfectly embodying a bevy of smalltown American “types.” Part of The Leaves Are Falling

title: Nosferatu with Live Score
description: This performance will feature a live score performed by Hugo Max . "I first saw Murnau’s Symphony of Horror when I was nine years old. The film’s expressionistic images continue to haunt me, the chiaroscuro compositions tapping vividly into timeless subconscious fears. My improvisations on viola and piano draw inspiration from the leitmotifs and sound effects of 70s horror soundtracks and the languages of Second Viennese School composers contemporary to Murnau, also Jewish Traditional Music that informs my personal approach to creating a score for the film." - Hugo Max Please view this YouTube video for a sample of Hugo's work. Photo Credit - Richard Ecclestone An iconic film of the German expressionist cinema, and one of the most famous of all silent movies, F. W. Murnau's Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror continues to haunt — and, indeed, terrify — modern audiences with the unshakable power of its images. By teasing a host of occult atmospherics out of dilapidated set-pieces and innocuous real-world locations alike, Murnau captured on celluloid the deeply-rooted elements of a waking nightmare, and launched the signature "Murnau-style" that would change cinema history forever. In this first-ever screen adaptation of Bram Stoker's Dracula, a simple real-estate transaction leads an intrepid businessman deep into the superstitious heart of Transylvania. There he encounters the otherworldly Count Orlok — portrayed by the legendary Max Schreck, in a performance the very backstory of which has spawned its own mythology — who soon after embarks upon a cross-continental voyage to take up residence in a distant new land... and establish his ambiguous dominion. As to whether the count's campaign against the plague-wracked populace erupts from satanic decree, erotic compulsion, or the simple impulse of survival — that remains, perhaps, the greatest mystery of all in this film that's like a blackout...

title: The Brides of Dracula
description: Two years after Horror of Dracula, Peter Cushing returned to the role of Doctor Van Helsing, summoned to deal with an outbreak of vampirism at a girls finishing school unleashed by a contaminated aristocrat, Baron Meinster (David Peel). Hammer’s high-finish craftsmanship is on display in every shot and in every aspect of The Brides of Dracula’s production, from Jack Asher’s baroque photography to Bernard Robinson’s exquisite set dressing to the uniformly fine work of the ensemble cast, with notable supporting turns by Martita Hunt and Yvonne Monlaur. Even without Christopher Lee, the genius of the system prevails under Fisher’s hand, giving us, per his biographer Tony Dalton, “One of those perfect Hammer ‘magic box’ productions.” Part of Terence Fisher: Hammer's Master Smith

title: PSYCHO
description: A secretary on the run for embezzlement takes refuge at a secluded California motel owned by a repressed man and his overbearing mother.

title: Halloween
description: It wouldn’t be Halloween without a visit from Michael Myers – the monster that made the holiday – stalking our big screen with terror! The original horror classic still startles over 45 years after its release. The small town of Haddonfield is under attack from an escaped murderer stalking the alleys and sidewalks of the idyllic burg. Laurie Strode (Jamie Lee Curtis) is just a studious teenager, planning on spending her All Hallow’s Eve carving pumpkins with her babysitting charge. When the killer begins to hound her and her friends, she’s got to discover the family secrets that led to this bloody rampage and escape his evil wrath. Also starring Donald Pleasance as Dr. Loomis, P.J. Soles, and Real Housewife of Beverly Hills Kyle Richards. Spend your Samhain with Vidiots and John Carpenter with the slasher that started it all!

title: QUEEN OF THE DAMNED
description: After years of slumber, the legendary vampire has awakened and found acceptance in a tattooed, pierced and black-clad world. He’s a rock star. And his awesome goth-riffed sound has echoed around the globe…and stirred to life the fearsome Mother of All Vampires (Aaliyah, in her final film role).

title: NIGHT OF THE LIVING DEAD
description: A deceptively simple tale of a group of strangers trapped in a farmhouse who find themselves fending off a horde of flesh-eating ghouls newly arisen from their graves, Romero’s claustrophobic vision of a late-sixties America (literally) tearing itself apart rewrote the rules of the horror genre, combined gruesome gore with acute social commentary and quietly broke ground by casting a black actor (Duane Jones) in the lead role.

title: Minority Report
description: Based on a Philip K. Dick short story, Spielberg’s wheeling, virtuoso science-fiction thriller stars Tom Cruise as an investigator of “PreCrime” who specializes in arresting criminals before they’ve done the deed in near-future Washington, DC. They’re still working on the jetpacks, but the film’s vision of a world run on touchscreens and bombarded with targeted advertising already looks frightfully prescient.

title: Bram Stoker's Dracula
description: Coppola at his most boldly baroque, Gary Oldman wearing cinema’s most iconic updo, a puppyish young Keanu Reeves trying to make his way back to Winona Ryder, and Anthony Hopkins as vampire hunter Abraham Van Helsing—it’s all here in this opulent production which returns to the original Stoker text and draws out the piercing sexual ache and romantic longing implicit therein. Part of Winona Ryder Analogue Youth

title: EC: FRANJU / GENET
description: Georges Franju BLOOD OF THE BEASTS / LE SANG DES BÊTES 1949, 20 min, 16mm. In French with English subtitles. “This documentary on the slaughterhouses of Paris is one of the great masterpieces of the subversive cinema; here, for once, we are face to face with death, and are neither protected nor cheated. […] A dream-like quality permeates the intense realism of the images; a surrealist intent – akin to Buñuel’s slitting of the eyeball in UN CHIEN ANDALOU – is discernible in this anti-bourgeois film. But the eyeball, however shocking, was fictional; BLOOD OF THE BEASTS is real.” –Amos Vogel, FILM AS A SUBVERSIVE ART Jean Genet UN CHANT D’AMOUR 1950, 26 min, 35mm, silent. Brand-new 35mm print by Anthology! “Genet’s only film – hounded by the censors, unavailable, secret – is an early and remarkably moving attempt to portray homosexual passions. Already a classic, it succeeds as perhaps no other film to intimate the explosive power of frustrated sex…. Like all Genet’s early work, the entire film is, in effect, a single onanistic fantasy, filled with desperate frustration and sensuous nostalgia.” –Amos Vogel, FILM AS A SUBVERSIVE ART “There’s no smoke without fire; UN CHANT D’AMOUR is a communion in which Genet takes us into the prison in order to liberate us from it.” –Derek Jarman Total running time: ca. 50 min. title: Sing-A-Long-A Rocky Horror Picture Show
description: The Campest Cult Classic of all time gets the Singalonga treatment it’s been SCREAMING for! Featuring the film, starring Tim Curry, Susan Sarandon, Meatloaf and Richard O’Brien, it’s the most outrageous, riotous, kitsch, wonderful romp ever. If you’ve done The Time Warp before, you’ll never have done it quite like this! The evening begins with your host leading a vocal warm-up before they show you how to use your free interactive props bag. Fancy dress is not obligatory but highly recommended! Please Note : The 15 rating we have placed upon this screening is due to the Adult content of the hosted pre-show which may not be suitable for those under 15. Please Note : This is a screening of the movie not a live stage show. Also this screening may contain sudden loud noises and flashing lights. For Sing-a-long-a Grease, Rocky Horror, Dirty Dancing and The Greatest Showman at the Prince Charles Cinema, London we can offer a discount for groups of 10+. Simply get in touch with us via email at [email protected] before buying so we can arrange!

title: The Texas Chain Saw Massacre
description: 52 years ago Tobe Hooper set a new high-water mark for horror with this brutal and gruesome exercise in terror, and few films since have matched its levels of visceral torture. After running out of gas, five friends end up hunted by a hulking monster with a human-skin mask and a whirring chainsaw. One of the most influential horror films of all time, and a truly terrifying experience, this low-budget nightmare is an opera of carnage.

title: 30th Anniversary of The Craft
description: Sarah Bailey (Robin Tunney), a teen with a troubled past, moves to Los Angeles with her parents for a fresh start. Upon arrival in a Catholic school, Sarah is introduced to Bonnie (Neve Campbell), Rochelle (Rachel True), and Nancy (Fairuza Balk), a clique of outsiders rumored to practice witchcraft. Born a natural witch herself, Sarah is welcomed to the group, completing their coven. Together they invoke the ancient spirit of Manon, a pagan deity. Critically panned upon release, the film has since gained a cult following for its fierce, defiant portrayal of sisterhood, female agency, and rage, resonating with independent spirits, outcasts, and, as Balk so proudly puts it onscreen, “the weirdos, mister.” Join us as we gather after hours on All Hallows' Eve to commemorate 30 years since the release of a spellbinding classic.
director: Andrew Fleming PRODUCED BY: Douglas Wick

title: RAW
description: At 16, Justine is a brilliant, promising student and a strict vegetarian. But when she starts veterinary school, she quickly encounters a decadent, merciless and dangerously seductive world. Desperate to fit in, she strays from her principles and eats raw meat for the first time and faces the terrible and unexpected consequences of her actions as her true self emerges.

title: Rosemary's Baby
description: “He has his father’s eyes…” Satanists are on the loose in Central Park West in Polanski’s slow-burn thriller, which slips almost imperceptibly from the quotidian into the profane, and gives new meaning to the phrase “pregnancy scare.” Young marrieds Mia Farrow and John Cassavetes make friendly with their elder neighbors Ruth Gordon and Sidney Blackmer, but when Farrow’s abandoned and isolated Rosemary goes into a paranoiac tailspin while expecting her first child, she begins to wonder why everyone is so very eager for her to take her daily dosage of tannis root… A masterclass in slow-building, spine-tingling suspense, aided immeasurably by the dab-handed work of legendary editor Sam O’Steen. Part of Filmcraft: American Cinema Editors

title: Blade Runner: The Final Cut
description: While so many special effects spectacles are lost in time like tears in the rain, Blade Runner remains the template for imagining the neon-wreathed downer of the future, every bit as influential in its vision as was Fritz Lang’s Metropolis over a half century before. Working from a novel by cult writer Philip K. Dick to create a film that would become the gold standard for sci-fi noir, director Scott shares credit here with “visual futurist” Syd Mead’s design concepts and synth pioneer Vangelis’s atmospheric score. Part of A Cyberpunk Canon

title: Halloween Marathon
description: ALL NIGHTER : FAQs, HOUSE RULES & TIPS HALLOWEEN (1978): Fifteen years after murdering his sister on Halloween Night 1963, Michael Myers escapes from a mental hospital and returns to the small town of Haddonfield, Illinois to kill again. HALLOWEEN II (1981): After failing to kill stubborn survivor Laurie and taking a bullet or six from former psychiatrist Dr. Sam Loomis, Michael Myers has followed Laurie to the Haddonfield Memorial Hospital, where she’s been admitted for Myers’ attempt on her life. The institution proves to be particularly suited to serial killers, however, as Myers cuts, stabs and slashes his way through hospital staff to reach his favourite victim. HALLOWEEN III: SEASON OF THE WITCH (1982): After a terrified toy salesman is mysteriously attacked and brought to the hospital, clutching the year’s most popular Halloween mask, Dr. Daniel Challis sets out to investigate the strange events and finds himself thrust into a nightmarish conspiracy. HALLOWEEN 4: THE RETURN OF MICHAEL MYERS (1988): Ten years after his original massacre, the invalid Michael Myers awakens on Halloween Eve and returns to Haddonfield to kill his seven-year-old niece. HALLOWEEN 5: THE REVENGE OF MICHAEL MYERS (1989): After lying in a coma for a year, Michael Myers awakens and stalks his way back to his small hometown in Illinois, intent on killing his niece, Jamie, who has been confined to a mental institution since his last attempt to slay her. HALLOWEEN: THE CURSE OF MICHAEL MYERS [Producer's Cut] (1995): Six years after being presumed dead in a fire, and just as the town prepares to finally celebrate Halloween again, Michael Myers returns to Haddonfield to continue his reign of terror. ----------------------------------------------------------------------- NO ADMISSIONS TO THE CINEMA AFTER MIDNIGHT NO ALCOHOL PURCHASED FROM OUTSIDE IS PERMITTED IN THE BUILDING! AGE RESTRICTIONS: This event is strictly 18+

title: Queer Horror Nights: THE ROCKY HORROR PICTURE SHOW with Shadow Cast
description: The ultimate Halloween thrill ride, QUEER HORROR NIGHTS returns to the Rio with our spectacular midnight sing-along screening of THE ROCKY HORROR PICTURE SHOW (1975) featuring a live Shadow Cabaret Cast performing in front of the film.  A “phenomenal night” of "pure chaotic queer joy”, our shadow ca...

title: Halloween: H20
description: Twenty years after the horrific events of Halloween , Laurie Strode must battle the Shape one last time. Jamie Lee Curtis triumphantly returns to the role that made her a scream queen, playing Strode as a woman haunted by her past and living under an assumed name as the headmistress of a private boarding school. But when her rebellious son and his friends skip their school trip to party on the quiet campus, knife-wielding maniac Michael Myers sees them as perfect victims for his belated bloodbath. A game cast of fresh faces, including Josh Hartnett, Michelle Williams, Joseph Gordon-Levitt, and Jodi Lyn O’Keefe, co-star alongside LL Cool J and Janet Leigh.

title: Trick 'r Treat
description: Five interwoven stories that occur on Halloween: An everyday high school principal has a secret life as a serial killer; a college virgin might have just met the guy for her; a group of teenagers pull a mean prank; a woman who loathes the night has to contend with her holiday-obsessed husband; and a mean old man meets his match with a demonic, supernatural trick-or-treater.

title: Homicidal             / Mr. Sardonicus
description: In the small town of Solvang, there’s a killer on the loose… and a bizarre household may hold the key to murder. Nurse Emily takes care of her husband Warren’s childhood guardian, a wheelchair-bound stroke victim. But this nurse’s bedside manner is to die for. As Warren’s half-sister closes in on the truth, she uncovers a town’s most chilling mystery… and her family’s darkest secret. (Sony)

title: The Bride of Frankenstein
description: Mary Shelley reveals the main characters of her novel survived: Dr. Frankenstein, goaded by an even madder scientist, builds his monster a mate.

title: Shaun the Sheep: The Beast of Mossy Bottom
description: Shaun the Sheep: The Beast of Mossy Bottom sees the residents of Mossy Bottom Farm looking forward to Halloween – until the…

title: The Addams Family
description: Among the most perfectly cast Hollywood studio films of the last half-century, cinematographer-cum-director Sonnenfeld’s adaptation of Charles Addams’s macabre recurring New Yorker feature stars Raul Julia as the suave patriarch of the Addams clan (“You lady-killer…” “Acquitted!”), Anjelica Huston as his waxen, witchy bride, and an outstanding preadolescent Christina Ricci as doomy daughter Wednesday. A drolly dark comedy that moves with the fearsome speed of a 1930s screwball, thanks to the surgical precision of Dede Allen’s editing. Part of Screen Time at Metrograph

title: Donnie Darko [Theatrical Cut]
description: During the presidential election of 1988, a teenager named Donnie Darko sleepwalks out of his house one night and sees a giant, demonic-looking rabbit named Frank, who tells him the world will end in 28 days. When Donnie returns home, he finds that a jet engine has crashed into his bedroom. Is Donnie living in a parallel universe, is he suffering from mental illness - or will the world really end?

title: All That Heaven Allows
description: Perhaps the very finest of Sirk’s Ross Hunter-produced melodramas, All That Heaven Allows pairs Jane Wyman and Rock Hudson as, respectively, a well-off widow in country club Connecticut, and the broad-necked, Thoreau-reading gardener who she falls for. Her priggish children, aghast, conspire to break off the pairing, an endeavor that ends in a bone-chilling Christmas conciliation—the presentation of a gift television set as a kind of death sentence. Of this scene Rainer Werner Fassbinder, profoundly marked by his encounter with Sirk’s film, would write: “At that point everyone in the moviehouse breaks down. They suddenly understand something about the world and what it does to people.” Right on. Part of The Leaves Are Falling

title: Black History Month:  Alain Gomis' DAO
description: DAO weaves together two ceremonies marking one family’s journey through love and loss. In the French countryside, Gloria marries off her daughter Nour; in Guinea-Bissau, she honours her late father, welcomed among the ancestors. Blending documentary and fiction, with the cast playing tender, unguard...

title: Sans Soleil
description: Marker's voyage through memory, history, and video games is a free-flow of images shot largely in Japan (a cat temple, sacred phalluses, horror movies, sleeping subway riders, an animatronic JFK), with detours to Guinea-Bissau, Iceland, and, for an extended homage to Vertigo, San Francisco. An alien travelog? The world’s most profound home movie? There’s nothing quite like it in the history of cinema. “Some of Sans Soleil’s trains carry dozing commuters, others travel to distant planets. The film itself moves like a ride through an ever-shifting landscape, shuttling between dreams and waking, here and there.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue Part of Trains: Local Routes

title: Beetlejuice
description: Tim Burton’s afterlife spooktacular is an energetic mix of goth fantasy and laugh-out-loud comedy! When two newlyweds (Geena Davis & Alec Baldwin) die in a car accident, they must haunt their recently departed home and scare away the obnoxious replacement residents (Jeffrey Jones & Catherine O’Hara), while befriending the new tenants’ teenage daughter (Winona Ryder). But they get more trouble than they bargained for when they recruit Michael Keaton’s rambunctious “bio-exorcist” Beetlejuice to help.

title: THE NICKEL’S PSYCHOTRONIC HALLOWEEN MYSTERY MOVIE MASH - DAY TWO 1/11
description:
DAY TWO ONLY - 1/11
Presenting four deep-cut psychotronic horror films: forgotten exploitation, regional nightmares, video-era mutations, disreputable sleaze and eye-popping oddities that have slipped through the cracks of horror history.
Every title remains secret until showtime. Come for one day or sacrifice yourself to the entire weekend.
Films will screen at 2:00pm, 4:15pm, 6:30pm and 9pm on Sunday 1st November. Weekend passes and day tickets for Saturday the 31st also available.
Costumes highly encouraged.
Artwork by
Jordan McLaughlin

title: Gosford Park
description: A weekend party at an English mansion in the 1930s leads to murder in this seriocomic whodunit, with Robert Altman directing an all-star cast. The Oscar-winning screenplay came via Julian Fellowes, who later explored the same milieu for Downton Abbey . The remarkable transatlantic cast includes Alan Bates, Bob Balaban (who also produced and came up with the story idea with Altman), Clive Owen, Kristin Scott Thomas, Emily Watson, and Helen Mirren and Maggie Smith, who were both nominated for their performances. The film’s seven nominations include Best Picture, Directing, and Art Direction, with production designer Stephen Altman and set decorator Anna Pinnock mixing authentic English mansions and soundstage sets to evoke the glamour and class divisions of the era.

title: The Gorgon
description: In their tireless search for new monsters to add to their menagerie Hammer turned here to Greek mythology, unleashing the fatal gaze of the Gorgon on the residents of a German village, c. 1910. Seven Vandorf residents have in recent years been found frozen into statuary, and it falls on the esteemed Prof. Meister of Leipzig (Christopher Lee) to overcome interference by local physician Dr. Namaroff (Peter Cushing) and track down the culprit, Megaera (ballerina-turned-film actor Prudence Hyman), a she-devil with the ability to turn flesh to stone. A small miracle of high style on a pinched budget, praised by Raymond Durgnat in Films and Filming for its “romantic warmth… with oil lamps casting a rich glow on the patchwork counterpanes and through coloured windows, and with some extraordinarily beautiful cloudscapes and dusk skies.” Part of Terence Fisher: Hammer's Master Smith

title: News from Home + Interior NY Subway, 14th Street
The Hound of the Baskervilles
description: An ardent aficionado of the work of Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, Cushing takes over the chambers at 221B Baker Street with aplomb and gives us a Sherlock for the ages in Fisher’s adaptation of the 1902 Holmes adventure of the same name, in which our hero is called to Dartmoor to investigate the mysterious death-by-fright of one Sir Charles Baskerville, leaving his estate in the hands of his heir and nephew, Henry (Christopher Lee). With the invaluable assistance of Jack Asher’s subdued Technicolor photography, Fisher wrings every drop of atmosphere out of Doyle’s tale of mist-shrouded moors and ancestral curses, making this one of Holmes’s very finest big-screen outings. (Special mention is due to Fisher’s ingenious use of child stand-ins for his leads to establish the terrible proportions of the eponymous mastiff.) Part of Terence Fisher: Hammer's Master Smith

title: Perfect Blue
description: A young Japanese singer is encouraged by her agent to quit singing and pursue an acting career, beginning with a role in a murder mystery TV show. Our 11th October performance of Perfect Blue will be preceded by the European Premiere of brand-new short film, IDOLS. Idols | South Korea, Japan, UK | 20 min. Dir. by Matt Halsall Kim Min-ha (Hojo Shin) has always dreamed of the spotlight. Now, nearing 30, she’s still chasing a K-pop debut while everyone else sees only her uncanny resemblance to superstar Park Hye-mi (Hojo Shin)—the woman she believes is living the life that should have been hers. Matt Halsall’s slick, darkly funny short turns that obsession into an increasingly unhinged psychological thriller. IDOLS made its world premiere at Fantasia before being selected for Sitges, Beyond Fest and Tokyo’s Yami International Film Festival.

title: THE TWELVE CHAIRS
description: In 1920s Soviet Russia, a fallen aristocrat, a priest and a con artist search for a treasure of jewels hidden inside one of twelve dining chairs, lost during the revolution.

title: Eungyo
description: Renowned poet Lee Juk-yo, 70, has become a recluse, mechanically pushing through his bland days, until they are pleasantly disrupted by high school student Eun-gyo, who comes into his life, bringing fresh energy. Lee starts working on a new novel, the dullness of his life giving way to color, possibilities, even daydreams. But that color starts to dim when Seo Ji-woo, Lee’s former student/assistant, becomes involved with Eun-gyo, and jealousy moves in instead. Based on a novel of the same name by Park Beom-shin, Eungyo explores themes of youth, and the poignant notion of its loss and redemption, with Park Hae-il delivering a notable interpretation of those themes through his character’s numbness and dissociation.

title: Rushmore
description: Extracurricular-mad but otherwise unpromising 15-year-old student Max Fisher (Jason Schwartzman) is too busy competing (or so he thinks) with sad sack industrialist Bill Murray for the affections of teacher Olivia Williams to survive “sudden death academic probation” in Anderson’s deeply funny, deeply melancholic—and very class-conscious—sophomore feature. A back-to-school perennial, all dressed up in prep school navy blue and the muted colors of north Texas autumn, positively thrumming with the upstart energy of British Invasion anthems. (“Anderson,” noted admirer Martin Scorsese, “has a fine sense of how music works against an image.”) An irresistible, disarmingly original, delicately wrought comic fable. Part of The Leaves Are Falling

title: F. W. Murnau’s Faust
description: The haunting tale of a scholar, tempted by the Devil to sign away his soul in exchange for universal knowledge, has been a resonant cultural motif across five centuries. If the essential literary text for the Faustian myth is Johan Wolfgang von Goethe’s 19th century poetic drama, its cinematic equivalent is F. W. Murnau’s visionary 1926 silent adaptation, a masterpiece of haunting visual design that explores rich themes of morality and materialism. Starring Oscar-winning actor Emil Jannings as the terrifying trickster Mephisto, Murnau’s tale emerges from the disturbing underworld into the dreams of lost innocence for one of the most remarkable films from the German Expressionist milieu. A century later, scores of international filmmakers, including Guillermo del Toro, Jennifer Kent, and Robert Eggers, continue to be influenced by this masterwork. The Academy Museum is thrilled to present this film with live accompaniment on the occasion of its centennial and of MUBI’s newest publication, The Faust Bible: The Making of F. W. Murnau’s Masterpiece , which will be available for purchase in the Academy Museum Store. Programmed and note by K.J. Relth-Miller.
director: F. W. Murnau PRODUCED BY: Erich Pommer

title: The Thing
description: In remote Antarctica, a group of American research scientists are disturbed at their base camp by a helicopter shooting at a sled dog. When they take in the dog, it brutally attacks both human beings and canines in the camp and they discover that the beast can assume the shape of its victims. A resourceful helicopter pilot (Kurt Russell) and the camp doctor (Richard Dysart) lead the camp crew in a desperate, gory battle against the vicious creature before it picks them all off, one by one.

title: CITIZEN TOXIE: THE TOXIC AVENGER IV
Autumn Sonata
description: Ingmar and Ingrid, Bergman and Bergman, together at last. Sweden’s most popular export before the Volvo, in her final screen role, plays a world-renowned concert pianist who returns home to reunite with her now-married daughter (Liv Ullmann), long a distant second to her mother’s career ambitions, the two women exhuming old resentments and struggling towards reconciliation over the course of an emotionally draining 24 hours. “So unrelenting, so harrowing, that I walked out of the theater on shaking legs. If you’re open to the experience that Bergman means to provide, you may leave the film muttering a wrung-out ‘Whew!’ followed quickly by an appreciative ‘Wow!’” —Richard Corliss, Time Magazine Part of The Leaves Are Falling

title: Midnight in Paris
description: Screenwriter, would-be novelist, and romantic-at-heart Owen Wilson, on vacation in the City of Lights with level-headed fiancée Rachel McAdams, sets out on his own one night after a wine tasting and finds himself suddenly in the Jazz Age Paris of Fitzgerald and Hemingway, Dali and Picasso—an invigorating draught of bohemian freedom that sets our protagonist to seriously interrogating his life choices. “We talked about pushing the color even more in the period scenes, in order to distinguish them from the present-day ones. The Paris of today would be normal and generic, bland and desaturated, and when you entered the Paris of the 1920s the colors would be more warm, lush and flamboyant, with lots of brown and gold and red.” —Darius Khondji Part of Radical Chiaroscuro: The Work of Darius Khondji

title: Paris, Texas
description: A disheveled man who wanders out of the desert, Travis Henderson (Harry Dean Stanton) seems to have no idea who he is. When a stranger manages to contact his brother, Walt (Dean Stockwell), Travis is awkwardly reunited with his sibling. Travis has been missing for years, and his presence unsettles Walt and his family, which also includes Travis's own son, Hunter (Hunter Carson). Soon Travis must confront his wife, Jane (Nastassja Kinski), and try to put his life back together.

title: Your Name [Kimi no Na wa.]
description: Two teenagers share a profound, magical connection upon discovering they are swapping bodies. Things manage to become even more complicated when the boy and girl decide to meet in person.

title: In the Realm of the Senses
description: Still censored in its own country, In the Realm of the Senses (Ai no corrida), by Japanese director Nagisa Oshima, remains one of the most controversial films of all time. A graphic portrayal of insatiable sexual desire, Oshima’s film, set in 1936 and based on a true incident, depicts a man and a woman (Tatsuya Fuji and Eiko Matsuda) consumed by a transcendent, destructive love while living in an era of ever-escalating imperialism and governmental control. Less a work of pornography than of politics, In the Realm of the Senses is a brave, taboo-breaking milestone. Content Warning: This film contains scenes of graphic sex and violence. Further information about content and age-appropriateness for specific films can be found on Common Sense Media , IMDb and DoesTheDogDie.com , as well as through general internet searches.

title: Bus Stop
description: This contemporary Western—in which Marilyn Monroe stars as saloon singer Cherie, who dreams of one day making it big in Hollywood—marked a turning point in Marilyn Monroe’s career. She had recently formed Marilyn Monroe Productions and signed a new contract with 20th Century-Fox, earning a higher salary and more creative agency in the process. For the role of Cherie, which was one of the more dramatic and serious of her career to date, she began working with Method acting pioneers Lee and Paula Strasberg, who placed an emphasis on delving into an actor’s own experiences.
director: Joshua Logan PRODUCED BY: Buddy Adler
