title: The Cook, the Thief, His Wife & Her Lover
description: When churlish mobster Albert Spica (Michael Gambon) acquires an upscale French restaurant in London, he dines there nightly, effectively scaring off the clientele with his bad manners. His wife, Georgina (Helen Mirren), is especially disgusted by him, and soon begins an affair with another restaurant guest, Michael (Alan Howard). Despite their efforts to keep it a secret, however, Spica finds out about their trysts, and he plans to exact a terrible revenge.

title: Cinematic Void Presents EUREKA
description: Gene Hackman, Mickey Rourke, Rutger Hauer and Theresa Russell are the all-star players in the strange tale, set in the Canadian Wilderness, about a gold prospector who, after a gold strike, moves to a Carribbean island where his reward will be misery and paranoia and pursuit by killers.

title: Eyes Wide Shut
description: Stanley Kubrick's daring last film is many things. It is a compelling psychosexual journey. A haunting dreamscape. A riveting tale of suspense. A major milestone in the careers of stars Tom Cruise and Nicole Kidman. And "a worthy final chapter to a great director's career" (Roger Ebert). Cruise plays Dr William Hartford, who plunges into an erotic foray that threatens his marriage - and may even ensnare him in a lurid murder mystery - after his wife's (Kidman) admission of sexual longings. As the story sweeps from doubt and fear to self-discovery and reconciliation, Kubrick orchestrates it with masterful flourishes. Graceful tracking shots, controlled pacing, rich colours, startling images: bravura traits that make Kubrick a filmmaker for the ages are here to keep everyone's eyes wide shut.

title: Arrival: A Conversation with Denis Villeneuve and Dr. Nina Beguš
description: Inspired by Denis Villeneuve's 2016 sci-fi drama Arrival, the director joins artificial-humanities scholar Dr. Nina Beguš live in the David Geffen Theater for an inspiring conversation about how language acts as a technology; how fiction shapes artificial intelligence; and how encounters with non-human intelligence might transform our most basic understanding of thinking, learning, consciousness, time, and more. To mark the 10th anniversary of this thought-provoking film, an 8pm screening follows the discussion. About Nina Beguš Nina Beguš is a scholar and author working on AI, literature, and film. She is a researcher at the University of California, Berkeley, where she leads the Artificial Humanities research group. Her work examines how stories, concepts, and cultural archetypes shape technology. She is the author of Artificial Humanities: A Fictional Perspective on Language in AI and the editor of First Encounters with AI: Writers on Writing . Beguš holds a PhD in comparative literature from Harvard University and edits the Artificial Humanities book series at the University of Exeter Press. About Denis Villeneuve Denis Villeneuve is an Academy Award-nominated director, screenwriter and producer whose masterful world-building and unique visuals have established him as one of the premier filmmakers working today. In 2021, Dune: Part One earned six Academy Awards and multiple guild and critics' awards. Its sequel, Dune: Part Two (2024), expanded with bolder visual ambition and complexity, surpassing $700 million worldwide and winning two Academy Awards, with additional recognition from BAFTA, Critics Choice and major guilds. Villeneuve will conclude the trilogy with Dune: Part Three this December, reuniting its core cast. He is also set to direct the next James Bond film for Amazon MGM Studios. About the film In director Denis Villeneuve’s thoughtful science-fiction drama, adapted from Ted Chiang’s award-winning novella Story of Your Life , a linguistics expert (Amy Adams) is recruited by the government when massive alien spaceships suddenly land across the globe. The film’s production designer, Patrice Vermette (nominated with set decorator Paul Hotte) also designed the film’s alien language—one of Arrival ’s many remarkable and imaginative visuals. The film was nominated in seven categories, including Best Picture and Production Design; it won an Oscar for Sound Editing.

title: British Horror Studio: In the Grip of Terror
description: Introducing a season from the British Horror Studio. An independent British film studio Focusing on Gothic drama and arthouse filmmaking with a distinctive British horror character. In the Grip of Terror marks the long-awaited return of Amicus Productions, the legendary British horror banner famed for its classic portmanteau films. Revived through the British Horror Studio, the picture restores the anthology tradition with a new collection of sinister tales bound together by dread, guilt, psychological torment, and the creeping sense that some stories should never be told aloud. Set within a shadowed world of troubled patients, strange confessions, and institutional unease, the film brings together a repertory cast led by Megan Tremethick, with appearances from Golden Globe nominee Jane Merrow, Laurence R. Harvey, Dorian Todd, Sam McMillan, Michael Daviot, Novarro Ramon, Nick Ford, and Lawrie Brewster https://www.britishhorrorstudio.com/

title: What Ever Happened To Baby Jane?
description: *ON SALE 23rd OCT * Jane Hudson (Bette Davis) is an aging child star left to care for her wheelchair-bound sister Blanche (Joan Crawford), also a former child actress. Stuck living together in a mansion in old Hollywood, Blanche plots to get even with Jane for the car crash that left her crippled years earlier. But Jane is desperate to keep Blanche imprisoned as she plans a new rise to fame, and tries to hide Blanche's existence from doctors, visitors and neighbors while she devises a way to get rid of her sister.

title: The Last Princess
description: In the early 20th century, the last princess of the Korean royal family under Japanese rule is forced to move to Japan to attend school, leaving behind her family, friends, and the only home she has ever known. Kim Jang-han (Park Hae-il), a childhood friend and Japanese army officer, helps to plan an escape route for her. This film, based on the real story of Princess Deokhye (Son Ye-jin), weaves fact with fiction to retell the story of a once-lost princess who stopped at nothing to return to the home she yearned for. –note written by Hannah Farkas.

title: Godzilla (1954)
description: Godzilla is the roaring granddaddy of all monster movies. It’s also a remarkably humane and melancholy drama, made in Japan at a time when the country was reeling from nuclear attack and H-bomb testing in the Pacific. Its rampaging radioactive beast, the poignant embodiment of an entire population’s fears, became a beloved international icon of destruction, spawning almost thirty sequels.

title: Antichrist
description: While a married couple (Willem Dafoe, Charlotte Gainsbourg) is having sex, their infant son in a nearby room falls out a window to his death. She becomes distraught and is hospitalized, but her husband, who is a psychiatrist, attempts to treat her. Deciding that she needs to face her fears, he takes her to a cabin in the woods where she spent a previous summer with the boy. Once they are there, she becomes more unhinged and starts perpetrating sexual violence on her husband and herself.

title: Heat
description: A group of high-end professional thieves start to feel the heat from the LAPD when they unknowingly leave a verbal clue at their latest heist. Original Cut from a 35mm print.

title: Black Narcissus
description: This explosive work about the conflict between the spirit and the flesh is the epitome of the sensuous style of Michael Powell and Emeric Pressburger. A group of nuns—played by some of Britain's finest actresses, including Deborah Kerr, Kathleen Byron, and Flora Robson—struggle to establish a convent in the Himalayas, while isolation, extreme weather, altitude, and culture clashes all conspire to drive the well-intentioned missionaries mad. A darkly grand film that won Oscars for Alfred Junge's art direction and Jack Cardiff's cinematography, Black Narcissus is one of the greatest achievements by two of cinema's true visionaries.

title: The Zone of Interest
description: The commandant of Auschwitz, Rudolf Höss, and his wife Hedwig, strive to build a dream life for their family in a house and garden next to the camp.The commandant of Auschwitz, Rudolf Höss, and his wife Hedwig, strive to build a dream life for their family in a house and garden next to the camp.

title: Funeral Parade presents "An Actor's Revenge"
description: Funeral Parade is proud to present An Actor’s Revenge, Kon Ichikawa’s melodrama about kabuki and vengeance. Taking place during Japan’s Edo period, the story follows Yukitaro, a kabuki theatre performer, as he seeks revenge on the three criminals who drove his parents to suicide twenty years earlier. A renowned onnagata — a male actor who portrays female characters — Yukitaro is as bewitchingly androgynous as he is deadly with a sword. However, his plan to mete out retribution is complicated when he develops feelings for Namiji, the daughter of one of his foes. A stunningly beautiful tragedy with lush widescreen compositions, An Actor’s Revenge is both a classic of 1960s Japanese cinema and landmark example of on-screen gender fluidity. With intro from curator Sarah Cleary.

title: Amelie - 25th Anniversary
description: 23-year-old Amélie is lonely. After an isolating childhood, she moves to Paris and becomes a waitress at the Café des Deux Moulins, a bar restaurant filled with a colourful cast of diners and employees. One night, Amélie happens across a box of treasures hidden in her apartment, left by a little boy in the Fifties, that changes the course of her life. Henceforth, she dedicates herself to giving back to her community, tracking down the owner of these keepsakes, consoling a widowed neighbour and befriending a reclusive artist. When completing these good deeds, she crosses paths with Nino, a photobooth collagist who shares her oddball sensibilities. She quickly falls in love with him.

title: La La Land
description: Sebastian (Ryan Gosling) and Mia (Emma Stone) are drawn together by their common desire to do what they love. But as success mounts they are faced with decisions that begin to fray the fragile fabric of their love affair, and the dreams they worked so hard to maintain in each other threaten to rip them apart.

title: Dogtooth [Kynodontas]
description: Newly restored in 4K, DOGTOOTH follows a controlling, manipulative father who locks his three adult children in a state of perpetual childhood by keeping them prisoner within the sprawling family compound.

title: Lost Boundaries (12)
description: This 1949 American drama looks at how 'liberal ideals' presented on screen back then; in which the groundbreaking filmmaker William Greaves stars as a young college graduate.

title: Fantastic Planet
description: On the planet Ygam, the Draags, extremely technologically and spiritually advanced blue humanoids, consider the tiny Oms, human beings descendants of Terra's inhabitants, as ignorant animals. Those who live in slavery are treated as simple pets and used to entertain Draag children; those who live hidden in the hostile wilderness of the planet are periodically hunted and ruthlessly slaughtered as if they were vermin.

title: Doc'n'Roll FF: KitKatClub: Kinks of Berlin + Q&A (zoom)
Mystery Movie
description: Don't miss our fan favourite MYSTERY MOVIE screenings! On a near weekly basis we will serve up a random mystery movie, with No Clues and No Hints as to what they will be. In 2026, we'll be presenting these as STAFF CURATED selections each and every week by our lovely Front of House, Duty Manager, and Projection Team! You can find the schedule below: --- You can find a list of every MYSTERY MOVIE we have ever screened HERE ; if a film is on this list, it is not eligible for future Mystery Movie screenings! --- Content Advice : As these films are a mystery, we aren't able to provide specific ratings / guidance on the film's content. We strongly advise that you take this into consideration before purchasing a ticket.

title: My Dad is 100 Years Old with Rome, Open City
description: My Dad Is 100 Years Old This short tribute casts celebrated actress Isabella Rossellini as herself as well as various filmmakers who influenced or were influenced by her father, filmmaker Roberto Rossellini. Conceived by Isabella on the eve of her father’s centenary, she took a “docu-fantasia” concept to avant-garde filmmaker Guy Maddin after her delightful experience on his 2003 feature, The Saddest Music in the World. A beautiful cinema poem for a beloved father and artist.
director: Guy Maddin PRODUCED BY: Jody Shapiro

title: In The Mood For Love
description: In 1962 Hong Kong, neighbors Su Li-zhen (Mrs. Chan) and Chow Mo-wan (Mr. Chow) discover their spouses are having an affair. As they spend time together, they develop feelings for each other, but their relationship remains chaste and unspoken, reflecting societal constraints and their own moral compass.

title: CAMP - A SHORT FILM SHOWCASE
description:
THE NICKEL teams up with cyberfemme studio EVERYONE IS A GIRL for a showcase of short films centred on the theme of CAMP, accompanied with readings.
The Nickel Cinema’s regular roster of B-movies, softcores, and underrated gems has begun to shed some buttery spotlight on underrepresented cinematic traditions. At EIAG, we make collaborative projects about the feminine, the seductive, the virtual, and the covert. For this CAMP showcase, we are joining forces to present films from our community that are not afraid to play, deceive, and perform. Join us for a night of London’s most sparkliest, performative, abject, delicious, and scandalicious emerging cinema.
Programme of films to be announced.

title: Memories of Murder
description: Bong Joon Ho’s phenomenal breakthrough film stars Park Hae-il as an enigmatic young loner and observer whose innocent demeanor seems too wholesome to be true. Inspired by a true story, Memories of Murder centers around the gruesome serial killings of women in South Korea in the 1980s, investigated by Doo-man (Song Kang-ho), a detective who relies on instinct rather than fact. Bong’s vision, which challenges conventional components of storytelling and blurs the boundaries between genres, is meticulously orchestrated in this crime thriller, and Park’s elegantly simple depiction of a complicated character is phenomenal.

title: Taste of Cherry
description: Winner of the Palme d’Or at the 1997 Cannes Film Festival, Iranian auteur Abbas Kiarostami’s _Taste of Cherry_ is an emotionally complex meditation on life and death. Middle-aged Mr. Badii (Homayoun Ershadi) drives through the hilly outskirts of Tehran—searching for someone to rescue or bury him.

title: The Last Temptation of Christ
description: Jesus, a humble Judean carpenter beginning to see that he is the son of God, is drawn into revolutionary action against the Roman occupiers by Judas - despite his protestations that love, not violence, is the path to salvation. The burden of being the saviour of mankind torments Jesus throughout his life, leading him to doubt. As he is put to death on the cross, Jesus is tempted by visions of an ordinary life married to Mary Magdalene.

title: The Godfather
description: Widely regarded as one of the greatest films of all time, this mob drama, based on Mario Puzo's novel of the same name, focuses on the powerful Italian-American crime family of Don Vito Corleone (Marlon Brando). When the don's youngest son, Michael (Al Pacino), reluctantly joins the Mafia, he becomes involved in the inevitable cycle of violence and betrayal. Although Michael tries to maintain a normal relationship with his wife, Kay (Diane Keaton), he is drawn deeper into the family business.

title: Salo, Or The 120 Days of Sodom
description: Four corrupted fascist libertines round up 9 teenage boys and girls and subject them to 120 days of sadistic physical, mental and sexual torture.

title: THE MUSICAL
description: The PROOF Film Festival is thrilled to announce to screen THE MUSICAL, the feature length version of the 2024 PROOF Film Festival audience award winner. Starring Will Brill, Rob Lowe and Gillian Jacobs, we are so proud of filmmaker Giselle Bonilla and screenwriter & producer Alexander Heller as they bring this hilarious feature that began as a short to the masses.

title: LIVE WIRE
description:
Bomb-disposal expert Danny O’Neill is pulled into a case of seemingly spontaneous human combustion when senators begin exploding without warning. The weapon is invisible, the conspiracy reaches into Washington, and Danny’s estranged family may be the next target.
A gloriously overheated early-nineties action thriller, LIVE WIRE treats liquid explosives, political skulduggery and marital crisis with equal urgency. Pierce Brosnan brings pre-Bond polish to the chaos, while Christian Duguay keeps the fuse short and the set pieces deliriously combustible.

title: Pink Palace: WHO KILLED TEDDY BEAR
description: Pink Palace and Lobotomy Room (devoted to Bad Movies for Bad People) present this tough as nails gritty thriller from the mean streets of sixties New York.  We invite you to take a walk on the wild side with this boundary-pushing and ultra-tawdry 1965 exploitation b-movie. Hip, independent and moder...

title: National Theatre Live: Golden Boy
description: Josh O’Connor (The Crown; Challengers) leads the cast in this searing revival of Clifford Odets’ knockout American classic. 1930s New York, at the height of the Depression. Joe Bonaparte is a gifted young violinist with a future in music, until a chance at fame and fortune lures him into the brutal world of professional boxing. He must confront what he’s willing to sacrifice, who he’s willing to become and how to find his place in a world that demands he choose a side. Brought to life with a live string quartet and filmed live from the Almeida Theatre. Olivier Award-winner Sam Yates (Vanya) directs this propulsive drama exploring ambition, identity, and the high price of success.

title: Viva Ingrid! with Journey to Italy
description: Viva Ingrid! A moving documentary tribute to a mother, wife, and actress, this mix of home movies, newsreels, and clips from films by Roberto Rossellini paints a shortform portrait of three-time Academy Award-winning Swedish actress Ingrid Bergman, as realized by one of Rossellini’s grandsons.

title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, The Devils lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color and Warner Bros. Sound. Following the sold-out LFF performance on 12th October, Ken Russell's THE DEVILS will screen daily from 30th October. Screenings from both 35mm and Digital. 35mm performances will be noted next to the time. If there is no note next to the time, the performance is Digital.

title: NFTS Collective Visions of Pleasure: Shakedown
RICOCHET
description:
Rookie Los Angeles cop Nick Styles becomes a public hero after his dramatic arrest of psychopathic criminal Earl Talbot Blake is captured on camera. Years later Styles is a successful prosecutor with a family and political future, while Blake has spent every day in prison planning revenge. After staging his escape, Blake begins an elaborate campaign to destroy Styles’s reputation, relationships and sense of reality.
Denzel Washington and John Lithgow face off in Russell Mulcahy’s feverishly heightened revenge thriller, written by Fred Dekker and produced by Joel Silver. RICOCHET pushes the police procedural into the territory of horror and comic-book melodrama, with Lithgow’s villain attacking not simply his enemy’s body but the public image on which his life has been built. Fast, lurid and unapologetically excessive, it is peak early-1990s studio action cinema.

title: V For Vendetta
description: In a future British dystopian society, a shadowy freedom fighter, known only by the alias of "V", plots to overthrow the tyrannical government - with the help of a young woman.

title: MOTHERWITCH
description: Eleni, a painter in Cyprus in 1882, reaches into the shadows to resurrect her lost children, but instead summons the ancient Kalikantzari of Cypriot lore. She must now confront the storm of her grief and anger, and lift the curse.

title: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
description: After a painful breakup, Clementine (Kate Winslet) undergoes a procedure to erase memories of her former boyfriend Joel (Jim Carrey) from her mind. When Joel discovers that Clementine is going to extremes to forget their relationship, he undergoes the same procedure and slowly begins to forget the woman that he loved. Directed by former music video director Michel Gondry, the visually arresting film explores the intricacy of relationships and the pain of loss.

title: Excalibur
description: Arthur fulfills his fate by bringing together the Knights of the Round Table at Camelot and unifying the country. However, this flawed monarch faces greater tests ahead in pursuit of love, the Holy Grail, and his nation's survival.

description: A multi-storied, fish-eyed look at the human condition against the backdrop of contemporary middle-class LA. Twenty two characters intersect, profoundly and fleetingly, through each other’s lives. It runs the emotional gamut from disturbing to humorous. title: Bus Stop
description: This contemporary Western—in which Marilyn Monroe stars as saloon singer Cherie, who dreams of one day making it big in Hollywood—marked a turning point in Marilyn Monroe’s career. She had recently formed Marilyn Monroe Productions and signed a new contract with 20th Century-Fox, earning a higher salary and more creative agency in the process. For the role of Cherie, which was one of the more dramatic and serious of her career to date, she began working with Method acting pioneers Lee and Paula Strasberg, who placed an emphasis on delving into an actor’s own experiences.
director: Joshua Logan PRODUCED BY: Buddy Adler

title: The Fifth Element
description: The Earth is about to be destroyed by a huge ball of fire racing toward the planet. Cornelius, an old monk, knows how to stop the burning sphere with the help of Korben Dallas, a taxi driver and former secret agent and a woman named Leeloo.

title: Akira
description: Iconic and game-changing, AKIRA is the definitive anime masterpiece! Katsuhiro Otomo's landmark cyberpunk classic obliterated the boundaries of Japanese animation and forced the world to look into the future. AKIRA's arrival shattered traditional thinking, creating space for future generations of ground-breaking movies. July, 1988 - World War III breaks loose. Then, in 2019, in megalopolis Tokyo...As the leader of a group of young robust delinquents, Kaneda spent his nights tearing through the urban wastes, racing his motorbike against rival groups. One night while riding with his gang, his friend Tetsuo suddenly encounters a strange boy - the product of human experimentation and is injured in the ensuing crash. Shortly thereafter, a military squadron appears on the scene to take the boy and Tetsuo away to an army research facility. Determined to free Tetsuo from capture, Kaneda sneaks into the army research lab. However, a regimen of extreme experimental procedures has awakened a new power in his friend, and now he is consumed by madness..

title: Mikey and Nicky
description: Our performance on 14th October is presented with an introduction by Christina Newland Elaine May crafted a gangster film like no other in the nocturnal odyssey Mikey and Nicky, capitalising on the chemistry between frequent collaborators John Cassavetes and Peter Falk by casting them together as small-time mobsters whose lifelong relationship has turned sour. Set over the course of one night, this restless drama finds Nicky (Cassavetes) holed up in a hotel after the boss he stole money from puts a hit out on him. Terrified, he calls on Mikey (Falk), the one person he thinks can save him. Scripted to match the live-wire energy of its stars—alongside supporting players Ned Beatty, Joyce Van Patten, and Carol Grace—and inspired by real-life characters from May’s own childhood, this unbridled portrait of male friendship turned tragic is an unsung masterpiece of American cinema. Our performance on 14th October is featured as part of Gangsters Have Feelings Too, a season exploring the sensitive gangster film. The season is presented with the National Film and Television School’s Film Studies, Programming and Curation MA.

title: FFC: Coco (PG)
description: One of Pixar’s most complex creations, Coco takes the audience from a village in Mexico to the Land of the Dead in this utterly beautiful, musical family drama.

title: The Haunted Mansion
description: Based on the iconic Disneyland ride, The Haunted Mansion stars Eddie Murphy as real estate agent Jim Evers, a workaholic who wants to close a mansion deal before going on a much-needed vacation with his wife, Sara, and his kids. Upon their arrival, the family is lured apart by ghosts who believe Sara can set them free by joining them in the afterlife. The Evers family battles ghosts, zombies, and spiders to save Sara from eternal damnation, also encountering – of course -- references to the amusement park ride, including Hidden Mickeys and the theme song, “Grim Grinning Ghosts.”
director: Rob Minkoff PRODUCED BY: Don Hahn, Andrew Gunn

title: Chungking Express
description: Every day, Cop 223 (Takeshi Kaneshiro) buys a can of pineapple with an expiration date of May 1, symbolizing the day he'll get over his lost love. He's also got his eye on a mysterious woman in a blond wig (Brigitte Lin), oblivious of the fact she's a drug dealer. Cop 663 (Tony Leung Chiu Wai) is distraught with heartbreak over a breakup. But when his ex drops a spare set of his keys at a local cafe, a waitress (Faye Wong) lets herself into his apartment and spruces up his life.

title: Bugsy Malone
description: It is 1929 in New York and the city is divided by gang warfare. On one side, Dandy Dan's mob terrorise the district, taking out those they turn against with their new splurge guns. On the other side, Dandy Dan's rival, Fat Sam, runs his successful Grand Slam Speakeasy.

title: Rossellini Through His Own Eyes
description: “Neo-realism is above all a moral standpoint from which to look at the world,” Roberto Rossellini proclaimed in 1954, and this conviction led him not just to make lasting contributions to the neo-realist mode, but also equipped him to articulate his artistic ideas into spoken language. In this loving documentary portrait of the father of the cinematic movement, scholar Adriano Aprà uses archival footage and interviews with Rossellini to underscore the filmmaker’s unique eloquence, and the ways his life and work combined into his singular vision.

title: Big Trouble in Little China
description: Kurt Russell plays hard-boiled truck driver Jack Burton, who gets caught in a bizarre conflict within, and underneath, San Francisco's Chinatown. An ancient Chinese prince and Chinatown crime lord has kidnapped a beautiful green-eyed woman, who is the fiancee to Jack's best friend. Jack must help his friend rescue the girl before the evil Lo Pan uses her to break the ancient curse that keeps him a fleshless and immortal spirit.

title: Manhunter : The Final Cut
description: A retired criminal profiler (William Petersen) reluctantly returns to the FBI to help track down a serial killer of families and is forced to consult an expert—the imprisoned Dr. Hannibal Lecktor (Brian Cox in a subtly chilling performance). The third feature written and directed by Michael Mann is a gripping adaptation of the first of Thomas Harris’s four novels featuring the iconic murderer, and benefits from the filmmaker’s typically striking visuals as well as a top-notch supporting cast , including Tom Noonan as the hunted killer, and three-time Oscar nominee Joan Allen (The Contender, 2000) as his blind love interest. -- This new 4K Final Cut, overseen by Mann, enhances the film’s depth, visual clarity and sound, offering audiences the ultimate immersive version. Shot in 1985, MANHUNTER was on a frontier in both its subject matter and film form, initiating an impressive list of subsequent films and series. “40 years ago – though armed with Thomas Harris’ excellent novel, “Red Dragon” – its subject matter, the profiling of serial killers, as well as being shocking and raw, was unknown. When adapting, I wanted to make its storytelling deliver audiences into a certain state of threat and emotional engagement. Integral to that was the visualization and use of music with lyrics sometimes working like a libretto. We have carefully remastered the film to try to evoke that mood and intensity, heightened with audio sourced from the original 5.1 35mm analog masters. This latest iteration is that version of the film with which I’m most satisfied.” said director Michael Mann. Under the guidance of Mann, this 4K scan of the original 35mm negative – with a few shots from an interpositive - was conformed and digitally restored at L’Immagine Ritrovata in Bologna. Both the theatrical version and the UHD HDR & SDR video color gradings were performed by Stefan Sonnenfeld at Company 3 in Los Angeles with the director. Sound restoration was done at Audio Mechanics from an original 35mm magnetic 6-track printmaster to release a new 5.1 mix by Luke Schwartzweller at Fox . Technical coordination and deliveries were managed by L’Immagine Ritrovata . This project was supervised by Becca Mann and STUDIOCANAL team, Jean-Pierre Boiget and Delphine Roussel . For Michael Mann, the process is about renewing the film’s immediacy for contemporary audiences: “If the picture was left the way it was, it would be interesting, but you’d feel some distance …you’d be observing it somewhat. I’m more interested in its original intent impacting you the same way it may have in 1986…that is, to bring you into it again in the original way.” As a film distinguished by its striking visual style, including Colleen Attwood’s costume design, Academy Award- winner Mel Bourne’s art direction, Dante Spinotti’s lighting, Mann worked with his long-time collaborator, Stefan Sonnenfeld (Company 3), to develop a new color grade for ‘The Final Cut’ that engages a contemporary audience while honoring the film’s lasting legacy. “A good example is the use of primaries and secondaries in combinations that don’t occur in nature for an unsettling ambiance or the use of blue for night-time imagery. We’ve changed values subtly sometimes, but significantly, to enhance the impact without changing the dramatic intent of the film,” said Stefan Sonnenfeld. He adds: “Michael… wants you to understand the story and the mood and the environment… and then asks you to interpret that in colour… He also tells you what emotion he’s trying to evoke from the scene.” The new version also introduces an HDR presentation, offering an intensified new experience. “So that nobody’s ever seen the movie like that,” noted Sonnenfeld.

title: Rome, Open City
description: Made for less than $20,000 just after the liberation of Italy by US forces, Rossellini’s first installment in his Neo-Realist Trilogy, which also includes Paisan (1946, screening on November 15) and Germany, Year Zero (1948, screening the same day), is also considered the first product of neo-realism. The devastation of Nazi-occupied Rome serves as an all-too-real backdrop for a story that could have been ripped from the headlines: a resistance leader (Aldo Fabrizi) is pursued through town as he seeks shelter and a safe escape. With “the terror of German occupation [...] still vivid in the minds of everyone,” (Patrizio Rossi, 1988) including Rossellini’s lead actress, the great Anna Magnani, Rome, Open City serves as a prototype for a series of films that characterize the best of Italian cinema.

title: Whisper of the Heart
description: Discover the brilliance of this heartwarming coming-of-age classic from the legendary Studio Ghibli, creators of My Neighbour Totoro and the Academy Award®-winning Spirited Away. A chance encounter with a mysterious cat sends Shizuku, a girl with her head in the clouds, on a quest for her true talent. Together with Seiji, a boy determined to follow his dreams, and enchanted by The Baron, an antique cat figurine who guides her to listen to the whispers of her heart, Shizuku embarks on a life-changing adventure that takes her beyond the boundaries of her imagination. Based on a screenplay and storyboards from Hayao Miyazaki, WHISPER OF THE HEART is a precious gem in the Studio Ghibli catalogue, directed by veteran animator Yoshifumi Kondo.

title: The 7th Voyage of Sinbad
description: When a princess is shrunken by an evil wizard, Sinbad must undertake a quest to an island of monsters to cure her and prevent a war.

title: All That Jazz
description: When he is not planning for his upcoming stage musical or working on his Hollywood film, choreographer/director Joe Gideon (Roy Scheider) is popping pills and sleeping with a seemingly endless line of women. The physical and mental stress begins to take a toll on the ragged perfectionist. Soon, he must decide whether or not his non-stop work schedule and hedonistic lifestyle are worth risking his life. The film is a semi-autobiographical tale written and directed by the legendary Bob Fosse.

title: Chicago
description: Wannabe celeb Roxie Hart murders her lover and is sent to jail, only to discover that a tabloid scandal may be her best route to true stardom in this stylish and lively version of the stage musical. Rob Marshall, making his feature directing debut, pays due homage to the distinctive style of Bob Fosse’s original Broadway production while bringing his own energetic approach to the material, which features such classic Kander and Ebb songs as “All That Jazz,” “Cell Block Tango,” and “Mister Cellophane.” The first movie musical to win Best Picture in the 34 years since Oliver! (1968), it received 13 nominations and also won for Costume Design, Film Editing, Sound, Catherine Zeta-Jones’s commanding performance as Roxie’s frenemy Velma Kelly. Production designer John Myhre and set decorator Gordon Sim also won for their Art Direction, featuring just the right blend of fantasy and reality.

title: One Flew Over The Cuckoo's Nest
description: Adapted from Ken Kesey’s novel, the film centres on Randle McMurphy (Nicholson), a convict who simulates mental illness in the hope that a transfer to psychiatric hospital might ensure his early release. But he hasn’t bargained for the rigid regimen of Nurse Ratched (Louise Fletcher, also superb), who dislikes his disruptive — though he’d say liberating — effect on the ward. Inspired casting (Danny DeVito, Brad Dourif and Christopher Lloyd are among the patients) and Forman’s naturalistic direction lend authenticity to the proceedings, so that the film succeeds both as anti-authoritarian parable and as an affecting reminder of the psychiatric practices of the past.

title: Doc'n'Roll FF: You Fuckers Figure It Out: A Jason Molina Story + Q&A
Fallen Angels
description: An assassin goes through obstacles as he attempts to escape his violent lifestyle despite the opposition of his partner, who is secretly attracted to him.

title: Waikiki Brothers
description: Park Hae-il’s big-screen debut is Yim Soon-rye’s second feature, which received critical praise upon its 2001 release, establishing Yim as one of Korea’s most significant directors. Seong-woo, lead singer and guitarist of Waikiki Brothers—a band formed with his friends back in high school—returns to his hometown with his bandmates in hopes of repairing their fragile relationship. But the band stagnates, and Seong-woo is torn between a dream that’s out of reach and his thin grasp on reality. Park, who portrays the teen version of Seong-woo, generates youthful energy, evoking the purity that Seong-woo and his bandmates once carried and now long for. Yim’s insightful and humane perception of the cruel split between dreams and reality in modern Korea permeates this portrayal of her sympathetic and intricate characters.

title: Dead Souls + Alex Cox Q&A
description: On Sunday 8th November, we will be joined by Director Alex Cox for a Live Post-Film Q&A For his directorial swan song, Alex Cox (Repo Man, Straight to Hell) stars in this frontier fable of American Greed, playing the mysterious drifter Strindler as he scours the West for the names of dead Mexican labourers. In this loose adaptation of Nikolai Gogol's 1842 novel Dead Souls, Strindler - or is it Swindler? - raises eyebrows when he offers to pay a pretty penny to add to his list of names. Wandering affably from saloon to ranch, Strindler exercises the old adage that money talks - but sometimes too loudly. Between the town drunk, hot-headed cowherds and local outlaws, Strindler soon finds himself tangled up in his own tall tales. Pistol duels and crooked officials abound, and Spaghetti Western legend Gianni Garko (If You Meet Sartana Pray For Your Death) claims a co-writer credit. But Cox's idiosyncrasy stands out as the film veers tonally through the picaresque, dark satire and other unexpected twists. Dead Souls is a meditative Western that takes place at the borderlands of the American nightmare: where fortunes rest on a dirty deal and legacies are built on blood and gold.

title: In The Mood For Love
description: In 1962 Hong Kong, neighbors Su Li-zhen (Mrs. Chan) and Chow Mo-wan (Mr. Chow) discover their spouses are having an affair. As they spend time together, they develop feelings for each other, but their relationship remains chaste and unspoken, reflecting societal constraints and their own moral compass.

title: Pulp Fiction
description: Vincent Vega (John Travolta) and Jules Winnfield (Samuel L. Jackson) are hitmen with a penchant for philosophical discussions. In this ultra-hip, multi-strand crime movie, their storyline is interwoven with those of their boss, gangster Marsellus Wallace (Ving Rhames) ; his actress wife, Mia (Uma Thurman) ; struggling boxer Butch Coolidge (Bruce Willis) ; master fixer Winston Wolfe (Harvey Keitel) and a nervous pair of armed robbers, "Pumpkin" (Tim Roth) and "Honey Bunny" (Amanda Plummer).

title: Classic Matinee: THE LUNCHBOX
description: For our November Classic Matinee, taking place the day after Diwali, we celebrate Indian cinema with Ritesh Batra’s beautifully observed and bittersweet THE LUNCHBOX . Lonely housewife Ila prepares a special lunch for her neglectful husband, only for Mumbai’s famously efficient lunchbox delivery sys...

title: Oldboy [Oldeuboi]
description: Dae-Su is an obnoxious drunk bailed from the police station yet again by a friend. However, he's abducted from the street and wakes up in a cell, where he remains for the next 15 years, drugged unconscious when human contact is unavoidable, otherwise with only the television as company. And then, suddenly released, he is invited to track down his jailor with a denouement that is simply stunning.

title: Some Like It Hot
description: Marilyn Monroe’s work in director Billy Wilder’s comedic classic is often cited as her best. The film was controversial for its racy humor and story about two musicians (Tony Curtis and Jack Lemmon) who disguise themselves as women to evade the Mafia. But of equal scandal were the Oscar-winning costumes made by Orry-Kelly for Monroe’s Sugar Kane Kowalczyk. Both dresses are on display in the exhibit Marilyn Monroe: Hollywood Icon , on view through February 28, 2027. Some Like It Hot was made during a year of dramatic highs and lows for Monroe, with this film standing as a high point.

title: Idiocracy
description: **ON SALE 23rd OCT** In 2005, average in every way private Joe Bowers (Luke Wilson) is selected to take part in a secret military experiment to put him in hibernation for a year along with a woman named Rita (Maya Rudolph). The slumbering duo is forgotten when the base they are stored on is closed down and are left in stasis until 2505. When they finally wake up, they discover the average intelligence of humans has decreased so much that Joe is now the smartest man in the world.

title: Cinematic Void Presents PHASE IV
description: Ecological suspense tale about a strange biological imbalance creating super intelligent ants which attack a scientific installation in the Arizona desert.

title: Short Cuts : 35mm Roadshow Tour
description: A multi-storied, fish-eyed look at the human condition against the backdrop of contemporary middle-class LA. Twenty two characters intersect, profoundly and fleetingly, through each other’s lives. It runs the emotional gamut from disturbing to humorous. Don't miss a rare opportunity to see Robert Altman's sprawling epic, showing from an original 35mm print as part of our SHORT CUTS 35mm Roadshow Tour. title: Boyhood
description: The joys and pitfalls of growing up are seen through the eyes of a child named Mason (Ellar Coltrane), his parents (Patricia Arquette, Ethan Hawke) and his sister (Lorelei Linklater). Vignettes, filmed with the same cast over the course of 12 years, capture family meals, road trips, birthday parties, graduations and other important milestones. Songs from Coldplay, Arcade Fire and other artists capture the time period.

title: Moss
description: Hae-guk (Park Hae-il) receives word that his estranged father has passed away, bringing him to an unusual village for the funeral. Sensing his presence is unwelcome, Hae-guk grows suspicious and begins to sense a deeper truth behind his father's death . Adapted from a Korean webtoon, Moss submerges audiences in a dark and thrilling mystery, blending suspense and horror to create a world of uncertainty. –Note written by Hannah Farkas.

title: Come and See
description: This widely acclaimed film from Soviet director Elem Klimov is a stunning, senses-shattering plunge into the dehumanizing horrors of war. As Nazi forces encroach on his small village in present-day Belarus, teenage Flyora (Aleksei Kravchenko, in one of the screen’s most searing depictions of anguish since Renée Falconetti’s Joan of Arc) eagerly joins the Soviet resistance. Rather than the adventure and glory he envisioned, what he finds is a waking nightmare of unimaginable carnage and cruelty—rendered with a feverish, otherworldly intensity by Klimov’s subjective camerawork and expressionistic sound design. Nearly suppressed by Soviet censors who took eight years to approve its script, Come and See is perhaps the most visceral, impossible-to-forget antiwar film ever made.

title: The Holy Mountain
description: In a corrupt, greed-fueled world, a powerful alchemist leads a messianic character and seven materialistic figures to the Holy Mountain, where they hope to achieve enlightenment.

Then, in 2019, in megalopolis Tokyo...As the leader of a group of young robust delinquents, Kaneda spent his nights tearing through the urban wastes, racing his motorbike against rival groups. title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, The Devils lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color and Warner Bros. Sound. Following the sold-out LFF performance on 12th October, Ken Russell's THE DEVILS will screen daily from 30th October. title: Sunset Boulevard
description: An aging silent film queen refuses to accept that her stardom has ended. She hires a young screenwriter to help set up her movie comeback. The screenwriter believes he can manipulate her, but he soon finds out he is wrong. The screenwriters ambivalence about their relationship and her unwillingness to let go leads to a situation of violence, madness, and death.

title: In the Realm of the Senses
description: Still censored in its own country, In the Realm of the Senses (Ai no corrida), by Japanese director Nagisa Oshima, remains one of the most controversial films of all time. A graphic portrayal of insatiable sexual desire, Oshima’s film, set in 1936 and based on a true incident, depicts a man and a woman (Tatsuya Fuji and Eiko Matsuda) consumed by a transcendent, destructive love while living in an era of ever-escalating imperialism and governmental control. Less a work of pornography than of politics, In the Realm of the Senses is a brave, taboo-breaking milestone. Content Warning: This film contains scenes of graphic sex and violence. Further information about content and age-appropriateness for specific films can be found on Common Sense Media , IMDb and DoesTheDogDie.com , as well as through general internet searches.

title: The Departed
description: To take down South Boston's Irish Mafia, the police send in one of their own to infiltrate the underworld, not realizing the syndicate has done likewise. While an undercover cop curries favor with the mob kingpin, a career criminal rises through the police ranks. But both sides soon discover there's a mole among them.

title: British Horror Studio Season: Spoiling You
description: Introducing a season from the British Horror Studio. An independent British film studio Focusing on Gothic drama and arthouse filmmaking with a distinctive British horror character. Spoiling You is a seductive and deeply unsettling ASMR psychological horror from award-winning filmmaker Megan Tremethick. What begins as a world of soft voices, intimate rituals, and online comfort soon curdles into something far more dangerous, as obsession, identity, and performance collapse into a nightmare of control. Starring Megan Tremethick, Stephen Kerr, and Laurence R. Harvey, Spoiling You blends J-horror unease, internet-age paranoia, and sensual psychological dread into one of The B-Team’s boldest and most disturbing features. Tremethick’s award-winning directorial debut turns the familiar language of online intimacy into a weapon, creating a film that is strange, stylish, uncomfortable, and impossible to shake. https://www.britishhorrorstudio.com/

title: Ms. 45
description: Eerie and unforgettable, MS. 45 is an essential snapshot of New York City in the early 1980s from Abel Ferrara (DRILLER KILLER, THE ADDICTION)—one of the greatest and most unique living filmmakers on the planet. Thana (Zoë Tamerlis) is a garment worker who’s had the ultimate bad day, as she’s assaulted twice in visceral fashion. Shocked to her core, Thana's nights become consumed by vengeful prowls through the city, which result in men winding up on the wrong end of a bullet. Knocking the DEATH WISH rip-off subgenre into a new stratosphere, MS. 45 showcases a haunting performance from Tamerlis and Ferrara's knack for transforming limited resources into genre revolutions. Content Warning: Contains scenes of sexual assault that some viewers may find distressing. title: The Texas Chain Saw Massacre
description: When Sally (Marilyn Burns) hears that her grandfather's grave may have been vandalized, she and her paraplegic brother, Franklin (Paul A. Partain), set out with their friends to investigate. After a detour to their family's old farmhouse, they discover a group of crazed, murderous outcasts living next door. As the group is attacked one by one by the chainsaw-wielding Leatherface (Gunnar Hansen), who wears a mask of human skin, the survivors must do everything they can to escape. * The first 35 customers to have tickets scanned in each of these performances will recieve an exclusive limited edition " I SURVIVED THE TEXAS CHAINSAW MASSACRE" badge. A replica of one's we gave out back in 1976 when we were the first cinema to debut this iconic film.

title: The Adventures of Prince Achmed
description: This performance will feature a live score performed by Hugo Max . Lotte Reiniger’s The Adventures of Prince Achmed is an enchanting amalgamation of stories from the Arabian Nights animated in cut paper silhouettes, an exquisite artefact of Weimar Cinema and a genre-defying experiment in melding international folk art traditions with the technical possibilities of a new medium. Taken from The Arabian Nights, a wicked sorcerer and the beautiful prince Achmed battle one another in a series of wondrous adventures. Please view this YouTube video for a sample of Hugo's work.

description: The third film in the contemporary version of the Planet of the Apes series finds the ape leader Caesar (another remarkable motion capture performance by Andy Serkis) seeking a safe haven for the survivors of a human-led massacre, only to wind up in a labor camp run by a vicious military officer (Woody Harrelson). title: Angel's Egg
description: In an underwater city, a young girl takes care of a large egg she holds carefully in her arms. A boy with a gun arrives in search of a bird he saw in his dream. At first, it seems as if feelings of sympathy are developing between the two. Forty years after the film’s original release, Anime Limited is proud to present an all-new 4K restoration of the film, supervised by director Mamoru Oshii, in cinemas nationwide for the very first time. The film is a creative collaboration between acclaimed director Mamoru Oshii (Ghost in the Shell), who wrote and directed the feature, and revered artist Yoshitaka Amano (Final Fantasy, Vampire Hunter D). The film beautifully intertwines Oshii’s thematic reflections on philosophy and theology with Amano’s distinctive ink painting style, culminating in an arrestingly beautiful hand-drawn allegorical fantasy.

title: Benedetta
description: With this orgiastic immersion in the mystic reveries of a real-life historical figure, the king of the erotic thriller Paul Verhoeven gives the nunsploitation flick a high-art makeover. Elegant, perverse, and teasingly scandalous, Benedetta critiques religious hypocrisy with an impish grin.

Orlando Bloom plays a humble blacksmith who discovers that he is the son of a knght, and travels to the Holy Land to fight in the crusades. A stranger in a strange land, he serves a doomed King, falls in love with an exotic and forbidden Queen, and rises to knighthood. Ultimately, he must protect the people of Jerusalem from overwhelming forces, while striving to keep a fragile peace.

To Death.” Addicted to love, Elaine – the love witch – casts love and sex spells to seek her perfect man, finding herself with more dead bodies than she does a long-term partner… A visually-striking, humorous and thought-provoking film by the continuously playful Anna Biller, The Love Witch has caused immense debate by audiences through its feminist themes. Visually drenched in 1970s fashion and cinematography, the film´s style feels as magical as the love witch herself. The Love Witch is featured as part of MANEATERS, a season exploring the female supernatural on screen. The season is presented with the National Film and Television School’s Film Studies, Programming and Curation MA.

description: When veteran anchorman Howard Beale is forced to retire his 25-year post because of his age, he announces to viewers that he will kill himself during his farewell broadcast. Network executives rethink their decision when his fanatical tirade results in a spike in ratings.

description: 23-year-old Amélie is lonely. After an isolating childhood, she moves to Paris and becomes a waitress at the Café des Deux Moulins, a bar restaurant filled with a colourful cast of diners and employees. One night, Amélie happens across a box of treasures hidden in her apartment, left by a little boy in the Fifties, that changes the course of her life. Henceforth, she dedicates herself to giving back to her community, tracking down the owner of these keepsakes, consoling a widowed neighbour and befriending a reclusive artist. When completing these good deeds, she crosses paths with Nino, a photobooth collagist who shares her oddball sensibilities. She quickly falls in love with him.

title: The Time Masters
description: Directed by visionary science-fiction animator René Laloux (Fantastic Planet) and designed by the legendary Jean Giraud (a.k.a. Mœbius) The Time Masters is a visually fantastic foray into existentialist space adventure. After his parents are killed on the dangerous planet Perdide, young Piel (voiced by Frédéric Legros) survives by maintaining radio contact with Jaffar (Jean Valmont), a pilot transporting the exiled Prince Matton (Yves-Marie Maurin) and Princess Belle (Monique Thierry) from their former kingdom. Jaffar seeks the help of Silbad (Michel Elias), a cheerful old-timer who knows how to circumvent Perdide’s hazards, including brain-devouring insects and watery graves. Along the way, Jaffar and company encounter a pair of impish homunculi stowaways, identity-less angels controlled by an amorphous hive mind, and the Masters of Time, mysterious beings who can bend reality and perhaps reveal to the heroes their secret origins and destinies. title: Black Fire
description: Since 2013, artist Kevin Jerome Everson and author and historian Claudrena N. Harold have cooperated on a series of lyrical short films—13 to date—that explore Black intellectual, social, and political life at the University of Virginia in Charlottesville, where both are professors. Collectively titled Black Fire , these works highlight the spaces where Black students have studied, learned, and organized through the years, including the school's student-run newspaper and a bus stop that became a locus for collective action. Through short films spotlighting figures such as Paulette Jones Morant, one of the first Black woman scholastic athletes at UVA, and Vivian Gordon, the director of UVA’s Black Studies program from 1974–1980, Black Fire creates significant space for otherwise under-the-radar figures. Employing interviews and reenactment, often casting their students as performers, Everson and Harold's films bring the history of UVA, as well as the historical experiences of Black students and faculty across the US, into meaningful conversation with the present day. Filmmakers Kevin Jerome Everson and Claudrena N. Harold appear in conversation after the films, moderated by filmmaker Cauleen Smith. Special thanks to Madeleine Molyneaux, Sam Raphael, and Now Instant Image Hall.

title: Troy
description: In year 1250 B.C. during the late Bronze age, two emerging nations begin to clash. Paris, the Trojan prince, convinces Helen, Queen of Sparta, to leave her husband Menelaus, and sail with him back to Troy. After Menelaus finds out that his wife was taken by the Trojans, he asks his brother Agamemnon to help him get her back. Agamemnon sees this as an opportunity for power. They set off with 1,000 ships holding 50,000 Greeks to Troy.

title: Frankenweenie
description: Based on Tim Burton’s 1984 short film, Frankenweenie follows young Victor Frankenstein as he goes about his childhood making short films with his four-legged canine friend, Sparky. When Sparky is killed by a car, a distraught Victor resurrects him. Soon other children start resurrecting their own pets, and a horde of undead creatures wreaks havoc, spurring the adults to plot Sparky’s permanent demise. This black-and-white stop motion Frankenstein adaptation features a score by frequent Burton collaborator Danny Elfman and is filled with homages to the classic horror films Burton grew up loving, resulting in a scary and sweet fairytale that will dazzle children and charm adults.

description:
STAY tells the story of an artist (The Artist) sentenced to do time in The Curfew Tower, with only a handheld puppet of Elvis (Puppet Elvis) as company. While doing time, The Artist is expected to write the second-best song he has ever written. And this song is for the Ghost of Elvis and is to be performed at The 25 Comeback Special. In reality The Artist is just trying to escape the gathering storm clouds of his inevitable midlife crisis. That, and the reality of being a bad father. The only dialogue in the film is an internal one between The Artist and Puppet Elvis.
STAY is probably the bleakest film you could ever watch. It contains no sex or violence, no kissing or killing, not even any fucking or fighting, or any of those other things some might want to vicariously experience via the medium of film. STAY is a film without HOPE.
The screening at The Nickel is to be the only screening in UK in 2026. Tracey Moberly, Tony Wright & Puppet Elvis will be there for a post screening interrogation. The former Bill Drummond will be there to chair the interrogation. He will also be there to stamp people’s wrists as they enter the building.
WARNING: It is expected that everyone attending this screening will bring their own handheld puppet to watch the film with them – No Puppet, No Entry. Also... Puppet Elvis will be the judge of the post Interrogation Puppet Contest.

title: Jealousy Is My Middle Name
description: Park Hae-il plays Lee Won-sang, the hero of Park Chan-ok’s debut feature, in his second big-screen appearance. Lee is a 27-year-old graduate student in literature, finishing up his thesis before he leaves for London. When he starts writing an article for a magazine as a favor, he realizes that the head editor, Han Yun-shik, is the reason his girlfriend left him. Lee’s complicated feelings toward Han, a mixture of admiration and jealousy, brings more confusion when he is introduced to a mesmerizing photographer, Park Sung-yeon, a cool, down-to-earth woman who is also having an affair with Han. Calm on the surface but roiling underneath, the story explores human emotions in a macro lens, excavating endless variables that shape characters while they struggle to stay composed. Park’s undefinable approach to Lee allows his character’s purity and honesty to roam free.

title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, The Devils lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. title: The Grand Budapest Hotel
description: Writer-director Wes Anderson was inspired by Austrian novelist Stefan Zweig (1881-1942) for his seriocomic and visually dazzling story about a posh resort, its vain concierge (Ralph Fiennes in a peerless comic performance) and a young lobby boy (Tony Revolori). Anderson directed an all-star international cast and brought his distinctive visual sensibilities to his original story (written with Hugo Guinness), set in a fictional European country on the eve of war. The film received nine nominations including Best Picture and won Oscars for Alexandre Desplat’s effervescent score, Milena Canonero’s costume design, the makeup and hair creations of Frances Hannon and Mark Coulier, and the production design of Adam Stockhausen and his set decorator, Anna Pinnock, who transformed a vacant German department store into the eponymous hotel.

title: Highlander
description: After inexplicably surviving a mortal wound during a clan battle in the Scottish Highlands in 1536, Connor MacLeod (Christopher Lambert) is accused of witchcraft and banished from his village. Years later, he meets Ramirez (Sean Connery), a swordsman who teaches MacLeod the truth about himself: he belongs to an immortal race who can only die when the head is cut from the body. MacLeod fights his way through the centuries until the time of The Gathering, when the few immortals who have survived the ages will come together to fight until just one remains. In 1980s New York City the final fight is about to begin and, in the end, there can be only one...

title: Paisàn
description: The second installment in his WWII trilogy and one of Rossellini’s favorites of his films, the episodic Paisàn is another depiction of the tribulations of the Italians under German occupation. Its title translates to “fellow countryman” and takes a broader view of Italy than his previous Rome, Open City (1945) , moving the action outside the capital to focus on the interactions between American armed forces and the country residents impacted by conflict. Future Italian auteur Federico Fellini co-wrote the screenplay, which came together on the fly, with dialogue of each sequence written just before it was filmed.

description: In an underwater city, a young girl takes care of a large egg she holds carefully in her arms. A boy with a gun arrives in search of a bird he saw in his dream. At first, it seems as if feelings of sympathy are developing between the two. Forty years after the film’s original release, Anime Limited is proud to present an all-new 4K restoration of the film, supervised by director Mamoru Oshii, in cinemas nationwide for the very first time. The film is a creative collaboration between acclaimed director Mamoru Oshii (Ghost in the Shell), who wrote and directed the feature, and revered artist Yoshitaka Amano (Final Fantasy, Vampire Hunter D). The film beautifully intertwines Oshii’s thematic reflections on philosophy and theology with Amano’s distinctive ink painting style, culminating in an arrestingly beautiful hand-drawn allegorical fantasy.

title: Germany Year Zero
description: Released the same year the first theories of neo-realism were published in film magazines Esprit, La Revue du Cinéma , and Bianco e Nero by acclaimed critics, including André Bazin, Germany Year Zero rounds out Rossellini’s WWII trilogy and brings a continental scope to the devastating impact of Hitler’s final solution. By centering the story on a young boy navigating the devastating implications of war, Rossellini accentuates the stark contrast between generations. A major influence on François Truffaut’s The 400 Blows (1959) and cast with people the director found by exploring the four zones of Berlin, Germany Year Zero would, Rossellini hoped, “reproduce the truth exactly as the camera saw it for that audience through the entire world which has a heart capable of love and a brain capable of thought.”

title: Empire of Passion
description: With an arresting mix of eroticism and horror, Oshima plunges the viewer into a nightmarish tale of guilt and retribution in Empire of Passion (Ai no borei). Set in a Japanese village at the end of the nineteenth century, the film details the emotional and physical downfall of a married woman and her younger lover following their decision to murder her husband and dump his body in a well. Empire of Passion was Oshima's only true kaidan (Japanese ghost story), and the film, a savage, unrelenting experience, earned him the best director award at the Cannes Film Festival.

title: Taxi Driver
description: Suffering from insomnia, disturbed loner Travis Bickle (Robert De Niro) takes a job as a New York City cabbie, haunting the streets nightly, growing increasingly detached from reality as he dreams of cleaning up the filthy city. When Travis meets pretty campaign worker Betsy (Cybill Shepherd), he becomes obsessed with the idea of saving the world, first plotting to assassinate a presidential candidate, then directing his attentions toward rescuing 12-year-old prostitute Iris (Jodie Foster).

title: The Misfits
description: Penned by Arthur Miller, this contemporary Western centers on the recently divorced Roslyn (Marilyn Monroe) and her relationship with an aging former cowboy, Gay (Clark Gable), who now survives by rounding up wild mustangs to sell them to a slaughterhouse. Considered a commercial failure at the time of its original release, the film has since been regarded as a classic by critics and audiences, perhaps notably because it was the final completed film of both Gable and Monroe, and a fitting bookend to Monroe’s career—she credited Huston for her first big break in his The Asphalt Jungle (1950).

description: * ON SALE 23rd OCT * With excruciating honesty, The Squid and the Whale chronicles the experiences of two young brothers growing up in 1980s Park Slope, Brooklyn, as they navigate the jagged contours of the divorce of their parents, both writers. The acclaimed third feature by Noah Baumbach marked a critical development for the filmmaker as he turned toward an increasingly personal style—a move that garnered him an Academy Award nomination for best original screenplay. Shot in Super 16 mm and featuring a quartet of nuanced, understated performances from Jeff Daniels, Laura Linney, Jesse Eisenberg, and Owen Kline, this comic and poignant drama, peppered with autobiographical elements, deftly captures the heartache and confusion of a fracturing family.

title: Trainspotting - 30th Anniversary
description: Heroin addict Mark Renton (Ewan McGregor) stumbles through bad ideas and sobriety attempts with his unreliable friends -- Sick Boy (Jonny Lee Miller), Begbie (Robert Carlyle), Spud (Ewen Bremner) and Tommy (Kevin McKidd). He also has an underage girlfriend, Diane (Kelly Macdonald), along for the ride. After cleaning up and moving from Edinburgh to London, Mark finds he can't escape the life he left behind when Begbie shows up at his front door on the lam, and a scheming Sick Boy follows.

title: Cinematic Void Presents W.R.: MYSTERIES OF THE ORGANISM
description: What does the energy harnessed through orgasm have to do with the state of communist Yugoslavia circa 1971? Only counterculture filmmaker extraordinaire Dušan Makavejev has the answers (or the questions). His surreal documentary-fiction collision WR: MYSTERIES OF THE ORGANISM begins as an investigation into the life and work of controversial psychologist and philosopher Wilhelm Reich and then explodes into a free-form narrative of a beautiful young Slavic girl’s sexual liberation. Banned upon its release in the director’s homeland, the art-house smash WR is both whimsical and bold in its blending of politics and sexuality.

title: Love Exposure
description: The story of a teenage boy named Yu, who falls for Yoko, a girl he runs into while working as an "up-skirt" photographer in an offshoot of the porn industry. His attempts to woo her are complicated by a spot of cross-dressing – which convinces Yoko that she is lesbian – dalliances with kung-fu and crime, and a constant struggle with the guilt that's a legacy of his Catholic upbringing. Contains very strong bloody violence and sex references

title: Barry Lyndon
description: Stanley Kubrick bent the conventions of the historical drama to his own will in this dazzling vision of a pitiless aristocracy, adapted from a novel by William Makepeace Thackeray. In picaresque detail, Barry Lyndon chronicles the adventures of an incorrigible trickster (Ryan O’Neal) whose opportunism takes him from an Irish farm to the battlefields of the Seven Years’ War and the parlours of high society. For the most sumptuously crafted film of his career, Kubrick recreated the decadent surfaces and intricate social codes of the period, evoking the light and texture of eighteenth-century painting with the help of pioneering cinematographic techniques and lavish costume and production design, all of which earned Academy Awards. The result is a masterpiece—a sardonic, devastating portrait of a vanishing world whose opulence conceals the moral vacancy at its heart. Please Note: The film will be presented with a brief 5-10min intermission.

L’amore
description: “I’ve made films in episodes because I feel more at ease like that.” —Roberto Rossellini, 1952 Rossellini’s appreciation for episodic storytelling, which his later forays into television allowed him to explore with more freedom, first began in feature-length filmmaking. Part one, titled “Una voce umana,” is based on a play by Jean Cocteau and features the filmmaker’s then-lover, esteemed actress Anna Magnani, known only as the woman on the phone, speaking to a former flame. In part two, “Il miracolo,” a woman is sure she is pregnant with the child of a saint. Dubbed the best foreign film that year by New York critics, Amore was also met with derision when Rossellini was charged with blasphemy by the city’s archbishop due to the content of the film’s second half.

title: British Horror Studio: Black Chariot
description: Introducing a season from the British Horror Studio. An independent British film studio Focusing on Gothic drama and arthouse filmmaking with a distinctive British horror character. Black Chariot is a supernatural noir horror film steeped in guilt, grief, and the lingering shadows of a crime gone wrong. Set within a world of doomed criminals, haunted survivors, private detectives, and sinister apparitions, the film draws on the mood of classic noir and the dread of Gothic horror to tell a character-driven story of violence, memory, and consequence. Starring Laurence R. Harvey, Megan Tremethick, Novarro Ramon, Dorian Todd, Sam McMillan, Richard Pate, and Nick Ford, Black Chariot places damaged characters at the centre of its supernatural mystery. As the past tightens its grip, the film becomes a dark meditation on trauma, masculinity, guilt, and the terrible price of trying to outrun the dead. https://www.britishhorrorstudio.com/

title: Before Sunrise
description: On his way to Vienna, American Jesse (Ethan Hawke) meets Celine (Julie Delpy), a student returning to Paris. After long conversations forge a surprising connection between them, Jesse convinces Celine to get off the train with him in Vienna. Since his flight to the U.S. departs the next morning and he has no money for lodging, they wander the city together, taking in the experiences of Vienna and each other. As the night progresses, their bond makes separating in the morning a difficult choice.

title: Who Can Kill a Child?
description: Tom and Evelyn (Lewis Fiander and Prunella Ransome), a young couple from England, plan an idyllic getaway to a remote Spanish island, in anticipation of the birth of their third child. When they arrive, they find their destination almost entirely deserted, with the exception of a number of children, all of whom are acting strangely. When the couple begin to find evidence of a number of atrocities on the island, they quickly find themselves embroiled in a terrifying battle for survival, as well as being forced to confront a previously unthinkable question… Directed by Narciso Ibáñez Serrador (El televisor, The House That Screamed), the legendary master of horror dubbed the ‘Spanish Hitchcock’, Who Can Kill A Child? is his undisputed masterpiece, an extreme and unbearably tense work that remains deeply shocking in its disregard for societal taboos. With a cult reputation that has continued to grow among genre aficionados since its release in 1976, Who Can Kill A Child? is now considered not just as a landmark work of Euro-horror, but as one of the greatest horror films ever made (Slant Magazine). Content warning: Please be aware that this version of the film contains a restored eight-minute documentary prologue composed of real archival footage of children suffering in global conflicts including The Holocaust, The Vietnam War and the Nigerian Civil War. The filmmakers included it to underline how adults have historically used and harmed children as helpless victims of conflict, but the use of real-life tragedies has proved controversial and disturbing for audiences. Presented from a brand-new 4K restoration of the film courtesy of Radiance Films.

title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
description: Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision. Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, accused of bewitching a convent of nuns, The Devils lays bare the collusion of church and state through a searing vision of religious persecution, collective hysteria and institutional corruption. The restoration many believed would never happen reaffirms Russell’s incendiary masterpiece as among the most overwhelming and uncompromising achievements in British cinema. Assembled from original camera negative, this 4k restoration is Ken Russell’s 2004 preferred edit. Picture and sound restoration by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color and Warner Bros. Sound. Following the sold-out LFF performance on 12th October, Ken Russell's THE DEVILS will screen daily from 30th October. Screenings from both 35mm and Digital. 35mm performances will be noted next to the time. If there is no note next to the time, the performance is Digital.

For one of his first produced screenplays, Walter Hill adapted one of noir master Jim Thompson’s darkest novels into a more light-hearted but still cynical romantic thriller, with director Sam Peckinpah staging the film’s action sequences with his usual vividness.

title: Vertigo
description: A former San Francisco police detective juggles wrestling with his personal demons and becoming obsessed with the hauntingly beautiful woman he has been hired to trail, who may be deeply disturbed.

title: The Time Masters
description: Directed by visionary science-fiction animator René Laloux (Fantastic Planet) and designed by the legendary Jean Giraud (a.k.a. Mœbius) The Time Masters is a visually fantastic foray into existentialist space adventure. After his parents are killed on the dangerous planet Perdide, young Piel (voiced by Frédéric Legros) survives by maintaining radio contact with Jaffar (Jean Valmont), a pilot transporting the exiled Prince Matton (Yves-Marie Maurin) and Princess Belle (Monique Thierry) from their former kingdom. Jaffar seeks the help of Silbad (Michel Elias), a cheerful old-timer who knows how to circumvent Perdide’s hazards, including brain-devouring insects and watery graves. Along the way, Jaffar and company encounter a pair of impish homunculi stowaways, identity-less angels controlled by an amorphous hive mind, and the Masters of Time, mysterious beings who can bend reality and perhaps reveal to the heroes their secret origins and destinies. Restored in 4K in 2023 at the initiative of CITE FILMS in collaboration with the Fondazione Cineteca di Bologna and with the support of the CNC

title: Whisper of the Heart
description: Discover the brilliance of this heartwarming coming-of-age classic from the legendary Studio Ghibli, creators of My Neighbour Totoro and the Academy Award®-winning Spirited Away. A chance encounter with a mysterious cat sends Shizuku, a girl with her head in the clouds, on a quest for her true talent. Together with Seiji, a boy determined to follow his dreams, and enchanted by The Baron, an antique cat figurine who guides her to listen to the whispers of her heart, Shizuku embarks on a life-changing adventure that takes her beyond the boundaries of her imagination. Based on a screenplay and storyboards from Hayao Miyazaki, WHISPER OF THE HEART is a precious gem in the Studio Ghibli catalogue, directed by veteran animator Yoshifumi Kondo.

title: Byzantium
description: “We are a brotherhood. There are no women amongst us” Hunted for two centuries, Clara and Eleanor Webb are the only female vampires alive: a mother who feeds on human blood and will go to any lengths to survive, and her daughter who despises what she is and tries to live a moral life. Forced to find refuge in a run-down coastal hotel, they realise that they can not hide forever; not when their past and secrets are coming back to haunt them. Blood waterfalls, razor-sharp claws and cults of knowledge; from the director of Interview with the Vampire (1994), Byzantium is deliciously gothic, seductively atmospheric, and inescapably tragic. A must-watch title in the vampire genre, Neil Jordan depicts vampire lore in a contemporary way while staying true to its archaic themes. Byzantium is featured as part of MANEATERS, a season exploring the female supernatural on screen. The season is presented with the National Film and Television School’s Film Studies, Programming and Curation MA.

After inheriting a century-old moustache from an eccentric great-aunt, David Bramwell follows the trail of its former owner through séances, spiritualist churches, Brighton basement clubs and an increasingly strange occult odyssey.
Blending filmed monologue, memoir and psychedelic folklore, this funny and affecting modern fireside tale won a Special Mention Audience Award at CINECITY 2025. The screening is followed by an on-stage Q&A.

title: Ten Years of Monkey Tennis (with Peter Serafinowicz)
description: “One of the best TV and film podcasts” – The Telegraph “What’s the best thing?” It’s a question for our times. It’s the question of our lives. And it’s one of Alan Partridge’s best-known phone-in topics. Finally, as part of their 10-year birthday celebrations, the hosts of Monkey Tennis (the award-winning, chart-topping Alan Partridge fan podcast) will tackle it live, armed with only four microphones and a live audience. Join them as they pit elements of the APU (Alan Partridge Universe) against each other to determine, once and for all, the answer to Alan’s largest question: “What’s the Best Thing?” Will it be 'Alpha Papa’ or Sidekick Simon, a shop-soiled chocolate orange or a can of Sprünt, Flench and Sons Tanning or Bangkok Chick Boys? Afterwards, they’ll also be speaking to star of I’m Alan Partridge (as well as Guardians of the Galaxy , Amandaland , Parks & Recreation , Shaun of the Dead , Spaced and 100+ more), Peter Serafinowicz, about his epic career and his time as Alan’s antagonist and lover of American things, Tex. In the meantime, catch up on over 150 episodes of the Monkey Tennis podcast, covering almost everything Alan's ever done, at podfollow.com/monkeytennis
